findings.title: create_application returns Err after the app registration was already created, so no cache is invalidated and a retry creates a duplicate
findings.rationale: caching-and-search.md's rule for multi-step mutations is "a partial success is a real write — invalidate, gated on 'something actually changed'", which `downgrade_application_permission_core`, `remove_expired_passwords` and the bulk commands obey. Here `POST /applications` succeeds, then a 403/429 from `ensure_service_principal` (or `add_password`) propagates via `?`; the command returns Err and `invalidate_app_lists` never runs. `apps_pairing`, `app_name_index` and `search_corpus` are pinned (LRU cannot evict them) with a 60-minute TTL, so the App Registrations list and global search do not show the new app, the operator sees only an error, and the natural retry creates a second registration with the same display name (Entra allows duplicates). `bulk_create` avoids this only because it passes `..Default::default()` (no SP, no secret).
findings.proposal: Give `create_application_core` the shape `downgrade_application_permission_core` already has: return `Ok((CreateApplicationResult, Option<UiError>))` (or add `error: Option<UiError>` to `CreateApplicationResult`) once `create_application` has landed, collecting SP/secret failures instead of `?`-ing them; in the command, call `invalidate_app_lists` whenever `application` exists and then surface the error. Update `bulk.rs:570` and `restore.rs:218` callers (both already tolerate per-item errors). Add a wiremock handler test (POST /applications 201, POST /servicePrincipals 403) asserting `apps_pairing`/`app_name_index` are dropped and the error is returned.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is real: applications/mod.rs:322-323 `create_application_core(..).await?` then `invalidate_app_lists`; mod.rs:338 POST lands, mod.rs:343-347 `ensure_service_principal(..).await?` and mod.rs:356 `add_password(..).await?` propagate after the registration exists. UI reaches it: views/dialogs/create_app_dialog.rs:54 sends `create_service_principal: csp` (rest `..Default::default()`). `ensure_service_principal` (graph service_principals.rs:506-516) has no replication retry, while sso/mod.rs:52-72 exists precisely because a create-then-reference call can fail right after a POST — so the partial path is reachable in practice, not just under 403/429. Consequence checked: apps_pairing/app_name_index/search_corpus are pinned (cache.rs:214-222, 296-304; mod.rs:220) so only TTL or the list's explicit Refresh (application_list.rs:249 `invalidate_list_cache`) recovers; restore.rs:213-235 also treats the Err as 'not created' so a re-run restore would duplicate too. bulk.rs:566-570 is safe only via `..Default::default()`. caching-and-search.md 'a partial success is a real write — invalidate' names `downgrade_application_permission` as the model (permissions.rs:887-890). Severity downgraded from high to medium: the operator gets an error, the app exists, and the list Refresh button busts the cache; the duplicate-on-retry is real but is clutter (an orphan finding), not a security regression.

findings.title: get_application_detail caches a degraded permission resolution: a transient failure resolving one resource SP marks all of that resource's permissions as not granted for the 60-minute TTL
findings.rationale: `.ok().flatten()` collapses `Err(429/5xx/dead token)` into the same `None` as `Ok(None)` (resource SP genuinely absent). With `live_sp == None` both join closures return `None`, so every `ResolvedPermission` for that resource carries `runtime_assignment_id: None` / `runtime_grant_id: None`, which the Permissions tab renders as not granted and offers to grant. The detail is then stored unconditionally under `app_detail_key` for the Lists TTL. AGENTS.md says a degraded run is never cached nor shown as all-clear; here a permission that IS granted is shown as absent, and only the operator's manual Refresh clears it. `resolve_resource_sp` itself caches only `Ok`, so the graph layer got this right and the command layer undid it.
findings.proposal: Make `resolve_required_resource_access` return `(Vec<ResolvedPermission>, bool /*degraded*/)` by keeping `Result<Option<SP>>` per resource and setting `degraded` on any `Err`; in `get_application_detail` skip `state.cache.put` when degraded, and add `#[serde(default)] resolution_degraded: bool` to `ApplicationDetail` so the tab can show a `Callout` ("Permission grants could not be fully resolved; Refresh to retry"). Unit-test the resolver with one `Err` resource: rows still returned, flag set.
findings.verifier_notes: permissions_resolve.rs:277 `client.resolve_resource_sp(&id).await.ok().flatten()` collapses Err into the same `None` the ladder reserves for 'resource SP genuinely absent' (resolve_one_permission's step 2/3 comments). With `resource_sp_id == None` both closures at :303-304 and :310-311 return None, so every row for that resource has no runtime id; permissions_tab.rs:912-913 renders 'Not granted' from exactly those fields and :559 feeds `granted` into LegacyExchangeGrantsCallout; the not-granted Trash path at :948-960 removes the declaration. mod.rs:292 then `state.cache.put(CacheKind::Lists, detail_key, &detail)` unconditionally for the 60-min TTL. Graph layer caches only Ok (service_principals.rs:664-686), so the finding's 'undone at the command layer' is accurate. No comment documents the swallow as deliberate. Severity downgraded to medium: a dead token fails earlier at `get_application` (mod.rs:252-256) with `?`, so the realistic trigger is retry-budget exhaustion under throttling, and the detail-pane Refresh (application_detail_pane.rs:57-71) clears it; the proposal (degraded flag, skip cache, Callout) is consistent with the repo's 'degraded run is never cached' rule and the existing `#[serde(default)]` additive-field pattern.

findings.title: global_search (and prefetch_search_corpus / get_directory_index_status) answer from cache without proving the session, and the invariant that pins the rule cannot see them
findings.rationale: session.rs documents that a read-through command whose hit path returns before a token is fetched must call `prove_tenant_session` first, because otherwise the `tenant_id` argument alone decides whose directory data is returned (tenant switch mid-flight; dead session with data caches kept). `graph_for` only constructs token adapters (no token is acquired until a request), so on a warm corpus `global_search` returns the previous session's app/SP names having proven nothing. The invariant passes vacuously: the `cache.get_typed` lives inside `search_corpus`, not the command body, and `graph_for(` is accepted as a proof. `prefetch_search_corpus` (search.rs:235-236) and `get_directory_index_status` (mod.rs:108-109, via `sp_index_cached`) have the same shape, with less to leak. Sign-out sweeps the caches, so the exposure is the mid-flight switch and dead-session cases, which is why this is medium rather than high.
findings.proposal: Add `crate::commands::session::prove_tenant_session(&state, &tenant_id)?;` as the first statement of `global_search`, `prefetch_search_corpus` and `get_directory_index_status`. Harden the invariant: extend `first_cache_read` to also match the cached-accessor names (`sp_index_cached(`, `app_name_index_cached(`, `indexes_cached(`, `search_corpus(`, `sp_index_hit(`, `load_gallery_corpus(`), and drop `graph_for(`/`*_for(` from `SESSION_PROOFS` (a factory call is not a proof); bump `KNOWN_CACHE_READING_COMMANDS` accordingly.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise holds: search.rs:254 builds the client via `graph_for` (state.rs:415-440 only constructs `ScopedTokenAdapter`s — token_adapter.rs:54-65 is a plain struct build, no token acquired), and search.rs:302 / :235-236 / applications/mod.rs:108-109 answer from `get_typed` inside helpers (search.rs:114-118, cache.rs:234-236), which repo_invariants/cache.rs `first_cache_read` (scans only `cmd.body`, sources.rs:138-178) cannot see; `graph_for(` is in SESSION_PROOFS at cache.rs:564-571. The repo's own commands already say `graph_for` on the miss path is not a proof (mod.rs:134-136, :231-233; credentials.rs:41-44). The dead-session exposure is real: auth service/mod.rs:537 and :624 purge `known_tenants` on RefreshTokenMissing while data caches are kept, so `tenant_context` is None yet a warm corpus is served. Severity lowered to low: sign_out sweeps the tenant cache (service/mod.rs:561-566), so the data returned always belongs to a tenant this same process/operator signed into; the practical effect is search keeps answering from cache instead of raising `not_signed_in` to trigger in-place re-auth. Proposal note: dropping `graph_for(` from SESSION_PROOFS also catches keyvault_rbac.rs:106/:227 (`graph_for` before a per-item `cache.get` inside a closure), which would need a `prove_tenant_session` too — cheap and correct.

findings.title: grant_single_permission_core and grant_admin_consent_core return Err after real writes (manifest PATCH, SP creation) so the command layer never invalidates
findings.rationale: In the single-grant core the `requiredResourceAccess` PATCH lands, then `ensure_service_principal` (creates an SP, a new Enterprise App row) or `resolve_resource_sp` fails with `?`. The command receives Err and busts nothing: the cached detail shows the old manifest, and a newly created SP is missing from `sp_index`/enterprise/search for the TTL. In the admin-consent core the SP is created and then the idempotency `try_join` fails (a 403 on `oauth2PermissionGrants` for an operator without `DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All` is realistic); same outcome. The repo already solved this exact shape in `downgrade_application_permission_core` and its doc comment explains why; the two grant cores predate it.
findings.proposal: Adopt the `(outcome, Option<UiError>)` return in both grant cores: once the manifest PATCH or `ensure_service_principal` has landed, collect later errors instead of `?`, and have `grant_single_permission` / `grant_admin_consent` (and the bulk/restore callers) invalidate on `manifest_changed || sp_created` before surfacing the error. Mirror the two `downgrade` tests for these cores with wiremock.
findings.verifier_notes: permissions.rs:635-643 PATCHes `requiredResourceAccess`, then :648 `ensure_service_principal(..).await?`, :649-656 `resolve_resource_sp(..).await?` / `ok_or_else(..)?`, and :665 `list_app_role_assignments(..).await?` after a possibly-created SP — all propagate as Err, and grant_single_permission (:578-588) invalidates only on Ok. grant_admin_consent_core :394 creates the SP then :408-412 `try_join(..).await?`; grant_admin_consent (:344-353) likewise. The repo already solved this shape with the `(outcome, Option<UiError>)` return and doc comment at :887-890 / :846-855. The bulk caller has the same gap: bulk.rs:470-482 maps a core Err to `sp_created: false`, and :513-517 busts nothing if no other app granted, so a created SP stays out of sp_index/enterprise/search for the TTL. restore.rs:274 also tolerates per-item Err without recording sp creation. Medium is right: stale detail/enterprise rows for up to 60 min after a real write, recoverable by Refresh.

findings.title: list_app_role_resources is cached with "no mutation-driven invalidation" although the App roles tab mutates exactly what it lists
findings.rationale: `list_tenant_app_role_resources` returns tenant-owned SPs exposing an enabled Application role plus a role count. `upsert_enterprise_app_role`/`delete_enterprise_app_role` change that set (first Application role added, last one disabled), and `create_application`/`delete_application` add or remove the SP. None of them drop `{tenant}|app_role_resources`, so the Grant-access picker's "Tenant app registrations" group (permission_picker.rs:119) omits a freshly published API, keeps a deleted app, and shows stale counts for up to 60 minutes. The graph crate already busts its own `resource:` prefix on the same writes for the same reason (applications.rs:622-625); the command-side list was not given the same treatment.
findings.proposal: Move `app_role_resources_key` into `applications/cache.rs`; drop it inside `invalidate_app_lists`, and add a targeted `cache.invalidate(CacheKind::Lists, &app_role_resources_key(tenant))` on the Ok path of `upsert_enterprise_app_role` and `delete_enterprise_app_role`. Extend `detail_cache_tests` with an assertion that `invalidate_app_lists` drops it. Fix the doc comment.
findings.verifier_notes: permissions.rs:26-28 `app_role_resources_key` is private to the module; :68 `cache.put(CacheKind::Lists, key, &rows)`; the doc comment at :39-41 claims 'read-only directory ... no mutation-driven invalidation is wired'. But the app mutates the set: app_roles.rs:336-339 and :365 `invalidate_app_details` only (which sweeps `app_detail|`/`mail_scopes|` prefixes, cache.rs:83-90), and `invalidate_app_lists` (cache.rs:107-133) has no `app_role_resources` key; grep confirms nothing else touches it. The graph crate busts its own `resource:` prefix on the same write (applications.rs:622-625), so the command-side list is the odd one out. permission_picker.rs:112-122 loads it once per wizard open with no Refresh affordance and renders the 'Tenant app registrations' optgroup (:190). The documented rationale is unsound (the directory is mutated by this app), so it does not refute. Medium is fair: an operator who exposes a new Application role and immediately opens Grant access won't find the API for up to an hour.

findings.title: list_credential_expirations stores a tenant-wide scan unguarded, the store-after-invalidate race the doc records as fixed for the other list caches
findings.rationale: A `remove_password`/`add_password` landing during the multi-second `/applications` scan calls `invalidate_app_credentials`, which drops `credential_expirations`; the scan then stores its pre-mutation snapshot, so the Credential Expiry tab and the Home tile show a removed secret as still expiring (or miss a new one) until the 60-minute TTL. The entry is not pinned, so LRU can evict it under pressure, but nothing else corrects it. The guard invariant only counts `put_index(`/`put_typed_index(`, so a plain `put` after a tenant-wide scan is invisible to it.
findings.proposal: Capture `let watch = state.cache.generation_for(CacheKind::Lists, &cache_key);` before `list_applications_all` and store via `state.cache.put_index_if_current(watch, &rows)` (this is a full-directory-scan entry, exactly what the doc says pinning is for; the bucket already pins `apps_pairing`). Extend the invariant to flag a `cache.put(` in any command body that also contains `list_applications_all(`/`list_service_principals_index(`.
findings.verifier_notes: credentials.rs:214-230 runs the multi-second `list_applications_all` scan and :249 stores with plain `cache.put` — no `generation_for` watch. `invalidate_app_credentials` (cache.rs:157) drops `credential_expirations` mid-scan, so the snapshot re-lands stale until the 60-min TTL. caching-and-search.md 'The other half' section records fixing exactly this for apps_pairing/enterprise/MI (enterprise_application.rs:115, managed_identity.rs:88 use `put_index_if_current`), and the invariant at repo_invariants/cache.rs:229 counts only `put_index(`/`put_typed_index(`, so this plain `put` is invisible to it. Severity lowered to low: the window is a credential mutation landing during a tenant-wide scan, the entry is unpinned so LRU can also evict it, and the Credential Expiry view has a Refresh (credentials_dashboard.rs:40). Proposal caveat: core cache.rs has no unpinned guarded store (only `put`, `put_index`, `put_index_if_current`, `put_typed_index_if_current`), so the fix either pins this key (consistent with the three list caches, which are pinned the same way) or adds a `put_if_current`.

findings.title: list_applications_with_pairing bypasses the SP-index single-flight gate and has no gate of its own; two frontend surfaces call it
findings.rationale: On a cold tenant, Home mounting and the operator clicking App Registrations before it returns runs two full `/applications` scans and two `/servicePrincipals` scans (tens of seconds each on a large tenant), and a concurrent gated reader (Enterprise Apps, MI list, search prewarm) runs a third SP scan because `state.single_flight(sp_index_key)` never sees this caller. The same file's sibling helpers were explicitly rewritten to avoid this. The dedicated `sp_index_watch` helper exists only to serve this bypass.
findings.proposal: Replace the `None` arm with `futures::future::try_join(client.list_applications_all(query, Some(APPS_MAX)), cache::sp_index_cached(&state, &client, &tenant_id))` (keeps the concurrency, gains the gate and the correctly-keyed watch; `sp_index_watch` and the `Some(cached_index)` arm become unnecessary since `sp_index_cached` hit-checks). Wrap the miss path in `state.single_flight(&cache_key)` with a post-lock re-check, as `search_corpus` does.
findings.verifier_notes: mod.rs:174-196: the `None` arm calls `client.list_service_principals_index()` directly under `try_join`, bypassing `state.single_flight(sp_index_key)` that `sp_index_cached` holds (cache.rs:242-258); there is also no gate on `apps_pairing_key` itself. cache.rs:352-355 documents that the sibling `indexes_cached` was rewritten to avoid exactly this bypass, and `sp_index_watch` (cache.rs:199-207) exists only to serve this arm. Both frontend callers are real (home_dashboard.rs:38, application_list.rs:234); a Tauri invoke already in flight when the operator switches view keeps running on the backend, so two `/applications` + two `/servicePrincipals` scans plus a third SP scan from any gated reader is the cold-tenant cost. The proposed `try_join(list_applications_all, sp_index_cached)` keeps concurrency (both return GraphError) and inherits the correctly-keyed watch; wrapping the miss path in `single_flight(&cache_key)` mirrors search.rs:120-131. Perf-only, so medium is the ceiling.

findings.title: Certificate upload does not parse the pasted PEM/DER: a private-key paste is forwarded to Graph and no thumbprint/notAfter is checked or shown
findings.evidence:
credentials.rs:249-259
/// ... Performs minimal validation:
/// strips headers/whitespace and confirms the remainder is valid base64.
fn normalize_cert_blob(input: &str) -> std::result::Result<String, String> {
    let stripped: String = input
        .lines()
        .filter(|line| !line.trim_start().starts_with("-----"))
credentials.rs:117-118
        key: key_b64,
        end_date_time: input.end_date_time,
Cargo.lock: `x509-parser` is already a dependency of `p12-keystore` 0.2.1 and `rcgen` (both direct deps of src-tauri).
findings.rationale: The armour filter strips every `-----` line regardless of label, so the common openssl output that holds `CERTIFICATE` followed by `PRIVATE KEY` decodes as one valid base64 string and the private-key bytes are transmitted to Graph before it rejects the blob; a lone `[PEM BEGIN PRIVATE KEY]` paste behaves the same. Nothing parses the DER, so `end_date_time` is never checked against the certificate's notAfter, the row's soonest-expiry and the audit's expiring-credential finding can disagree with the real certificate, and the operator gets no thumbprint to confirm what they uploaded. For a security-critical app whose own generate path zeroizes private keys, the upload path should refuse to forward one.
findings.proposal: In `normalize_cert_blob`, reject any `-----BEGIN` label other than `CERTIFICATE` (PRIVATE KEY, RSA PRIVATE KEY, ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY, PKCS7) and take only the first CERTIFICATE block; parse the DER with `x509_parser::parse_x509_certificate` (already in the lock via rcgen) to reject non-certificates and compute the SHA-1 thumbprint via `aws_lc_rs::digest` + `core::thumbprint::hex_upper` as cert.rs does, setting `custom_key_identifier` and optionally surfacing thumbprint/notAfter in the dialog. Drop the end_date_time/notAfter cross-check unless the dialog gains an expiry field (it sends None today). Add tests for the private-key paste and bundle cases.
findings.verifier_notes: True part: applications/credentials.rs:252-259 `normalize_cert_blob` strips every `-----` line regardless of label and only checks base64, so a lone `[PEM BEGIN PRIVATE KEY]` paste is forwarded to Graph (which rejects it), and nothing parses DER, so no thumbprint is shown before upload; `x509-parser` 0.18.1 is already in Cargo.lock via rcgen, and cert.rs:135-137 already has the SHA-1/`thumbprint::hex_upper` pattern. Overstated: (a) 'the expiry is whatever the operator typed' is false — upload_certificate_dialog.rs:81-85 sends `end_date_time: None` and there is no UI field; Graph assigns it (docs: 'If you don't specify it, the system automatically assigns'), so the audit/expiry mismatch does not exist today; (b) the cert+key bundle claim is only sometimes true — `STANDARD.decode` rejects `=` padding mid-string, so a concatenated bundle only passes when the cert DER length is a multiple of 3. The private key goes to Microsoft Graph over TLS in a request Graph rejects — an operator-error path, not an exploitable one. Reclassify as enhancement/robustness at low.

findings.title: GUID search swallows probe failures, so a throttled or dead-session lookup renders as "No matches"
findings.rationale: The module's own contract is that search must never silently omit. On the GUID path a 429, a 403 (operator without SP read), or a dead token on all four probes is indistinguishable from a genuine 404, and the frontend has no signal to show, so an admin pasting an appId from the portal concludes the app does not exist. `Err(GraphError::NotFound)` is the only error that means "not there".
findings.proposal: Distinguish `Err(GraphError::NotFound(_))` (a real miss) from other errors in the GUID branch; add `#[serde(default)] pub lookup_degraded: bool` to `GlobalSearchResults` (additive, like the five existing defaults) set when any probe failed with a non-404, and render it through the same `cap_notice` slot ("Directory lookup failed; results may be incomplete"). Unit-test `assemble_guid_hits` with an `Err(Throttled)` input.
findings.verifier_notes: search.rs:263-276: all four probes are collapsed with `.ok()`/`.ok().flatten()`; only `get_application` (via `GraphError::NotFound`, http_error.rs:74) and the `Ok(None)` forms mean 'not there' (service_principals.rs:528-535 maps 404 to None), so a 429 past the retry budget or a 403 is indistinguishable from a miss, and search.rs:289 hardcodes `corpus_truncated: false`; global_search.rs:319 renders a notice only from that flag. The module doc (search.rs:12-16) states the contract the branch violates. The additive `#[serde(default)]` pattern already exists on GlobalSearchResults (dto/search.rs:34-40). Severity lowered to low: the result is per-query (not cached), the HTTP layer already retries throttling, and a dead token would fail every other surface too; still a genuine, cheap contract fix.

findings.title: Only add_password_core has handler-level (AppState::for_test + wiremock) tests; the grant/create/owners tiering decisions are review-only
findings.rationale: The tiering decisions in this slice (sp_created -> lists vs detail-state in both grant commands; `remove_expired_passwords` invalidating only when something was removed; `set_application_owners` likewise; `downgrade` invalidating on partial success; `create_application` after a partial create) are exactly the review-only rules the credentials.rs comment describes, and two of them are wrong today (findings 1 and 4). The three tests in `handler_tests` are a ready template.
findings.proposal: Refactor `create_application`, `grant_single_permission`, `grant_admin_consent`, `set_application_owners` and `remove_expired_passwords` so the invalidation-tiering body is a `pub(crate) async fn *_core(state: &AppState, ..)` (the `add_password_core` shape), then add `handler_tests` modules mirroring applications/credentials.rs:456-597: success busts the expected tier and keeps the two indexes; failure busts nothing; partial success (first write 2xx, later write 4xx) busts and returns the error. This is the same refactor findings 0 and 3 need, so land them together.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: `#[tokio::test]`/wiremock/`AppState::for_test` appear only in applications/credentials.rs:456-597 and backup.rs:1024 (bulk.rs/dispatch.rs/throttle.rs tokio tests are not handler tests); permissions.rs and applications/mod.rs have none; credentials.rs:26-35 describes the seam and state.rs:283 provides `for_test`. Overstated/imprecise: the grant cores take `&GraphClient` (permissions.rs:405, 611) and the tiering decision (`sp_created` → lists vs detail-state) lives in the `State`-taking commands at :344-353 and :578-588, which `for_test` cannot reach — the proposal must first move those bodies into `_core(&AppState, ..)` shapes like `add_password_core`. The finding also mis-numbers its own cross-references ('findings 1 and 4' should be 0 and 3).

findings.title: create_application_core computes the initial secret lifetime without the 1..=730 clamp used by add_password
findings.rationale: Three copies of the 180-day default and only one of the 1..=730 clamp. `initial_secret_lifetime_days: Option<u32>` accepts `Some(0)` (end == now, Graph 400, which then trips finding 1) and `Some(3650)` (a 10-year secret from a path whose sibling caps at 24 months). Today the create dialog never sends `initial_secret_*` (only bulk/restore reach the core, with `None`), so this is latent rather than live, but the seam is a public IPC argument.
findings.proposal: Extract `clamp_secret_lifetime_days` (or make `resolve_password_window` pub(super)) in applications/credentials.rs and have `create_application_core` compute the end via it and call `add_password_window(&application.id, name, None, end)`. Leave `GraphClient::add_password` in place (keyvault/restore/sso still call it) or migrate those three callers in a separate change. One table test for 0 / 9999.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: mod.rs:354-356 `unwrap_or(180)` + `Duration::from_secs(days as u64 * 86_400)` with no clamp (0 and 3650 accepted), versus applications/credentials.rs:53 `MAX_SECRET_LIFETIME_DAYS = 730` and :81-82 `.clamp(1, ..)`; graph credentials.rs:38-39 has a third 180 default. Latent as stated: create_app_dialog.rs:44-55 never sets `initial_secret_*` and bulk.rs:566-570 / restore.rs:213-219 pass None. Overstated: 'delete `GraphClient::add_password` once callerless' — it has three other callers (keyvault.rs:94, restore.rs:594, sso/mod.rs:359), so it is not callerless after this change.

findings.title: Search corpus reports SP-index truncation but discards the app-registration index's own truncation
findings.rationale: `app_name_index_cached` is capped at `APPS_MAX` (10 000) too. A tenant with more registrations than service principals (automation-heavy tenants accumulate registrations without SPs) has its app-reg half truncated while `corpus_truncated` stays false, so the dropdown says "No matches" for a registration that exists; the doc calls both caps "must not drift" and the SP one is already surfaced for exactly this reason.
findings.proposal: Compute `index_truncated: sps.len() >= SP_INDEX_MAX || apps.len() >= APPS_MAX` (rename the field; the DTO field `corpus_truncated` already abstracts the source), or return the `truncated` bool from `list_application_index_named` and carry it through `app_name_index_cached`.
findings.verifier_notes: search.rs:196-199 sets `sp_index_truncated: sps.len() >= SP_INDEX_MAX` only; `app_name_index_cached` (cache.rs:333-335) caps at `APPS_MAX` and `list_application_index_named` discards `_truncated` (graph applications.rs:378-381). caching-and-search.md says both caps are 10 000 and 'must not drift', and the SP cap is surfaced for exactly this reason (search.rs:190-195 comment even says 'the two indexes are bounded', but only checks one). `corpus_cap: SP_INDEX_MAX` stays numerically right since both are 10 000. `apps.len() >= APPS_MAX` is a one-line fix consistent with the existing pattern.

findings.title: PermissionKind -> manifest entry-type mapping is written three times in permissions.rs, one copy being the helper extracted to avoid that
findings.rationale: `entry_type_for` was "split out so the mapping is testable" yet `declare_app_permission` re-inlines an identical match with identical code and message; a future change to the message or code (the frontend can branch on `code`) would need to be made twice.
findings.proposal: `declare_app_permission`: `let entry_type = entry_type_for(kind)?;`. `remove_declared_permission`: `let entry_type = entry_type_for(kind).ok();` (Unknown legitimately maps to None there).
findings.verifier_notes: permissions.rs:597-606 `entry_type_for` (doc: 'Split out so the mapping is testable', tested at :1063-1073); :759-768 `declare_app_permission` re-inlines the identical match with identical code/message; :232-236 `remove_declared_permission` has the Option form. `entry_type_for(kind)?` and `entry_type_for(kind).ok()` are drop-in and behaviour-preserving.

`app_name_index`, and `search_corpus` keys, plus — transitively — the per-app detail cache
(`invalidate_app_details`) and the cached audit run

AGENTS.md:101 names `invalidate_app_lists / invalidate_app_credentials / invalidate_app_details`; the fourth tier `invalidate_app_detail_state` (cache.rs:99-102, 'the ~dozen call sites', and the one most mutations in permissions.rs/owners.rs/authentication.rs call) is absent, though cache.rs:4-7 module doc does list it. The doc paragraph itself records two prior mis-reads from the same drift, so a pinning test is proportionate. Note the 20 000-byte AGENTS.md budget when adding the name.

findings.title: progress.rs doc comment says tests can pass a tauri::test::mock_app() handle, but the tauri test feature is not enabled and was deliberately dropped
findings.rationale: A contributor following the progress.rs comment will re-add `tauri/test` and reintroduce the Windows breakage the credentials.rs comment records. The generic parameter is harmless but its stated justification is false.
findings.proposal: Reword to state that the generic keeps the helper testable with a caller-defined `Runtime` and that `tauri/test` is intentionally not enabled (link `d8d293e`), or drop the generic and take `&AppHandle`.
findings.verifier_notes: progress.rs:18-20 claims tests can pass a `tauri::test::mock_app()` handle; src-tauri/Cargo.toml:31 `tauri = { version = "2", features = [] }` and dev-dependencies (:87-96) enable no `test` feature; applications/credentials.rs:28-30 and bulk.rs:41 both record that the feature was dropped because it broke the Windows test binary. No test in the tree uses MockRuntime. The generic is harmless; only the justification is wrong and actively misleading.

findings.title: permissions.rs is 1417 lines spanning six concerns; applications/ was already split the same way
findings.rationale: The catalog picker, the pure manifest helpers (`remove_declared_access`, `declare_resource_access`, `swap_declared_role`), and three multi-step Graph orchestrations with different invalidation shapes share one file, which is why the three-way `PermissionKind` duplication and the `(outcome, error)` vs `?` asymmetry between the cores went unnoticed. The glob re-export pattern needed to keep `generate_handler!` paths stable is already proven in `applications/mod.rs`.
findings.proposal: Split into `permissions/{catalog,manifest,consent,grant,downgrade,revoke}.rs` with `pub use *::*` in `permissions/mod.rs`; move the pure manifest helpers and their tests into `manifest.rs`. No behaviour change; `command-parity-check.sh` will confirm the handler set.
findings.verifier_notes: Banners verified at permissions.rs:13, :212, :328, :561, :788, :986 and tests from :1038 (1417 lines). applications/mod.rs:24-32 documents the glob re-export pattern that keeps `generate_handler!` paths stable, so the split is mechanical and proven. The causal claim (the split-less file is 'why' findings 3/12 went unnoticed) is speculative, and this is a judgment-call refactor with no behaviour change; low is the right severity, and it would sensibly ride along with the finding-3 rework rather than stand alone.

findings.title: set_application_authentication validates every redirect URI but passes logout_url to Graph unchecked
findings.rationale: The front-channel logout URL is a browser redirect target with the same threat profile as a reply URL (wildcard, insecure http, javascript: scheme). A bad value today surfaces as a raw Graph 400 instead of the typed `invalid_redirect_uri` the dialog already renders for the other three fields.
findings.proposal: When `logout_url` is non-empty, run it through `validate_redirect_uri` (or a `validate_logout_url` that additionally requires an https scheme) before building the PATCH; add one test.
findings.verifier_notes: authentication.rs:298-304 validates the three redirect-URI lists; :311 passes `input.logout_url.unwrap_or_default()` to Graph unchecked; authentication_tab.rs:106-116 takes it from a free-text Input. core/redirect.rs:14-55 rejects wildcards, `urn:` and non-loopback http and is the obvious reuse. Note `validate_redirect_uri` admits custom schemes (`myapp://`), which a front-channel logout URL should not, so the 'additionally require https' variant is the better shape. Low: a bad value surfaces as a Graph 400 today rather than being accepted.

findings.title: Per-item loops (remove_expired_passwords, set_application_owners, initial owners) continue after a re-auth-fatal error and drop the UiError code
findings.evidence:
applications/credentials.rs:291-297
        match client.remove_password(&object_id, &cred.key_id).await {
            Ok(()) => removed_key_ids.push(cred.key_id.clone()),
            Err(err) => failures.push(KeyFailure { key_id: cred.key_id.clone(), message: err.to_string() }),
owners.rs:63-67
            Err(err) => failures.push(OwnerChangeFailure { principal_id: id.clone(), action: "add".into(), message: err.to_string() }),
dto/lib.rs:78-81  `UiError` has a session-dead reading of `REAUTH_FATAL_CODES` (`refresh_missing`, `not_signed_in`) that needs the `code`.
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md's bulk rule ("degrade to `BulkError`, stop on a re-auth-fatal code") exists because a dead refresh token cannot be re-minted silently, so every remaining item fails identically. These loops are small (one app's secrets/owners) so cancellation is not needed, but `err.to_string()` discards the code, so the frontend cannot recognise the dead session and trigger the in-place `reauthenticate`; the operator sees N identical failure strings.
findings.proposal: Convert each error with `UiError::from(err)`, carry `code` in `KeyFailure`/`OwnerChangeFailure` (additive `#[serde(default)]` field), and `break` the loop when the code is re-auth-fatal, flagging the result.
findings.verifier_notes: applications/credentials.rs:291-297 and owners.rs:60-77 push `err.to_string()` into `KeyFailure`/`OwnerChangeFailure` (dto/applications.rs:270-283 carry only `message`), and mod.rs:363-371 only `tracing::warn!`s; none breaks on a re-auth-fatal code. The frontend routes re-auth centrally on `UiError::is_reauth_fatal` (state/errors.rs:50-55, shell.rs:126) so a carried `code` would be actionable. Correctly scoped by the reviewer as an enhancement: AGENTS.md's stop-on-fatal rule targets long-running/bulk writes, these loops are one app's items, and the very next command fails with a proper code anyway — so low.

findings.title: DirectoryIndexStatus is the only IPC result type defined in a command module and hand-mirrored in the frontend bindings
findings.evidence:
mod.rs:86-95
#[derive(serde::Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct DirectoryIndexStatus {
    pub sp_index_truncated: bool,
    pub sp_index_cap: usize,
}
web-rs/src/bindings/applications.rs:22-28
#[derive(Clone, Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct DirectoryIndexStatus { pub sp_index_truncated: bool, pub sp_index_cap: usize }
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md's repo map places "serializable IPC boundary types (backend + frontend)" in `azapptoolkit-dto`, and the convention is that result DTOs stay snake_case ("DTOs/bindings snake"; `GlobalSearchResults`, which mirrors this struct, has no rename). This is the only result type in the slice that lives outside the DTO crate, uses camelCase, and is duplicated by hand, so a field rename is a silent wire break.
findings.proposal: Move `DirectoryIndexStatus` to `azapptoolkit_dto::applications` with `Serialize + Deserialize` and `use` it from both `commands/applications/mod.rs` and `bindings/applications.rs`; keeping or dropping `rename_all` is a wire-format choice that must change on both sides together (the demo fixture in web-rs/src/demo must match), not a convention requirement.
findings.verifier_notes: True: applications/mod.rs:86-95 defines `DirectoryIndexStatus` with `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` in the command module and bindings/applications.rs:22-28 hand-mirrors it; grep shows it is the only `Serialize` result struct defined under src-tauri/src/commands, and the repo map places IPC boundary types in azapptoolkit-dto. Overstated: 'the convention is that result DTOs stay snake_case' is not accurate — the dto crate carries ~70 `rename_all = "camelCase"` attributes (applications.rs alone has 10, e.g. `OwnerChangeFailure`), so camelCase on a result DTO is not itself a deviation; only the location and the duplicate definition are.

findings.title: ConcurrencyThrottle halves only once under sustained 429 pressure because the window re-anchors on every event
findings.rationale: `HALVE_WINDOW_SECS` is documented as the 'Minimum seconds between cap halvings', but `*last = Some(now)` runs before the `within_window` early return, so a suppressed event still moves the anchor. With 4-8 lanes each receiving 429s more often than every 2s (the normal shape of a Graph throttle storm) `within` is true for every event after the first, and the cap goes 8→4 and stays there — the 'degrade to per-object reads / floor at 1' behaviour never engages. The existing paused-clock test only fires bursts at a single instant and then advances past the window, so it cannot see this.
findings.proposal: Track two instants: `last_throttle` (updated on every event; drives the recovery quiet check) and `last_halved` (updated only when `next < prev`; drives the halving window). Add a `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` that fires `on_throttle` every 1s for 10s on `new(8)` and asserts the limit reaches `MIN_CONCURRENCY`.
findings.verifier_notes: throttle.rs:102-104 sets `*last = Some(now)` unconditionally before the `within_window` early return at :106, so the anchor slides on every suppressed 429 and a stream of events spaced <2s apart never halves past the first 8→4. The struct doc at :41-43 ("halves ... at most once per HALVE_WINDOW_SECS") and the const doc at :21 ("Minimum seconds between cap halvings") both promise repeated halvings under sustained pressure, so this is a real divergence, not a documented decision. The transport fires `on_throttle` on every 429 including retries (transport.rs:626-631, batch.rs:297), which is the exact shape that keeps the window open. The only test (`on_throttle_halves_once_per_window_and_floors_at_one`, :232-252) fires bursts at one instant then advances past the window, so it cannot observe it. Consequence is bounded (the per-request Retry-After handling still works) but a cap stuck at half under a storm burns retry budget and can turn into `unscored` → degraded runs. Proposal (separate `last_halved` from `last_throttle`) is small and correct.

findings.title: Readiness scope probe keeps a hardcoded CAE list that has drifted from the capabilities catalog (group_membership probed non-CAE)
findings.rationale: The catalog carries `scope_feature: Some("group_membership")` (capabilities.rs:308) and `AppState::ensure_group_member_token` acquires it with `cae = true` (state.rs:630-645), but this list omits `group_membership`, so the readiness page pre-warms a non-CAE token for a Graph scope set. state.rs:563-568 states the invariant this breaks: 'cae MUST match the CAE-ness of the adapter that later consumes the same scope set: the token cache key omits CAE-ness, so a non-CAE pre-warm would make a new_cae adapter reuse a non-CAE token'. The same list also names `sync` and `policy_write`, which no catalog entry probes, showing it is maintained by hand and nothing pins it.
findings.proposal: Move CAE-ness next to the scope set: have `AppState::consent_scopes_for` return `(Vec<String>, bool /*cae*/)` (or add a `cae: bool` column to a small feature table) and make both `ensure_scoped_token` wrappers and `probe_scope` read it. Delete the `is_graph` match. Add a unit test asserting every catalog `scope_feature` resolves through `consent_scopes_for`.
findings.verifier_notes: readiness.rs:276-279 hardcodes `"write" | "sync" | "audit_log" | "policy" | "policy_write" | "sharepoint"` while the catalog carries `scope_feature: Some("group_membership")` (capabilities.rs:308) and `ensure_group_member_token` acquires it with `cae = true` (state.rs:630-637). readiness.rs:56-66 probes every distinct catalog `scope_feature`, so `group_membership` is probed through the non-CAE `access_token_for_scopes` branch. The token cache is keyed only by `(tenant_id, scope_key)` (token_cache.rs:120-128; service/mod.rs:396-419 pass different `claims` but the same scopes), so the readiness pre-warm seeds a non-CAE token that the `new_cae` group-member adapter (state.rs:465) then reuses — the invariant state.rs:563-568 spells out in caps. `sync` and `policy_write` in the list have no catalog `scope_feature`, confirming hand maintenance; nothing in tests/ references `is_graph` or `probe_scope`. Practical blast radius is a Graph token without cp1 (CAE revocation delayed until expiry, not a hard failure), so medium rather than high. Proposal to co-locate CAE-ness with `consent_scopes_for` is sound.

findings.title: Redundant-permissions Fix silently drops values whose covering permission is vetoed — doc says they land in `skipped`, and the UI then clears the Fix button
findings.rationale: The handler's fail-closed comment (remediation.rs:373-377) promises: 'skipping it costs the operator a re-run once Exchange answers, and the value shows up in `skipped` saying so'. But when every covering permission is vetoed (`Err(_) => HashMap::new()` at :401 for a non-Exchange-admin, or a transient Exchange failure via `.unwrap_or_default()` at :399) the loop hits `continue` without `skipped.push`. The command returns `Ok { removed: [], skipped: [] }`; `RedundantPermsAction` (web-rs row.rs:377-395) then toasts 'Removed 0 redundant permissions' and calls `on_done`, which `retain`s the RemoveRedundantPermissions button away while the finding and the live permission remain. An operator without Exchange RBAC rights can never see why the Fix did nothing.
findings.proposal: In `plan_redundant_removals`, collect the pre-veto broaders first; if non-empty but the post-veto set is empty, push the value into `skipped` (or a new `vetoed: Vec<String>` on `RedundantPermissionsOutcome` with a reason string). In the UI, only fire `on_done` when `removed` is non-empty, and render the veto reason ('could not confirm the covering permission is org-wide — Exchange unavailable'). Add a planner test for the all-vetoed case.
findings.verifier_notes: remediation.rs:256-264: broaders are filtered by `!broader_is_confined(...)` and an empty post-veto set hits `continue` with no `skipped.push`, contradicting the handler's own comment at :373-377 ("the value shows up in `skipped` saying so"). With `Err(_) => HashMap::new()` (:401) or `.unwrap_or_default()` (:399), `broader_is_confined` (:403-408) returns true for every Graph mail permission, so a non-Exchange-admin gets `Ok { removed: [], skipped: [] }`. The scorer, by contrast, treats an empty `mail_scopes` as org-wide (scoring.rs:47-48, :274-275) and DOES raise the finding. UI: row.rs:377-395 toasts "Removed 0 redundant permissions ... re-run the audit" and calls `on_done` unconditionally on `Ok`, and row.rs:127-129 wires that to clear the remediation kind from the row, so the Fix button disappears while the finding and grant remain. None of the planner tests at remediation.rs:573-660 pass a vetoing closure, so the all-vetoed case is untested. Proposal is correct.

findings.title: score_one swallows a failed SP lookup, skips the org-wide reconciliation, and the run still caches as a clean complete scan
findings.rationale: When the lean lookup fails (Graph 5xx after retries, or a task that runs after the LRU seed was evicted — `seed_lean_sps_from_index` caps at the bucket size), `sp` is `None` but scoring continues: Rule 4 (disabled SP) and Rule 3 (admin consent) lose their input, and — more importantly — `orgwide` is empty so `resolve_mail_scopes_audit_cached` can return a `Scoped { Rbac }` verdict that is never reconciled against a surviving org-wide grant. That is exactly the under-report the AuditCoverageGap::GraphAppRoleAssignments doc (dto/audit.rs:141-146) calls out, yet here nothing is added to `degraded`, so the run passes `run_is_cacheable` and is served from cache as authoritative. Contrast `ResourceResolver.unresolved`, which exists precisely to flag the equivalent hole for resource indexes.
findings.proposal: Either return `Err(err.into())` from score_one on a failed SP lookup (it classifies as Transient → `unscored` → `PerPrincipalScoring`, and a dead session is caught by the same match), or add an `sp_unresolved: AtomicBool` to ScoreCtx and push a new `AuditCoverageGap::ServicePrincipalLookup` when set. In both cases skip the Exchange probe when `sp` is `None` (reconciliation is impossible, so the reduced weight must not be awarded).
findings.verifier_notes: audit.rs:1489-1499 maps a failed `get_service_principal_by_app_id_lean` to `None` with only a warn; the lean lookup propagates Graph errors via `?` (service_principals.rs lean fn, `get_json(...).await?`), so a 5xx after the retry budget lands here. With `sp = None`, `orgwide` is `HashSet::new()` (:1527-1541) and `resolve_mail_scopes_audit_cached` (mail_scopes.rs:228-253 → `reconcile_orgwide_grant` at :173) can no longer defeat a `Scoped` verdict — precisely the under-report `AuditCoverageGap::GraphAppRoleAssignments` documents (dto/audit.rs:141-146). Nothing pushes to `degraded` on this path (contrast `unscored` → `PerPrincipalScoring` at :393-396 and `resolver.had_unresolved()` → `PermissionResolution` at :402-404), so `run_is_cacheable` (:445) passes and the run is cached as complete, against the AGENTS.md "degraded run is never cached" rule. Rare in practice (the SP index seeds most lookups; `seed_lean_sps_from_index` caps at the bucket size, service_principals.rs:296-297), so medium not high. Returning `Err` (→ `Transient` via `classify_audit_failure`, audit.rs:65-73) is the minimal fix consistent with the existing shape.

findings.title: Claims-mapping (Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration) and provisioning read (Synchronization.Read.All) have no capabilities-catalog entry, so readiness never lists them and SSO 403s carry no role remediation
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md: 'three auth planes share one capabilities catalog — add an entry instead of a hardcoded role string'. The SSO claims-mapping flow acquires `policy_write` via `ensure_policy_write_token` (two call sites in commands/sso/mod.rs) and the Graph client carries a `sync_token`, but `CAPABILITIES` has no entry whose `scope_feature` is `policy_write` or `sync`. The readiness checklist therefore cannot tell an operator that claims-mapping needs `Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration` plus Cloud Application Administrator, and a 403 on those paths has no `capability_key` for `graph_err::forbidden_remediation`. The probe list even names both features, so the probing code exists and simply has nothing to attach to.
findings.proposal: Add `sso_claims_mapping` (scope_feature `policy_write`) and `provisioning_read` (scope_feature `sync`) entries to `CAPABILITIES`; splice `forbidden_remediation(&err, "sso_claims_mapping")` into the two `ensure_policy_write_token` call paths' error handling in commands/sso/mod.rs; add a test asserting the set of `consent_scopes_for` feature keys equals the set of catalog `scope_feature`s. Fold the readiness `is_graph` list removal (finding 1) into the same change so the two tables can't drift.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise holds: `consent_scopes_for` accepts `policy_write` and `sync` (state.rs:534-551), `ensure_policy_write_token` is called at sso/mod.rs:158 and :1637, `request_scope_consent(.., "policy_write")` is called from sso_wizard_dialog.rs:223 and sso_tab.rs:682, and the Graph client's `sync_token` gates provisioning reads (client.rs:294-295, directory.rs:12) — yet no `Capability` in capabilities.rs has `scope_feature` `policy_write` or `sync` (the grep at :142-395 lists write/audit_log/policy/sharepoint/group_membership/keyvault/arm/log_analytics/exchange only), and sso/mod.rs has no `forbidden_remediation` splice. Overstated: the consent half is already surfaced — both SSO paths pre-acquire via `ensure_policy_write_token` so a missing consent reaches the UI typed as `consent_required` with a Grant consent button; what is missing is the readiness checklist row and the 403 role remediation. That is a coverage gap, not a bug, so low. Corrected proposal below.

findings.title: bulk_remove_expired_credentials walks the whole tenant even for an explicit selection and hardcodes 10_000 instead of APPS_MAX
findings.rationale: The Findings pane's 'Fix all N' and the App Registrations bulk bar always pass `Some(object_ids)` (a handful to a few hundred ids), yet the command still walks every page of `/applications` — tens of seconds on a large tenant — before discarding all but the selection. `ids.contains` is a linear scan per app (10 000 × selection size). And the comment's 'where the cap cannot matter' is wrong: a selected app beyond the 10 000th page position is dropped from `apps`, so `apps_scanned` is short and the UI has no signal (the flag is bound to `_truncated`). The literal `10_000` also duplicates `applications::APPS_MAX`, which audit.rs:84 uses by name.
findings.proposal: When `object_ids` is `Some`, fetch exactly those apps via `batch_get_json::<Application>` on `/applications/{id}?$select=id,appId,displayName,passwordCredentials` (falling back to per-id `get_application` on a whole-batch failure) and skip the list walk; keep the walk only for the `None` tenant sweep. Replace the `10_000` literal with `super::applications::APPS_MAX`. Drop the `HashSet`/O(n·m) and 'dropped selection' points.
findings.verifier_notes: Core premise holds: bulk.rs:163-176 walks `/applications` to the 10_000 cap even when `object_ids` is `Some`, and the only frontend caller always passes `Some(&ids)` (bulk_action_bar.rs:511), so every 'Fix all N' pays a full tenant walk before `retain`. The literal `10_000` duplicates `applications::APPS_MAX` (applications/mod.rs:75), which audit.rs:82, credentials.rs:32 and backup.rs:59 all use by name. `batch_get_json` (batch.rs:88-92) exists and returns per-URL results in order, so fetching the selection by id is feasible. Overstated: (a) `ids.contains` over a few-hundred-id `Vec` against ≤10 000 apps is sub-millisecond — a non-issue; (b) 'silently drop a selected app' requires a tenant with >10 000 app registrations, where the App Registrations list and the audit are already truncated at the same `APPS_MAX`, so the selection could not have come from beyond the cap in the first place; the comment at :157-159 is essentially right. Medium stands for the wall-clock cost on large tenants (the repo's own cache.rs:140-147 comment calls a full re-enumeration 'tens of seconds').

findings.title: Bulk expired-credential sweep busts both tenant-wide indexes (invalidate_app_lists) for a credential-only mutation; the per-app fix uses the tiered invalidation
findings.rationale: applications/cache.rs:140-147 documents why credential mutations must use `invalidate_app_credentials`: it 'deliberately leaves the shared SP pairing index, the app-name search index, the Enterprise Apps list, and every mailbox-scope verdict intact… dropping them forces the next list visit to re-enumerate every app and every service principal (tens of seconds on a large tenant) for a change that touched neither.' `remediate_remove_expired_credentials` (remediation.rs:97-99) follows that rule; the bulk sweep of the same mutation does not, so after every sweep the operator pays a full SP-index + app-name-index rebuild.
findings.proposal: Replace the `invalidate_app_lists` call with a loop over `summaries.iter().filter(|s| !s.removed_key_ids.is_empty())` calling `invalidate_app_credentials(&state.cache, &tenant_id, &s.object_id)` (or add an `invalidate_app_credentials_many(cache, tenant, &[object_id])` that drops the shared keys once and the per-app detail keys per id). Extend `repo_invariants/cache.rs` to pin that no credential-only command calls `invalidate_app_lists`.
findings.verifier_notes: bulk.rs:283-285 calls `invalidate_app_lists` after a sweep whose only mutation is `client.remove_password` (:237) — a credential-only change. applications/cache.rs:134-147 documents in detail why credential-only mutations must use `invalidate_app_credentials` (keeps `sp_index`, `app_name_index`, the Enterprise Apps list and every mailbox-scope verdict; dropping them costs a full app + SP re-enumeration), and the per-app fix `remediate_remove_expired_credentials` follows it (remediation.rs:97-99 with an explicit comment). `invalidate_app_credentials` takes one `object_id` (cache.rs:148), so the sweep needs a loop or a `_many` variant as proposed. `repo_invariants/cache.rs` lists both invalidators (:100-101) but pins nothing about which command may call which; the proposed pin fits the existing style. No CHANGELOG or doc marks the bulk path as a deliberate exception.

findings.title: Exchange mailbox-scoping unavailability (no Exchange client, or breaker tripped) is invisible in the run result, the workbench and every export
findings.rationale: By design a non-Exchange-admin gets org-wide weight for every mail permission (never under-report), and that trade-off should stay. But the consequence for the operator is that apps already scoped via RBAC are listed as Critical 'Org-wide mailbox access' with a 'Scope…' Fix that will fail, the healthy 'Mailbox access scoped' group is empty, and the run is cached and exported as complete. `coverage_sentences` (audit.rs:636-642) already adds a caveat when the sign-in report was unavailable; the analogous, higher-impact caveat for mailbox scoping does not exist, and `AuditRunResult` carries no field for it. Nothing in web-rs/views/audit_view or security_view mentions Exchange availability (grep).
findings.proposal: Add `mailbox_scoping_resolved: bool` (`#[serde(default = true)]`-style) to `AuditRunResult`, `AuditExportCoverage` and `CachedAuditRun`, set false when `exo` is `None` or `exo_tripped` is set at the end of the run; add a sentence in `coverage_sentences` ('Mailbox scoping could not be resolved — org-wide mailbox findings may include applications already confined via Exchange RBAC; sign in as an Exchange Administrator to refine') and a Callout in the Org-wide mailbox finding group. Keep it out of `degraded` so the run stays cacheable, matching the sign-in precedent.
findings.verifier_notes: audit.rs:899-907 logs Exchange unavailability at `info!` and returns `None`; score_one flips `exo_tripped` at :1569 with another `info!`. Neither reaches `AuditRunResult` (dto/audit.rs:16-56: only `sign_in_report_available`/`sign_in_consent_required`/`truncated`/`degraded`), `AuditExportCoverage` (dto/audit.rs:92-102) or `coverage_sentences` (audit.rs:613-651, which does carry the sign-in caveat at :636-642). The frontend never mentions Exchange availability: audit_view/filter.rs:71-72 only acknowledges the degrade in a comment, and groups.rs:57/127 blurbs assume scoping was resolved. The degrade-to-org-wide scoring is a documented decision (audit-findings-and-remediation.md:22-25 'never under-reported'), but not surfacing it is not — and for a non-Exchange-admin the Critical 'Org-wide mailbox access' rows offer a Scope Fix that needs the same Exchange client and will fail. The proposal (a serde-defaulted flag on the run/cache/export plus a sentence and a Callout, kept out of `degraded` so caching is unchanged) mirrors the sign-in precedent exactly and is feasible.

findings.title: Split commands/audit.rs (2011 lines) into a directory module by concern
findings.evidence:
126:#[tauri::command]  pub async fn run_audit            (to ~475)
476..540: cancel_audit / invalidate_audit_cache / get_cached_audit
542:#[tauri::command]  pub async fn save_audit_to_file  + cached_run_coverage, coverage_sentences, severity_summary, audit_to_json (667), audit_to_html (702), html_escape, export_audit_csv (788)
854:// ---------------- internals ----------------
860:struct ScoreCtx  … 914/952/1007/1070/1137/1182: six prefetch_* fns
1238:fn score_sp_only  1312:fn sp_audit_candidates  1329:struct ResourceResolver  1437:async fn resolve_permissions  1483:async fn score_one
1615:#[cfg(test)] mod tests (≈400 lines)
findings.rationale: The file interleaves five independent concerns: run orchestration and cancellation, the six tenant-wide prefetchers (~380 lines), per-principal scoring (ScoreCtx, ResourceResolver, resolve_permissions, score_one, score_sp_only, ~370 lines), the cache entry (CachedAuditRun, key, run_is_cacheable, get_cached_audit) and three export writers (~310 lines). Each has its own invariants (documented at length inline) and its own test group. `commands/exchange/` already proves the directory-module shape works here, and `repo_invariants/sources.rs` walks subdirectories and skips a sibling `tests.rs`, so the source-scanning pins keep working unchanged.
findings.proposal: Create `commands/audit/{mod.rs, prefetch.rs, score.rs, cache.rs, export.rs, tests.rs}`: `mod.rs` keeps run_audit/cancel_audit and re-exports the four commands so `lib.rs`'s `generate_handler![]` paths do not change; `prefetch.rs` takes the six `prefetch_*` + `derive_orgwide_mail_scopes`; `score.rs` takes ScoreCtx, ResourceResolver, resolve_permissions, score_one, score_sp_only, sp_audit_candidates; `cache.rs` takes CachedAuditRun, audit_cache_key, run_is_cacheable, invalidate_audit_cache, get_cached_audit; `export.rs` takes save_audit_to_file and the writers. Move each test group next to its subject. No behaviour change; run `just verify`.
findings.verifier_notes: audit.rs is 2011 lines (wc) and the layout matches the evidence: commands at :126/476-540/542, export writers :667/702/788, `// ---- internals ----` at :854, six `prefetch_*` fns, `score_sp_only` :1238, `ResourceResolver` :1329, `score_one` :1483, `mod tests` from :1615. Feasibility checks out: `commands/exchange/` already uses the directory-module + `tests.rs` shape; `repo_invariants/sources.rs:38-65` walks subdirectories and skips `tests.rs` by name; every external reference is path-based (`crate::commands::audit::invalidate_audit_cache` / `audit_cache_key` in applications/cache.rs:101/132/159/614/672 and managed_identity.rs:114, `commands::audit::*` in lib.rs:106-109), so re-exports from `mod.rs` keep them compiling. One constraint the proposal must respect: `repo_invariants/fanout.rs:196-222` checks per MODULE that a `dispatch_capped(` site contains `is_dead()` or `reauth_fatal` — keeping `run_audit` and `classify_audit_failure` together in `mod.rs` (as proposed) satisfies it. This is a maintainability preference rather than a defect, so low, not medium.

findings.title: No source-level pin that the CacheKind::Audit write is guarded by run_is_cacheable
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md states 'a cancelled/truncated/degraded run is never cached'. `run_is_cacheable` is exhaustively unit-tested (`only_a_complete_undegraded_run_is_cacheable`), but that pins the predicate, not its use: a refactor that moves the `cache.put` out of the `if` (or adds a second put, e.g. for a 'partial snapshot') compiles and passes every test. `repo_invariants/cache.rs` today only checks the cache-only *read* proves the session (line 580). The slice's other rules — claim-before-await, dead-session gate per call site — each have a source-scan pin; this one does not.
findings.proposal: Add a test in `repo_invariants/cache.rs`: read `commands/audit.rs` (or the future `audit/` directory), find every `.put(CacheKind::Audit` occurrence, and assert the nearest enclosing `if` condition (scan backwards to the previous `{` at the same brace depth) contains `run_is_cacheable(`; assert at least one occurrence exists so the rule cannot pass vacuously.
findings.verifier_notes: The guarded write is at audit.rs:445-449 and `run_is_cacheable` is unit-tested in-file (`only_a_complete_undegraded_run_is_cacheable`), but no test outside audit.rs references `run_is_cacheable` (grep over src-tauri/tests returns nothing) and `repo_invariants/cache.rs` mentions `CacheKind::Audit` only inside the detector's self-tests (:580, :590). AGENTS.md and .claude/rules state 'a cancelled/truncated/degraded run is never cached', and the sibling rules (claim-before-await, per-call-site dead-session gating) each have a source-scan pin, so the gap is real and the proposal is in the repo's idiom. It is a missing ratchet rather than a live defect, so low.

findings.title: Stale `reset()` narrative in run_bulk_seq's doc and the architecture deep-dive; cancel.rs cites a test that no longer exists
findings.rationale: `CancelFlag` no longer has a `reset()` — state.rs:44-49 explains it was removed because it was 'a destructive write on state a concurrent run was still reading', and `repo_invariants/cancel.rs` opens with 'Replaces the old "call reset() at the top" rule'. Three places still teach the retired model, and cancel.rs points at `the_audit_claims_its_token_before_the_prefetch`, which does not exist anywhere in the tree (grep) — it was generalised into `every_long_running_command_claims_before_its_first_await`. A reader following the doc will look for a `reset()` and a test that are both gone.
findings.proposal: Rewrite the run_bulk_seq doc line to 'The caller claims a `CancelToken` once, before its first await (pinned by `repo_invariants::cancel`), and passes it down'; update the arch doc sentence to 'They `claim()` a token + poll it'; change the cancel.rs intra-doc link to `every_long_running_command_claims_before_its_first_await`.
findings.verifier_notes: All three stale references verified: bulk.rs:974-975 ('The caller resets the flag ... the `reset()` must stay at the command top'), audit-findings-and-remediation.md:325 ('They `reset()` + poll `audit_cancel`'), and cancel.rs:34-35 links `the_audit_claims_its_token_before_the_prefetch`, which exists nowhere in the tree (grep finds only that doc line; the actual test is `every_long_running_command_claims_before_its_first_await` at cancel.rs:99). `CancelFlag` has no `reset()` — state.rs:44-49 explains its removal and cancel.rs:1-12 opens with 'Replaces the old "call `reset()` at the top" rule'. Pure doc rot; proposal is right.

findings.title: FanOutTicker::tick's doc claims count and cap are read under one lock — they are not — and progress events can arrive out of order
findings.rationale: The cap is read after `drop(guard)`, and `current` is an atomic the mutex never protected anyway, so the comment describes a guarantee the code does not provide. Separately, every caller (`audit.rs:335-346`, bulk delete/grant/sweep) emits *after* `tick()` returns and outside any lock, so two tasks can tick 5 then 6 and emit 6 then 5; `use_progress_stream` (web-rs hooks) does `progress.set(Some(p))` unconditionally, so the bar can step backwards — the very skew the comment says is prevented. A `tokio::sync::Mutex<usize>` is also heavier than needed for a counter.
findings.proposal: Replace `done: Arc<Mutex<usize>>` with `Arc<AtomicUsize>` and `fetch_add(1) + 1`; fix the comment to say the pair is best-effort. Make `use_progress_stream` (or a small `AuditProgress::newer_than`) ignore an event whose `done` is lower than the current one for the same `total`, so the bar is monotonic per run.
findings.verifier_notes: throttle.rs:216-224: the doc says both values are read 'under the same lock acquisition', but the code does `drop(guard)` at :223 before `self.tracker.current_limit()` at :224, and `current` is an `AtomicUsize` (:33) the mutex never protected. Emission is outside any lock at every caller (audit.rs:335-346 ticks then emits; bulk.rs:250-258 likewise), so two tasks can tick 5,6 and emit 6,5; `use_progress_stream.rs:26-28` does `progress.set(Some(p))` unconditionally and neither security_view.rs nor bulk_action_bar.rs filters by `done`. Real but cosmetic (a one-step backward blip on a multi-threaded runtime), hence low. Proposal is fine; note `FanOutMeter::done()` (:190-192) is `async` today and would become sync with an atomic.

findings.title: Demo registers a fixture for `export_audit_csv`, a command that no longer exists on the IPC boundary
findings.rationale: `export_audit_csv` was demoted to a `pub(crate)` helper (audit.rs doc: 'leaving an unreachable entry point on the IPC boundary'), and no binding invokes it, yet the Pages demo still mocks it and docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md:111 lists it among the infallible `invoke()` commands that need fixtures. `demo_fixture_coverage.rs` checks only that every infallible invoke has a fixture, not the reverse, so the dead fixture is invisible to CI.
findings.proposal: Delete the `mock_ok("export_audit_csv", …)` block and the mention in release-updater-demo.md:111. Optionally add the reverse assertion to `demo_fixture_coverage.rs` (every mocked command name appears in some `invoke`/`invoke_result` call in bindings), which would also catch future leftovers.
findings.verifier_notes: demo/mod.rs:665-668 still registers `mock_ok("export_audit_csv", ...)`; audit.rs:781-788 documents the demotion to a `pub(crate)` helper with `save_audit_to_file` as sole caller; lib.rs:106-109 registers only run_audit/cancel_audit/get_cached_audit/save_audit_to_file; grep finds no `export_audit_csv` in web-rs/src/bindings; CHANGELOG-archive.md:1890 records the removal; release-updater-demo.md:111 still lists it among fixtures that must exist. `demo_fixture_coverage.rs:85-114` checks bindings → fixtures only, so the dead fixture is invisible to CI. Cleanup plus an optional reverse assertion is correct.

findings.title: premium_feature_err hardcodes 'Ask a Global Administrator' while the catalog's admin_consent entry names Privileged Role Administrator or Global Administrator
findings.rationale: The same file's `forbidden_remediation` exists so that 'Adding a privileged feature means adding a catalog entry, never a hardcoded role string', and AGENTS.md repeats the rule. This message is the one remaining hardcoded role string on a 403 path in the slice, and it is narrower than the catalog's own answer (a Privileged Role Administrator can also grant the consent).
findings.proposal: Compose the consent branch from the catalog rather than a literal: either interpolate `capability("admin_consent")`'s `role_names()` joined with ' or ' (PRA or GA can both grant tenant-wide consent for Graph scopes), or — since a non-license 403 on these reads may equally be a missing directory role — have the two callers pass their capability key (`audit_reports` / `conditional_access`) and append that entry's `remediation`. Extend the test at graph_err.rs:137 to assert the message names both roles.
findings.verifier_notes: graph_err.rs:73-78 hardcodes 'Ask a Global Administrator' in the non-license 403 branch, while the same file's `forbidden_remediation` doc (:15-24) says 'Adding a privileged feature means adding a catalog entry, never a hardcoded role string' and the catalog's `admin_consent` entry (capabilities.rs:177-197) names Privileged Role Administrator OR Global Administrator. The two callers are activity.rs:241 (AuditLog.Read.All) and conditional_access.rs:144 (Policy.Read.All), whose own catalog entries (`audit_reports` :200-218, `conditional_access` :219-240) carry remediation text naming the reporting roles and the P1/P2 license. The existing test at :137-145 only asserts `contains("consent")`, so a rewrite is unconstrained. Low: message wording only.

findings.title: During the tenant-wide prefetch the audit progress block reads '0 / 0 apps' with no phase label
findings.rationale: The inline comment at :160-166 says the prefetch 'is the longest phase of a large run' and 'the most likely moment for an operator to press Cancel'. `security_view.rs:180-183` renders the progress block only once `progress` is `Some`, so for that entire phase the operator sees a disabled button with a tiny spinner and a Cancel button, with no indication of what is happening or that the app is alive. Progress events are best-effort and cheap (`emit_progress`), so a preparatory event costs nothing.
findings.proposal: Emit one preparatory `AuditProgress { done: 0, total: 0, current_app: Some("Reading tenant-wide directory data…"), in_flight_cap: meter.limit(), cancelled: false }` before the `join!` in run_audit, and in security_view.rs render the fraction/percentage only when `p.total > 0` (show the `current_app` label alone otherwise) so the seeded and preparatory events read as 'preparing' rather than '0 / 0'.
findings.verifier_notes: Backend premise is accurate: the first `audit-progress` emit is at audit.rs:280-289, after the six-way `join!` at :173-266 that :160-166 itself calls 'the longest phase of a large run'. But the UI claim is wrong: `AuditController::run` (audit_view/controller.rs:187-193) seeds `progress` with `Some(AuditProgress { done: 0, total: 0, in_flight_cap: 8, .. })` the moment the run starts, so security_view.rs:180-212 already renders the progress block ('0 / 0 apps (cap: 8)' with a 0% bar) throughout the prefetch — not merely a spinner. What is missing is a phase label. Also, the proposal's 'the view renders an indeterminate bar with that label' overstates it: with `total: 0` the view prints '0 / 0 apps' and a 0% bar; a small view tweak is needed to show an indeterminate state or hide the fraction when `total == 0`.

findings.title: Terminal bulk-progress events report done == total even for a cancelled or halted run (a documented contract with a one-frame UI effect); the credential sweep emits no terminal event
findings.rationale: After a Cancel at item 3 of 10, or a dead-session halt, the final event tells the UI '10 / 10 (cancelled)'. `BulkProgressRow` (bulk_action_bar.rs:227) renders `p.done / p.total`, so the bar snaps to 100% for a run that processed a fraction of the selection — the same 'partial reads as complete' shape the surrounding code is careful about elsewhere. `bulk_remove_expired_credentials` emits no terminal event at all, so the three fan-out paths and the sequential driver disagree on the contract.
findings.proposal: If harmonising: emit `done: outcomes.len()` (sequential) / collected count (fan-outs) as the terminal value, update run_bulk_seq's doc and `a_cancel_before_the_first_item_processes_nothing` (which currently pins `(1, None)`), and add a matching terminal event to bulk_remove_expired_credentials. Otherwise leave as-is and only add the missing terminal event to the sweep for contract consistency.
findings.verifier_notes: The events are as quoted: bulk.rs:1014-1020 (run_bulk_seq), :379-386 (bulk_delete_applications) and :497-504 (bulk_grant_permissions) all emit `done: total` regardless of cancellation, and bulk_remove_expired_credentials (:140-297) emits no terminal event at all. But this is a documented and tested contract, not an oversight: run_bulk_seq's doc (:970-971) states 'then a final `done = total` event', and `a_cancel_before_the_first_item_processes_nothing` (:1120-1133) asserts the terminal `(1, None)` with `cancelled == true` for a run that processed nothing. UI impact is negligible: `BulkProgressRow` is mounted only while `busy` (bulk_action_bar.rs:646-647, doc at :198-200) and the command returns immediately after the terminal emit, so the '100%' state is at most one frame; the bar also clears `progress` at the next run start for exactly this reason (:495-497). The security controller likewise sets `progress` to `None` when `run_audit` returns (controller.rs:210-211). Changing it means changing a pinned contract for a barely visible effect — low, and only worth doing for consistency across the four paths.

findings.title: Documented auto-update opt-out (AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE / settings.json auto_update) is never read; launch check always runs
findings.evidence:
updater.rs:26-28 `pub async fn check_for_update(app: AppHandle) -> Result<Option<UpdateInfo>, UiError> {
    let updater = app.updater().map_err(updater_err)?;
    match updater.check().await.map_err(updater_err)? {`
web-rs/src/views/shell.rs:167 `if let Ok(Some(info)) = updater::check_for_update().await {` (Effect runs once on mount, unconditionally)
README.md:262-283 "To stop the checks entirely ... `AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE=0` ... `{ "auto_update": false }` ... With auto-update disabled the app makes no network calls to the updater endpoint at any point in the session."
README.md:255-259 "If you deployed the `.msi`, **disable auto-update** (see Opting out)"
crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs:82-88 `pub fn load(config_dir: &Path) -> Self { ... if let Some(env_override) = auto_update_env_override() { s.auto_update = env_override; }`
repo-wide grep for `auto_update|AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE|UserSettings::load` outside settings.rs: only README.md and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md hits, no Rust callers.
findings.rationale: The README and DEVELOPMENT.md promise an MDM/CI opt-out and tell MSI deployers to rely on it to avoid a second conflicting NSIS install. `UserSettings::load` (the only place the env override is applied) has no callers, and neither `check_for_update`, `perform_update` nor the frontend consult `auto_update`. An operator who set the documented switch still gets a launch-time network call and an "Update available" toast, and an MSI install can still be driven into the conflicting-install state the README warns about. A documented security/deployment control that silently does nothing is the worst kind.
findings.proposal: In `commands::updater`, gate both commands on `UserSettings::load(&crate::config_directory()).auto_update`: `check_for_update` returns `Ok(None)` (no network call) and `perform_update` returns a `UiError::validation("updates_disabled", ...)` when it is false. Surface the flag to the UI (e.g. an `updates_enabled: bool` on `AuthConfigStatus` or a tiny `get_update_policy` command) so the account menu can hide/label the manual "Check for updates" item instead of showing a confusing failure. Add a unit test on a pure `updates_enabled(settings) -> bool` helper plus a source-scanning invariant that `check_for_update` references it. Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise holds end to end. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/updater.rs:26-37 (`check_for_update`) and :44-72 (`perform_update`) never read settings; lib.rs:24 registers the updater plugin unconditionally. `UserSettings::load` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs:82-88, the only place `auto_update_env_override` at :235-242 is applied) has zero non-test callers — repo grep for `auto_update|AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE|UserSettings::load` hits only settings.rs, README.md:262-283 and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:314. The frontend Effect at apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/shell.rs:162-176 calls `check_for_update()` on mount with no gate. `git log -S` over apps/ shows the flag was never wired at any point in history. README.md:279-283 explicitly promises 'no network calls to the updater endpoint at any point in the session' and :255-259 tells MSI deployers to rely on it, so this is a documented deployment control that is inert. Proposal is feasible as written (gate in the two commands, surface a flag so the account-menu item can be hidden); gating at the command layer rather than plugin registration is right since `check_for_update` is the only caller path.
findings.recheck_notes: Reproduced by reading the full path; nothing upstream gates it. `UserSettings::load` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs:82-88) is the ONLY place `auto_update_env_override()` (settings.rs:235-242) is applied, and a repo-wide grep over apps/ and crates/ for `UserSettings::load`, `.auto_update`, `AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE` finds no caller outside settings.rs's own #[cfg(test)] block. Every production reader of settings.json uses `UserSettings::stored` and reads other fields: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/state.rs:234 (client_id/tenant_id), state.rs:376 (last_account), commands/defaults.rs:19 and commands/exchange/mod.rs:74 (tenant_defaults). `commands/updater.rs:26-37` (`check_for_update`) and :44-72 (`perform_update`) call `app.updater().check()` with no policy check. The plugin is registered unconditionally at src-tauri/src/lib.rs:24 and both commands are in generate_handler at lib.rs:43-44; tauri.conf.json:45-53 has `plugins.updater.active: true` with the live GitHub `latest.json` endpoint, and capabilities/default.json:10 grants `updater:default`. The frontend fires the network check on every mount: web-rs/src/views/shell.rs:162-178 `Effect::new(... spawn_local(async { if let Ok(Some(info)) = updater::check_for_update().await { ... push_toast("Update available") }}))`, via bindings/updater.rs:11-12. Docs contradicted: README.md:262-283 ("To stop the checks entirely ... AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE=0 ... { \"auto_update\": false } ... With auto-update disabled the app makes no network calls to the updater endpoint at any point in the session"), README.md:255-259 (MSI deployers told to rely on it to avoid a conflicting NSIS install), docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:313-314. No repo invariant covers it (tests/repo_invariants/release.rs only pins version/CHANGELOG parity). The settings.rs unit tests (`settings_file_can_disable_auto_update`, :256-261) pass in isolation, so CI cannot detect the dead control. Severity stays high: it is a documented MDM/CI deployment control and a documented no-egress promise that silently does nothing in the shipped build; the one mitigating nuance is that the NSIS-over-MSI install still requires the operator to click "Update & restart", so the conflicting-install harm needs a user action, but the launch-time network call and the toast prompting that click both happen regardless of the switch.

findings.title: Restore is not idempotent, yet its own report instructs the operator to re-run it
findings.evidence:
restore.rs:748-753 `reason: format!(
    "Managed identity ({}{}) not found in the destination. Recreate it via your \
     infrastructure-as-code, then re-run the restore to re-bind its Graph \
     app-roles.",`
restore.rs:197-231 Pass 1 `for app in &backup.app_registrations { ... match create_application_core(&client, input).await { Ok(res) => { app_id_remap.insert(...); created.push(...) }` — no lookup of an existing app by name/identifier URI/marker before creating.
restore.rs:588-590 `for meta in &app.secrets { ... match client.add_password(&c.new_object_id, &name, lifetime).await {`
web-rs/src/views/dr.rs confirm modal: "This creates new app registrations in the current tenant and regenerates their secrets. It does not overwrite or delete anything that already exists."
