findings.rationale: `restore_tenant` unconditionally creates a shell for every app registration in the manifest and mints fresh secrets for each. The MI runbook item explicitly tells the operator to "re-run the restore" after recreating the identities via IaC. Following that instruction duplicates every app registration (same display names, `api://` URIs rewritten to a second appId, second set of live 180-day secrets, second admin consent) in the destination tenant. There is no dry-run warning either: `plan_restore` does not look at the destination at all.
findings.proposal: Two tiers. (S, removes the harm) Reword the ManualItem at restore.rs:748-753 and the arch doc sentence at docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:203 so they no longer say 're-run the restore'; add a 'Re-bind managed identities only' action that runs just `restore_managed_identities` (Pass 5) against a loaded manifest, and make `plan_restore` warn when `!tenant_changed`. (M, optional) Adoption-aware Pass 1 via a marker — note the core `Application` model has no `tags` field today (only `ServicePrincipal.tags`, crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/models.rs:165), so this needs the model and `AppPatch` extended plus a destination lookup; count adoptions in `RestoreReport`.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: Pass 1 (restore.rs:197-231) calls `create_application_core` for every manifest app with no lookup of an existing app (grep for existing/already/adopt/idempot in restore.rs finds only comments); secrets are minted per created app (restore.rs:588-598); the ManualItem at :748-753 and the architecture doc at backup-and-restore.md:203 both instruct 'recreate ... then re-run'. Severity trimmed from high to medium: the confirm modal (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/dr.rs:414-415) states plainly that restore 'creates new app registrations ... does not overwrite or delete anything', so the operator is warned that a re-run creates, and the defect is the instruction text rather than silent behaviour. The S-sized fix (reword + MI-only re-bind) removes the harm; the tag-based adoption is a larger design change and is better framed as an enhancement.

findings.title: Restore reports a failed Graph read as a confident runbook fact ('not found in destination' / 'app had none in the backup')
findings.rationale: If `list_managed_identities` fails (throttled, 403 for a role that lacks directory read, or a session that died mid-restore), `unwrap_or_default()` yields an empty list and EVERY managed identity is reported as "not found in the destination — recreate via IaC", sending the infra team to recreate identities that already exist. Likewise a transient `Err` from `get_service_principal_by_app_id` is reported as "the app had none in the backup", which is false when `has_service_principal` was true. The rubric's "result that misleads the operator" case; and because these two passes never note failures on the `SessionDead` latch, a dead session in Pass 4/5 produces a full page of wrong runbook items rather than the `session_expired` flag.
findings.proposal: In `restore_managed_identities`, match on the list result: on `Err(e)` call `session.note_code(e.ui_code())` (thread `&SessionDead` into the function), push ONE `ManualItem`/warning "could not enumerate destination managed identities: {e} — re-binding skipped" and return, instead of emitting per-MI 'not found' items. In `restore_enterprise_app`, split the arm: `Ok(None)` keeps the current text, `Err(e)` pushes "could not read service principal: {e}" and notes the session code. Add the same `note_code` to the tag/patch/assign/group-member failures in that function so Pass 4 latches like Pass 2. Unit-test the MI branch with a wiremock 500 on `/servicePrincipals` asserting no per-MI 'not found' item is produced. Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: Both sites are as quoted. restore.rs:734 `list_managed_identities().await.unwrap_or_default()` turns any Err into an empty map, so :740-753 emits a per-MI 'not found in the destination — recreate via IaC' item for every MI. restore.rs:653-661 collapses `Ok(None)` and `Err(_)` into 'the app had none in the backup'. Neither `restore_enterprise_app` (:623-720) nor `restore_managed_identities` (:723+) takes `&SessionDead` or calls `note_code`, whereas `wire_application` does (:412, :580, :603). Consequence for the latch: the Pass 4 loop (:296-304) checks `session.is_dead()` but nothing inside Pass 4 can set it, so a session dying during Pass 4 produces one false 'had no SP' item per remaining enterprise app and `report.session_expired` stays false (:327). Severity adjusted to medium rather than high: `list_managed_identities` (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/service_principals.rs:108-120) is a paged read behind the shared retry budget and Pass 5 only starts when the session is alive (:313), so the trigger window is a session death or budget exhaustion inside passes 4-5 — narrower than the reviewer implies — but when it fires the output is a confidently wrong DR runbook, which is exactly the misleading-result class. Proposal is small and feasible (`SessionDead` is a `pub(crate)` Arc<AtomicBool> in commands/dispatch.rs:29, trivially threaded).

findings.title: Backup Pass 3 (managed identities) is not session-latched and swallows per-MI read failures without recording them in `skipped`
findings.evidence:
backup.rs:675-683 `async fn backup_managed_identities(
    client: &GraphClient,
    managed: &[ServicePrincipal],
    cancel: &CancelToken,
    app_handle: &AppHandle,
    done: &Mutex<usize>,
    total: usize,
    throttle: &ConcurrencyThrottle,
) -> Result<Vec<ManagedIdentityBackup>, UiError> {` (no `session: &SessionDead`)
backup.rs:695-706 `.batch_list_app_role_assignments(&mi_ids).await
            // Per-item errors degrade to empty here (best-effort, as before);
            // only a WHOLE-batch failure takes the per-item path.
            .map(|v| v.into_iter().map(Result::unwrap_or_default).collect()),
        |id: String| async move { client.list_app_role_assignments(&id).await.unwrap_or_default() },`
Contrast backup.rs:388-391 (Pass 1) `// A DR backup that silently drops apps is the most dangerous artifact this app produces ... Classify every per-item failure so a dead session aborts the run instead of thinning it.
    note_graph_failures(session, app_jsons.iter().map(Result::as_ref));`
backup.rs:211-216 after Pass 2: `if session.is_dead() { return Err(session.err("the tenant backup")); }` — no equivalent after Pass 3.
findings.rationale: Passes 1 and 2 were hardened so a dead session aborts the backup and any dropped object lands in `TenantBackup.skipped`. Pass 3 predates that: if the refresh token dies (or Graph 5xx/429s past the retry budget) during the MI phase, every assignment read fails, is replaced with an empty `Vec`, and the run returns `Ok` — a manifest whose managed identities all have `held_app_roles: []`. Restore then re-binds nothing and reports success. The manifest neither records the gap in `skipped` nor fails, which is exactly the 'reads as complete' hazard the module documents for the other passes.
findings.proposal: Thread `session: &SessionDead` into `backup_managed_identities`; keep the per-item `Result` from `batch_or_serial`, call `note_graph_failures(session, ...)` on it, and for each `Err` push `SkippedObject::new("managedIdentity", &sp.id, Some(sp.display_name.clone()), format!("held app-roles could not be read: {err}"))` while still emitting the MI with empty roles (so the operator knows the entry is partial). After the pass, mirror passes 1-2: `if session.is_dead() { return Err(session.err("the tenant backup")); }`. Return `(Vec<ManagedIdentityBackup>, Vec<SkippedObject>)` and append to `skipped`. Extend the existing wiremock degrade test with a 500 on `/servicePrincipals/{id}/appRoleAssignments` asserting the skip is recorded. Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified. `backup_managed_identities` (backup.rs:675-683) takes no `SessionDead`; per-item and whole-batch failures both become empty Vecs (:695-706, `Result::unwrap_or_default` and `.unwrap_or_default()`); the caller (:243-251) `?`s only on cancel and then returns `Ok(TenantBackup {..})` with no `session.is_dead()` check, unlike after Pass 1 (:165) and Pass 2 (:233). Strong corroboration the reviewer missed: `SkippedObject.kind` is documented as 'application, enterpriseApp, or managedIdentity' (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/backup.rs:78) but backup.rs only ever emits 'application' (:407/:417/:427) and 'enterpriseApp' (:573) — no code path records an MI skip. The in-code comment 'best-effort, as before' is legacy preservation, not a rationale, and docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:113-116 describes Pass 3 without mentioning the degrade. A dead session or exhausted retry budget during Pass 3 yields an Ok manifest whose MIs all carry `held_app_roles: []`, which restore then treats as nothing to re-bind — the 'reads as complete' hazard the module's own doc (dto/backup.rs:59-66) names. High is fair given passes 1-2 were hardened for exactly this and `note_graph_failures` (:346-353) already exists to reuse.
findings.recheck_notes: Failing path constructed end to end. `backup_managed_identities` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/backup.rs:675-683) has no `session: &SessionDead` parameter, and `backup_tenant` calls it at :224-232 then immediately returns `Ok(TenantBackup { ... skipped })` at :234-243 with no `if session.is_dead() { return Err(session.err(..)) }` — unlike the checks after Pass 1 (:169-171) and Pass 2 (:211-213). Inside, :690-706 wraps `batch_list_app_role_assignments` with `.map(|v| v.into_iter().map(Result::unwrap_or_default).collect())` and the serial fallback with `.unwrap_or_default()`, so no `GraphError` survives to `note_graph_failures` (:342-350, used only by Pass 1 at :388-389 and Pass 2 at :541-543) and no `SkippedObject` is ever pushed for kind `managedIdentity` (the DTO explicitly reserves that kind: crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/backup.rs:78). Trigger: a refresh-token death (or 429 past `core::http_retry` budget / 5xx) once Pass 3 begins. The token adapter surfaces as `GraphError::Token(TokenError)` (core/http_error.rs:95) whose `ui_code()` passes `refresh_missing`/`not_signed_in` through (`http_error.rs:131-133` via `reauth::passthrough_code`) — exactly the code `SessionDead::note_code` (dispatch.rs:62-64) would latch, had it been called. `batch_get_json` (graph/src/client/batch.rs:145 `chunk?`) returns whole-batch Err, `batch_or_serial` (dispatch.rs:134-160) falls to per-item `list_app_role_assignments` (graph/src/client/roles_grants.rs:36-40) which fails identically, and every MI ends with `held_app_roles: []` in an `Ok` manifest. Nothing pins this: tests/repo_invariants/fanout.rs:203-221 inspects only `dispatch_capped(` call sites, and Pass 3 deliberately uses the batch helpers' internal concurrency (backup.rs:669-672), so the rule never sees it; grep of repo_invariants/ for `batch_or_serial`, `note_graph_failures`, `backup_managed_identities` finds nothing. Downstream: `restore_managed_identities` (commands/restore.rs:769-793) iterates `mi.held_app_roles`, so an empty list yields `app_roles_rebound: 0` with zero warnings and only the unconditional Azure-RBAC `ManualItem` (:796-803) — the restore reads as a clean success. The `skipped` contract (dto/backup.rs:59-71: "A DR backup that silently drops what it could not read is the most dangerous artifact this app produces ... Restore surfaces the same list") and the DR view that renders it (web-rs/src/views/dr.rs:299-339) confirm this is the intended surfacing mechanism and that Pass 3 bypasses it. The existing wiremock test (backup.rs:1000-1127) covers only `backup_app_chunk`. Note the module comment at :693-694 ('best-effort, as before') documents the degrade, but the architecture doc (docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:113-116 and :101-103) claims 'a per-object failure skips just that object' and passes 1-2 were hardened after that comment was written, so this is a real inconsistency rather than a deliberate exemption. Severity high is warranted: a DR manifest that reads complete but restores no MI permissions is the hazard the module itself ranks as its worst.

findings.title: Enterprise-app assignee/group read failures degrade to empty with no `skipped` record — manifest silently under-reports access
findings.rationale: The whole-object skip is recorded, but a per-SP failure of `appRoleAssignedTo` or `memberOf` produces an `EnterpriseAppBackup` with zero assignees/groups and no marker. On restore the app gets no assignments re-applied and the report shows nothing amiss; users who had access in the source silently do not in the destination. The architecture doc describes the degrade, but the `skipped` mechanism was added precisely so 'degrade to empty' is never invisible; extending it here is the consistent completion of that fix, not a re-litigation.
findings.proposal: When `assigned[i]` or `groups[i]` is `Err(e)`, push `SkippedObject::new("enterpriseAppAssignments" / "enterpriseAppGroups", &sp.id, Some(sp.display_name.clone()), format!("... could not be read: {e}"))` alongside the (partial) entry. Update the `SkippedObject.kind` doc list and the arch doc sentence to say partial reads are recorded. The DR view already renders `skipped` generically. Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: Accurate. backup.rs:553-563 maps `Err(_)` on `assigned[i]`/`groups[i]` to `Vec::new()` and pushes no `SkippedObject`; only the whole-SP failure at :566-576 is recorded. The session latch IS honoured here (`note_graph_failures` on assigned/groups at :546-548), so the dead-session case aborts — the gap is limited to transient per-item failures producing an entry with zero assignees/groups and no marker, which the reviewer states correctly. docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:111-112 documents the degrade but gives no rationale beyond it, and the `skipped` doc (dto/backup.rs:59-66) argues the opposite direction. The DR view renders `kind`/`reason` generically (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/dr.rs:299-326), so new kinds need only the `SkippedObject.kind` doc (dto/backup.rs:78) and the arch sentence updated. Medium is fair: silent under-reporting of access in a DR manifest, but bounded to transient failures.

findings.title: Managed Identities 'Refresh' invalidates only `{tenant}|mi`, but the list is rebuilt from the untouched shared SP index — refresh is a no-op
findings.rationale: `list_managed_identities` was refactored to derive from `sp_index_cached`, but the per-page Refresh invalidation for MIs was not updated. Pressing Refresh on the Managed Identities page drops the derived `{tenant}|mi` row set, which is then immediately re-derived from the still-cached SP index — an MI created seconds ago (the common reason to press Refresh) stays absent until the SP index TTL lapses or the operator refreshes the Apps/Enterprise page instead.
findings.proposal: In the `ManagedIdentities` arm also invalidate `sp_index_key(&tenant_id)` (and `search_corpus_key`, matching the Enterprise arm's reasoning that the corpus derives from the index). Add a `repo_invariants/cache.rs` rule or a unit test asserting every `ListCacheKindDto` arm that backs a list derived from `sp_index_cached` drops the index. Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified. diagnostics.rs:97-101 (`ManagedIdentities` arm) drops only the `{tenant_id}|mi` prefix; `mi_key` is exactly `{tenant_id}|mi` (managed_identity.rs:39-41); `list_managed_identities` rebuilds that key from `sp_index_cached` (managed_identity.rs:73-84) which is untouched. The Apps (:61-79) and Enterprise (:80-95) arms both also invalidate `sp_index_key` with the comment 'a manual refresh of either must also drop it'. The MI page and detail window Refresh buttons both call `invalidate_list_cache(.., ManagedIdentities)` (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/managed_identities/mod.rs:111-114, detail_window.rs:199-202), so the operator's Refresh is a no-op for a newly created MI until `LISTS_CACHE_TTL` (1 h, crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/constants.rs:55) lapses or another page is refreshed. No repo_invariants rule covers `invalidate_list_cache` (grep of tests/repo_invariants is empty). Proposal matches the sibling arms' reasoning (drop `sp_index_key` + `search_corpus_key`).

findings.title: `plan_restore` dry-run skips the schema check and omits enterprise/MI/skipped counts the restore will act on
findings.rationale: The plan is what the operator confirms against. A too-new manifest passes the dry-run and is refused only after Confirm; the plan lists app-registration work only, though Passes 4-5 will also re-apply SP settings, role assignments, group memberships and MI role re-binds; and restoring into the SOURCE tenant (which duplicates the entire estate) is the one case that shows no note, because the note is gated on `tenant_changed`.
findings.proposal: Call `check_manifest_schema` in `plan_restore` (surface as a blocker like `cloud_mismatch`). Extend `RestorePlan` (all `serde(default)`) with `enterprise_apps_to_reapply`, `enterprise_apps_manual`, `managed_identities_to_rebind`, `skipped_in_backup: usize`, and render them in `RestorePlanView`; render an explicit warning when `!tenant_changed` ("This manifest was taken from THIS tenant — restoring will create duplicates of every app"). Effort S-M.
findings.verifier_notes: All three sub-claims hold. `plan_restore` (restore.rs:87-98) calls only `build_restore_plan`; `check_manifest_schema` is invoked solely in `restore_tenant` (:155). `RestorePlan` (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/backup.rs:351-368) has no enterprise/MI/skipped fields, and `build_restore_plan` (:129-147) sums only app-registration fields. The only tenant note in the plan view is `<Show when=move || plan.tenant_changed>` (dr.rs:444); the confirm modal (dr.rs:414-415) says 'creates new app registrations' generically but nothing flags the same-tenant duplicate case. Two honest caveats that keep this at medium rather than higher: the schema gap fails closed (refused at Confirm, never partially applied), so it is UX not safety; and all `RestorePlan` fields are `serde(default)`-compatible so the extension is additive and wire-safe as proposed. The same-tenant warning is the most valuable piece.

findings.title: Restore regenerates a live secret for every backed-up password credential, including ones already expired at backup time
findings.rationale: Long-lived app registrations commonly carry several expired secrets nobody rotated away. Restore turns each of them into a fresh, valid credential whose plaintext lands in the report — widening the destination tenant's credential surface beyond what was actually in use, and inflating the redistribution work. The metadata needed to distinguish them is already in the manifest.
findings.proposal: Skip secrets whose `end_date_time` is earlier than `backup.created_at` (TenantBackup.created_at, dto/backup.rs:44) — not `Utc::now()`: a secret that was live when the manifest was taken but expired since is exactly the one a DR client still holds and needs re-issued. Push a per-app warning naming the skipped secret and its source expiry, have `build_restore_plan` count only non-expired-at-backup secrets plus an `expired_secrets_skipped` count, and rewrite the comment at restore.rs:78-81 to state the rule. Unit-test both branches.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise true: restore.rs:588-598 iterates every `app.secrets` entry with no expiry filter, backup.rs:461 captures all password credentials, and `CredentialMeta.end_date_time` (dto/backup.rs:263) is available. However the reviewer did not engage with restore.rs:78-81, which explicitly acknowledges 'the original expiry ... may be in the past' and chooses to mint a fresh window anyway — a documented decision, though its rationale is thin (a secret expired before the backup cannot have been in use). The proposal's `Utc::now()` cutoff is wrong for DR: it would drop secrets that were live at backup and expired during the outage. Severity lowered to low: the report is already handled as secret-bearing (restore.rs:337-341), and the exposure is orphaned live credentials (hygiene the app's own audit flags), not disclosure.

findings.title: Webview grants wider than used: connect-src external hosts and updater/dialog capabilities are backend-only concerns
findings.evidence:
tauri.conf.json:25 `"csp": "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; connect-src 'self' https://graph.microsoft.com https://graph.microsoft.us ... https://login.microsoftonline.com ... https://*.vault.azure.net ... https://management.azure.com ..."`
capabilities/default.json:6-12 `"permissions": ["core:default", "core:window:default", "core:app:default", "updater:default", "dialog:allow-save"]`
AGENTS.md: "**CSP governs the webview only** — backend reqwest egress needs no `connect-src` change."
web-rs/Cargo.toml has no HTTP client (only `web-sys` features for DOM/clipboard/storage); grep of web-rs/src for `plugin:` finds only `plugin:event|listen` in ipc_mock; all updater/dialog work is backend-side (`commands::updater`, `export::write_bytes_via_dialog`).
backup.rs:301-306 `load_backup_from_file` uses `.blocking_pick_file()` with NO `dialog:allow-open` capability — proving backend dialogs need no webview grant.
findings.rationale: All network egress is backend reqwest; the WASM frontend only invokes custom commands and listens to events. The `connect-src` allowlist therefore protects nothing and, should the webview ever be compromised, permits it to reach Graph/login endpoints directly. `updater:default` grants `plugin:updater|check/download/install/download_and_install` to the webview, and `dialog:allow-save` grants a save dialog, neither of which the frontend uses — the backend already drives both via Rust APIs (the `pick_file` path works without any dialog grant). Least privilege says drop them.
findings.proposal: Remove `updater:default` and `dialog:allow-save` (and the redundant `core:window:default`/`core:app:default`) from capabilities/default.json, then run the export/updater GUI shards. Separately tighten `connect-src`: Tauri's `set_csp` (tauri-2.11.6/src/manager/mod.rs:53-106) only rewrites script-src/style-src hashes and does not append IPC origins, and the tauri-utils example (config.rs:2741) writes `connect-src ipc: http://ipc.localhost` explicitly — so confirm with `just dev` on each OS that invokes still flow with `'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost`, and pin the final directive in a repo_invariants test so it cannot regrow. Update the AGENTS.md CSP sentence.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise is accurate: web-rs has no HTTP client (apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml deps are leptos/thaw/tauri-sys core+event/web-sys), the only `plugin:` strings are `plugin:event|*` in ipc_mock/mod.rs:125-146, all updater work is in commands/updater.rs and all dialogs go through the Rust API (export.rs `write_bytes_via_dialog`, backup.rs:305-310 `pick_file` with no `dialog:allow-open` grant — proof capabilities do not gate the Rust side). No test or doc pins the CSP or capabilities (grep of tests/, docs/architecture, AGENTS.md). Overstated on risk: tokens never reach the webview and updater payloads are signature-verified (README.md:250-253), so a compromised webview gains little from either the hosts or the grants — this is least-privilege hygiene, hence low. The CSP replacement value needs the verification step the reviewer already includes.

findings.title: rcgen `KeyPair` holds an un-zeroized copy of the PKCS#8 private key; the `zeroize` feature that fixes it is not enabled
findings.evidence:
cert.rs:106-110 `let key_pair = rcgen::KeyPair::generate_rsa_for(&rcgen::PKCS_RSA_SHA256, rcgen::RsaKeySize::_2048)...;
    // PKCS#8 PEM of the private key — surfaced once to the user, never persisted.
    let pkcs8_pem = key_pair.serialize_pem();`
cert.rs:57-63 `impl Drop for GeneratedCert { fn drop(&mut self) { self.private_key_pem.zeroize(); self.pfx_password.zeroize(); self.pfx_der.zeroize(); } }` (only the copies in GeneratedCert)
Cargo.toml:305 `rcgen = { version = "0.14", default-features = false, features = ["pem", "aws_lc_rs"] }`
rcgen-0.14.10/Cargo.toml:144-146 `[dependencies.zeroize] version = "1.2" optional = true`; rcgen-0.14.10/src/lib.rs:862-866 `#[cfg(feature = "zeroize")] impl zeroize::Zeroize for KeyPair { fn zeroize(&mut self) { self.serialized_der.zeroize(); } }`
Cargo.toml:334 `zeroize = { workspace = true }` (already a direct dep).
findings.rationale: The module promises the key does not linger on the heap, and `GeneratedCert` does wipe its PEM/PFX copies. But the source of truth — `key_pair.serialized_der` inside rcgen — is freed unwiped when `key_pair` goes out of scope at the end of `generate_self_signed`. Enabling rcgen's `zeroize` feature costs no new crate (zeroize is already in the graph) and gives a `Zeroize` impl; the caller then wipes it explicitly. (The DER copy p12-keystore takes for the bundle is a residual that upstream does not expose; worth a comment.)
findings.proposal: Add `"zeroize"` to the rcgen feature list and, in `generate_self_signed`, after `build_pfx(...)` returns, call `key_pair.zeroize()` (use `zeroize::Zeroize as _`) before it drops — e.g. bind `let mut key_pair`, or wrap in `zeroize::Zeroizing`-style scope. Document the p12-keystore residual copy beside `build_pfx`. Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified against both the repo and the vendored crate. cert.rs:106-110 binds `key_pair` immutably and it is dropped unwiped at the end of `generate_self_signed`; `GeneratedCert::drop` (cert.rs:57-63) wipes only its own three fields. The comment at cert.rs:141-148 shows the author knew rcgen holds the PKCS#8 bytes ('borrows the PKCS#8 bytes rcgen already holds') yet never zeroizes that copy. rcgen 0.14.10 exposes an optional `zeroize` feature (registry Cargo.toml:144-146) with `impl Zeroize for KeyPair` wiping `serialized_der` (src/lib.rs:862-866); `zeroize` is already a direct dependency (apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:87) so no new crate enters the graph, consistent with the crate's dependency discipline. Feasible: `let mut key_pair`, call `key_pair.zeroize()` after `build_pfx` (cert.rs:146-152) — `cert.pem()`/`cert.der()` no longer need it. Severity lowered to low: heap residue in a live desktop process is reachable only by an attacker with local memory access, who also has the OS keyring; it is a consistency gap against the module's own promise (cert.rs:29-32), not an exposure. The aws-lc-rs key inside `KeyPairKind` remains out of reach either way.

findings.title: Sign-out drops graph/exchange clients but never the kv/arm/la client maps; no helper makes the sweep exhaustive
findings.rationale: No data leaks (the clients hold only an http pool + a `ScopedTokenAdapter` that re-asks the auth service, which purged the tenant's tokens), but the sweep is inconsistent and a future client map or a client that grows state (e.g. a cached ARM subscription list) would be missed. `kv_clients` is keyed per `(tenant, vault)` and only ever grows. The AGENTS.md wording "sign-out sweeps every kind" implies exhaustiveness the code does not have.
findings.proposal: Add `AppState::forget_tenant(&self, tenant_id)` that clears all five maps (kv by `.retain(|(t, _), _| t != tenant_id)`), sweeps `inflight` gates with the `{tenant_id}|` prefix, and calls `cache.invalidate_tenant`; have `sign_out` call it. Pin with a `repo_invariants` rule that every `Mutex<HashMap<` field on `AppState` is named in `forget_tenant`. Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: Code facts hold: auth.rs:54-55 removes only `graph_clients`/`exchange_clients`; state.rs:203-212 declares `kv_clients` (keyed `(tenant, vault)`), `arm_clients`, `la_clients`; repo grep shows nothing ever removes from them. No leak: the clients hold only an http pool, `Arc<dyn BearerProvider>` and a base URL (crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/client.rs:27-33, crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/loganalytics.rs:19-23), and the adapter re-asks the auth service whose tokens `sign_out` purged. Overstated: the AGENTS.md sentence 'sign-out sweeps every kind' and docs/architecture/caching-and-search.md:11-12 refer to *cache kinds* via `invalidate_tenant`, not client maps — no document claims client-map exhaustiveness. The `inflight` gates (state.rs:199) are bare mutexes keyed by cache key. Proposal (`forget_tenant` + a repo_invariants rule over `Mutex<HashMap<` fields) is sound hygiene at low severity.

findings.title: `UserSettings::save` is still `pub`, bypasses the process-wide lock, and its stale doc is glued onto `mutate`
findings.evidence:
settings.rs:90-98 (doc now attached to `mutate`) `/// Writes the settings to `<config_dir>/settings.json` (creating the directory if needed), pretty-printed. Used by the first-run config screen — the only writer of this file.
    /// ...
    /// Read, modify and write `settings.json` under a process-wide lock.`
settings.rs:109-111 `/// Every writer must go through here. ...`
settings.rs:127-129 `/// The write half of [`Self::mutate`]. Private so a caller cannot take the read-modify-write apart and reintroduce the race.
    fn save_locked(&self, ...)`
settings.rs:136-141 `pub fn save(&self, config_dir: &Path) -> std::io::Result<()> { ... write_owner_only(...) }` — identical body, public, unlocked; only callers are this file's tests.
findings.rationale: The comment explains why the write half is private, then a public unlocked twin sits directly beneath it. Nothing in `apps/` calls it (config.rs, defaults.rs, state.rs all use `mutate`), so it is dead in production and an open door to the lost-update race `mutate` exists to close. The orphaned 'only writer of this file' sentence is now factually wrong and attached to the wrong function.
findings.proposal: Delete `save` (tests can use `mutate` or `save_locked` via `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate)`), and remove the stale first paragraph from `mutate`'s doc. Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: Exactly as described. crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs:136-141 `pub fn save` is a byte-identical, unlocked twin of the private `save_locked` at :129-134, directly beneath the comment (:127-128) explaining why the write half is private. Only callers are this file's tests (:281, :322); grep of apps/ and crates/ for `.save(` on settings finds none — config.rs:53, defaults.rs and state.rs:363 all use `mutate`. The doc block at :90-98 ('Writes the settings ... the only writer of this file' + 'Owner-only ...') is the old `save` doc now attached to `mutate`, contradicting :100-111 which describes three writers. Deleting `save` (tests use `mutate`) and trimming the doc is the right S fix.

findings.title: `set_tenant_defaults` blank-normalises two of three patterns; only direct IPC callers can observe the inconsistency
findings.evidence:
defaults.rs:38-47 `// A blank pattern is stored as "unset" so it falls back to the built-in default.
    defaults.scope_name_pattern = defaults.scope_name_pattern.map(|p| p.trim().to_string()).filter(|p| !p.is_empty());
    defaults.group_name_pattern = defaults.group_name_pattern.map(|p| p.trim().to_string()).filter(|p| !p.is_empty());`
defaults.rs:53-57 `for (label, pattern) in [("scope_name_pattern", ...), ("group_name_pattern", ...), ("secret_name_pattern", &defaults.secret_name_pattern)] { if let Some(pat) = pattern && !pat.contains(SCOPE_NAME_PLACEHOLDER) { return Err(...) } }`
web-rs/views/settings_view.rs:116 `let secret_pattern = RwSignal::new(initial.secret_name_pattern.clone().unwrap_or_default());` (editable field)
findings.rationale: Clearing the Key Vault secret-name field to a space (or the UI sending `Some("")`-with-whitespace) stores/validates it as a real pattern and errors with "secret_name_pattern must contain {appId}" instead of reverting to the documented `secret-{appId}` default as the sibling fields do.
findings.proposal: Apply the same `.map(trim).filter(!empty)` to `secret_name_pattern` at defaults.rs:38-47 for consistency and add a test; no UI change needed.
findings.verifier_notes: The backend asymmetry is real: defaults.rs:38-47 normalises `scope_name_pattern` and `group_name_pattern` but the placeholder loop at :53-57 validates `secret_name_pattern` raw. But the user-facing scenario in the rationale is refuted: the Settings view trims every pattern and sends `None` for blank before invoking (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/settings_view.rs:226-237, `secret_name_pattern: { let p = secret_pattern.get().trim().to_string(); (!p.is_empty()).then_some(p) }`), and the consumer `TenantDefaults::secret_name_for` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/defaults.rs:160-172) trims and falls back at use, with a `Some("  ")` test at :280. So 'clearing the field to a space' cannot reach the backend as `Some(" ")`; only a hand-built IPC call can, and being told the pattern must contain `{appId}` is arguably correct fail-closed behaviour for such a caller. Low, consistency-only.

findings.title: CSV exports are written without a UTF-8 BOM; non-ASCII display names open garbled in Excel on Windows
findings.rationale: Excel (the README's implied consumer for CSV) sniffs encoding by BOM; without one it decodes UTF-8 as the ANSI code page, so `Zürich Finanz` or a Japanese app name renders as mojibake. The formula-injection guard shows this code already targets Excel. `#`-comment-block readers (`pandas`, R) accept a BOM with `encoding='utf-8-sig'`.
findings.proposal: In `save_export_via_dialog`'s `"csv"` arm and in `save_csv_via_dialog`, prefix the content with `\u{FEFF}` (one place: a `fn csv_bytes(s: String) -> Vec<u8>` used by both). Add a test that the first three bytes are `EF BB BF` and that `csv_columns` on the header line is unaffected. Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: `write_via_dialog` (export.rs:113-128) writes `content.into_bytes()` raw and is the single sink for every CSV — both `save_export_via_dialog`'s csv arm (:46-60) and `save_csv_via_dialog` (:141-154) route through it; repo grep for FEFF/BOM in apps/ and crates/ finds nothing. The formula-injection guard at export.rs:12-13 explicitly names Excel/Sheets as the consumer, so Excel's ANSI fallback for BOM-less UTF-8 is a legitimate concern for non-ASCII display names. One trade-off worth documenting in the fix: the `#` comment-block convention (export.rs:157-165) targets pandas/R readers; pandas strips a UTF-8 BOM automatically but base R `read.csv` needs `fileEncoding="UTF-8-BOM"`. Low, S effort, one choke point.

findings.title: `resolve()` precedence (env > settings.json > baked > placeholder) has no unit test, and DEVELOPMENT.md/.env.example omit the settings.json tier
findings.evidence:
state.rs:124-146 `/// Resolution order ...: a non-empty runtime env var ..., then the user's `settings.json` value ..., then the build-time bake from `.env`, then the placeholder default
fn resolve(env_var: &str, settings: Option<&str>, baked: Option<&'static str>, default: &'static str) -> String {`
state.rs `mod tests` (lines 704-787) contains only `CancelFlag` tests — no `resolve` test.
docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:76-80 "At runtime `state.rs` prefers a real `AZAPPTOOLKIT_*` env var, then the baked-in value, then the placeholder" (no settings.json tier)
.env.example:9-11 "Precedence at runtime: a real `AZAPPTOOLKIT_*` env var on the user's machine overrides the baked-in value"
README.md:410-411 "environment variable → in-app `settings.json` → baked-in value → unset" (correct).
findings.rationale: `resolve` decides which tenant the whole app binds to; its empty-string handling (an empty env var or empty settings value must fall through) is subtle and untested. The two developer-facing docs describe a three-tier order that predates the first-run config screen, so a developer debugging 'why is my `.env` ignored' is told the wrong answer.
findings.proposal: Add table-driven tests for `resolve` covering: env wins over settings/baked; empty env falls through; empty settings falls through; empty baked falls to default. Fix DEVELOPMENT.md:78 and `.env.example` to name the settings.json tier. Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: All claims check out. `resolve` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/state.rs:128-146) implements env → settings → baked → default with empty-string fall-through at each tier; the `mod tests` block (:710-787) contains only `CancelFlag` tests. docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:76-80 describes 'env var, then the baked-in value, then the placeholder' (no settings.json tier); .env.example:9-11 likewise mentions only env-over-baked. README.md:410-411 and crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/config.rs:3-4 have the correct four-tier order, so the two developer docs are the stale ones. Table-driven tests on a pure fn are cheap and the docs fix is one sentence each.

findings.title: Pass numbering and 'verbatim' federated-credential wording drift between restore.rs, its function docs and the architecture doc
findings.evidence:
restore.rs:292 `// ---- Pass 4: enterprise applications ----`; restore.rs:307 `// ---- Pass 5: managed identities ----`
restore.rs:623 `/// Pass-5 work for one enterprise app.`; restore.rs:723 `/// Pass-6 work: re-bind managed-identity permissions.`
restore.rs:187 `// One latch across all five passes`
restore.rs:1-14 module doc lists three passes; restore.rs:11 `federated credentials (verbatim)`
docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:184 "**Enterprise applications** restore in Pass 5"; :197 "**Managed identities** restore in Pass 6"
backup-and-restore.md also states: "pass 2 treats each one as untrusted input ... validated through `core::federation::validate_federated_credential`" — contradicting the module doc's 'verbatim'.
findings.rationale: Three different numberings for the same two passes, and a module doc that says federated credentials are restored verbatim when the code validates and reports each one (the architecture doc calls that validation a security property). Anyone using the docs to locate the code, or auditing the security claim, is misled.
findings.proposal: Pick one scheme (the inline `Pass 1..5` markers), fix the two function docs, the 'five passes' latch comment (fine) and the arch doc's 5/6 to 4/5, and change the module doc's `(verbatim)` to `(validated + reported)`, listing passes 4-5 in the module doc. Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: Drift confirmed and slightly wider than stated. Inline markers: restore.rs:292 'Pass 4: enterprise applications', :307 'Pass 5: managed identities'; function docs: :623 'Pass-5 work for one enterprise app', :723 'Pass-6 work'; latch comment :187 'all five passes' (consistent with the inline markers); module doc :4-15 lists three passes and says federated credentials '(verbatim)' at :11. docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:184 and :197 say Pass 5 / Pass 6. Additional inconsistencies the reviewer did not cite: the arch doc itself says federated credentials 'restore **verbatim**' at :45 while :148 and :157-172 describe them as validated via `core::federation::validate_federated_credential` and reported as `ManualItem`s (which is what restore.rs:29 and the `trusts` return at :255-257 actually do), and the plan view says 'federated credential(s) restored as-is' (dr.rs:459). Normalising on the inline 1..5 scheme and 'validated + reported' wording is the right call.

findings.title: `save_backup_to_file` / `save_restore_report_to_file` write `{}` on a serialization failure instead of erroring
findings.evidence:
restore.rs:354 `|| serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report).unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}".to_string()),`
backup.rs:295 `|| serde_json::to_string_pretty(&backup).unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}".to_string()),`
restore.rs:337-341 doc: "**The report contains the regenerated client-secret values** (show-once) ... the UI warns the operator to store it securely"
findings.rationale: Serialization of these plain structs is practically infallible today, but the failure direction is wrong: the report is the ONLY place the show-once secrets exist, and this path would silently write an empty object and return the chosen path as success. A future field (e.g. a map with non-string keys) would turn this into silent data loss.
findings.proposal: Make `save_export_via_dialog`'s `to_json` closure return `Result<String, UiError>` (or serialize before calling it) and map the error to `UiError::serde(...)`; apply to both call sites. Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: Both sites verified: restore.rs:354 and backup.rs:295 pass `|| serde_json::to_string_pretty(&x).unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}".to_string())` as `to_json`, and `save_export_via_dialog` (export.rs:39-61) then writes whatever string it gets and returns the path as success. The restore report is documented as the only home of the show-once secrets (restore.rs:337-341), so the failure direction is wrong even though serialization of these plain structs cannot realistically fail today. `UiError::serde` already exists (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/lib.rs:103). Scoping note for the fix: `save_export_via_dialog` has eight callers (enterprise_application.rs:553, sharepoint.rs:1072, backup.rs:290, managed_identity.rs:471, permission_tester.rs:1188, restore.rs:349, keyvault_rbac.rs:392, applications/mod.rs:461), so the least invasive change is to serialize before the call and `?` the error at the two DR sites rather than changing the closure signature for all eight.

findings.title: AuthConfigStatus lacks the resolution source; the Tenant-connection hint is generic rather than reflecting whether an env/baked override is active
findings.evidence:
config.rs:18-24 `pub fn get_auth_config(state: State<'_, AppState>) -> AuthConfigStatus { AuthConfigStatus { configured: state.is_configured(), client_id: state.display_client_id().to_string(), tenant_id: state.display_tenant_id().to_string() } }`
config.rs:26-29 `/// Persists the user-entered client/tenant IDs to `settings.json` ... The new IDs take effect on the next launch`
state.rs:128-146 `resolve` prefers env var over settings.json.
dto/config.rs:12-24 `pub struct AuthConfigStatus { configured, client_id, tenant_id }` — no source field.
findings.rationale: With `AZAPPTOOLKIT_TENANT_ID` set (MDM) or a `.env` baked, an operator can 'reconfigure' in-app, restart, and see the old value come back with no explanation. The baked value is also otherwise undiscoverable from the binary except by signing in. A `source` field lets the config screen say 'set by environment variable — in-app changes are ignored' and lets support confirm what a team build shipped.
findings.proposal: Return the resolution tier from `resolve` (an enum `ConfigSource { Env, Settings, Baked, Unset }`), store it on `AppState`, add `client_id_source`/`tenant_id_source` to `AuthConfigStatus` (serde default for the demo fixtures), and render a one-line note in the config view when the source is `Env`/`Baked`. Also emit `cargo:warning=` from `build.rs` when `.env` exists but a value is missing or `AZAPPTOOLKIT_CLIENT_ID` is not a GUID, so a mistyped bake is caught at build time. Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise true: `get_auth_config` (config.rs:18-24) and `AuthConfigStatus` (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/config.rs:12-24) carry no source, and `resolve` (state.rs:128-146) lets an env var win over settings.json. Overstated on 'silently defeats': the Settings → Tenant connection tab already warns that 'an AZAPPTOOLKIT_CLIENT_ID / AZAPPTOOLKIT_TENANT_ID environment variable still overrides it' (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/settings_view.rs:335-339), so the operator is told an override is possible — what is missing is telling them one is *active* (and the baked tier is not mentioned there at all). The build.rs sub-proposal is valid: bake_client_config (apps/desktop/src-tauri/build.rs:24-34) silently `continue`s on an empty value and never validates the GUID shape, so a mistyped `.env` is discovered only at sign-in. Low enhancement; the `serde(default)` source fields are additive and demo-fixture safe.

findings.title: resolve_mail_scopes hardcodes Microsoft Graph, so the EWS full_access_as_app scope never gets a verdict (Permissions tab shows Unknown forever; audit scores a correctly scoped EWS app org-wide)
findings.rationale: graph_mail_role("full_access_as_app") is None, so the value is dropped in all three resolver paths. get_mail_permission_scopes emits no MailScopeEntry for it (an app declaring only the EWS scope gets an empty Vec cached without any Exchange call); get_mail_scopes_for_principal returns Unknown for it (scopes.get(&value) misses). The audit's lean resolver drops it too, so after a successful `Application EWS.AccessAsApp` scoping the audit still scores the app at org-wide weight (empty map = org-wide). The mod.rs comment justifying MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID is contradicted by the crate's own resource-aware mapping and by the repo's tests; this is not a documented decision but a regression left behind when the value-only helper was deleted.
findings.proposal: Change resolve_mail_scopes and resolve_mail_scopes_audit_cached to accept the role alongside the value — e.g. `&[(String, &'static str)]` (the shape get_mail_scopes_for_principal already builds at 377-383) or `&[ExchangeTarget]` (which carries exchange_role) — and stop re-deriving the role inside. Fix the entries filter at 341 to read the role from the target rather than calling exchange_role_for_resource_permission(MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID, ..). Update the audit caller (audit.rs:1553) to pass perms.app_role_grants' (resource, value) pairs. Correct the mod.rs:32-35 comment. Add a unit test that resolve_mail_scopes' output keys include full_access_as_app mapped to "Application EWS.AccessAsApp" and that an EWS-only input does not short-circuit before the probe. Expected effect: the EWS row shows Org-wide/Scoped like Graph rows, and the audit's reduced scoped-mail weight applies to an RBAC-scoped EWS grant.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise holds at every cited line. mail_scopes.rs:108-116, :242 and :341 all call exchange_role_for_resource_permission(MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID, ..); core scoping.rs:106-116 maps full_access_as_app ONLY under OFFICE365_EXCHANGE_ONLINE_APP_ID and graph_mail_role (scoping.rs:77-93) has no EWS arm, so the value is dropped in all three resolver paths. Downstream: get_mail_permission_scopes builds `scopable` from targets_from_declared (mail_scopes.rs:312-315), which exchange/tests.rs:81-106 proves includes full_access_as_app; an EWS-only app therefore passes the empty check at :316, pays exchange_client_checked (consent prompt) at :334, gets an empty map back from resolve_mail_scopes (:114-115), and the :341 filter drops the row, caching an empty Vec (:353). get_mail_scopes_for_principal gates correctly by resource (:377-383) but then feeds bare values into resolve_mail_scopes, so scopes.get misses and the row is Unknown (:432-435). Frontend scope_badge.rs:104-112 renders ScopeCell::Mailbox(Unknown) for (EXO, full_access_as_app) since is_exchange_scopable_on is a re-export of is_scopable_exchange_resource_permission (scope_badge.rs:35), and :330-340 expects a verdict cell for that row. Audit: core audit/types.rs:386-396 scope_mechanism passes the resource gate for (EXO, full_access_as_app) then misses mail_scopes.get → None → full weight; derive_orgwide_mail_scopes (audit.rs:1100-1130) only feeds the reconciliation set, and apply_legacy_policy_verdict (verdict.rs:192-210) only covers the legacy-AAP verdict, never an RBAC 'Application EWS.AccessAsApp' scope. The mod.rs:32-35 rationale ('only Microsoft Graph's mail permissions ever are') is contradicted by scoping.rs:112-114, tests.rs:104 and mail_scopes.rs:422-425 in the same file. No repo_invariants test, doc (exchange-scoping.md:98-140 describes the EWS row as scopable and rendered) or CHANGELOG entry documents Graph-only resolution as deliberate. One caveat: the 'regression when the value-only helper was deleted' history claim is unverifiable — the repo history is squashed at 0389543 (exchange.rs lands whole, 2987 insertions) — but that does not affect the code-level verdict. Proposal (pass (value, role) or ExchangeTarget, fix :341, correct mod.rs comment, add a unit test) is feasible and consistent with the 'carry the resource, never the bare value' rule.
findings.recheck_notes:
Could not refute; every path traced end to end reproduces the defect in the shipped build.

(1) Role mapping: crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/scoping.rs:106-116 returns Some("Application EWS.AccessAsApp") only for (OFFICE365_EXCHANGE_ONLINE_APP_ID, "full_access_as_app"); scoping.rs:77-96 graph_mail_role has no arm for it, and the crate's own test at scoping.rs:579-582 asserts exchange_role_for_resource_permission(MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID, EWS_FULL_ACCESS_AS_APP) == None. So the hardcoded MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID at apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/exchange/mail_scopes.rs:111, :242 and :341 drops the EWS value unconditionally.

(2) Declared path (app-reg Permissions tab): mail_scopes.rs:312-315 builds `scopable` from targets_from_declared, which the test at commands/exchange/tests.rs:81-105 proves yields ["Mail.Read", "full_access_as_app"] with exchange_role "Application EWS.AccessAsApp". resolve_mail_scopes then filters it out (:108-113); an EWS-only app hits `scopable.is_empty()` at :114 and returns Ok(empty) with no probe, and the entries filter at :341 emits no MailScopeEntry for it either. web-rs/src/views/tabs/permissions_tab.rs:156-161 keys the map by entry, so the EWS row misses; scope_badge.rs:35 aliases is_exchange_scopable_on to the resource-aware gate (true for EXO+full_access_as_app), so scope_cell_for:105-112 renders ScopeCell::Mailbox(Unknown) once loading ends. The result is then cached at :353 under `declared|{object_id}` until invalidate_app_details, so it is stable, not transient.

(3) Held path (enterprise app / MI pane): get_mail_scopes_for_principal's gate at :377-383 is resource-aware and keeps the EWS pair, but :426-427 passes values only into resolve_mail_scopes, which drops it; :432-435 falls back to MailPermissionScope::Unknown for that entry and caches it (:443).

(4) Audit: audit.rs:1260 pushes ResourcePermission::exchange_online(EWS_FULL_ACCESS_AS_APP) into app_role_grants, so `declared_values = perms.app_role_values()` (audit.rs:1523; core/audit/types.rs:338-343) includes it; resolve_mail_scopes_audit_cached filters it away at mail_scopes.rs:240-244 (and excludes it from the cache key). core/audit/types.rs:386-397 scope_mechanism reads mail_scopes.get(&grant.value) -> None -> full org-wide weight for an app whose only mailbox grant is an RBAC-scoped `Application EWS.AccessAsApp`. Only apply_legacy_policy_verdict (audit.rs:1585) can ever mark the EWS grant scoped, and only via a surviving legacy AAP, not RBAC.

(5) Not a documented decision: docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md:31-33 says the probe/badge paths were meant to use the value-only role form precisely because "the two resources share no mapped value names" (i.e. EWS is unambiguous there). The value-only form was then deleted and pinned out by repo_invariants/commands.rs:129-134, and the replacement at mail_scopes.rs:101-107 / mod.rs:32-35 asserts "only Microsoft Graph's mail permissions ever are" scopable, which scoping.rs:113 and the deep-dive contradict. No unit test or repo invariant covers resolve_mail_scopes' output for the EWS value (the only resolver test, exchange/tests.rs:200-231, uses a non-mail permission), so nothing upstream or in CI prevents it.

Severity note: the audit-side error is in the conservative direction (over-reports risk, never under-reports), so there is no security exposure; the high severity rests on the Permissions tab permanently showing Unknown for the broadest mailbox grant there is and the RBAC-scoping workflow for EWS never visibly converging. remediation.rs:381-397 only passes Graph values and is unaffected. The proposal (carry the role/resource into the resolver or accept ExchangeTarget/(value, role) pairs; fix :341; correct the mod.rs comment; add a unit test) is correct and sufficient.

findings.title: test_site_access claims "holds no organization-wide SharePoint grant" when the grants read actually failed
findings.rationale: When sharepoint_grants_held returns None (SP lookup or appRoleAssignments read failed), path 1 is silently skipped and, if no permission entry exists on the chain, the command returns a definitive no_access whose detail asserts a fact it never established. An app holding org-wide Sites.Read.All reads as having no access during a transient Graph failure — the exact under-report the doc forbids, and the Exchange half of the same file already avoids (RbacReach::Indeterminate).
findings.proposal: Extract a pure site_verdict(held, hit, label) and return `unknown` when the grants could not be READ and no entry exists — but distinguish the two things sharepoint_grants_held currently folds into None (permission_tester.rs:888-893): `get_service_principal_by_app_id` returning Ok(None) (the SP genuinely does not exist in this tenant, so `no_access` is the right answer) versus an Err on the SP lookup / graph_role_index / list_app_role_assignments (unreadable → `unknown`). Return a tri-state (or Result<Option<..>>) from sharepoint_grants_held so the verdict table has: org-wide wins; unreadable + no entry → unknown; unreadable + entry → unknown (already at :1113-1123); no SP → no_access; entry + matching scope → scoped; entry without scope → no_access naming required_scope_for.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is real: permission_tester.rs:1067 reads `held` once; path 1 at :1077-1089 is skipped whenever held is None; :1091-1101 then returns a definitive `no_access` whose detail asserts 'it holds no organization-wide SharePoint grant'; only the entry-found branch handles None (:1113-1123). The docstring on sharepoint_grants_held (:882-884) and on HeldSharePointGrants (:857-859) both say None must be reported as unknown, and docs/architecture/sharepoint-selected.md:103 states 'A failure to read the assignments reports `unknown`, never "no access"' — so this is a contract breach, not a decision. No unit test covers the branch (tests module :1230-1535 has no test_site_access assembly tests). Severity adjusted from high to medium: the false negative requires a Graph failure on the SP/assignment reads while the site resolve and chain walk succeed (a narrow, transient window), and the fix is an hour's work. The proposal needs one correction: `??` at :888-892 also maps a non-existent SP to None, and for that case `no_access` is correct, so the tri-state must keep it apart from a read failure.

findings.title: orgwide_mailbox_grant folds a failed Graph read into EntraReach::NotHeld, yielding a definitive no_access for managed identities on a transient error
findings.rationale: Three distinct Graph failures collapse into "not held". Combined with RbacReach::None{had_assignments:false} (the managed-identity / not-in-EXO-store case, which rbac_reach_for returns for a missing-object error), synthesize produces verdict no_access and the detail states positively that no Entra grant exists. The sibling sharepoint_grants_held (884-887) explicitly distinguishes unreadable from none; the mailbox side does not. The same helper feeds the `exchange_client` failure branch (379-397) where None becomes a generic unknown, so only the main path is affected.
findings.proposal: Return a tri-state (e.g. `Result<Vec<String>, ()>` or an enum Held(Vec)/None/Unreadable) and add `EntraReach::Unreadable`, scored at level 1 (unknown) in synthesize with detail "Entra app-role assignments couldn't be read". Reuse mail_scopes::held_orgwide_mail_grants for the body (see the duplication finding) once it, too, exposes read failure. Add a synthesize test: Unreadable + RbacReach::None{false} => verdict unknown, not no_access.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: orgwide_mailbox_grant (permission_tester.rs:63-93) returns None for `get_service_principal_by_app_id` Err or Ok(None) (`.ok()??` at :70-73), for mailbox_resource_roles Err (:76) and for list_app_role_assignments Err (:77) — the docstring at :58-60 even says 'or can't be resolved'. test_mailbox_access maps None straight to EntraReach::NotHeld (:404-411) and synthesize writes 'No organization-wide Graph mailbox permission is granted in Entra ID.' (:264-266). With RbacReach::None{had_assignments:false} — which rbac_reach_for returns for a missing-object error (:161-166, the managed-identity / not-in-EXO-store case) — the verdict is `no_access`. The SharePoint sibling sharepoint_grants_held (:882-884) documents the opposite contract, and the exchange_client-failure branch (:379-397) already turns None into unknown, so the asymmetry is real. docs/architecture/resource-access-and-permission-tester.md:76-95 describes the Entra layer but never states that an unreadable assignment list should read as not-held, so this is not a documented decision. Proposal is sound; note that Ok(None) from the SP lookup (SP genuinely absent) should stay NotHeld — only the Err paths become Unreadable. held_orgwide_mail_grants (mail_scopes.rs:48-73) has the same fold-to-empty shape but there empty is the safe (org-wide) direction, so only the tester side is wrong.

findings.title: find_mailbox_reachers discovers candidates from the Microsoft Graph resource only, so an app whose sole mailbox grant is org-wide EWS full_access_as_app is missed or reported as no_access
findings.rationale: The reverse lookup answers "who can reach this mailbox?". A principal granted only full_access_as_app (full access to every mailbox over EWS) is not a Graph appRoleAssignedTo hit; if it is registered in Exchange's SP store it enters with empty held permissions and, absent an RBAC assignment, reads no_access — the strongest possible mailbox grant reported as none. The single-app tester and the audit both already close this gap, so the two surfaces disagree for the same principal.
findings.proposal: Replace graph_role_index + one appRoleAssignedTo read with mailbox_resource_roles (both resource SPs) and page list_app_role_assigned_to on each, filtering with is_scopable_exchange_resource_permission(Some(resource.app_id), value); or, simpler, reuse prefetch_ews_full_access_grants' shape to add EWS holders to `candidates` with held = ["full_access_as_app"]. Extend merge test to cover an EWS-only candidate.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: find_mailbox_reachers builds candidates from graph_role_index + one list_app_role_assigned_to on the Graph SP only (permission_tester.rs:466-479) and filters with Some(MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID) (:476); merge_exchange_candidates (:687-699) adds EXO-store principals with an empty held list; probe_candidate then sets EntraReach::NotHeld when held is empty (:800-806), so an EWS-only principal with no RBAC assignment reads `no_access` (or is absent entirely when not in Exchange's SP store). The single-app tester (:71-79) and the audit's prefetch_ews_full_access_grants (audit.rs:1007-1040) both already read the Office 365 Exchange Online SP for exactly this grant, and docs/architecture/resource-access-and-permission-tester.md:60-61 claims the probe uses 'the same two-layer union the Permission tester uses' — which is currently untrue for the candidate discovery step. No doc or comment names the Graph-only sweep as deliberate. Proposal (page appRoleAssignedTo on both mailbox resources via mailbox_resource_roles, or reuse prefetch_ews_full_access_grants' shape, and extend the merge test at :1511) is feasible; a tenant with no EWS-consenting app has no SPO/EXO SP, which must read as an ordinary empty set, as audit.rs:1015-1021 does.

findings.title: MailboxReachersResult.exchange_available can never reflect the realistic degraded mode (missing Exchange consent / 403), so the summary's partial-coverage caveat never fires
findings.rationale: For a signed-in operator with a UPN, exchange_available is always true. When Exchange.Manage is unconsented or the caller lacks Exchange admin rights — the common degraded case — the AAP read fails, the Exchange SP-store candidate source is dropped at info level, and every RBAC layer is Indeterminate, yet the result and its CSV export carry no coverage flag beyond the per-row unknown count. The doc's promised caveat is unreachable in practice.
findings.proposal: Best-effort pre-acquire with `state.ensure_exchange_token(&tenant_id).await` and set exchange_available=false (keeping exo=None) on failure; additionally add `exchange_sp_store_read: bool` (or fold into exchange_available) set from the list_service_principals outcome so the summary/export can say "Exchange-registered apps without an Entra grant could not be enumerated". Update the doc sentence to match.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: exchange_available = exchange_client(..).ok().is_some() (permission_tester.rs:496-497); exchange_client only checks tenant_context and username (exchange/mod.rs:90-107) and never touches a token — exchange_client_checked (:116-122) is the pre-acquiring variant. So for any signed-in operator with a UPN the flag is always true; a missing Exchange.Manage consent or an admin-API 403 surfaces only as an Err from get_application_access_policies (dropped to None at :500-508) and from list_service_principals (info-log at :511-518), silently removing the Exchange-SP-store candidate source. The frontend caveat (web-rs views/resource_access/mailboxes.rs:54-57) and the doc sentence (resource-access-and-permission-tester.md:64-66) are therefore unreachable in the realistic degraded case. Partial mitigation the finding under-weights: the per-row unknown count does render ' · N couldn't be confirmed (need Exchange admin rights)' (mailboxes.rs:49-52), so the operator gets a hint about RBAC verdicts — but nothing flags that Exchange-only principals were not enumerated at all, which is the real under-report. Medium is fair. Proposal is feasible: AppState::ensure_exchange_token exists (state.rs:661-664) and is the same pre-acquire exchange_client_checked uses; adding a bool to MailboxReachersResult (dto/permission_tester.rs:99-106) is an additive wire change the CSV coverage block should also carry.

findings.title: Site sweep silently truncates at MAX_SITES_PER_SWEEP and caches the result as complete; is_complete() has no truncation dimension (the audit result does)
findings.rationale: A tenant with more than 5 000 enumerable sites gets total_sites = 5000, sites_scanned = 5000, sites_failed = 0 → cached for 60 minutes and is_complete() = true. The per-app panel then states "no per-site grants" for an app whose grants live on site 5 001+, and the CSV coverage line claims full coverage — the exact overstatement the sweep's own comments promise never to make. Nothing tells the operator the cap was hit, so "Raise if a user legitimately hits it" can never be acted on.
findings.proposal: Make list_all_sites return `(Vec<Site>, truncated: bool)` (fetch until len > max or nextLink exhausted, then truncate and flag), add `truncated: bool` to SiteSweepResult / AppSiteAccessDto, include `!self.truncated` in is_complete(), exclude truncated runs from the cache (or cache with the flag), and render "more than 5 000 sites — coverage is partial" in the summary and export. Add a DTO test mirroring the audit's truncated case.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: MAX_SITES_PER_SWEEP = 5_000 with the 'Raise if a user legitimately hits it' comment (sharepoint.rs:756-758) is passed to list_all_sites (:843); the graph client stops paging at `out.len() < max` and `out.truncate(max)` with no signal (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/sharepoint.rs:87-106); the sweep caches on `!cancelled && sites_failed == 0` (:988-992) and SiteSweepResult/AppSiteAccessDto::is_complete is `!cancelled && sites_failed == 0` (dto/sharepoint.rs:130-132), whereas the audit's AuditExportCoverage::is_complete includes `!self.truncated` (dto/audit.rs:125-127). The UI summary reads 'scanned X of Y sites' with Y == total == 5000 and no cap mention (web-rs views/resource_access/sites.rs:115-123), the export reuses that sentence (:144-149), and neither sharepoint-selected.md nor CHANGELOG.md mentions the cap. So a >5000-site tenant gets a cached, is_complete()==true result and the per-app panel's 'no per-site grants' overstates coverage — contradicting the 'coverage is never overstated' promise at sharepoint.rs:826-829 and sharepoint-selected.md:30-34. Not a documented decision. Proposal is right; prefer caching WITH the truncated flag (and letting is_complete carry it) over excluding truncated runs from the cache, otherwise a large tenant re-sweeps 5000 sites on every panel visit.

findings.title: apply_exchange_mailbox_scope's warnings name each failed strip/assignment but never summarize which permissions remain org-wide, unlike migrate_one
findings.rationale: When the operator asked for the strip but a role assignment failed, or the assignments list could not be read, the result still carries scope_name/scope_filter and the UI shows "N roles assigned, M grants removed". The per-item failure lines say what failed but not that the app remains org-wide for those permissions; only the remove_unscoped=false branch spells out the consequence. The migration path produces exactly the sentence needed, so the two callers of the same core diverge in what they tell the operator.
findings.proposal: After the strip in apply_exchange_mailbox_scope (grants.rs:276-289), compute the targets whose value is not in removed_entra_grants and, when remove_unscoped is set and that list is non-empty, push ONE consolidated warning through a helper shared with aap_migration.rs:392-398 ('Scoping is NOT effective for {list}: still granted organization-wide in Entra ID …'). Optionally add an additive `effective: bool` to ExchangeAccessResult so scope_wizard's count-only summary (scope_wizard.rs:91-101) can badge it; the Exchange scoping section already lists warnings verbatim.
findings.verifier_notes: The evidence is real (grants.rs:276-289, :22-27, :39-42, :118; aap_migration.rs:392-398; scope_wizard.rs:91-101) but the impact is overstated. The UI does NOT show only 'N roles assigned, M grants removed': exchange_scoping_section.rs:213 toasts only when warnings is empty, and :400-415 renders every warning as a <li> under a warn Callout — so the operator does see 'failed to remove unscoped grant Mail.Read: …' / 'failed to assign Application Mail.Read: …' / 'could not list Entra app-role assignments: …', each of which names the permission left broad. Only the ScopeWizard summary collapses warnings to a count. What is genuinely missing is the one-line consequence statement migrate_one already produces, which is a small wording/consistency enhancement, not a medium-severity gap.

findings.title: grant_exchange_mailbox_access creates the Entra service principal before validating that anything is scopable; the error path leaves a new SP behind with no list invalidation
findings.rationale: targets_from_declared needs only `app` and `resources`, yet the SP creation (a directory write that adds an enterprise app) runs first. If validation then fails, the command reports "nothing to scope" while having created an SP, and the cached App Registrations/Enterprise Apps lists are not busted on that path. The "(line ~450)" comment is also stale — the invalidation now lives in apply_exchange_mailbox_scope at 294.
findings.proposal: Reorder: get_application → mailbox_resource_roles → targets → require_scopable_targets → ensure_service_principal. Replace the stale line pointer with "invalidate_app_lists runs in apply_exchange_mailbox_scope on success".
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: grant_exchange_mailbox_access calls graph.ensure_service_principal(&app.app_id) at grants.rs:332 before mailbox_resource_roles (:333), targets_from_declared/filter (:335-338) and require_scopable_targets (:340-346); ensure_service_principal POSTs /servicePrincipals when none exists (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/service_principals.rs:506-516) and on creation sweeps only the ServicePrincipal cache kind (:514) — the Lists/app indexes are busted by invalidate_app_lists only inside apply_exchange_mailbox_scope's success path (grants.rs:290-294), so a validation failure after SP creation leaves stale App Registrations / Enterprise Apps lists. The comment '(line ~450)' at :330-331 is stale (the invalidation is at :294 in a different file now). targets_from_declared needs only `app` and `resources`, so the reorder is trivially feasible and apply_exchange_mailbox_scope still receives entra_sp.id. Severity low is honest: the created SP is the app's own, idempotent, and harmless, and the list staleness heals on TTL.

findings.title: The org-wide strip loop and the declare-then-grant-appRole step are duplicated across the SharePoint paths and against the Exchange core instead of being shared helpers
findings.rationale: Four copies of two small algorithms drift independently (the Exchange copy already names the resource explicitly; the SharePoint copy checks resource_id then value). A future fix to one — e.g. the SPO-resource strip the scoping.rs docs invite, or the "still org-wide" warning above — has to be applied in each. A shared strip helper keyed on a (resource_sp_id, value) predicate and a shared ensure-declared-and-granted helper would make the AGENTS.md claim literally true.
findings.proposal: In graph_roles.rs add `strip_app_role_grants(client, sp_id, assignments: &[AppRoleAssignment], keep: impl Fn(&AppRoleAssignment) -> Option<String /*value*/>, warnings) -> Vec<String>` used by remove_unscoped_grants and convert_site_access_to_selected; in sharepoint.rs add `ensure_graph_role_declared_and_granted(client, cache, tenant, object_id, sp_object_id, graph_sp_id, role_value_by_id, value) -> Result<(String /*role_id*/, bool /*declared*/, bool /*added*/), UiError>` used by both SharePoint commands. Pin with a small test that both SharePoint commands route through it (repo_invariants style grep) if desired.
findings.verifier_notes: All four duplicates are real and byte-for-byte as described: the Sites.Selected / permission_value reverse lookup at sharepoint.rs:292-303 and :515-525; the declare_graph_role → `existing.iter().any(resource_id == graph_sp_id && app_role_id == id)` → grant_app_role(.. 'grant_failed') → granted_role_added block at :311-338 and :531-559; the org-wide strip loop at :366-393 vs remove_unscoped_grants at grants.rs:15-43. One shape difference to keep in mind for the helper: the SharePoint strip is predicate-driven over ALL existing assignments (any org-wide Sites.* on the Graph resource) while the Exchange strip is target-driven (specific (resource_sp, app_role_id) pairs and a per-target 'safe to strip' guard via targets_safe_to_strip, targets.rs:254-259), so the proposed `keep: Fn(&AppRoleAssignment) -> Option<String>` closure form is the right abstraction. The framing stretches AGENTS.md slightly: 'Scoped grants reuse shared cores' (and .claude/rules/scoping-and-audit.md) is about grant-before-strip ordering within each plane, not about cross-plane helpers, so the finding is a plain DRY refactor rather than a rule violation. Drift risk is genuine (findings 6 and 15 each want to touch one copy), but two-copies-each of ~15-line loops is low severity, not medium.

findings.title: Two internal helpers (migrate_one, probe_candidate) could take context structs; converting the three Tauri commands to request structs is a wire-format change, not a drop-in
findings.evidence:
aap_migration.rs:148-158: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] pub(super) async fn migrate_one(graph, exo, app_id, policies, resources, scope_override, tenant_defaults, dry_run)
grants.rs:369-379: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] pub async fn grant_managed_identity_scoped_exchange_access(state, tenant_id, managed_identity_id, app_id, app_display_name, mail_permissions, groups, remove_unscoped_entra_grants)
sharepoint.rs:275-286 convert_site_access_to_selected (9 args), sharepoint.rs:488-499 grant_selected_item_access (9 args), permission_tester.rs:719-729 probe_candidate (9 args).

grants.rs:47-50 (the precedent): "Inputs to [`apply_exchange_mailbox_scope`], grouped so each is named at the call site. Several are `&str` (tenant/app/sp ids), where a long positional list is easy to transpose — hence a struct rather than 12 bare arguments."

web-rs bindings/sharepoint.rs:176 and 293 build the args as `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` structs already.
findings.rationale: migrate_one takes six values that are constant across the whole-tenant loop (graph, exo, resources, scope_override, tenant_defaults, dry_run) plus two per-app ones; probe_candidate takes five run-constant values plus four per-candidate ones. The transposition hazard the grants.rs comment describes (several adjacent &str ids: tenant_id/managed_identity_id/app_id/app_display_name) applies verbatim to the three Tauri commands. For commands, a single `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` request struct is wire-compatible as long as field names match the current argument names, because the bindings already send one camelCase object.
findings.proposal: Introduce MigrationContext<'a> for migrate_one (aap_migration.rs:148-158; six run-constant values) and ProbeContext<'a>/ProbeCandidate for probe_candidate (permission_tester.rs:719-729), dropping those two allows and the orphaned `//` rationale at :709-711. Leave the three #[tauri::command] signatures (grants.rs:369-379, sharepoint.rs:275-286, :488-499) flat unless the bindings are changed in the same PR: Tauri extracts each parameter by name, so a single `args: ConvertSiteAccessArgs` parameter requires the frontend to send `{ args: {...} }` — see the repo's own precedent set_cache_config(input: SetCacheConfigInput) invoked as `invoke_result("set_cache_config", SetCacheConfigArgs { input })` (web-rs bindings/diagnostics.rs:56-57). The flat ConvertArgs / GrantSelectedItemArgs structs (bindings/sharepoint.rs:129, :241) and the ipc_mock/demo fixtures would all have to be nested accordingly.
findings.verifier_notes: The five allows exist where cited (plus three more the finding omits: backup.rs:506, :674, applications/permissions_resolve.rs:14), and the ApplyExchangeMailboxScopeParams precedent (grants.rs:47-60) is real. The context-struct half is sound. The command half is wrong as stated: 'wire-compatible as long as field names match' and 'Keep the existing per-command bindings unchanged' contradict how Tauri 2 deserializes command arguments (per-parameter by name from the invoke payload), which the repo's existing struct-arg command demonstrates by nesting the struct under its parameter name. Also, permission_tester.rs:709-711 carries an explicit (if orphaned) rationale for probe_candidate's allow that the finding should engage with; it is weak — five run-constant values across a dispatch loop is exactly the transposition hazard grants.rs:47-50 describes — but it is a stated decision.

findings.title: probe_candidate's doc comment is attached to struct ProbeOutcome, leaving the function undocumented and its too_many_arguments rationale orphaned
findings.rationale: Rustdoc accumulates consecutive `///` blocks (plain `//` lines do not break the run) onto the next item, so ProbeOutcome carries both paragraphs and probe_candidate has none. The `//` justification for the allow is now separated from the fn it justifies (and, per the previous finding, no longer holds once a context struct exists).
findings.proposal: Move `struct ProbeOutcome` (with its own doc) above the `/// Probes one candidate…` block, and place that block plus the allow rationale directly on `probe_candidate`. `cargo doc` would show the fix immediately.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified at permission_tester.rs:701-721: a `///` block ('Probes one candidate principal…') is followed by three `//` lines, then a second `///` block ('One candidate's row, plus whether…'), then `struct ProbeOutcome` at :716-719, then `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] async fn probe_candidate` at :719-720 with no doc of its own. Doc comments are `#[doc]` attributes attached to the next item and plain `//` comments do not interrupt that run, so rustdoc attaches both paragraphs to ProbeOutcome and probe_candidate is undocumented. Proposal (move the struct + its own doc above, keep the fn doc and allow rationale on the fn) is correct and trivial.

findings.title: Orphaned doc comment in mail_scopes.rs describes is_org_wide_auth_row, which moved to azapptoolkit-exchange::verdict
findings.rationale: The first paragraph is the former doc of is_org_wide_auth_row (now in the crate, imported by permission_tester.rs:47) and is glued onto legacy_aap_scope's doc, so rustdoc shows legacy_aap_scope as being about ScopeType rows.
findings.proposal: Delete lines 9-15 (or move the text onto verdict.rs:29, which currently has no doc comment).
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: mail_scopes.rs:9-15 is the former doc of is_org_wide_auth_row (ScopeType / OrganizationConfig / NotApplicable / AllowedResourceScope) and runs without a blank line into :16-22, the doc of legacy_aap_scope (:23). crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/verdict.rs:29 `pub fn is_org_wide_auth_row` has no doc comment (line 28 is blank after the `use` at :27), and permission_tester.rs:47 imports it from the crate. Either deleting :9-15 or moving the paragraph onto verdict.rs:29 is correct; moving is the better fix since the text is accurate and the crate function is otherwise undocumented.

findings.title: permission_tester re-implements sharepoint_client_checked, map_sharepoint_err and held_orgwide_mail_grants instead of reusing them
findings.rationale: The sharepoint.rs docstring asserts a single-home contract that this file already violates; three near-identical helpers will drift (the two Exchange copies already differ in how they surface read failure, which is the root of the NotHeld finding).
findings.proposal: Make sharepoint_client_checked, sharepoint_item_err/map_sharepoint_err pub(crate) and use them from permission_tester; have orgwide_mailbox_grant resolve the SP and then call held_orgwide_mail_grants (after that helper is taught to report unreadable, per the NotHeld finding).
findings.verifier_notes: Verified all three duplications. sharepoint_test_err (permission_tester.rs:1023-1033) has the same body as map_sharepoint_err (sharepoint.rs:164-176) with capability 'sharepoint_selected_items', i.e. it IS sharepoint_item_err (sharepoint.rs:154-156); both sharepoint.rs helpers are private, and the tester's own docstring (:1020-1022) says 'Mirrors commands::sharepoint', acknowledging the copy. sharepoint_client_checked (sharepoint.rs:118-134) is private and its doc claims 'every SharePoint command routes its pre-acquire through here … in one place', while test_site_access inlines `ensure_sharepoint_token(..).map_err(UiError::from)?; graph_for(..)` (permission_tester.rs:1059-1063). orgwide_mailbox_grant (:63-93) and held_orgwide_mail_grants (mail_scopes.rs:48-73) share the mailbox_resource_roles → list_app_role_assignments → resolve_grant → is_scopable_exchange_resource_permission pipeline, differing in the SP-by-appId resolve, Vec-vs-HashSet, and how read failure is surfaced (the root of finding 2). Making the sharepoint.rs helpers pub(crate) and routing the tester through them is a safe, small cleanup; the mail helper unification should ride finding 2's tri-state change.

findings.title: Sweep constants and docstrings still describe the pre-$batch, per-site shape
findings.rationale: The unit of the cap changed from one site to one chunk of 100 sites (so up to 600 site reads can be in flight across 30 $batch requests, not 6), and progress granularity is per chunk. Someone tuning the throttle from the comment would size it wrongly; the doc line also misstates what the UI sees.
findings.proposal: Reword SWEEP_CONCURRENCY's doc to "concurrent chunk tasks (each a `$batch` fan-out over up to SWEEP_BATCH sites)" and the command doc to "after each chunk of SWEEP_BATCH sites".
