Also collapse `let mut cancelled = false;` (870) and the two `cancelled = cancelled || …` lines (933-935) into `let cancelled = stopped_early || cancel.is_cancelled();`.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: SWEEP_CONCURRENCY's doc says 'In-flight cap for per-site permission reads' (sharepoint.rs:744-749) but the tracker built from it (:862-863) caps dispatch_capped over `chunks` of SWEEP_BATCH = 100 sites (:755, :879-885), each chunk issuing $batch POSTs of 20 (:892) — so up to 6 chunk tasks, not 6 site reads, are in flight. The command doc says 'emits `site-sweep-progress` after each site' (:822) while progress is emitted per chunk with `done += chunk.len()` (:913-925). The `cancelled` flag is declared `let mut cancelled = false;` (:870) and only ever assigned at :933 and :935, so `let cancelled = stopped_early || cancel.is_cancelled();` is an exact equivalent (the progress closure uses cancel.is_cancelled() directly, not the flag). Docs-only plus a two-line tidy; low is right.

findings.title: The site tester's verdict assembly and its two pure helpers (roles_for_app, scope_for_level) have no unit tests; the level asymmetry itself is already pinned in core
findings.rationale: These pure functions decide the tester's SharePoint verdict, including the one asymmetry sharepoint-selected.md calls out (ListItems.* covers a file, Files.* does not cover a plain-list item) and the held-unreadable branch that is currently wrong. A regression here would ship unnoticed; the Exchange side of the same file demonstrates the intended test density.
findings.proposal: Extract site_verdict(held: tri-state, hit: Option<EntryHit>, label) as in finding 1 and table-test: org-wide wins; entry + matching scope → scoped; entry without scope → no_access naming required_scope_for(level); unreadable + entry → unknown; unreadable + no entry → unknown; no SP → no_access; roles_for_app case-folds appId and dedupes/sorts roles; scope_for_level picks a ListItem scope for a File-level hit and rejects a File scope for a ListItem hit (as wiring tests over the already-pinned selected_scope_accepts).
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: the tests module (permission_tester.rs:1230-1535, 15 tests) covers synthesize, rbac_reach_from_rows, classify_reacher, merge_exchange_candidates and CSV only; grep finds no test call of roles_for_app (:922-933) or scope_for_level (:873-877), and test_site_access's verdict assembly (:1077-1140) is inline behind a State. Overstated part: 'the one asymmetry sharepoint-selected.md calls out' is already unit-tested where it lives — crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/scoping.rs:940-965 pins selected_scope_accepts(ListItem, File) == true and (File, ListItem) == false — so the tester only needs wiring tests for that, not a re-derivation. The untested held-unreadable branch is the real gap and is the bug in finding 1, which justifies keeping medium.

findings.title: Office 365 SharePoint Online is the documented seam: the tester ignores org-wide Sites.* grants on that resource and the converter can't strip them
findings.rationale: The converter limitation is a documented, gated decision and is not re-litigated here. But the read-only tester has no such gate: an app holding Sites.FullControl.All on Office 365 SharePoint Online (SharePoint REST/CSOM) reaches every site, yet sharepoint_grants_held never sees that resource, so path 1 is skipped and the app can read as no_access. Widening the tester is safe and is the first half of the seam the core docs describe; the converter is the second.
findings.proposal: Step 1 (S): add a `sharepoint_resource_roles(client)` sibling of mailbox_resource_roles that resolves both SP resources; in sharepoint_grants_held classify with is_sharepoint_orgwide_permission(Some(resource.app_id), value) and label the resource in the org-wide detail. Step 2 (M): extend convert_site_access_to_selected to strip org-wide grants on the SPO resource too and widen is_scopable_sharepoint_resource_permission per its own comment, with a CHANGELOG note since the audit fix gate widens.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: sharepoint_grants_held (permission_tester.rs:884-905) resolves roles via graph_role_index, which reads only the Microsoft Graph SP (graph_roles.rs:53-71), and classifies with the name-shaped is_sharepoint_orgwide, so an org-wide Sites.* grant on Office 365 SharePoint Online is never seen and path 1 (:1077-1089) is skipped for it; with no permission entry the app then reads `no_access` (:1091-1101). Core already exposes the resource-aware is_sharepoint_orgwide_permission accepting OFFICE365_SHAREPOINT_ONLINE_APP_ID (scoping.rs:366-376), and the converter's Graph-only limit is explicitly documented as a handler limitation with an invitation to widen (scoping.rs:378-404); the finding correctly leaves that gate alone for step 1. Nothing in test_site_access's doc (:1037-1041, 'An org-wide Sites.* … app-role grant reaches every resource') or sharepoint-selected.md describes the tester as Graph-only by design, so the read-only widening is a legitimate first half of the documented seam. Implementation note: mirror prefetch_ews_full_access_grants (audit.rs:1015-1021) — a tenant with no SPO-consenting app has no SP for that resource, which must read as an ordinary empty set, not a failure. Step 2 (converter strips SPO grants, gate widens, CHANGELOG note) is correctly scoped as M with a ranking-shift note per AGENTS.md.

findings.title: Claims codec mis-models transformation-sourced schema entries: emits TransformationID instead of ID and conflates both on read
findings.rationale: Graph's schema entry for a transformation-sourced claim carries TWO ids: its own `ID` (which `OutputClaims[].ClaimTypeReferenceId` joins to) and `TransformationID` (which names the transformation). The DTO has one `id`, the writer emits it under `TransformationID` and omits `ID`, so every transformation policy this editor writes has an output claim with nothing to join to (the claim is never emitted). Worse, `parse_schema_entry` reads `ID` first, then `TransformationID`, into the single `id`; an existing Graph policy `{"Source":"transformation","ID":"DataJoin","TransformationID":"JoinTheData"}` parses as id="DataJoin", loses the transformation reference, and "Save claims" rewrites it as `TransformationID:"DataJoin"` — pointing at a transformation that does not exist. The round-trip test `claims_policy_round_trips_transformation` masks this by using the same string for the schema id, the transformation id and the output ClaimTypeReferenceId. Graph's own example additionally carries `"DataType":"string"` on InputParameters, which `TransformParamDto` drops on round-trip.
findings.proposal: Add `transformation_id: Option<String>` to `ClaimSchemaEntryDto`; in `build_schema_entry` always emit `ID` from `id` and emit `TransformationID` from `transformation_id` when set; in `parse_schema_entry` read `ID` and `TransformationID`/`TransformationId` into their own fields. Add `data_type: Option<String>` to `TransformParamDto` and round-trip it. Replace the masking test with one that uses Graph's documented shape (schema ID "DataJoin", TransformationID "JoinTheData", OutputClaims ClaimTypeReferenceId "DataJoin") and asserts both keys survive parse→build. Fix the DTO doc comments at sso.rs:21/33/91 and the ClaimsEditor to expose the extra field.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sso/claims.rs:46-53 emits the single DTO `id` under `TransformationID` (and omits `ID`) when source==transformation; claims.rs:204 reads `ID` then `TransformationID` into that one field. Microsoft's claims-customization-powershell example is `{"Source":"transformation","ID":"DataJoin","TransformationId":"JoinTheData","JwtClaimType":"JoinedData"}` with `OutputClaims[].ClaimTypeReferenceId == "DataJoin"`, and reference-claims-customization states OutputClaims join on the schema entry's ID while TransformationID names the transformation — so a policy written by this codec has no schema ID for the output claim to join to, and an existing policy parses `ID` and drops the transformation reference, then re-saves it as `TransformationID:"DataJoin"`. The round-trip test claims.rs:411-458 uses one string for schema id, transformation id and ClaimTypeReferenceId, masking it. Graph's claimsMappingPolicy resource example carries `"DataType":"string"` on InputParameters, which TransformParamDto (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sso.rs:69-74 / claims.rs:91,240-243) drops. Two extra tolerances worth adding on read: Microsoft's example uses `TransformationId` casing (the parser reads only `TransformationID`) and the PowerShell page uses a `ClaimsTransformations` (plural) top-level key. No doc/comment argues for the current shape; sso.rs:20-21,32-33,91 restate the wrong model. High is honest: every transformation claim the editor writes is never emitted, and Save corrupts existing policies.
findings.recheck_notes: Confirmed end to end; could not refute. (1) Documented shape: Microsoft Learn (reference-claims-customization; claims-customization-powershell example) shows a transformation-sourced schema entry carrying BOTH keys: {"Source":"transformation","ID":"DataJoin","TransformationId":"JoinTheData","JwtClaimType":"JoinedData"}, with OutputClaims[].ClaimTypeReferenceId="DataJoin" joined to the entry's ID. (2) Writer: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sso/claims.rs:46-53 emits only TransformationID for source=="transformation" and never ID; apply_claims_policy (commands/sso/mod.rs:108-124) passes the string unmodified to GraphClient::create_claims_mapping_policy (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/policies.rs:7-21), which POSTs it verbatim — no validation or repair anywhere. Reachable in the shipped build via set_claims_mapping (mod.rs:1627-1660, registered in src-tauri/src/lib.rs:192) and create_saml_sso_application (mod.rs:250-252). (3) Reader: claims.rs:204 str_field(obj,&["ID","TransformationID"]) reads ID first, so Microsoft's own example parses as id="DataJoin" and the transformation reference is lost; the TransformationId casing Microsoft's example uses is not read at all. get_sso_config (mod.rs:498-506) feeds this into the editor (web-rs/src/components/claims_editor.rs:199 binds e.id to the single `attribute` field; :320 writes it back), so the UI cannot represent both values. set_claims_mapping then detaches the existing correct policy (mod.rs:1642-1652) and assigns a rewritten one whose entry references a transformation that does not exist — a silent, data-destroying save of a policy the operator never edited. (4) Masking test: claims.rs:411-458 uses one string for the schema id, transformation id and OutputClaims reference and asserts entry.get("ID").is_none(), pinning the wrong behaviour; no repo_invariants test covers the codec. (5) DataType: the Graph claimsMappingPolicy resource example does carry "DataType":"string" on InputParameters and TransformParamDto (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sso.rs:69-74) drops it, but the reference page lists only ID/Value for InputParameters, so this part is a lossy-round-trip nit rather than the core defect. Severity stays high: not a security exposure, but a correctness bug on a security-critical SSO surface that both writes unusable transformation policies and corrupts existing correct ones on a no-op save.

findings.title: set_claims_mapping leaks one orphan claimsMappingPolicy per save and swallows the listing error
findings.rationale: `remove_claims_mapping_policy` is a `$ref` DELETE — it unassigns but never deletes the tenant-level `claimsMappingPolicy` object, and every save then POSTs a fresh one via `apply_claims_policy`. A tenant accumulates one orphan under `/policies/claimsMappingPolicies` per "Save claims" click, forever, with the operator's display name on each. The comment's premise ("effectively replace-only") is wrong: Graph documents Update (PATCH) for claimsMappingPolicy, so the existing policy's `definition` can be replaced in place — no detach→assign window during which tokens carry default claims either. Separately, `if let Ok(existing)` turns a transient listing failure into an attempt to assign a second policy, which Graph rejects (one per SP) with an opaque 400.
findings.proposal: Add `update_claims_mapping_policy(id, definition_json)` (PATCH /policies/claimsMappingPolicies/{id}) and `delete_claims_mapping_policy(id)` to crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/policies.rs. In `set_claims_mapping` (sso/mod.rs:1628-1664): propagate the listing error with `?` instead of `if let Ok`. When exactly one policy is assigned, read its `appliesTo` (or count assignments) first: PATCH its definition in place only if this SP is its sole subject; if the policy is shared with other SPs, fall back to unassign + create + assign (editing a shared policy in place would change claims for every other app). When the new policy is empty, unassign then DELETE the old policy only if `appliesTo` is now empty. Also apply the same ownership check before deleting in the create flow's failure path. CHANGELOG entry for the removed orphan accumulation.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise confirmed: sso/mod.rs:1642-1650 calls `remove_claims_mapping_policy`, which is a `$ref` DELETE (policies.rs:60-72, unassign only); `apply_claims_policy` (mod.rs:104-121) then POSTs a fresh policy on every save, and policies.rs exposes only create/assign/list/remove — no update or delete. Microsoft's claimsMappingPolicy resource page lists Update and Delete methods, so the docstring's "effectively replace-only" (mod.rs:1623-1624) is wrong, and docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md:89 records no rationale for orphaning. `if let Ok(existing)` at mod.rs:1643 does swallow a transient listing failure and proceeds to assign a second policy. What the proposal missed: Microsoft documents that one claims-mapping policy may be assigned to multiple service principals, so an unconditional PATCH-in-place would silently alter other apps' claims — the in-place path needs an `appliesTo` guard (the reviewer only mentioned it for DELETE). Medium is fair.

findings.title: Managed-identity Azure RBAC view duplicates management-group-inherited assignments once per subscription
findings.rationale: The per-subscription `principalId eq` query returns assignments ABOVE the subscription too (management group / root). The command fans out over every reachable subscription and flattens without deduplicating, so a managed identity holding Reader at a management group over N subscriptions renders N identical rows (same `RoleAssignment.id`, same scope), each tagged with a different subscription display name. `scope_level` explicitly classifies "Management group" scopes, so these rows are expected output — and they are wrong by a factor of N. For an operator reviewing MI privilege this both inflates the count and hides the fact that it is a single inherited grant.
findings.proposal: Dedupe `flat` by `RoleAssignment.id` (fall back to `(scope, role_definition_id, principal_id)` when id is None) with a `HashSet` before role-name resolution; for an assignment whose scope is above the subscription, label `subscription` as "(inherited)" or the MG name rather than the first subscription that happened to return it. Extract a pure `dedupe_assignments(Vec<(String, RoleAssignment)>) -> Vec<(String, RoleAssignment)>` and unit-test with one MG assignment returned by two subscriptions.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/managed_identity.rs:213-258 fans out `list_role_assignments_for_principal` per subscription and flattens with no dedupe; there is no HashSet on assignment id anywhere (the only HashSet in managed_identity_detail_pane.rs:115 tracks visited tabs). crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/client.rs:55-57 says 'at or below', but Microsoft's Role Assignments API doc says `$filter=principalId eq {id}` returns assignments 'at, above or below the scope' — so a management-group (or root) assignment is returned once per subscription queried. `scope_level` (managed_identity.rs:420-424) explicitly labels 'Management group', confirming such rows are expected output, yet each is tagged with whichever subscription returned it. `RoleAssignment.id` is `Option<String>` (arm/src/models.rs:73-77) so the proposed fallback key is needed. No doc or comment treats the duplication as deliberate. Medium is fair for an N-fold inflated privilege view.

findings.title: AzureRolesResult.scanned is a constant alias of total; the DTO doc and the UI's "(capped)" branch are dead
findings.rationale: The cap was removed but the field survived as `scanned = total`. The DTO doc still says "(capped for safety)", and the frontend keeps a message branch ("scanned X of Y subscriptions (capped)") that can never fire. A reader of either side is told a coverage guarantee that no longer exists in the code. Since a subscription whose lookup failed is counted in `skipped`, "scanned" as a distinct number is simply `total - skipped`.
findings.proposal: Either drop `scanned` from `AzureRolesResult` (DTO + `managed_identity_detail_pane.rs` + `ipc_mock/fixtures.rs`; it is a wire-format change so note it) and let the UI render only `skipped`/`total`, or set `scanned = total - skipped`, fix the DTO doc to "subscriptions whose role-assignment lookup succeeded", and reword the UI branch. Add a one-line unit test pinning `scanned + skipped == total`.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real. managed_identity.rs:211-219 sets `let scanned = total;` with a comment admitting the cap was removed; crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/managed_identity.rs:100-103 still documents `scanned` as '(capped for safety)' and `total` as '(before the cap)'; apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/managed_identity_detail_pane.rs:414-422 keeps the `res.scanned < res.total` branch and the '(capped)' message that can never fire. Fixture at ipc_mock/fixtures.rs:1514 sets `scanned: 2`. The proposal (drop the field or redefine as total - skipped, fix doc + UI branch, pin `scanned + skipped == total`) is sound. Severity downgraded to low: it is a stale doc and a dead UI branch with no wrong behaviour at runtime.

findings.title: OIDC create leaves the client-secret lifetime unbounded, unlike the SAML cert lifetime and the rotation path
findings.rationale: `secret_lifetime_days` is caller-supplied and reaches `add_password` unchecked: `0` mints a secret that is already expired when the summary shows it; an absurd value hits Graph's rejection only AFTER `instantiate_application_template` has created the app+SP, producing exactly the half-configured app the SAML path pre-validates `cert_lifetime_days` to avoid. The sibling `rotate_app_credential` clamps to 1..=730, so the same concept has two policies in the same crate.
findings.proposal: Add `resolve_secret_lifetime_days(Option<u32>) -> Result<u32, UiError>` (typed `invalid_secret_lifetime`, bounds 1..=730 shared as a `core` constant with `keyvault.rs`), call it in `create_oidc_sso_application` before `instantiate_application_template`, and reuse the value in `configure_oidc`. One table test mirroring `a_signing_certificate_lifetime_is_bounded_by_entras_three_year_ceiling`.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real and the failure mode is worse than stated. sso/mod.rs:351-358 takes `input.secret_lifetime_days.unwrap_or(180)` with no bounds, while the SAML path gates `cert_lifetime_days` via `resolve_cert_lifetime_days` before instantiate (mod.rs:149-152, 415-427) and keyvault.rs:85 clamps 1..=730 — two policies for one concept. The wizard field is a free-text `<Input value=secret_days />` parsed as u32 (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/dialogs/sso_wizard_dialog.rs:58,195,319) with no min/max. Downstream, `GraphClient::add_password` (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/credentials.rs:38-39) computes `chrono::Utc::now() + chrono::Duration::from_std(lifetime)`; for u32::MAX days (~11.7M years) that addition overflows chrono's date range and panics rather than returning a Graph 400 — inside the command, after `instantiate_application_template` has already created the app+SP. `0` yields an already-expired secret. Proposal (shared typed bound, checked before instantiate, reused in `configure_oidc`, table test) is consistent with the existing SAML pattern. Medium is fair.

findings.title: SAML create silently drops a failed claims policy or notification-email step; the wizard shows an unqualified success
findings.rationale: Degrading rather than failing is a documented decision, but the degradation is invisible: `SamlSsoSummary.claims_policy_id` is `None` on failure and nothing in the frontend reads it, so an operator who filled in the Attributes & claims step sees the same success screen as one who did not, and discovers the missing claims at the first federated sign-in. The same applies to notification emails (the "nobody is warned" column on the expiry board). `RotateCredentialResult.warnings` already establishes the pattern for exactly this situation.
findings.proposal: Add `#[serde(default)] pub warnings: Vec<String>` to `SamlSsoSummary`; in `configure_saml` push a human message on each degraded step ("Custom claims were not applied: <err>; open the SSO tab → Save claims to retry" / "Notification emails were not saved: <err>"). Render a warn `Callout` in `components/sso_summary.rs` when non-empty, and add a fixture with a warning so the GUI test covers it.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real. sso/mod.rs:240-244 and 254-267 log-and-continue on notification-email and claims-policy failures; `SamlSsoSummary` (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sso.rs:201-225) has no `warnings` field, and a grep of apps/desktop/web-rs/src for `claims_policy_id`/`claimsPolicyId` outside ipc_mock returns nothing — `components/sso_summary.rs` never mentions claims, warnings or a Callout. So an operator who filled in claims sees the same success screen whether or not the policy landed. Degrading is documented as deliberate (mod.rs:254-256) but the invisibility is not. `RotateCredentialResult.warnings` (dto/keyvault.rs:149) is the established precedent and `Callout` is a listed UI primitive. Medium is fair.

findings.title: Split sso/mod.rs (2349 lines) by concern: create, validate, config, rollover, board, metadata
findings.evidence:
sso/mod.rs section markers as they stand:
  46:  // ---------------- helpers ----------------
 124:  // ---------------- create ----------------
 449:  // ---------------- read / edit (detail tab) ----------------
 754:  // ---------------- staged rollover ----------------
 982:  pub async fn list_sso_certificate_expirations(
1279:  fn metadata_http_client() -> &'static reqwest::Client {
1309:  fn element_open_at(xml: &str, local: &str, at: usize) -> bool {
1458:  fn build_rollover(
1783:  mod tests {   (566 lines of tests spanning all six concerns)
claims.rs header: "Self contained — it never touches Graph or `State`, so it lives apart from the SSO orchestration in `super`" — the same argument applies to the metadata parser and the rollover projection.
findings.rationale: One file holds six independent concerns — wizard orchestration, input validation, the detail-tab config CRUD, the rollover state machine, the tenant-wide expiry board, and a hand-rolled XML scanner — plus ~570 lines of tests. `claims.rs` was already extracted on exactly the "pure, State-free" rationale that applies to `build_rollover`+`is_preferred_key` and to `parse_signing_certs`+`element_open_at`. The mixing makes the load-bearing rollover code hard to review, and the file is the largest in `commands/` by a wide margin.
findings.proposal: `sso/mod.rs`: `mod` declarations, `pub use` re-exports of every `#[tauri::command]` (so `lib.rs` `generate_handler!` paths stay unchanged), `CUSTOM_TEMPLATE_ID`, `LOGIN_HOST`, `saml_summary_urls`, `oidc_summary_urls`. `sso/create.rs`: `create_saml_sso_application`, `configure_saml`, `create_oidc_sso_application`, `configure_oidc`, `with_replication_retry`, `augment_with_object_id`, `apply_claims_policy`. `sso/validate.rs`: `validate_cert_subject`, `resolve_cert_lifetime_days`, the two lifetime consts, `sanitize_notification_emails`, `invalid_redirect_uri` + their tests. `sso/config.rs`: `get_sso_config`, `extract_sp_sso_fields`, `extract_app_sso_fields`, `set_sso_mode`, `set_saml_urls`, `set_oidc_redirect_uris`, `set_notification_emails`, `set_claims_mapping`, `get_sso_summary`. `sso/rollover.rs`: `build_rollover`, `canonical_thumbprint`, `is_preferred_key`, `get_signing_cert_rollover`, stage/activate/revert/retire/rotate, `set_preferred_signing_key`, `mint_signing_certificate`, `stage_if_not_already` + the rollover tests. `sso/board.rs`: `list_sso_certificate_expirations`, `save_sso_certificates_to_file`, `sso_certificates_to_csv`, `sso_cert_status`, `sso_certificate_expirations_key`, both `invalidate_sso_cert_board*`. `sso/metadata.rs`: `probe_federation_metadata`, `metadata_http_client`, `element_open_at`, `find_element_open/close`, `parse_signing_certs` + parser tests. Update the `.claude/rules` pointer and the arch doc's "Commands live in commands/sso/mod.rs" line.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise real: sso/mod.rs is 2349 lines, the largest file under commands/ (next is audit.rs at 2011), with the six section markers at the cited lines and ~566 lines of tests spanning all concerns. The repo already applied exactly this rationale twice: claims.rs:1-8 ('never touches Graph or State, so it lives apart') and gallery.rs:5-11 (split out of enterprise_application.rs). `.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:15` requires domain subdirs to re-export flat so `commands::sso::name` paths stay stable — the proposal honours that. One correction to the proposal: `.claude/rules/auth.md:8` already scopes by the glob `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sso/**`, so no rules pointer needs updating; only docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md:159 ('Commands live in commands/sso/mod.rs') does. Severity adjusted to low: maintainability refactor with no defect.

findings.title: Rollover guard logic (five error codes) has no test coverage because it is only reachable through State-bound commands
findings.rationale: The arch doc calls these guards out by name ("refuses a thumbprint that is missing or expired; activating the already-active certificate is a no-op; retire refuses the active certificate ... and the staged one"), and the expired-but-still-nominated message variant is a deliberate UX decision — yet none of it is asserted. `build_rollover` is thoroughly table-tested; the decisions layered on top of it are not, so a refactor could swap `cert_is_active`/`cert_is_staged`, drop the idempotent activate, or invert the expired check without a failing test.
findings.proposal: Extract two pure functions next to `build_rollover`: `retire_target<'a>(roll: &'a SigningCertRolloverDto, key_id: &str) -> Result<&'a SigningCertDto, UiError>` and `activation_target<'a>(roll: &'a SigningCertRolloverDto, thumbprint: &str) -> Result<Option<&'a SigningCertDto>, UiError>` (None = already active, no-op). Have `retire_saml_signing_certificate` and `set_preferred_signing_key` call them. Table-test every code and both `cert_is_active` messages using the existing `sp_with`/`cred` fixtures.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real. The five codes appear only at their definition sites (sso/mod.rs:936, 951, 955, 1248, 1254); a repo-wide grep including apps/desktop/web-rs/tests and web-rs/src finds no test or GUI-test reference. The expired-but-nominated message variant (mod.rs:941-950) and the idempotent activate (mod.rs:1258-1260) are documented behaviours in docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md yet unasserted, while `build_rollover` is table-tested extensively (mod.rs:1949-2130). Both guards are pure decisions over a `SigningCertRolloverDto` plus a key/thumbprint, so the proposed `retire_target`/`activation_target` extraction is straightforward and reuses the existing `sp_with`/`cred` fixtures. Medium kept: these guards are what stop an operator from deleting the certificate that signs assertions today.

findings.title: Conditional Access view ignores workload-identity targeting (conditions.clientApplications)
findings.rationale: Graph's `conditionalAccessConditionSet` also carries `clientApplications { includeServicePrincipals, excludeServicePrincipals, servicePrincipalFilter }` — workload-identity Conditional Access, which targets precisely the service principals this tool manages. The model omits it, so (a) a policy that blocks THIS app's SP is invisible if its `applications` condition names other resources, and (b) a workload-identity policy with the usual `applications.includeApplications=["All"]` is reported as "applies (all)" for every app in the tenant, whether or not its SP is the targeted client. For an app-registration/enterprise-app admin tool this is the most relevant CA dimension and it is currently mis-reported in both directions.
findings.proposal: Add `client_applications: Option<CaClientApplications>` (includeServicePrincipals / excludeServicePrincipals / servicePrincipalFilter) to `CaConditions` in crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/models.rs:614-617. Resolve the SP object id backend-side in `list_conditional_access_for_app` via the existing `get_service_principal_by_app_id` (the CA tab is mounted on the app-registration pane keyed only by appId — conditional_access_tab.rs:20-23, application_detail_pane.rs:257 — and the shared `ConditionalAccessPanel` takes only `app_id`), tolerating a missing SP by skipping the client-side check. In `applies_reason`, apply exclude-wins on `excludeServicePrincipals`, then require an SP match when `clientApplications` is present (`workloadIdentity` / `workloadIdentityAll` / `workloadIdentityFilter` codes) before falling back to the resource-side `applications` reasons. Extend the table tests, document the new codes on `ConditionalAccessPolicyDto.applies_reason`, and update the tab copy at conditional_access_tab.rs:58-60.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise real: `CaConditions` (models.rs:614-617) has only `applications`; conditional_access.rs:53-58 returns None when `applications` is absent and `applies_reason` (:73-116) evaluates only resource-side includes. A repo-wide grep for workload/clientApplications finds nothing in the CA path or docs, so this is an unaddressed gap, not a documented decision. The two mis-reporting directions follow from the code: a workload-identity policy with `includeApplications=["All"]` yields "all" for every app, and one whose `applications` names other resources is invisible for the targeted SP. Overstated detail: 'pass the SP object id in (the detail pane has it)' — the tab lives on the app-registration pane which only has appId, so the resolution belongs in the backend. Medium is fair for a feature gap that mis-reports in both directions.

findings.title: Key Vault rotation writes secret versions with no ownership tags and no collision check
findings.rationale: `set_secret` on an existing name silently appends a version. Nothing in the written version records which app registration, object id or `keyId` it belongs to, so (1) a typo or a shared secret name across two apps overwrites another app's live secret with no warning — consumers of the old value break at their next read — and (2) an operator auditing the vault later cannot tell which app a version was minted for. The tool already knows all three identifiers at this point and already persists the vault→app binding in `UserSettings`, so the information exists; it just is not written where the vault reader can see it.
findings.proposal: Populate `SecretSetRequest.tags` (`azapptoolkit-app-id`, `azapptoolkit-object-id`, `azapptoolkit-key-id`) and `content_type` in `rotate_app_credential` (keyvault.rs:117-122) via a pure, unit-tested builder. For the ownership check, do not call `get_secret` (it returns the secret value just to read tags); add a metadata-only `list_secret_versions(name)` (`GET /secrets/{name}/versions`, returns attributes + tags) to crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/client.rs and compare the latest version's `azapptoolkit-app-id` tag. Return `UiError::validation("secret_owned_by_other_app", …)` on mismatch; defer a `force` override until the rotation dialog grows a control for it (RotateCredentialInput has no such field today).
findings.verifier_notes: Premise real: keyvault.rs:117-122 sets `tags: None, content_type: None`; `SecretSetRequest` supports both (crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/models.rs:72-80); the vault→app binding is persisted only in UserSettings (keyvault.rs:155-175), invisible to a vault reader. Proposal adjustments: the KV client exposes only `list_secrets`/`get_secret`/`set_secret` (client.rs:72-102), so the collision check needs a new metadata-only versions call rather than reading the live value, and `input.force` does not exist in `RotateCredentialInput` (dto/keyvault.rs:125-138). Severity downgraded to low: it is an enhancement; the hazard requires an operator to type another app's secret name, and tagging alone is cheap and safe.

findings.title: assign_managed_identity_azure_role never busts the Key Vault access sweep cache
findings.rationale: The sweep result is cached for the 60-minute Audit TTL and is the answer to "who can touch this vault?". A role assigned by this very app at a `/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/...` scope changes that answer, but `get_cached_key_vault_access` keeps serving the pre-assignment sweep until TTL — contradicting the repo's invalidate-on-Ok rule and the sweep's own "coverage is never overstated" stance.
findings.proposal: Make `kv_sweep_cache_key` `pub(crate)` (keyvault_rbac.rs:55) and, on the `Ok` path of `assign_managed_identity_azure_role` (managed_identity.rs:389-419), invalidate `CacheKind::Audit` / `kv_sweep_cache_key(&tenant_id)` unconditionally rather than only when the scope string contains a vault path: the sweep's rows keep `props.scope` (keyvault_rbac.rs:268) from an `atScope()` query, and per Microsoft's Role Assignments docs `atScope()` returns assignments at or above the scope, so an RG- or subscription-level assignment also changes the vault answer. The key is one per tenant and only re-filled by an explicit sweep, so an unconditional bust costs nothing. Add the pairing to repo_invariants/cache.rs.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise confirmed: `assign_managed_identity_azure_role` ends with `Ok(())` and no cache call; `kv_sweep_cache_key` is private and referenced only in keyvault_rbac.rs (:55, :320, :368, :480); no repo_invariants file mentions the command or the key; the frontend lets an operator type any `/subscriptions/...` scope (managed_identity_detail_pane.rs:538). The sweep result is cached for the Audit TTL (keyvault_rbac.rs:320) and `get_cached_key_vault_access` serves it (:358-370), so the pre-assignment answer is served until TTL — contradicting invalidate-on-Ok. Overstated part: the vault-path-only condition is too narrow given the sweep retains inherited scopes (and the ARM client's own comment at client.rs:90-94 that atScope() excludes ancestors disagrees with Microsoft's documentation). Low is fair.

findings.title: set_sso_mode / get_sso_summary are stringly typed and an unrecognised mode silently disables SSO
findings.rationale: Three string protocols (`mode`, `protocol`, `SsoConfigDto.sso_mode`) are matched by literal in both trees, and the backend's catch-all turns a casing slip ("SAML") or a future value ("password") into a destructive PATCH that clears SSO. `get_sso_summary` returns untagged `serde_json::Value` that the frontend re-branches on the same string. The repo's own convention (`CertStatus`, `RolloverPhase`) is a serde enum in `dto/sso.rs`.
findings.proposal: Add `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")] enum SsoMode { Saml, Oidc, Disabled }` to `dto/sso.rs`; take it in `set_sso_mode` and `get_sso_summary` (unknown values then fail deserialization instead of clearing SSO); return `enum SsoSummary { Saml(SamlSsoSummary), Oidc(OidcSsoSummary) }` with `#[serde(tag = "protocol")]`. Update `bindings/sso.rs` (whose doc still says `""` disables) and the `<select>` in `sso_tab.rs`.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real. sso/mod.rs:642-647 matches `mode.as_str()` and maps anything else to `Null`, so a casing slip or a future value is a destructive PATCH clearing SSO; mod.rs:1745 branches `get_sso_summary` on `protocol == "oidc"` and returns untagged `serde_json::Value`; the frontend re-derives the same literals (sso_tab.rs:503-521, 695-702) and bindings/sso.rs:68-69 documents 'anything else (e.g. "") to disable SSO'. The repo convention for exactly this is a serde enum in dto/sso.rs (`CertStatus`, `RolloverPhase` at sso.rs:309-342). Wire-compatible since the values stay lowercase strings; `#[serde(tag = "protocol")]` for the summary is a wire change the frontend consumes from the same DTO crate. Low is fair.

findings.title: set_sso_mode docstring says "No cache bust" while the body busts the expiry board
findings.rationale: The docstring was written before the expiry board existed and now states the opposite of both the code and the architecture doc. A reader trusting the docstring could remove the bust as "unnecessary".
findings.proposal: Replace the two docstring lines with: "Busts only the SSO-certificate expiry board (`invalidate_sso_cert_board`): the mode decides whether the app is on the board at all. The SSO tab reads the mode live and no other cached payload carries it."
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real and unambiguous. sso/mod.rs:633-634 says 'No cache bust' while the body at 652-655 calls `invalidate_sso_cert_board`, and docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md:306-307 plus the helper's own doc (mod.rs:1122-1126) say `set_sso_mode` must bust the board. The docstring is simply stale. Proposed wording is accurate. Low.

findings.title: Inconsistent not-found wire codes: two SSO sites emit a bare `not_found`, and three other sites double the suffix via the factory
findings.rationale: The same condition (SP vanished between list and detail) reaches the frontend as code `not_found` from the SSO tab and `service_principal_not_found` from the enterprise-app detail. The factory exists precisely to keep `_not_found` codes uniform; the two SSO sites predate or bypass it. Harmless today (the frontend does not branch on it) but it is the kind of drift that breaks a future `ends_with("_not_found")` handler.
findings.proposal: Replace sso/mod.rs:471 and :769 with `UiError::not_found("service_principal", "Service principal not found.")`. Also fix the three misuses of the factory that produce doubled codes: exchange/aap_migration.rs:175 (`not_found("service_principal_not_found", …)` → `service_principal_not_found_not_found`), aap_migration.rs:196 (`scope_group_not_found`) and exchange/scope_group.rs:412 (`group_not_found`) — pass the bare resource. Add a repo_invariants scan rejecting both `UiError::validation("not_found"` / `validation("*_not_found"` and `UiError::not_found("*_not_found"`.
findings.verifier_notes: Both SSO sites are as cited and are the only bare `not_found` codes in the tree; `UiError::not_found` (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/lib.rs:63-65) formats `{resource}_not_found` and is used at 18 sites. Overstated: 'every other command uses UiError::not_found(resource)' — three sites (exchange/aap_migration.rs:175,196; exchange/scope_group.rs:412) pass an already-suffixed code into the factory, yielding `*_not_found_not_found` on the wire, so the drift is broader than the SSO pair and the proposed invariant scan is well motivated. Frontend does not branch on these codes today, so low is honest.

findings.title: active_thumbprint (and the board's Thumbprint column) bypass core::thumbprint::canonical
findings.evidence:
sso/mod.rs:1478-1481

        .get("preferredTokenSigningKeyThumbprint")
        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
        .map(str::to_string);
sso/mod.rs:1616

sso/mod.rs:1027

apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/sso_certificates_dashboard.rs:201-204

docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md: "`azapptoolkit-core::thumbprint::canonical` is the **single** converter ... every display and every comparison in both trees goes through it"
findings.rationale: `certs[].thumbprint` is canonical uppercase hex, but `active_thumbprint` is the raw `preferredTokenSigningKeyThumbprint` — which the same doc notes "can differ in case" — and it is what the expiry board prints as the app's thumbprint. On a tenant with a lowercase preferred value the board shows a lowercase string beside the SSO tab's uppercase one for the same certificate, which is exactly the operator confusion the canonical rule exists to prevent.
findings.proposal: In `build_rollover`: `active_thumbprint: preferred.as_deref().and_then(canonical_thumbprint).or(preferred)` (keep the raw value only when it cannot be normalised, so an unparseable nomination is still visible). Extend `rollover_matches_the_preferred_thumbprint_case_insensitively_and_sorts_newest_first` to assert `roll.active_thumbprint == Some(B_HEX)` for the lowercase input.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real. `build_rollover` reads `preferredTokenSigningKeyThumbprint` raw (sso/mod.rs:1478-1481) and stores it unchanged as `active_thumbprint` (:1616), while each `certs[].thumbprint` goes through `canonical_thumbprint` (:1497-1502). The board copies it as the row's `thumbprint` (:1027) and sso_certificates_dashboard.rs:201-204 prints it; the SSO tab prints the canonical `c.thumbprint` (sso_tab.rs:311). docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md:174 and :224-226 state the preferred field can differ in case and that `canonical` is the single converter for every display and comparison. The DTO doc 'as Entra has it, expired or not' (dto/sso.rs:382) is about nomination-regardless-of-expiry, not a casing decision. Proposed `.and_then(canonical_thumbprint).or(preferred)` keeps an unparseable value visible; the cited test already has the lowercase fixture to extend. Low.

findings.title: with_replication_retry skips steps 4 and 5 of the SAML create flow
findings.rationale: Steps 2, 3 and 5b are wrapped against the post-instantiate replication 404, but the two writes between them — the certificate POST and the activation PATCH, both against the same freshly created SP — are not. Graph front-doors are not sticky, so a request routed to a lagging replica at step 4 fails with NotFound and leaves the half-configured app the retry exists to prevent, while the cheaper best-effort step right after it would have retried.
findings.proposal: Wrap both: `with_replication_retry(|| client.add_token_signing_certificate(sp_id, &subject, end)).await?` and the step-5 PATCH. Both closures are `FnMut() -> Fut` over borrowed data, so no restructuring is needed.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real. sso/mod.rs:207-236: steps 2, 3 (and 5b at :240-241) are wrapped in `with_replication_retry`, while `add_token_signing_certificate` (:221-223) and the activation PATCH (:226-234) against the same fresh SP are not; the module doc (:12-14) states the PATCH steps after instantiate are wrapped, so the omission reads as an oversight, not a decision. Both closures are feasible as `FnMut() -> Fut` over borrowed data (`end` is `Copy`, `subject` borrowed; build the patch body once). Retrying a POST on NotFound is safe because NotFound means nothing was created. Mitigating: step 2 has already succeeded against the SP by step 4, so the window is narrower than for step 2 itself — low is right.

findings.title: IPC parity (generate_handler ↔ #[tauri::command] ↔ bindings) has no CI pin — only an advisory hook that always exits 0 and needs jq
findings.evidence:

if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then

apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/repo_invariants/sources.rs:133  pub(crate) fn commands() -> Vec<Command>  (already extracts every handler by name)
findings.rationale: A command missing from `generate_handler![]`, a binding whose invoke string is misspelt, or an arg-struct field that does not match the command's parameter name compiles fine on both sides and fails only at runtime with an opaque IPC error; the GUI tests mock IPC so they cannot catch it either. The hook fires only for Claude Code Write/Edit tool calls, never for `sed`/other agents/humans, and is skipped without jq. A prototype scan over the real tree (186 commands: registered 186, bound 186, every arg struct's fields == command params, every return `T` equal) shows the check is mechanical and would pass today.
findings.proposal: Add `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/repo_invariants/ipc.rs` reusing `sources::commands()`: (1) every command name appears once in `lib.rs`'s `generate_handler![]` and vice versa; (2) every command name appears as a `"name"` literal in `web-rs/src/bindings/*.rs` and every invoke literal names a command; (3) for each `invoke*("name", Struct { .. })` the struct's field names (from the same file or `common.rs`) equal the command's non-`State`/`AppHandle` parameter names and the struct carries `rename_all = "camelCase"` whenever a field has an underscore; (4) the enclosing binding fn's `Result<T, UiError>` `T` matches the command's after stripping paths. Include vacuity floors (`>= 150` commands). Keep the hook as the fast local escort.
findings.verifier_notes: No mechanical pin exists: `grep generate_handler|bindings` over apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/repo_invariants/*.rs and `grep src-tauri` over apps/desktop/web-rs/tests/ both return nothing; demo_fixture_coverage.rs only checks infallible invokes against demo fixtures. The hook (.claude/hooks/command-parity-check.sh:15 `exit 0 always`, :23-26 silent skip without jq) is registered only as a PostToolUse hook in .claude/settings.json:19, and ci.yml:217-223 explicitly says nothing in CI runs it beyond shellcheck. I re-derived the reviewer's numbers: 186 `#[tauri::command]` fns, 186 `generate_handler![]` entries, 0 declared commands without a `"name"` literal under web-rs/src/bindings/, and the only unmatched snake_case literals in bindings are feature names (`arm`, `oidc`, `saml`, `write`, ...), so the check is mechanical and green today. `sources::commands()` (repo_invariants/sources.rs:133) already extracts every handler by name. Parts (3)/(4) of the proposal (arg-struct fields vs params, return types) need param-list parsing and common.rs resolution, so effort M is honest.

Dead secret-bearing types are still surface area an audit has to reason about.

findings.title: `ManagedIdentityBackup.azure_roles` / `azure_role_coverage` are never populated; backup-and-restore.md:89 and the DTO field doc claim an ARM scan that pass 3 deliberately skips
findings.rationale: Every MI in every manifest is written as `"azureRoles": [], "azureRoleCoverage": null`. The field doc says an empty list means "the ARM scan was unavailable", the schema bullet at doc line 89 says RBAC is captured with coverage, while lines 115-116 and 207 say it is deliberately not scanned. A DR reader (or a future restore) has no way to tell "never scanned" from "scanned, held nothing" except by reading the source. The app already has the scan (`list_managed_identity_azure_roles`, commands/managed_identity.rs:194), so this is one seam from real.
findings.proposal: Decide once: (a) remove the two fields plus `AzureRoleRef`/`AzureRoleCoverage` and fix doc line 89 (S); or (b) populate them from `list_managed_identity_azure_roles`'s core under the ARM token in pass 3 and have restore list unresolved roles as `ManualItem`s (M). Either way reword dto/backup.rs:238-239 so 'empty' is not described as 'scan unavailable' (that is what `azure_role_coverage == None` already means) and make :89 agree with :115-116/:207.
findings.verifier_notes: The dead-field premise holds: commands/backup.rs:734-742 builds `ManagedIdentityBackup` with `..Default::default()`, and `AzureRoleRef`/`AzureRoleCoverage` (dto/backup.rs:322, :338) have zero references outside the DTO crate. docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:89 ('+ Azure RBAC assignments (with scan-coverage)') contradicts :115-116 and :207 ('deliberately does not scan Azure RBAC'), and the field doc at dto/backup.rs:238-239 ('empty when the ARM scan was unavailable') is misleading. Overstated: 'a DR reader has no way to tell never-scanned from scanned-empty' — `azureRoleCoverage: null` is exactly that tell, and the DTO doc at :242-243 says so ('so an incomplete scan never reads as this MI holds no Azure roles'). Severity low: a doc/DTO inconsistency, no data loss (restore never reads the fields).

Medium is fair for a create-without-delete asymmetry on a permission grant.

findings.title: Closed-set wire fields typed as `String` where the crate already uses serde enums elsewhere
findings.rationale: Each of these is a documented closed vocabulary matched by string literals on the frontend with a silent `_ =>` fallback, so a typo or rename on either side degrades to "Unknown"/"not migrated" at runtime instead of failing to compile. The crate shows the intended pattern already (`CertStatus`, `RolloverPhase`, `readiness::Verdict`, `AuditCoverageGap` with `#[serde(other)]`, `PermissionKind`), and the wire format need not change: `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` reproduces the current strings.
findings.proposal: Introduce enums (`TestVerdict`, `BulkCreateStatus`, `AapMigrationStatus`, `OwnerChangeAction`, `SkippedObjectKind`, `AppRolesTarget`, `RiskLevel`, `ScopeConsentType`, `CaAppliesReason`) with the matching `rename_all` and `#[serde(other)] Unknown` where the producer set may grow; replace the frontend `match` on literals with `match` on variants (the compiler then flags every consumer). Start with the two `verdict` fields and the two `status` fields, which have the most literal consumers.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified for every cited field: permission_tester.rs:17-19 `verdict: String` documented as a closed set; bulk.rs:124-126 `status`; exchange.rs:204 `status` ('planned/migrated/partial/failed'); applications.rs:281 `action`; backup.rs:79 `kind`; enterprise_application.rs:110 `target_kind`; consent.rs:18 `risk`; expose_api.rs:30 `scope_type`; conditional_access.rs:21 `applies_reason`. Frontend matches on literals with silent fallbacks (resource_access/mod.rs:84-89 and :98-100, permission_tester_view.rs:31-33, mailboxes.rs:37/129/276, migrate_legacy_scope.rs:84, aap_migration_report.rs:112, app_roles.rs:238, app_permission_grants_view.rs:49-120, bulk_actions_view.rs:89). No rationale for String is documented anywhere in the DTO crate, and the crate already uses serde enums for the same shape (`CertStatus` sso.rs:311, `RolloverPhase` :329, `readiness::Verdict`, `AuditCoverageGap` with `#[serde(other)]`, `PermissionKind`, `MiSubtype`). Wire-compat via `rename_all` holds; `SkippedObject.kind` and any persisted/cached payload need the `#[serde(other)]` variant the reviewer already calls for. Severity downgraded to low: no defect today, this is hardening.

findings.title: Backup manifest restates the `MiSubtype` and `CloudEnvironment` wire vocabularies as hand-written strings
findings.rationale: `MiSubtype`'s serde `rename_all = "camelCase"` already produces exactly `systemAssigned`/`userAssigned`/`unknown`, so `mi_subtype_wire_label` is a second definition of the same wire strings — the pattern AGENTS.md's "one definition per policy" exists to prevent. `TenantBackup.cloud` likewise round-trips `CloudEnvironment::as_str()` as a `String` and the restore compares strings.
findings.proposal: Type `ManagedIdentityBackup.subtype` as `MiSubtype` and delete `mi_subtype_wire_label`; type `TenantBackup.cloud` (and `CloudMismatch`'s two fields) as `azapptoolkit_core::cloud::CloudEnvironment` with a serde repr matching today's `as_str()` labels so existing manifests still parse. Bump nothing — the JSON is unchanged.
findings.verifier_notes: backup.rs:893-899 `mi_subtype_wire_label` restates exactly what `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` on `MiSubtype` (dto/managed_identity.rs:14-20) emits; its own doc admits 'matching its serde wire form'. There IS a unit test (backup.rs:980-989 `mi_subtype_label_matches_camel_case_wire_form`) the reviewer did not mention, but it pins hand-typed strings rather than comparing against `serde_json::to_string(&MiSubtype::X)`, so a rename on the enum would still drift silently — the test does not rescue the duplication. Cloud half: `TenantBackup.cloud: String` (dto/backup.rs:51) is filled from `state.auth.cloud().as_str()` (backup.rs:259) and string-compared in restore.rs:127. One extra step the proposal needs: `CloudEnvironment` has no serde derives (core/cloud.rs:15 derives only Debug/Clone/Copy/PartialEq/Eq/Default), so a `rename_all = "lowercase"` serde repr must be added (core already depends on serde, Cargo.toml:14). Bonus supporting evidence: dto/backup.rs:49 documents the labels as `Commercial`/`UsGov`/`UsGovDod`/`China`, but `as_str()` (cloud.rs:32-35) emits `commercial`/`usgov`/`usgovdod`/`china` — the doc is already wrong. Low severity, no runtime bug.

findings.title: Trust/redirect validation rules check the validator at module granularity, not per command — the helper-bleed the suite was rewritten to remove
findings.rationale: `src` here is the whole module. `sso/mod.rs` already contains `validate_redirect_uri`, so a 19th command there that builds `ApplicationWebPatch {` straight from its input passes this rule; likewise a new command in `applications/federated.rs` constructing `FederatedCredentialRequest {` passes because the module imports the validator for its siblings. That is exactly the gap the rule's own doc describes ("the interactive editor and the DR restore had drifted apart") — it will not catch the next drift if it happens inside an existing module. The cache, cancel and fanout rules already scan per `Command.body`.
findings.proposal: Rewrite both rules over `super::sources::commands()`: for each command whose body contains a `TRUST_WRITES`/`REDIRECT_WRITES` literal, require the validator name (or the module-local wrapper: `check_federated_credential(` / `checked_uris(`) inside that body, resolving one level of local helper by name when the write itself sits in a helper (walk the helper's brace-balanced body with `balanced_block`). Keep the `found >= 2` floors.
findings.verifier_notes: Both rules iterate `command_modules()` and test `src.contains(VALIDATOR)` where `src` is the whole module (trust.rs:32-43 and :91-102), while the cache (cache.rs:485), cancel (cancel.rs:42, :103) and fan-out (fanout.rs:63) rules already scan per `sources::commands()` body — the exact bleed sources.rs:123-131 documents. Per-module write sites (excluding `//` lines): authentication.rs 3, federated.rs 2, restore.rs 4, sso/mod.rs 6 (reviewer's counts differ slightly but the shape holds); sso/mod.rs (18 commands) and restore.rs already contain the validator name, so any new unvalidated writer in those modules passes today. Feasibility caveat: writes and validators often sit in module-local helpers (`check_federated_credential` federated.rs:57, `checked_uris` restore.rs:65, sso/mod.rs:307/695/1712), so the per-command rewrite must resolve one helper level as the proposal says — effort is M rather than S. Medium is right: it is a security invariant whose pin is silently lenient.

findings.title: 'Every paged read sends `$top`' has no source-scanning pin, and two `collect_all_pages` callers already do not send it

crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/transport.rs:269-283

        &self,

(the first-page URL — where `$top` lives — is built by each caller)
crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client.rs:33-36

AGENTS.md:106  **Every paged read sends `$top`** (`client::MAX_PAGE_SIZE`; `/applications` sends `DEFAULT_APP_PAGE_SIZE`) — paging is serial.

The second rule over `$batch` sub-URLs in commands/ is a reasonable follow-up.

But the reviewer's inventory covers only the 6 `collect_pages_from` sites; `collect_all_pages` (transport.rs:171) has 11 more call sites (service_principals.rs:119/150/407, roles_grants.rs:63/86/184/204, credentials.rs:83, directory.rs:175, applications.rs:388/575) and two of them send no `$top` today: `list_federated_credentials` (credentials.rs:77-84, Graph caps FICs at 20/app) and `list_all_application_templates` (applications.rs:568-575, which uses `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=2800` by documented design). So the proposed test as written fails on day one, and AGENTS.md:106's 'every paged read sends `$top`' is itself slightly inaccurate. ... have a typed stub in `web-rs/src/bindings/` calling `invoke_result()` (never bare `invoke`, which panics on a rejected promise).

findings.title: Stale module headers and dead assertions in the invariants suite

Harmless, but this suite is the repo's stated source of truth for its rules and is read more than it is run.
findings.proposal: Delete the `stale` vec and its assertion and the `_handled_by_driver` line (fold its intent into the comment above); update the two headers ("seven concern modules"; move the "shared source table" phrase to `sources.rs`).

findings.title: `From<AuthError>` needs a wildcard arm because an internal crate's error enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so a new variant silently becomes `unknown_auth`
findings.rationale: `azapptoolkit-auth` is a workspace-internal, unpublished crate, so `#[non_exhaustive]` buys nothing except forcing the wildcard. Any future variant (e.g. a device-code or broker path) maps to `unknown_auth`, non-retryable and not re-auth-fatal, and the hand-listed test cannot notice because it only enumerates variants someone remembered to add — the same allowlist failure mode the invariants suite documents.
findings.proposal: Remove `#[non_exhaustive]` from `AuthError` and the `_ =>` arm; the match then fails to compile when a variant is added, and the code-map test remains the behavioural pin.
findings.verifier_notes: crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/error.rs:6 `#[non_exhaustive]` has no rationale comment, and the workspace sets `publish = false` (root Cargo.toml:22-23, 'Internal crates: this is a desktop app, not a published library set'), so the attribute only forces the `_ => ("unknown_auth", false)` arm at dto/lib.rs:173. The behavioural pin (dto/lib.rs:180-186 `auth_error_maps_to_stable_code_and_retryable`) is a hand-enumerated list. Removing the attribute makes the dto match exhaustive; token_adapter.rs:22-27 has a second match whose `_ => "token_error"` is a deliberate collapse of non-fatal variants and can keep its wildcard by intent. Low severity: no variant is missing today.

findings.title: Timestamps cross IPC as `DateTime<Utc>` in some DTOs and RFC3339 `String` in others, with no documented convention on either side
findings.evidence:
crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sso.rs:360-361
    pub start_date_time: Option<String>,
    pub end_date_time: Option<String>,
crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/audit.rs:564  pub completed_at: Option<String>,   (doc: "RFC3339 UTC")
crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/applications.rs:247  pub expires: String,   (doc: "RFC3339 certificate expiry")
vs
crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/credentials.rs:21-22
    pub start_date_time: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    pub end_date_time: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/backup.rs:44  pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
Also String: sso.rs:222,292,391,409,434,456; keyvault.rs:56,65,99,147; usage.rs:14; enterprise_application.rs:64; updater.rs:13.
findings.rationale: Same concept, two representations: consumers of the `String` fields re-parse (or string-compare) on the frontend, and a producer can emit a non-RFC3339 value with no type error. `chrono` is already a dependency of the crate and serializes to the same RFC3339 text, so the wire format would not change for well-formed values.
findings.proposal: Pick and document one convention in dto/lib.rs. If converging on `DateTime<Utc>`, use a tolerant `deserialize_with` (or `Option<DateTime<Utc>>` with a lenient adapter) for Graph-sourced fields so one malformed value cannot fail a whole payload, and fix util.rs:184's 'every backend DTO' claim; if converging on String, say so and keep `util::time_ago` as the single parse point. Do it module by module.
findings.verifier_notes: Inconsistency confirmed: `DateTime<Utc>` appears on 11 DTO lines (e.g. credentials.rs:21-22, backup.rs:44) and RFC3339 `String` on 12 (sso.rs:360-361, audit.rs:564, applications.rs:247, keyvault.rs:56/65, ...). Overstated on the cost side and silent on the trade-off: the frontend has a single parse point, `util::time_ago(rfc3339: &str)` (util.rs:184-190), whose doc explicitly chooses per-field tolerance ('a stamp we can't read → render nothing'), whereas a `DateTime<Utc>` field makes one odd Graph timestamp fail deserialization of the entire payload. That doc also claims 'as every backend DTO carries one', which is itself inaccurate given the mixed state. No rationale is written down in the DTO crate either way, so the real defect is an undocumented split convention rather than the String fields per se.

findings.title: Retry-class rule walks only `crates/`, so a `with_retries` call site in the desktop crate is unscanned
