findings.title: The documented auto-update opt-out (settings.auto_update / AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE) is never consulted; UserSettings::load has no production caller
findings.rationale: The whole `auto_update` field, `default_true`, `auto_update_env_override`, and `UserSettings::load` are dead code: nothing in the backend or frontend reads them, so `check_for_update` always egresses to the GitHub release endpoint on launch. README and DEVELOPMENT.md tell MDM/CI operators the opt-out works, and DEVELOPMENT.md refers to a "settings toggle" that does not exist in web-rs either (no `auto_update` binding or view). An operator who set the env var per the docs believes update checks are disabled; they are not — a misleading-the-operator result plus unexpected network egress in locked-down deployments.
findings.proposal: Gate in the backend, not just on the launch path: have both `check_for_update` and `perform_update` read `UserSettings::load(&crate::config_directory()).auto_update` and return `Ok(None)` / a `UiError` ('update checks are disabled by policy') when false — this honours README.md:281-282 ('no network calls to the updater endpoint at any point in the session') and the MSI guidance at README.md:255-259. Expose the policy to the frontend (e.g. an `update_policy` command, or fold a `disabled_by_policy` flag into the check result) so shell.rs hides or disables the manual 'Check for updates' item with a reason rather than toasting a misleading 'You're on the latest version'. Add a settings.rs test that `load` honours `AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE` (the existing tests deliberately avoid the env var), a src-tauri test that the two updater commands short-circuit when `auto_update == false`, and a `demo::register_fixtures` entry if a new infallible invoke is introduced. Either implement the 'settings toggle' or delete that clause from docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:314.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise holds end to end. `check_for_update` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/updater.rs:26-37) calls `app.updater().check()` unconditionally; `perform_update` (43-72) likewise. `UserSettings::load` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs:82-88) is the only place `auto_update_env_override` is applied and its only callers are the module's own tests (251, 259, 267); every production reader uses `UserSettings::stored` (state.rs:234, 376; commands/defaults.rs:19; commands/exchange/mod.rs:74). `grep auto_update|AUTO_UPDATE` under apps/ (rs/json/toml) returns nothing, so no binding, command, or view consults the field; the frontend launch effect (web-rs/src/views/shell.rs:164-176) and the manual button (186-200) both fire unconditionally. README.md:262-282 promises two opt-outs and states 'With auto-update disabled the app makes no network calls to the updater endpoint at any point in the session'; docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:313-314 refers to a 'settings toggle' that does not exist in web-rs. No repo invariant, GUI test, or architecture doc (release-updater-demo.md:42-56 describes the flow without mentioning the opt-out) pins the gate. High is fair: README.md:255-259 tells MSI/MDM deployers to rely on this opt-out to avoid a conflicting NSIS install, and the toast actively invites the click. One correction to the proposal: README promises no updater egress at any point, so gating only the launch path is not enough.
findings.recheck_notes: Traced end to end; nothing upstream gates the check. (1) apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/updater.rs:26-28 `check_for_update` and :44-46 `perform_update` call `app.updater()?.check().await` unconditionally; no settings read anywhere in the file. (2) `UserSettings::load` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs:83-89, the only place `auto_update_env_override` at :235 is applied) has zero callers outside that module's own tests — every production reader uses `UserSettings::stored` (state.rs:234, :376; commands/exchange/mod.rs:74; commands/defaults.rs:19) or `mutate`. `grep auto_update` under apps/ returns nothing: the field is never read by the backend or web-rs, so neither the env var nor `{"auto_update": false}` in settings.json has any effect. (3) Reachable in the shipped build: tauri.conf.json:45-48 has `plugins.updater.active: true` with the GitHub `releases/latest/download/latest.json` endpoint, capabilities/default.json:10 grants `updater:default`, lib.rs:24 registers the plugin and lib.rs:43-44 exposes both commands. (4) The frontend fires the check on every mount with no policy check: web-rs/src/views/shell.rs:162-177 (`Effect::new` -> `updater::check_for_update()`), plus the manual path at :189 which toasts 'You're on the latest version.' on `Ok(None)`; no `auto_update` binding, view, or toggle exists in web-rs. (5) Docs promise the opposite: README.md:264-282 documents both opt-outs and states 'With auto-update disabled the app makes no network calls to the updater endpoint at any point in the session'; README.md:255-259 tells MSI deployers to rely on this to avoid a second conflicting NSIS install; docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:314 cites a 'settings toggle' that does not exist; docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md:42-50 never mentions the opt-out at all. Repo-invariant tests (tests/repo_invariants/release.rs) pin version/notes parity only, not the opt-out. Git history in this clone shows no src-tauri commit ever referencing `auto_update`, so this is not a recent regression — the gate was never wired. Mitigating factor that keeps this from being worse: installation still requires the user to click 'Update & restart' (UpdateSplash), so the failure is unexpected egress + a misleading update prompt (and the MSI-conflict guidance being ineffective), not a silent install. High stands because the README makes an explicit no-egress guarantee to MDM/CI operators and the MSI guidance depends on it.

findings.title: Exchange transport open-codes the retry loop with no RetryClass, so New-/Remove- cmdlets are replayed after transient failures and misreport a committed write as a failure; the hand-rolled loop escapes the trust.rs invariant
findings.rationale: Every Exchange admin call is a POST to InvokeCommand, and `send_core` retries a connection reset or 5xx up to MAX_RETRIES times regardless of the cmdlet. A `New-ManagementRoleAssignment` that committed server-side before a 502 is re-run and creates a second, identical role assignment; a later `Remove-ManagementRoleAssignment` by identity removes one and the app keeps its mailbox access — the operator sees "removed" while access persists. `New-ServicePrincipal`/`New-ManagementScope` replays surface as "already exists" failures after a successful write. This is exactly the class `RetryClass::NonIdempotent` closed for Graph/ARM/Key Vault, but the `trust.rs` invariant scans only `with_retries(` call sites, so the hand-rolled Exchange loop is invisible to it. http_retry.rs's own header ("Shared retry policy for the Graph, ARM, Key Vault and Exchange HTTP clients") and the `with_retries` doc ("The four HTTP clients each open-coded this loop", past tense) both state a unification that has not happened for Exchange.
findings.proposal: Port `send_core` onto `with_retries(label, class, |_| ...)` with a `retry_class_for(cmdlet)` helper: `Get-`/`Test-`/`Search-` and paging continuations → Idempotent; `New-`/`Remove-`/`Set-`/`Update-` → NonIdempotent (`Add-DistributionGroupMember` may stay Idempotent since `is_already_member_body` already makes a re-add benign). Keep the `x-ms-diagnostics`/`request-id` capture inside the per-attempt closure. Extend `repo_invariants/trust.rs` so any crate source outside `http_retry.rs` that references `MAX_RETRIES`, `next_backoff_ms` or `sleep_before_retry` directly (rather than via `with_retries`/`RetryBudget`) fails the test. Add a wiremock test that a `New-ManagementRoleAssignment` answered 502 is NOT re-sent and a `Get-*` answered 502 IS. Fix the http_retry.rs:160-165 doc that presents the four-client unification as complete. Drop the 'duplicate assignment survives removal' framing — grants.rs:74-78 and 459-468 show Exchange rejects the duplicate and removal sweeps every assignment.
findings.verifier_notes: The mechanism is real: crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/client/transport.rs:11-14 imports only the raw primitives, and `send_core` retries every POST on a reqwest error (181-188) and on 429/5xx (265-270) up to `MAX_RETRIES` with no `RetryClass`; `New-ManagementRoleAssignment` (rbac.rs:243), `New-ServicePrincipal` (rbac.rs:31), `New-ManagementScope` (rbac.rs:80), `Remove-ManagementRoleAssignment` (rbac.rs:260) all ride it. The `trust.rs` invariant (apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/repo_invariants/trust.rs:163) skips any file without `with_retries(`, so the loop is invisible to it; commit 8fb1ac7 (the RetryClass fix) touched transport.rs only for the same-origin check, and its CHANGELOG entry (CHANGELOG.md:504-515) claims 'the transports route everything through it'. No Exchange test covers a 5xx/network replay (only `retry_after_is_honored_on_429`, tests.rs:492). This is a genuine gap against AGENTS.md's 'one definition per policy' rule. But the headline harm is refuted by the repo's own code: (a) a duplicate `New-ManagementRoleAssignment` for the same role/app/scope FAILS on Exchange rather than creating a second assignment — grants.rs:74-78 records exactly that ('every duplicate `New-RoleAssignment` failed'); (b) `remove_exchange_mailbox_access` (grants.rs:459-468) enumerates every assignment via `Get-ManagementRoleAssignment -RoleAssignee` and removes each, so even a duplicate would not leave access behind; (c) `assign_scoped_roles` (grants.rs:92-93) plans against the live snapshot, so a replay-induced 'failed to assign' leaves `role_in_place = false` and `targets_safe_to_strip` keeps the org-wide grant — fail-closed, healed on re-run; (d) `ensure_management_scope`/`ensure_service_principal` re-read before creating, and `Add-DistributionGroupMember` already treats 'already a member' as success (error.rs:166, tests.rs:412). So the realistic consequence is a misreported outcome (a committed write replayed surfaces as 'failed to assign' / 'failed to remove') and a wasted re-run, not widened or persisting access. Medium, not high.

findings.title: UserSettings::mutate overwrites an unparseable or unreadable settings.json with defaults — vault bindings and tenant defaults are permanently lost
findings.rationale: The atomic temp-and-rename closed the *torn write* cause of an unparseable file, but `mutate` still treats "file exists but cannot be parsed" and "file exists but cannot be read (EACCES, EIO, AV lock on Windows)" identically to "file missing", then serialises defaults over it. Any of: a hand-edit typo (which defaults.rs explicitly expects), a future field type change, or a transient read failure, followed by the very next `mutate` (sign-in calls `remember_account` via `mutate` on every successful login) wipes `tenant_defaults` including `app_vaults` — the map the rotation flow needs to find secrets again — and the only trace is a `warn!` in the log. Data loss with no recovery.
findings.proposal: Make `from_file` return `Result<Option<Self>, io::Error>` distinguishing `ErrorKind::NotFound` (→ `Ok(None)`) from parse/IO failures. Keep `stored()`'s lenient fallback for read-only callers, but have `mutate` refuse (`Err(InvalidData)`) when the file exists and cannot be parsed — or first rename it to `settings.json.corrupt-<timestamp>` and log at `error!` before writing defaults. Callers already treat `mutate` errors as non-fatal (state.rs:347-355, keyvault.rs:167-171). Add a test: write `not json`, call `mutate`, assert the original bytes (or a `.corrupt` sibling) survive.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is exact. `mutate` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs:121-123) starts from `Self::stored`, which is `from_file(..).unwrap_or_default()` (75-77), and `from_file` (223-232) collapses both an I/O error (`std::fs::read(path).ok()?` — EACCES/EIO/AV lock) and a parse error into `None` with only a `warn!`. `save_locked` then serialises the defaults over the file. private_file.rs:39-41 documents this exact loss mechanism but only closed the torn-write cause; defaults.rs:125-126 explicitly anticipates hand-edited settings.json. `remember_account` (state.rs:345-355) runs `mutate` on every successful sign-in, so the overwrite happens promptly. No `.bak`/`.corrupt` sibling or recovery exists (grep). No test covers 'unparseable file survives a mutate'. One nuance on the proposal: only two of the four writer files treat a `mutate` error as non-fatal (state.rs:347-355 warn, keyvault.rs:167-171 push a warning); config.rs:52-57 and defaults.rs:72-75 return `UiError::io('Could not write settings.json: ...')` to the operator — which is the desirable behaviour for a refused write, so the proposal still fits. Medium is honest: silent, permanent loss of `app_vaults`/tenant defaults, but requires a prior corruption/read failure.

findings.title: private_file temp path is predictable and opened without O_EXCL, so a symlink pre-planted in a shared export directory is followed — cheap hardening with create_new
findings.rationale: The temp name is `<target>.tmp<pid>` — pid is readable by any local user — and the open is `create(true)` without `create_new`/`O_NOFOLLOW`, deliberately reusing a pre-existing temp. In a shared or world-writable export directory (the operator picks the path via a save dialog; `/tmp` or a shared drive is plausible) another local user can pre-plant `<name>.tmp<pid>` as a symlink to a file the victim owns. The write then truncates and overwrites that victim-owned file with the secret payload (fchmod on the fd succeeds because the victim owns the target), and `rename(temp, path)` moves the symlink itself into place. Result: destruction of an arbitrary victim-owned file and the secret landing where the attacker chose. The app-config directory is per-user so `settings.json` is not exposed, but the export choke point is.
findings.proposal: Open the temp with `.create_new(true)` (O_CREAT|O_EXCL refuses to follow an existing symlink, so no libc/`O_NOFOLLOW` is needed — libc is not a direct dependency of core) and add an in-process `AtomicU64` counter to the temp name so a stale temp from a crashed run yields `AlreadyExists` once and is retried with the next suffix (or removed first). With `create_new`, the `set_permissions` call becomes belt-and-braces and its 'reused temp' comment at 73-74 should be rewritten. Add a unix-only test that a pre-existing `<name>.tmp<pid>` symlink to a decoy file causes the write to fail (or use a fresh name) and leaves the decoy untouched.
findings.verifier_notes: The mechanics are correct: `temp_sibling` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/private_file.rs:57-61) yields `<target>.tmp<pid>`, and `write_then_rename` (67-75) opens with `create(true).truncate(true)` and no `create_new`/`O_NOFOLLOW`, deliberately reusing a pre-existing temp (comment at 73-74); `set_permissions` is fchmod on the followed target, so a pre-planted symlink in the destination directory is followed, truncated, overwritten with the payload, and `rename(temp, path)` (85) moves the symlink into place. export.rs:103 (every operator-chosen export, .pfx via credentials.rs:200) is the exposed call site; `settings.json` lives in the per-user config dir and is not. No test covers a symlink temp. However the severity is overstated: it needs a unix host, a world-writable/shared directory the operator picks in a save dialog, the victim's pid, and a filename that carries a to-the-second timestamp (export.rs:56-59, 153; credentials.rs:195-199), which the attacker must pre-plant before the open; Windows — the primary target per README — needs symlink privilege. Disclosure additionally requires the attacker to hold a pre-opened fd on the victim file, since the fchmod leaves it 0600. A real but narrow hardening item; the fix is cheap and standard.

findings.title: UserSettings::save is a public, unlocked writer duplicating save_locked, with a doc block that contradicts the module's own invariant
findings.rationale: The module states that `save_locked` is private precisely so nobody can split read-modify-write apart, yet `save` — the same body, public, unlocked — remains as the open door for the next writer; the "only writer of this file" / "first-run config screen" doc is stale (config.rs uses `mutate`) and has been spliced onto `mutate`'s doc. No repo invariant pins "settings writers go through mutate".
findings.proposal: Delete `save` (convert the two tests that call it to `mutate`, or make it `#[cfg(test)]`), have `save_locked` be the only serialiser, and split the doc block so `mutate` carries only its own text (move the owner-only rationale to `save_locked`). Optionally add a `repo_invariants` scan that `UserSettings::stored(` is never followed by a write in the same function.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified at crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs: lines 90-97 ('Writes the settings ... Used by the first-run config screen — the only writer of this file. Owner-only: ...') run straight into line 98 ('Read, modify and write ... under a process-wide lock') as one doc block on `mutate`, while `save` at 136-141 is `pub`, undocumented, not under `SETTINGS_LOCK`, and byte-identical to the private `save_locked` (129-134) whose doc says it is private 'so a caller cannot take the read-modify-write apart'. Production callers of `.save(` outside settings.rs: none (config.rs:52, defaults.rs:72, keyvault.rs:167, state.rs:347/363 all use `mutate`); only tests at 281 and 322 use it. No repo_invariants test mentions `UserSettings`/`mutate` (grep). The finding is real and the proposal is right, but with zero production callers and every call site carrying a 'through mutate, not stored + save' comment, this is a cleanup rather than a live race — low, not medium.

findings.title: http_error/http_retry docs claim all four clients are unified; Exchange still has a hand-written enum and loop, and the macro doc miscounts its variants
findings.rationale: The macro cannot express Exchange's `Forbidden { detail, had_diagnostics }` (it only supports *extra* variants, not a replacement shape), so Exchange being outside the macro is a legitimate consequence — but the docs present the unification as complete, and the miscount suggests the doc was not re-read after `Protocol` was added. A reader trusting the header would not look for a fourth `ui_code` table to keep in sync.
findings.proposal: Either (a) add an optional `forbidden = { $($field:ident : $ty:ty),* }` override arm to `http_error_enum!` so `ExchangeError` can join, keeping one `ui_code` table for all four; or (b) correct both module docs to say three clients share the macro and name Exchange's `had_diagnostics` Forbidden as the reason it stays hand-written, and fix "nine" → "ten". (a) is the durable fix and pairs naturally with the Exchange retry-loop port.
findings.verifier_notes: All three statements check out. crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/http_error.rs:1-2 says 'the four typed clients share' while its own body (4-8) and the macro users (graph/error.rs:10, arm/error.rs:10, keyvault/error.rs:10) show three; http_error.rs:23 says 'nine common variants' but the macro emits ten (Unauthorized, Forbidden, NotFound, Throttled, Api, Server, Network, Deserialize, Token, Protocol at 73-101). http_retry.rs:160-165 ('The four HTTP clients each open-coded this loop', past tense) is contradicted by exchange transport.rs:181-188/265-270 still doing so. `ExchangeError::Forbidden { detail, had_diagnostics }` (exchange/src/error.rs:12-21) genuinely cannot be expressed by the macro's `extra` arm, so Exchange staying hand-written is defensible — but nothing in docs/architecture or AGENTS.md records that exception (grep `had_diagnostics` in docs: none), and Exchange has no `error_conformance.rs` unlike arm/keyvault. Note `.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:19` already correctly says 'Graph/ARM/Key Vault'. Option (b) — fix both docs and name the exception — is proportionate; option (a) is more machinery than the drift warrants unless done alongside the Exchange retry port ([1]).

findings.title: Docs-in-code drift around the cache caps and the settings writer count
findings.rationale: Each of these was true once and drifted when `Lists` joined the per-object cap and when `mutate` replaced `stored`+`save`. AGENTS.md is read by every agent on session start, so its stale writer count and wrong function name actively misdirect the next change to settings.json.
findings.proposal: Update constants.rs:58-61 to name both `ServicePrincipal` and `Lists` and point at `Cache::cap_for`/`capacity_for`; reword cache.rs:4-5 and constants.rs:47-48 to say the cap is `MAX_CACHE_SIZE` for aggregate kinds and `MAX_PER_OBJECT_CACHE_SIZE` for the two per-object kinds. Change AGENTS.md:110 AND `.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:26` to 'every writer (config, tenant defaults, vault binding, remembered account) goes through `UserSettings::mutate`', and align settings.rs:100 ('three') with the same count.
findings.verifier_notes: Each cited drift is real. constants.rs:58-61 says the per-object cap applies to 'currently only ServicePrincipal', but `Cache::cap_for` (cache.rs:601-603) applies it to `ServicePrincipal | Lists`, and `capacity_for`'s doc (cache.rs:575-587) already lists both kinds — so constants.rs contradicts cache.rs. cache.rs:4-5 ('Eviction is LRU once per-kind entry count exceeds MAX_CACHE_SIZE') and constants.rs:47-48 ('5000-entry-per-kind cap') ignore `MAX_PER_OBJECT_CACHE_SIZE`. AGENTS.md:110 says 'two writers read-modify-write via `UserSettings::stored`'; actual writers are `mutate` call sites in config.rs:52, defaults.rs:72, keyvault.rs:167, state.rs:347/363 (four files, five sites), and settings.rs:100-103 itself says 'three'. The same stale sentence also lives in `.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:26` ('Two writers ... via `UserSettings::stored`'), which the reviewer did not cite and which should be fixed together with AGENTS.md. Low is right: doc-only, but AGENTS.md is loaded every session.

findings.title: TenantDefaults has three copy-pasted pattern resolvers, each carrying the same 8-line comment (including Exchange-scope text on the Key Vault resolver)
findings.rationale: Three copies of a load-bearing guard (the placeholder check that prevents every app collapsing onto one scope/group/secret name) are three places a future edit can miss; the commands layer (`commands/defaults.rs:53-57`) already iterates the three patterns as a table, so the core side should too. The duplicated comment also misattributes the Exchange rationale to the secret-name resolver.
findings.proposal: Add `fn resolve_pattern(pattern: Option<&str>, default_prefix: &str, app_id: &str) -> String` holding the guard and the comment once; make the three public methods one-liners over it. Keep the existing tests (they exercise all three), and add one asserting `resolve_pattern` directly. Optionally rename `SCOPE_NAME_PLACEHOLDER` → `NAME_PATTERN_PLACEHOLDER` since it now serves three patterns.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified at crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/defaults.rs:117-131, 139-153, 159-173: three bodies identical except for the field and prefix, each carrying the same 8-line comment; commands/defaults.rs:53-57 already iterates the three patterns as a table. Tests (defaults.rs:182-206 and below) exercise all three, so a shared `resolve_pattern` is a safe refactor. One overstatement: the comment on `secret_name_for` is not strictly irrelevant — it ends with 'the same collapse cross-wires Key Vault secret names between apps' — it is a copy-pasted shared rationale rather than a misattribution. Low/refactor is the honest severity; the placeholder guard is the load-bearing part and centralising it is worthwhile.

findings.title: No cache test covers clear()/clear_kind() racing an in-flight IndexWatch (the diagnostics "Clear cache" path)
findings.rationale: The `bump_watches` calls in `clear`/`clear_kind` are the only thing stopping an operator's "Clear cache" click mid-scan from being followed by a re-pinned pre-clear index for the full TTL — and `clear_kind(Audit)` must *not* refuse a concurrent `Lists` index store. Neither direction is asserted, and both are one-line regressions away (drop a `bump_watches`, or pass `None` instead of `Some(kind)`).
findings.proposal: Add two tests beside the existing watch tests: (1) `generation_for(Lists, k)` → `clear()` → `put_typed_index_if_current` returns false and the key stays empty; (2) `generation_for(Lists, k)` → `clear_kind(Audit)` → store succeeds. Both are ~10 lines using the existing helpers.
findings.verifier_notes: cache.rs:608-619 shows `clear` bumping all watches (`bump_watches(None, |_| true)`) and `clear_kind` bumping only its kind (`Some(kind)`); `bump_watches` (1037-1044) filters on `k.idx() == *watched_kind`, so the two behaviours the reviewer wants asserted are exactly what the code does today. `grep clear crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/cache/tests.rs` returns nothing; the watch tests (tests.rs:68-135 and onwards) cover `invalidate_prefix`/`invalidate`/`invalidate_tenant` only, and no src-tauri test drives `clear_cache` (diagnostics.rs:33-46). Both proposed tests are ~10 lines using `generation_for` + `put_typed_index_if_current`, consistent with the existing style. Low is right.

findings.title: CacheKind::idx is `self as usize` while the bucket array is sized by the hand-maintained ALL — a new variant compiles and panics with index-out-of-bounds on first use
findings.rationale: The comment's claim is only half true: `ttl_for`'s exhaustive match forces a TTL arm, but a developer who adds `CacheKind::Foo`, a `ttl_for` arm and `record`/`CacheStats` arms gets a clean compile and a runtime panic (`index out of bounds: the len is 4 but the index is 4`) the first time `Foo` is read or written — inside a Tauri command, taking the request down. Nothing ties `ALL.len()` to the variant count.
findings.proposal: Make `idx()` an exhaustive `match self { ServicePrincipal => 0, Permissions => 1, Audit => 2, Lists => 3 }` (so a new variant is a compile error here too) and add `const _: () = assert!(CacheKind::ALL.len() == CacheKind::Lists as usize + 1);` plus a unit test `for (i, k) in ALL.iter().enumerate() { assert_eq!(k.idx(), i) }`. Alternatively collapse `CacheStats`'s eight fields and `record` into `[Counters; ALL.len()]` indexed by `idx()`, removing two more hand-maintained tables.
findings.verifier_notes: cache.rs:37-42 hand-lists `ALL: [CacheKind; 4]`, `idx()` (45-47) is `self as usize`, and `buckets: [Mutex<Bucket>; CacheKind::ALL.len()]` (366). The comment at 31-36 correctly notes `ttl_for` forces a new variant to be handled there (and `record` at 1108-1120 does too), but nothing forces `ALL` to grow: a fifth variant compiles and `buckets[4]` panics on first `get`/`put`. No test asserts `ALL[i].idx() == i` (grep). The proposal — exhaustive `match` in `idx()`, a `const` assert tying `ALL.len()` to the last discriminant + 1, and a small unit test — is cheap and idiomatic; collapsing `CacheStats` into `[Counters; ALL.len()]` is optional and would change the DTO shape diagnostics reads, so keep it separate. Low: latent, only bites on a future variant, but the failure mode is a runtime panic inside a Tauri command.

findings.title: mutate's process-wide lock does not cover a second app instance; std's File::lock (stable since 1.89, MSRV 1.98) would close the gap without a dependency
findings.rationale: The lost-update race `mutate` fixes reappears across processes: two windows/instances (nothing prevents launching a second) each read-modify-write settings.json; the atomic rename means the file is never torn, but the second writer's snapshot silently drops the first's field (e.g. a vault binding recorded by a rotation in one instance is overwritten by a defaults save in the other). Since MSRV is 1.98, `std::fs::File::lock`/`try_lock` (stabilised in 1.89) gives a cross-process advisory lock with no new crate.
findings.proposal: In `mutate`, after taking `SETTINGS_LOCK`, open (create) `<config_dir>/settings.lock` and call `.lock()?` on it for the duration of the read-modify-write; the guard drops with the `File`. This composes with the atomic rename and keeps `stored()` lock-free for readers. Alternatively adopt `tauri-plugin-single-instance`, but that is a dependency and a broader behaviour change.
findings.verifier_notes: settings.rs:116-120 shows a process-wide `static Mutex`, so two processes can interleave `stored()`/`save_locked()`. No single-instance plugin is registered (lib.rs:24-25 has only updater + dialog; grep for `single_instance`/`File::lock`/`fs2`/`fd-lock` finds nothing), so a second instance is possible on Windows (the primary target) and Linux. rust-toolchain.toml:5 pins 1.98.1, above the 1.89 stabilisation of `File::lock`/`try_lock`/`unlock`, so an advisory lock on `<config_dir>/settings.lock` needs no new dependency and composes with the atomic rename in private_file. The race requires two instances writing within milliseconds of each other, which is rare in practice — low/enhancement is honest. Note `File::lock` releases when the `File` is dropped (or `unlock()`), so holding the `File` for the read-modify-write scope is sufficient; keep it inside the existing `SETTINGS_LOCK` so in-process callers still serialise without contending on the OS lock.

findings.title: FederatedIdentityCredential.subject is a bare String; a flexible FIC (subject: null) fails the whole list and skips the app from backup
findings.evidence:
models.rs:315-321:
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct FederatedIdentityCredential {
    pub id: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub issuer: String,
    pub subject: String,

crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/credentials.rs:80-82:
    let params: [(&str, &str); 1] =
        [("$select", "id,name,issuer,subject,description,audiences")];
    let page: Paged<FederatedIdentityCredential> = self.get_json(&path, &params, false).await?;

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/backup.rs:414-421:
                Err(err) => {
                    tracing::warn!(%object_id, error = %err, "backup: federated creds failed; skipping app");
                    skipped.push(SkippedObject::new(
                        "application",
                        object_id,
                        None,
                        format!("federated credentials could not be read: {err}"),

Microsoft Graph federatedIdentityCredential reference: "[Subject <String>]: Nullable. Defaults to null if not set. ... If subject is defined, claimsMatchingExpression must be null." and flexible-FIC doc: "If claimsMatchingExpression is defined, subject must be set to null."
findings.rationale: Flexible federated identity credentials (claimsMatchingExpression, the pattern GitHub now recommends for PR/branch workflows) store `subject: null`. Because `Paged<FederatedIdentityCredential>` is deserialized as one document, a single flexible FIC on an app makes `list_federated_credentials` fail with `invalid type: null, expected a string`, so the Federated credentials tab errors for that app and, worse, the DR backup records the whole application as skipped. The repo already learned this lesson for `AppRole.value` and `OAuth2PermissionGrant.scope` (models.rs:185-189, 396-399); the FIC model was never revisited. No test covers a null subject, and `claimsMatchingExpression` appears nowhere in the repo.
findings.proposal: Make `subject: Option<String>` with `#[serde(default)]` and add `#[serde(default)] claims_matching_expression: Option<FederatedIdentityExpression>` (harmless on v1.0 which omits it); add a null-subject test next to `oauth2_grant_tolerates_null_scope`; make `FederatedCredentialDto.subject: Option<String>` and render the row as 'expression-matched (flexible)' when None; in restore, skip only that credential with a 'flexible credential not restored' warning instead of skipping the app. Beta-endpoint recreation is a separate follow-up.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is real: models.rs:317-326 has `pub subject: String` with no default; credentials.rs:74-84 deserializes `Paged<FederatedIdentityCredential>` as one document over the v1.0 endpoint (no beta base used for FICs); backup.rs:414-421 records the whole app as skipped when that list fails. Microsoft's flexible-FIC doc (learn.microsoft.com/entra/workload-id/workload-identities-flexible-federated-identity-credentials) states 'If claimsMatchingExpression is defined, subject must be set to null', and the Graph beta reference says 'Subject: Nullable. Defaults to null if not set.' `claimsMatchingExpression`/`flexible` appear nowhere in the repo (grep). No null-subject test exists (models.rs tests at 994-1130 cover other fields). The repo did fix the identical class for AppRole.value (185-189) and OAuth2PermissionGrant.scope (396-399). Severity adjusted from high to medium: flexible FICs are still labelled preview, the failure is loud (tab error) and the backup records the skip in `SkippedObject` rather than silently dropping the app. The minimal fix (Option<String> + null test + a 'not restored: flexible credential' warning) is sound; recreating through the beta endpoint is optional and should not gate the fix.

findings.title: Mailbox advisory's name-shaped fallback misses MailboxItem.*/MailboxFolder.*/Mail-Advanced.* — org-wide read/write of every mailbox item scores as all-clear
findings.rationale: `starts_with("MailboxSettings.")` does not match `MailboxItem.*`/`MailboxFolder.*`, and `starts_with("Mail.")` does not match `Mail-Advanced.*`, so the fallback fails exactly the case its own comment says it exists for. A Microsoft Graph application grant of `MailboxItem.ReadWrite.All` or `Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All` (tenant-wide read/write of all mailbox content) enters neither the mailbox advisory nor the high-risk list: no finding, no ScopeMailboxAccess fix, healthy-looking score. docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md:46-49 deliberately keeps these out of `graph_mail_role` (scopability/AAP parity), but that decision is about the *fix* gate, not advisory membership — `is_mailbox_reaching_permission` is documented as a superset ("over-reporting is the safe side", scoping.rs:210).
findings.proposal: (1) Extend `mailbox_named` with "MailboxFolder.", "MailboxItem.", "MailboxConfigItem.", "Mail-Advanced." and add a table test over Microsoft's supported-roles list. (2) Add the write/export variants to HIGH_RISK_APP_PERMISSIONS and the read variants to MEDIUM. (3) Either add them to `graph_mail_role` (with the CHANGELOG note exchange-scoping.md:46-49 requires) or reword the UNCONFINABLE_MAILBOX recommendation so it does not claim RBAC has no role for them.
findings.verifier_notes: scoping.rs:194-198 `mailbox_named` prefixes are exactly ["Mail.", "MailboxSettings.", "Calendars.", "Contacts."]; `starts_with("MailboxSettings.")` cannot match `MailboxItem.*`/`MailboxFolder.*`/`MailboxConfigItem.*`, and `starts_with("Mail.")` cannot match `Mail-Advanced.*`. Microsoft's RBAC-for-Applications table (learn.microsoft.com/exchange/permissions-exo/application-rbac) lists all six as MS Graph application permissions with RBAC roles (`Application MailboxItem.ReadWrite` -> `MailboxItem.ReadWrite.All`, `Application Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All`, etc.). grep for MailboxItem|MailboxFolder|Mail-Advanced|MailboxConfigItem over *.rs hits nothing; only docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md:46-49 mentions them, and that passage is about keeping them out of `graph_mail_role` (AAP parity), not out of advisory membership, which scoring.rs:288-296 derives solely from `is_mailbox_reaching_permission`. HIGH_RISK_APP_PERMISSIONS (audit/permissions.rs:67-93) lists none of them, so an org-wide `Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All` grant produces no finding and no score. Severity kept high: tenant-wide mailbox write scoring zero is the exact class the audit exists to catch (the file's own comments treat the earlier `full_access_as_app` zero-score the same way), and adoption of MailboxItem.* is rising as EWS retires. One correction to the proposal: with step (1) alone these land in `unconfinable_other` (scoring.rs:322-360) whose recommendation text says 'RBAC for Applications exposes no supported application role for them' - false for these six - so either do step (3) (`graph_mail_role` + CHANGELOG per exchange-scoping.md) or adjust that text.
findings.recheck_notes:
Failing path traced end to end; nothing upstream prevents it.

1. The permissions are real Graph APPLICATION permissions (admin-consent, tenant-wide). Microsoft Graph permissions reference lists `MailboxItem.ReadWrite.All` (id 1583d471-fede-4e7c-b062-57e9d60cfb49, Application), `MailboxFolder.ReadWrite.All` (fef87b92-...), `MailboxItem.Read.All`, `MailboxItem.Export.All`, `MailboxItem.ImportExport.All`, and `Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All` (e118f1da-5c1c-46cf-bff6-8858d786f46f, 'create, read, update, and delete all email ... in user mailboxes, without a signed-in user'). The RBAC-for-Applications doc's 'Supported Application Roles' table (fetched live) maps each to an `Application MailboxItem.*` / `Application MailboxFolder.*` / `Application Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All` role, protocol MS Graph.

2. Advisory membership: crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/scoping.rs:204 `Some(MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID) => graph_mail_role(value).is_some() || mailbox_named(value)`. `graph_mail_role` (scoping.rs:77-92) has no arm for any of these -> None. `mailbox_named` (scoping.rs:194-198) tests only `Mail.`, `MailboxSettings.`, `Calendars.`, `Contacts.`; `"MailboxItem.ReadWrite.All".starts_with("MailboxSettings.")` is false and `"Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All".starts_with("Mail.")` is false (char 5 is '-' not '.'). So `is_mailbox_reaching_permission(Some(GRAPH), v)` is false, and the filter at audit/scoring.rs:288-296 drops the grant before the scoped/org-wide/unconfinable partition; neither ORG_WIDE_MAILBOX, UNSCOPABLE_LEGACY_MAILBOX nor UNCONFINABLE_MAILBOX (scoring.rs:350-361) is emitted and no ScopeMailboxAccess fix is offered. The fallback's own comment (scoping.rs:200-203) says it exists precisely so 'a Graph permission this build's graph_mail_role table doesn't know yet still reports reach', which is exactly what fails here.

3. Scoring: rule_app_permission_risk (scoring.rs:49-92) is exact-match `HIGH_RISK_APP_PERMISSIONS.contains(&g.value.as_str())` / MEDIUM; neither table (audit/permissions.rs:67-140) has any MailboxItem/MailboxFolder/Mail-Advanced entry (grep across all *.rs: zero hits outside docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md:46-47). No generic `.All` / `ReadWrite` heuristic exists anywhere in audit (grep for ends_with(".All")/contains("ReadWrite") finds only tests). rule_admin_consent (scoring.rs:201-213) fires on `has_admin_consent`, i.e. DELEGATED consent, not app-role grants. `least_privilege_alternative_for` (permissions.rs:264-277) routes through `is_scopable_exchange_resource_permission` -> None. The bundled permissions catalog (azapptoolkit-permissions/data/catalog.json) holds only `appId`/`displayName` per resource — no permission values — so it cannot supply a fallback. The only test guarding the mailbox-family/risk-table agreement (permissions.rs:603-605) also uses `Mail.`/`Calendar`/`Contacts.` prefixes and so cannot notice the gap. No repo_invariants test references mailbox_named or these names.

Net: an app holding only Graph `MailboxItem.ReadWrite.All` or `Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All` contributes 0 points and zero mailbox issues -> healthy row in a security audit whose purpose is to surface exactly this. Reachable in the shipped build (core scoring, not test/demo code). Severity high stands: silent false negative on tenant-wide mailbox content read/write/export. The doc's deliberate exclusion (exchange-scoping.md:46-49) concerns the scopable set / AAP parity, not advisory membership, so it does not justify the omission.

findings.title: rewrite_identifier_uris only rewrites the exact `api://{appId}` form; `api://{tenantId}/{appId}`, `api://{string}/{appId}` and `api://{tenantId}/...` fail the Expose-an-API PATCH on restore
findings.rationale: `api://{tenantId}/{appId}` is one of Microsoft's two 'default' identifier URIs (the only two allowed once an org enables `nonDefaultUriAddition`), and `api://{string}/{appId}` is a common alternative. Both keep the SOURCE appId (and, cross-tenant, the SOURCE tenant GUID), which the destination tenant rejects because the GUID matches neither the new appId nor the destination tenant. The failure is not isolated: the identifier URIs share one PATCH with `oauth2PermissionScopes` and `preAuthorizedApplications`, so the app's whole Expose-an-API surface is lost with a single warning line. The backup carries `source_tenant_id` and the restore knows the destination tenant, so a correct rewrite is possible.
findings.proposal: Change the helper to `rewrite_identifier_uris(uris, source_app_id, new_app_id, source_tenant_id, dest_tenant_id)` and rewrite every `api://` URI whose host or path segment equals `source_app_id` → `new_app_id` or equals `source_tenant_id` → `dest_tenant_id` (segment-wise, case-insensitive GUID compare; leave `https://` and verified-domain forms untouched). Add table tests for `api://{tenant}/{app}`, `api://{tenant}/api`, `api://productapi/{app}`, and a substring non-match. Update docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:148 ("`api://{old}` → `api://{new}`"). Effect: cross-tenant restores keep their Expose-an-API configuration instead of dropping URIs, scopes and pre-authorized clients together.
findings.verifier_notes: The helper is at restore_plan.rs:50-61 (not :176, which is inside the tests) and matches only the exact `api://{source_app_id}` string. restore.rs:419-437 puts the rewritten URIs, `oauth2PermissionScopes` and `preAuthorizedApplications` in ONE `patch_application_expose_api` call, so a rejected URI drops the whole Expose-an-API surface with a single warning. Microsoft's identifier-URI restrictions page lists `api://<tenantId>/<appId>`, `api://<tenantId>/<string>`, `api://<string>/<appId>` as supported forms and says a GUID 'must match either the app ID or the tenant ID'; the `nonDefaultUriAddition` policy allows only `api://{appId}` or `api://{tenantId}/{appId}`. The reviewer did not cite the deliberate-decision comment at restore_plan.rs:151-154 ('the appId form is the ONLY one that encodes an identity the restore invalidates'), but that rationale is factually incomplete - `api://{tenantId}/{appId}` encodes both identities the restore changes - so it does not refute the finding. `TenantBackup.source_tenant_id` (dto/backup.rs:48) and `destination_tenant_id` (restore.rs:136-138) are available. Proposal is feasible; note the tenant segment rewrite is a no-op on same-tenant restores and GUID comparison should be case-insensitive. docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:148 needs the wording update.

findings.title: AZAPPTOOLKIT_CLOUD cannot be baked like the client/tenant ids, so a sovereign-cloud team build still needs a per-workstation env var
findings.rationale: The whole point of build-time baking (README, build.rs doc comment) is that a team distributes one installer and recipients configure nothing. A GCC High / DoD / 21Vianet team cannot get that today: the cloud is read only from the process environment at runtime, so every recipient must set `AZAPPTOOLKIT_CLOUD` or the app silently targets the commercial endpoints and sign-in fails with an unhelpful AADSTS error. The settings screen also has no cloud field (README resolution order covers only client/tenant ids).
findings.proposal: Add `"AZAPPTOOLKIT_CLOUD" => "AZAPPTOOLKIT_BUILD_CLOUD"` (+ rerun-if-env-changed) to build.rs; add `const BUILD_CLOUD: Option<&str> = option_env!("AZAPPTOOLKIT_BUILD_CLOUD")` in src-tauri/state.rs; give `EntraAuthService` a constructor (or `CloudEnvironment::from_env_or(fallback)`) that takes the resolved cloud so state.rs applies env var -> baked -> Commercial; document in README/DEVELOPMENT.md/.env.example.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise holds: build.rs:26-30 bakes only CLIENT_ID/TENANT_ID; cloud.rs:66-81 reads only the runtime env var; .env.example carries only the two GUIDs; README.md:414-420 tells sovereign users to set `AZAPPTOOLKIT_CLOUD` per workstation, contradicting the 'no per-workstation configuration' promise at README.md:405-407. cloud.rs:6-7 itself calls the cloud a 'deployment-time choice', so baking is consistent with the design. Two corrections: (a) severity - this is an enhancement for a minority deployment with a documented MDM/env-var workaround, so low, not medium; (b) the proposed fallback location is wrong: `cargo:rustc-env` emitted by src-tauri's build.rs is visible only to the src-tauri crate, so `option_env!("AZAPPTOOLKIT_BUILD_CLOUD")` cannot live in `azapptoolkit-core::cloud::from_env` or in the auth crate. The baked value must be read in src-tauri (state.rs, next to BUILD_CLIENT_ID at :39-40) and passed into `EntraAuthService::new` (currently calls `CloudEnvironment::from_env()` at auth/service/mod.rs:84 with no injection point).

findings.title: Seven Vec fields use bare #[serde(default)] without null_to_default - inconsistent with the file's null-tolerance pattern (no observed failure)
findings.evidence:
models.rs:13-17 (the rule):
/// `#[serde(default)]` alone only covers a *missing* key — a key present with
/// a literal `null` still gets fed to `T`'s deserializer and fails for
/// non-`Option` fields (`invalid type: null, expected a string`/`a sequence`).
/// Graph emits explicit nulls for some apps (e.g. `displayName: null`, or a
/// `null` collection), so pair this with `#[serde(default)]` to stay tolerant.

Fields that do not follow it:
models.rs:179-180:    #[serde(default)]
    pub allowed_member_types: Vec<String>,
models.rs:448-449:    #[serde(default)]
    pub group_types: Vec<String>,
models.rs:693-696:    #[serde(default)]
    pub roles: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub granted_to_identities: Vec<SiteIdentitySet>,
models.rs:731-732:    #[serde(default)]
    pub roles: Vec<String>,
models.rs:910-911:    #[serde(default)]
    pub categories: Vec<String>,
models.rs:914-915:    #[serde(default)]
    pub supported_single_sign_on_modes: Vec<String>,
findings.rationale: The file's own regression tests (application_tolerates_explicit_null_fields, required_resource_access_tolerates_null_resource_access, directory_audit_log_tolerates_null_collections_and_type_alias) document that Graph has emitted `null` for collections the OData schema marks non-nullable, and each of those took down a whole tab. Every remaining bare-`Vec` field is one such null away from failing an entire paged response: a gallery template with `categories: null` breaks the Add-from-gallery list, a group with `groupTypes: null` breaks the group picker, a site permission with `roles: null` breaks the Sites.Selected panel and the tenant sweep. There is no reason for the inconsistency — the helper exists and costs nothing.
findings.proposal: Add `deserialize_with = "null_to_default"` to the seven fields and extend the doc comment at models.rs:11-17 to say new Vec/String fields should use it; a source-scanning test is optional (exempt `Paged.items`). No CHANGELOG entry needed (internal hardening).
findings.verifier_notes: The seven fields are real and bare (models.rs:179-180 allowed_member_types, :448-449 group_types, :693-696 roles/granted_to_identities, :731-732 roles, :910-911 categories, :914-915 supported_single_sign_on_modes); `Paged.items` (:972) is also bare but `value` is never null. However the doc block at models.rs:11-17 is guidance for fields Graph has been observed nulling, not a stated 'every Vec must' rule, and every existing regression test (:994-1130) cites an observed Graph null. No evidence is offered that Graph emits null for `groupTypes`, `roles`, `categories`, etc., so 'bug / medium' overstates it: this is cheap defensive hardening, not a demonstrated failure. Adding `deserialize_with = "null_to_default"` is harmless and consistent; the source-scanning test would need to exempt `Paged.items` and is optional.

findings.title: azure_roles: 'Log Analytics Reader' satisfaction set omits Reader/Contributor/Owner, so a Reader-only operator gets '?' instead of 'Have' despite the catalog saying '(or Reader)'
findings.evidence:
azure_roles.rs:43:
        "Log Analytics Reader" => &[LOG_ANALYTICS_READER, LOG_ANALYTICS_CONTRIBUTOR],

capabilities.rs:365-368 (same capability's guidance):
        remediation: "Usage analysis needs Microsoft Entra diagnostic settings exporting \
                      MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs to a Log Analytics workspace, the Log Analytics \
                      Reader Azure RBAC role (or Reader) on that workspace, plus the \
                      api.loganalytics.azure.com scope.",

docs/operator-rbac/OPERATOR-ROLES.md caveat 6: "the **Log Analytics Reader** Azure RBAC role (or **Reader**) on that workspace"

Microsoft 'Manage access to Log Analytics workspaces': "The `/read` permission is usually granted from a role that includes `*/read` or `*` permissions, such as the built-in Reader and Contributor roles." Log Analytics Reader itself is defined as `*/read` + query actions.
findings.rationale: The catalog and the operator doc both tell an operator that plain Reader on the workspace is enough (correct: Reader's `*/read` covers `Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces/query/read` and `.../query/*/read`), but the readiness checklist's Azure-RBAC enumeration will report a Reader-only operator as not holding the role. Two halves of the same catalog entry disagree, which is exactly the drift the module doc says the catalog exists to prevent. The conservative-set rationale in azure_roles.rs:7-12 is about not assuming control-plane roles grant Key Vault *data-plane* access; log query is a control-plane action, so that rationale does not apply here.
findings.proposal: Change the arm to `&[LOG_ANALYTICS_READER, LOG_ANALYTICS_CONTRIBUTOR, READER, CONTRIBUTOR, OWNER]` and add a test mirroring `control_plane_supersets_satisfy_reader_but_not_kv_data_plane`; extend the module doc to say control-plane `*/read` satisfies Log Analytics query.
findings.verifier_notes: Drift is real: azure_roles.rs:43 satisfies 'Log Analytics Reader' only with the two LA roles, while capabilities.rs:365-368 and OPERATOR-ROLES.md:185 both say '(or Reader)'. Microsoft confirms the docs are right: 'The /read permission is usually granted from a role that includes */read or * permissions, such as the built-in Reader and Contributor roles' and 'The standard Reader or Contributor roles, which include the */read action, override table-level access control' (learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/manage-access); Log Analytics Reader itself is `*/read` + Microsoft.Support/*. The module's conservatism rationale (azure_roles.rs:7-12) is about Key Vault data-plane, not control-plane query, so it does not apply. The consequence is overstated though: readiness.rs:167-200 (`azure_role_verdict`) never returns Missing for the Azure plane - a Reader-only operator sees Unknown ('No direct Azure role assignment found - you may still hold ... via a group'), not a false 'not holding the role'. So: real inconsistency, correct fix, low severity.

findings.title: CSP connect-src allowlists 13 Microsoft hosts the webview never contacts (and is missing the Exchange/Log Analytics hosts, harmlessly)
findings.evidence:
tauri.conf.json:25:
"csp": "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; connect-src 'self' https://graph.microsoft.com https://graph.microsoft.us https://dod-graph.microsoft.us https://microsoftgraph.chinacloudapi.cn https://login.microsoftonline.com https://login.microsoftonline.us https://login.partner.microsoftonline.cn https://*.vault.azure.net https://*.vault.usgovcloudapi.net https://*.vault.azure.cn https://management.azure.com https://management.usgovcloudapi.net https://management.chinacloudapi.cn; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'"

AGENTS.md:111: "**CSP governs the webview only** — backend reqwest egress needs no `connect-src` change."
`grep -n "gloo|reqwest|reqwasm" apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml` → no matches; the only `fetch` hits in web-rs/src are closure parameter names (audit_dashboard.rs:67 `fetch: Fetch`). cloud.rs also defines `exchange_resource()` (outlook.office365.com etc.) and `log_analytics_resource()` hosts, none of which appear in connect-src.
findings.rationale: Every Microsoft call goes through the Rust backend; the WASM frontend has no HTTP client and only invokes Tauri IPC. The connect-src list therefore grants the webview an outbound allowlist it never uses — a residual capability an XSS in the webview could use (e.g. to call Graph with a token it tricks the user into pasting) for no benefit. The fact that the list omits the Exchange and Log Analytics hosts (which the backend does call) without anything breaking is direct proof nothing in the webview depends on it, and also shows there is no test tying it to `CloudEnvironment`.
findings.proposal: Reduce to `connect-src 'self'` (Tauri 2 injects its own ipc origins). If a webview-side fetch is ever added, re-derive the list from `CloudEnvironment` and pin it with a repo_invariants test. Update the `.claude/skills/debug/SKILL.md` row that says 'only WASM-side fetches need CSP' to note there are none.
findings.verifier_notes: tauri.conf.json:25 allowlists 13 Microsoft hosts in connect-src. web-rs/Cargo.toml has no HTTP client (no gloo/reqwest/reqwasm; web-sys features omit Request/Response/fetch); the only `fetch` identifiers in web-rs/src are closure names. Sign-in uses the system browser + loopback listener (auth/service/loopback.rs:142 `webbrowser::open`), the updater is the Rust `tauri-plugin-updater` (src-tauri/Cargo.toml:32), and all Graph/ARM/KV/Exchange calls are backend reqwest. The list omits `exchange_resource()` and `log_analytics_resource()` hosts (cloud.rs) with nothing broken, which corroborates that nothing in the webview depends on it. AGENTS.md:111, .claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:28 and .claude/skills/debug/SKILL.md:69 all already state connect-src governs only WASM fetches, so reducing to `connect-src 'self'` is consistent with documented intent; Tauri 2 appends its own IPC origins. No `devCsp` is set, and the Trunk dev websocket is not in the current list either, so the proposal changes nothing there. Low severity is honest: it is residual attack surface, not an exploitable defect.

findings.title: redirect validator accepts `http://[::1]` and unbounded length, both of which Entra rejects
findings.rationale: The validator is explicitly the pre-flight that points at the offending row before the round trip. A row with `http://[::1]:5173/cb` or a 300-character URI passes the inline check and then fails the whole three-platform PATCH with a generic Graph 400, which is the experience the editor was built to avoid. The module doc scopes itself to 'security best practices', but nothing prevents adding Entra's two hard limits.
findings.proposal: Drop `"::1"` from the loopback set (keep a comment citing Microsoft's note so it is restored when supported) and reject URIs longer than 256 characters with a pointed message; update the tests at redirect.rs:382 and 424. Effect: the inline hint catches both before save.
findings.verifier_notes: Line citations are wrong (redirect.rs is 130 lines), but the substance is exact: the loopback set `matches!(host, "localhost" | "127.0.0.1" | "::1")` is at redirect.rs:46, and `http://[::1]:8400/cb` is asserted Ok at :73 and :115; there is no length check anywhere in the file. Microsoft's reply-URL page states 'The IPv6 loopback address ([::1]) isn't currently supported' and 'You can use a maximum of 256 characters for each redirect URI'. uri_list_editor.rs:15-22 confirms the validator's purpose is to flag the offending row before the backend `?`s out on the first bad URI. The validator is also used by restore.rs:67/466, sso/mod.rs:138/307/695/1712 and authentication.rs:87, so both checks would apply uniformly (the 256 limit also applies to SAML reply URLs per Microsoft). The userinfo test at :96-101 (`http://[::1]@evil.com/cb`) remains rejected. Enhancement, low.

findings.title: SelectedScopeLevel::key() has no callers and no test binding it to the serde spelling it claims to be
findings.rationale: The doc promises the wire form equals `key()`, but the wire form is produced independently by `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` and nothing asserts the two agree; renaming a variant would silently split them. `key()` itself is dead code today. Either the function should go, or the invariant it documents should be pinned.
findings.proposal: Prefer: add a test `for level in [...] { assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(level).unwrap(), serde_json::json!(level.key())) }`, so `key()` becomes the pinned spelling the doc says it is (and can be used by the DTO layer). Otherwise delete `key()` and reword the doc to name serde as the single spelling.
findings.verifier_notes: scoping.rs:244-245 doc claims 'Serializes as its SelectedScopeLevel::key', :247 derives serde with `rename_all = "snake_case"`, :270-277 defines `key()`. Grep across apps/ and crates/ finds no caller of `SelectedScopeLevel::key()` (only DOM `ev.key()` hits); the DTO (dto/sharepoint.rs:238 `pub level: SelectedScopeLevel`) serializes through serde, and no test compares `serde_json::to_value(level)` with `key()` (tests at :820-940 cover level mapping, `breaks_inheritance`, `selected_scope_accepts`). `ScopeKind::capability_key` (:465) is tested at :929/:1072-1080, so the sibling asymmetry is real. Proposal (pin with a round-trip test, or delete and reword the doc) is correct and small.

findings.title: disabledByMicrosoftStatus is not modeled on Application/ServicePrincipal — apps Microsoft has disabled for policy violation are invisible to the audit
findings.evidence:
models.rs:26-75 `pub struct Application { ... }` and models.rs:127-173 `pub struct ServicePrincipal { ... }` have no `disabled_by_microsoft_status` field; `grep -rn "disabledByMicrosoft\|disabled_by_microsoft" --include=*.rs --include=*.md .` → no matches.

Adding an `Option<String>` with `#[serde(default)]` to `Application` is IPC-compatible (shared struct, additive). Needs a table-driven rule test and a CHANGELOG entry per AGENTS.md.

findings.title: federation: audiences accepts more than one value although the code comment and Graph say exactly one

Small, correct hardening; low.

findings.rationale: The module doc says all three feedback mechanisms (403 hints, 'Requires:' labels, readiness checklist) read from this one table so guidance never drifts. Two consented-scope features the app actually probes — SCIM provisioning read and claims-mapping-policy write (the SAML custom-claims step in create_saml_sso_application) — have no catalog row, so the checklist cannot show their scope half and a 403 on the claims-policy POST carries no role guidance. `probe_scope` already knows how to probe them; only the rows are missing.
findings.proposal: Add two capabilities: `provisioning_read` (label 'SCIM provisioning (read)', roles Application Administrator / Cloud Application Administrator / GA, scopes ["Synchronization.Read.All"], scope_feature Some("sync")) and `claims_policy_write` (label 'Claims-mapping policies', roles Application Administrator / Cloud Application Administrator / GA, scopes ["Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration"], scope_feature Some("policy_write")), and splice `forbidden_remediation(.., "claims_policy_write")` into the SSO claims step. Update OPERATOR-ROLES.md's built-in-equivalent line.
findings.verifier_notes: capabilities.rs:125-404 has no entry with `scope_feature: Some("sync")` or `Some("policy_write")`, yet both are real consent features: state.rs:537/540 in `consent_scopes_for`, the `sync_token` adapter (state.rs:427-431, `.with_sync_token` :478) used by enterprise_application.rs provisioning reads, and `ensure_policy_write_token` at sso/mod.rs:158 and :1637 with the UI requesting consent for "policy_write" (sso_wizard_dialog.rs:223, sso_tab.rs:682). readiness.rs:276-279 already whitelists both as Graph features in `probe_scope`. No `forbidden_remediation` call exists in sso/mod.rs (all callers: enterprise_application.rs:315, sharepoint.rs:166, managed_identity.rs:402, permission_tester.rs:1026, keyvault_rbac.rs:66). OPERATOR-ROLES.md:158-166 lists both scopes. One correction: the checklist does not currently 'probe' them - readiness.rs:54-60 derives the feature set from CAPABILITIES, so today they are simply absent; adding the two rows is sufficient. The proposed role lists should be checked against Microsoft's least-privileged-role tables for claimsMappingPolicy and synchronization before landing.

findings.title: Exchange transport replays non-idempotent cmdlets (New-/Remove-) on 5xx and network errors
findings.rationale: Commit 8fb1ac7 ("stop replaying writes") added RetryReason/RetryClass to with_retries so a POST that hit a connection reset or 502 after the server committed is not replayed; Graph, ARM and Key Vault all route through with_retries + retry_class_for. The Exchange transport never used with_retries (it open-codes attempt/delay_ms/MAX_RETRIES), so it escaped both the fix and the repo invariant `every_retry_call_site_derives_its_idempotency_class` (trust.rs:160: files without `with_retries(` are skipped). Every cmdlet here is a POST, and the crate's own writes are not replay-safe: a replayed `New-ManagementRoleAssignment` (rbac.rs:232-246) after a committed write fails as a duplicate, which grants.rs:118 records as `failed to assign` -> role_in_place=false -> targets_safe_to_strip keeps the org-wide grant, so the scope silently has no effect (the exact failure mode RoleStep::SameRoleAs was added to prevent). A replayed `Remove-ApplicationAccessPolicy` (rbac.rs:277-284) after a committed delete returns a not-found 400, which aap_migration.rs:371-376 reports as `failed to remove legacy policy` and status `partial` while the policy is actually gone. `New-ServicePrincipal`, `New-ManagementScope`, `New-DistributionGroup`, `Remove-ManagementRoleAssignment` and `Remove-DistributionGroup` have the same exposure.
findings.proposal: Same as proposed, with one adjustment: name the helper `retry_class_for(` (taking the cmdlet name), not `retry_class_for_cmdlet(` — trust.rs:167 matches the literal `retry_class_for(`, so once transport.rs contains `with_retries(` the differently named helper would make the crate an offender. Extend the trust.rs invariant so a crate whose transport calls `.send()` without `with_retries(` is flagged instead of skipped.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified. transport.rs:168-190 retries a reqwest send error and :263-271 retries every 429/5xx unconditionally, for every cmdlet (all POSTs). `git log -S with_retries -- crates/azapptoolkit-exchange` is empty: the exchange transport never adopted `with_retries`/`RetryClass`; 8fb1ac7 touched transport.rs only for the nextLink same-origin check. trust.rs:163 skips any file without `with_retries(`, so the invariant is silently vacuous for this crate, while http_retry.rs:1-3 claims Exchange is among the unified clients. Consequence chain checks out: grants.rs:118 `failed to assign` -> role_in_place=false -> targets_safe_to_strip keeps the org-wide grant; aap_migration.rs:371-376 reports `partial`. Severity downgraded from high: Exchange objects are name-keyed, so a replayed New-*/Remove-* fails as duplicate/not-found rather than double-committing (no analog of the orphaned-secret outcome that motivated 8fb1ac7); the result is a false failure that is reported (grants.rs:286 warns 'scoping is NOT effective') and self-heals on re-run via RoleStep::AlreadyScoped (rbac.rs / targets.rs plan). Still a real invariant gap worth fixing. Membership mutators are already idempotent (groups.rs:77-108 swallow already-/not-a-member), so classing them Idempotent is right.

findings.title: Mid-pagination errors are flattened to Protocol, losing auth/throttle classification and the re-auth-fatal signal
findings.rationale: The comment justifies the reclassification only for NotFound (so invoke_optional cannot read a 404 on page 2 as an empty collection), but the arm catches every error. A `Token` error carrying `refresh_missing`/`not_signed_in` from the bearer() call on page 2 becomes `protocol_error`, so `is_reauth_fatal` is false and a long-running fan-out (the audit's Exchange probes, bulk remediations) keeps going on a dead session, contrary to the AGENTS.md invariant that every long-running loop stops on a re-auth-fatal code. Likewise a 401/403/429 on page 2 no longer matches the audit's Exchange breaker or ui_hint branches; the operator sees a generic protocol error instead of the stale-token guidance.
findings.proposal: Narrow the arm: reclassify to Protocol only `ExchangeError::NotFound(_)` and `ExchangeError::Api { body, .. } if is_not_found_body(&body)`; return every other error unchanged (they already prevent a truncated Ok). Add two wiremock tests: page-2 401 -> `ExchangeError::Unauthorized`; page-2 StaticTokenProvider failure with code refresh_missing -> `ui_code() == "refresh_missing"`.
findings.verifier_notes: transport.rs:78-83 reclassifies EVERY page>1 error to Protocol; the adjacent comment (:71-77) and invoke_optional's doc (:131-135) justify it only for NotFound. `bearer()` is called inside send_core (:155) on every page, so a `Token{refresh_missing}` on page 2 is realistic and becomes `protocol_error` (error.rs:79) instead of passing through via error.rs:76-78 -> `is_reauth_fatal` false (audit.rs:68, bulk.rs:73 rely on it). audit.rs:1565-1570's breaker matches only Unauthorized|Forbidden{..}, so a page-2 401/403 also misses it. The only pinned test (client/tests.rs:709) covers the 404 case. Proposal is correct and minimal.

findings.title: ExchangeError is hand-rolled outside core::http_error_enum! and has no error-conformance test, contradicting AGENTS.md
findings.rationale: Graph, ARM and Key Vault errors are generated by the macro; ARM and Key Vault additionally carry `tests/error_conformance.rs` pinning that every variant's `ui_code`/`is_retryable` agree with core. The Exchange enum is the fourth copy the macro's own doc says the refactor 'did not reach', kept separate because `Forbidden` carries `had_diagnostics`. The `.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:24` wording ("Graph/ARM/Key Vault error taxonomy") is honest about the gap but AGENTS.md is not, and there is nothing pinning that Exchange's `ui_code` table (error.rs:64-81) stays aligned with the shared codes the frontend branches on.
findings.proposal: Take option (b): add crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/tests/error_conformance.rs mirroring the ARM one (every variant -> ui_code; is_retryable == is_retryable_code(ui_code); Token passthrough of refresh_missing/not_signed_in), and amend AGENTS.md:108 to 'Graph/ARM/Key Vault error taxonomy from core::http_error_enum! (Exchange keeps a struct-variant Forbidden and is pinned by its own conformance test)'.
findings.verifier_notes: error.rs:7-48 is hand-rolled; `Forbidden { detail, had_diagnostics }` cannot be expressed by the macro, whose `extra` arm accepts only single-field tuple variants (http_error.rs:56-62, 104-108), so option (a) needs macro surgery plus rewriting every `Forbidden { .. }` matcher (audit.rs:1567, ui_hint). AGENTS.md:108 is unqualified while .claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:24 says 'Graph/ARM/Key Vault'; http_error.rs:1-2 says 'four typed clients' then lists three. Only arm/ and keyvault/ have tests/error_conformance.rs; the exchange crate has no tests/ dir and dto's tests cover AuthError only. Severity lowered: the ui_code table (error.rs:64-81) currently matches the macro's byte-for-byte, so the risk is future drift, not a live defect. Option (b) is the realistic fix.

findings.title: Tenant-wide list reads that gate the irreversible group delete use invoke_optional, so a misclassified 400 reads as 'no references'
findings.rationale: invoke_optional exists so an `-Identity` that does not resolve reads as None. An identity-less `Get-ManagementScope`/`Get-ApplicationAccessPolicy` has no object to be missing: an empty tenant returns 200 with `value: []`. Routing them through invoke_optional means any 400 whose sanitized body happens to contain "not found"/"couldn't be found" (a parameter set that cannot be resolved, a cmdlet the caller's role does not expose, an EXO wording change) becomes `Ok(vec![])`. `retired_scope_groups` then reports `reference_check_complete: true` and `delete_exchange_scope_group` re-checks live through the same path and finds zero references - exactly the 'unknown read as clean' the docs say must never happen. `list_service_principals` (rbac.rs:59-64) already uses invoke_command, so the two list-alls are also inconsistent with their sibling.
findings.proposal: Switch `list_management_scopes` and `get_application_access_policies` to `invoke_command` (keep `get_management_scope`/`get_service_principal`/`get_group`, which take an Identity, on invoke_optional). Add a wiremock test: `Get-ManagementScope` with `{}` returning 400 "...not found..." must be `Err(ExchangeError::Api{..})`, not `Ok(vec![])`. Optionally tighten `is_not_found_body` to require the cmdlet-shaped phrasings ("couldn't be found", "ManagementObjectNotFound") and drop the bare "not found".
findings.verifier_notes: rbac.rs:220-225 and :270-275 route the identity-less list-alls through invoke_optional; transport.rs:144 maps any `Api` whose body passes is_not_found_body to Ok(vec![]), and error.rs:158 matches bare 'not found'. list_service_principals (rbac.rs:59-64) uses invoke_command, so the siblings are inconsistent. scope_group.rs:354 `readable = scopes.is_ok() && policies.is_ok()` and :438-443 treat an Ok(empty) as 'no references' before an irreversible Remove-DistributionGroup (:457). Introduced in 0389543 with no rationale comment; references.rs:11-17 explicitly says an unknown must never read as clean. The trigger (a 4xx with 'not found' text on an identity-less list) is hypothetical, but the fix is one line per call site and the consequence is irreversible, so medium is fair.

findings.title: DN set comparisons are case-sensitive in the consolidation path but case-folded in the post-write proof, so a landed repoint can be reported as a mismatch
findings.evidence:
repoint: !(source_dns.len() == 1 && source_dns[0] == managed_dn),
-- targets.rs:480-486 (same file): "Exchange Online normalises the casing of the DNs it returns ... a case-sensitive HashSet comparison of 'what I wrote' against 'what the server reports' can differ on a write that DID land." rbac.rs:197 `if wanted_groups.folded_dns() != landed.folded_dns()`; but scope_group.rs:540 `g.complete && g.dns == group_dns_in_filter(wanted)` and scope_group.rs:744 `&& source_dns[0] == dn`.
findings.rationale: The crate documents (targets.rs:480-486, aap_migration.rs:288-292) that Exchange echoes DNs in its own casing and that the post-write proof must fold case for that reason, yet `plan_consolidation` and both desktop consumers of the same DN sets compare raw strings. Consequences: (1) in `reconcile_scope_filter` (aap_migration) the repoint passes rbac.rs's folded proof, then `scope_filter_agrees` compares unfolded and returns `scope_filter_mismatch`, refusing an app whose scope is correct; (2) in `move_exchange_scope_to_managed_group`, a scope already on the managed group with a case-different echoed DN skips the early return at :744, is 'repointed' again, and `retired_scope_groups(&source_dns)` then lists the app's own managed group as a retired cleanup candidate (only the downstream `identity.matches(&managed)` guard in delete stops the deletion).
findings.proposal: Add one helper in the crate, e.g. `ScopeGroups::same_groups_as(&self, other: &ScopeGroups) -> bool` (both complete and `folded_dns()` equal) plus `pub fn same_dn(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool` (ASCII-fold), and use them at targets.rs:716, scope_group.rs:540 and :744. Extend `consolidation_is_a_no_op_when_the_scope_is_already_managed` with a case-variant DN. Consider `to_lowercase()` instead of `to_ascii_lowercase()` in `folded_dns` so a `CN=Zürich…` DN folds too.
findings.verifier_notes: All three sites verified raw: targets.rs:716 `source_dns[0] == managed_dn`, scope_group.rs:540 `g.dns == group_dns_in_filter(wanted)`, scope_group.rs:744 `source_dns[0] == dn`; versus folded comparisons at rbac.rs:197 and aap_migration.rs:288-293 (both citing Exchange re-casing DNs as the reason). In every case one side is a DN parsed from Exchange's echoed RecipientFilter and the other a DN from a group object (grants.rs:162, aap_migration.rs:200, scope_group.rs:742), which is exactly the pair targets.rs:480-486 says can differ. Consequence (1) is real: reconcile_scope_filter (scope_group.rs:575-619) would issue a redundant repoint, pass rbac.rs's folded proof, then fail `scope_filter_agrees(f, wanted)` at :612 with scope_filter_mismatch, blocking a correct migration. Failure direction is safe (refusal/redundant write, never widening), and the trigger rests on the crate's own claim about Exchange casing rather than a pinned observation, so medium rather than high. The existing test at targets.rs:1353 uses identical casing and would not catch it.

findings.title: exchange-scoping.md still documents the deleted value-only scoping functions and a moved helper path
findings.evidence:
the value-only `exchange_role_for_permission` exists for the probe/badge paths and is unambiguous
-- :49 "it widens `is_scopable_exchange_permission`"; :123-124 "`held_orgwide_mail_grants` filters with the **value-only** `is_scopable_exchange_permission`"; :141 "sanitized (`client.rs::sanitize_error_body`)".
-- roles.rs:11-13: "Only the resource-aware forms exist to re-export now: the value-only ones were deleted"; repo_invariants/commands.rs:130-134 pins `exchange_role_for_permission` / `is_scopable_exchange_permission` as GONE; sanitize_error_body now lives at client/transport.rs:293.
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md says to read this deep-dive before editing the subsystem. It tells the reader that two functions exist and are the right tool for the probe/badge paths, while a repo-invariant test fails the build if anyone reintroduces them; a contributor following the doc will write code the test rejects. The `client.rs::sanitize_error_body` path is stale since the client was split into client/{transport,rbac,groups}.rs.
findings.proposal: Rewrite :29-34 to name `exchange_role_for_resource_permission` / `is_scopable_exchange_resource_permission` and state that the value-only forms were removed (link the invariant). At :49 and :123-124 name the resource-aware gate and, for `held_orgwide_mail_grants`, describe what it actually does today. Change :141 to `client/transport.rs::sanitize_error_body`.
findings.verifier_notes: exchange-scoping.md:33 names `exchange_role_for_permission`, :49 and :123-124 name `is_scopable_exchange_permission`, :141 names `client.rs::sanitize_error_body`. roles.rs:11-17 re-exports only the resource-aware forms and says the value-only ones were deleted; repo_invariants/commands.rs:130-134 fails the build if either name reappears; sanitize_error_body is at client/transport.rs:293 since the client split (client.rs:8-10). The :123-124 paragraph is stale in substance too: held_orgwide_mail_grants (mail_scopes.rs:67-70) now filters with is_scopable_exchange_resource_permission, so EXO's own Mail.* grants are excluded rather than 'entering the org-wide set' — the causal story it tells no longer happens via that path. AGENTS.md directs contributors to this doc before editing the subsystem, so medium stands.

findings.title: set_management_scope_filter's pre-write refusals, ensure_management_scope's create path and the transport's 5xx/network paths have no wiremock tests
findings.rationale: These refusals are the only thing standing between a caller and 'widen every role assignment on the scope to the whole organization'; the comments say 'no caller does' is not a property the function may rely on, yet nothing proves the refusal happens before the cmdlet is issued. Similarly `ensure_management_scope` (create-only, the invariant AGENTS.md names) has no test that the Get-first/New-second sequence runs or that an existing scope suppresses `New-ManagementScope`. The transport's retry-then-`Server`/`Network`/`Throttled` terminal mappings (transport.rs:273-282) are likewise untested; only the 429-then-200 happy path is.
findings.proposal: As proposed, but give the 5xx/429 mocks a `Retry-After: 0` header (sleep_before_retry honours it exactly, http_retry.rs:81-89) so a 4x503 test does not spend ~7 s of real jittered backoff; the existing 429 test at :492-496 already uses this trick.
findings.verifier_notes: client/tests.rs mocks only statuses 200/400/401/403/404/429 (no 5xx), has no test naming New-ManagementScope or ensure_management_scope, no `.expect(0)`, and no assertion on ExchangeError::Server/Network/Throttled (only Protocol at :698/:734). The three set_management_scope_filter tests (:267, :314, :364) cover post-write behaviour, not the pre-write refusals at rbac.rs:115-136. Lowered to low: the parser behind the refusals is well pinned in targets.rs (e.g. :1273 incomplete parse, :958 lookalike/blank DN), so what is unpinned is only the ordering (refuse before the cmdlet) and the terminal mappings at transport.rs:273-282.

findings.title: Desktop commands/exchange/tests.rs duplicates the crate's pure-function tests in the slowest-to-build crate
findings.rationale: verdict.rs's module doc explains the logic was moved into the crate precisely so it is testable without a Tauri State; the desktop tests that predate the move were left behind (a few are marked '---- relocated ----' in the crate, the rest were copied not moved). Roughly 15 of the 33 desktop tests (lines 81-190, 234-350, 363-470, 532-590) exercise only crate-pure functions with their own fixtures, so every rule now has two fixture sets that can drift, and they run only in `apps/desktop/src-tauri`, which cannot compile without WebKitGTK and is the slowest `just test-crate` target.
findings.proposal: Delete the duplicates from the desktop tests and keep only those exercising desktop glue (`resolve_mail_scopes_audit_cached`, `retired_groups_note_*`, `scope_filter_agrees` via `a_divergent_or_unreadable_scope_filter_is_never_agreement`, `migration_keeps_the_policy_*`, `scope_and_group_names_*`, `alias_is_safe_and_bounded`). Where a desktop test covers an angle the crate test does not (e.g. `reconcile_lets_a_surviving_ews_grant_defeat_every_scope` already has a twin), fold the extra assertion into the crate test first.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified duplication. Desktop tests.rs has 29 `#[test]`s (not 33); roughly 14 exercise only crate-pure functions with their own fixtures: targets_from_declared (:81, :109, :124 vs targets.rs:801/820/851), filter_targets_by_value (:141, :179, :298 vs targets.rs:1173-1180), targets_safe_to_strip (:305, :319 vs targets.rs:1160), group_dns_in_filter (:325, :339 vs targets.rs:1200/1228), verdict_from_rows/row_grants_permission (:363, :380, :417 vs verdict.rs:424/392/414), aap_verdict_for (:440, :458, :466 vs verdict.rs:457), reconcile_orgwide_grant (:234-297 vs verdict.rs:626/561), policies_safe_to_remove (:513, :548 vs targets.rs:1184-1190), mailbox_resources_complete (:564 vs targets.rs:1194), two_permission_values_can_share_one_exchange_role (:532 vs targets.rs:1119). verdict.rs:701 marks a '---- relocated ----' block, confirming the rest were copied.
