Glue tests worth keeping: :149, :162, :213, :472, :591, :639. Cleanup value is real but small, hence low.

findings.title: AccessRight/ScopeType are stringly typed; the two RestrictAccess comparisons already disagree on trimming
findings.evidence:
#[serde(rename = "AccessRight", default)]
pub access_right: Option<String>,
-- aap.rs:60-61: `match policy.access_right.as_deref().map(str::trim) { Some(right) if right.eq_ignore_ascii_case("RestrictAccess") => {}`
-- verdict.rs:131-133: `p.access_right.as_deref().is_some_and(|r| r.eq_ignore_ascii_case("RestrictAccess"))`
-- verdict.rs:34-42: `matches!(r.scope_type ... "" | "notapplicable" | "organizationconfig" | "organizationscope" | "organization")`
findings.rationale: The RestrictAccess-vs-DenyAccess distinction is the single most consequential decision in the migration (a DenyAccess policy must never be inverted) and it is spelled as a case-insensitive string comparison in two modules that each had to independently remember to trim and casefold (the aap.rs doc notes 'this one did not' for an earlier casefold miss). models.rs already has the tolerant-deserializer pattern (`ps_access_check`, `ps_optional_bool`) for exactly this shape.
findings.proposal: As proposed (tolerant `AapAccessRight` enum via deserialize_with, `is_restrict()`, used by group_policies_for_migration and aap_verdict_for), plus a test asserting a padded/odd-cased AccessRight yields the same verdict in both modules. ExoScopeType is optional polish.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: aap.rs:60-61 and verdict.rs:131-133 each spell the RestrictAccess check as a case-insensitive string compare; verdict.rs:34-42 matches ScopeType literals. Two overstatements: (1) the aap.rs:49 note 'this one did not' refers to the AppId comparison, not AccessRight, so it is not evidence of an AccessRight casefold miss; (2) both sites are already pinned case-insensitive (aap.rs:283, verdict.rs:489). The one concrete drift the reviewer missed and that supports the refactor: aap.rs:60 trims before comparing, verdict.rs:133 does not, so a padded `" RestrictAccess "` is migratable in one module and reported org-wide in the other. Refactor is sound but not medium.

findings.title: Cargo.toml declares unused `url` and `tokio` dependencies and a per-crate `bytes` instead of a workspace dependency
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md: 'Workspace dependency - add to [workspace.dependencies], use name.workspace = true ... Dependencies are a cost'. `url` and `tokio` in [dependencies] are dead (tokio is only needed by the `#[tokio::test]`s, and it is already re-declared with features under [dev-dependencies]); `bytes` is the one HTTP-client dependency not centralised, so a version bump is a four-file edit.
findings.proposal: Remove `url` and `tokio` from [dependencies] (keep the dev-dependency), add `bytes = "1"` to the root [workspace.dependencies] and switch the four crates to `bytes.workspace = true`. Consider adding `cargo udeps` (or `cargo machete`) to `just verify-full` to catch this class.
findings.verifier_notes: Cargo.toml:13 `tokio` and :18 `url` in [dependencies]; grep for `url::`, `Url`, `tokio` over crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src excluding client/tests.rs finds nothing (sleeps come from core::http_retry), and tokio is already a dev-dependency with features (:24). `bytes = "1"` is declared per-crate in arm/exchange/graph/keyvault Cargo.toml:14 and absent from root [workspace.dependencies]. No udeps/machete in justfile or workflows; [workspace.lints.rust] has only unsafe_code. Removing the two deps is safe (nothing in src references them).

findings.title: No cleanup path for an app's orphaned management scope / SP pointer / managed group after decommissioning
findings.rationale: An operator who removes an app's scoped Exchange access (or decommissions the app) is left with an orphaned `app_scope_<appId>` scope, an SP pointer and a managed group. Because `ensure_management_scope` is create-only by design, re-granting later with a different group set hits the `scope_group_mismatch` refusal (grants.rs:245-258) until someone deletes the stale scope by hand in PowerShell - the one thing this toolkit exists to replace. The crate already has the enumeration primitives (`get_role_assignments`, `list_management_scopes`, `references_to_group`) needed to prove the scope is unreferenced before deleting it.
findings.proposal: Optional feature: an opt-in, separately confirmed teardown (proving zero Get-ManagementRoleAssignment rows reference the scope and zero assignments remain for the pointer) modelled on delete_exchange_scope_group's live re-checks. Do not present it as unblocking re-grants — that path already exists via 'Move to managed group'.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: no Remove-ManagementScope/Remove-ServicePrincipal anywhere; grants.rs:471-473 pushes the 'left in place' warning; ensure_management_scope is create-only (rbac.rs:75-77). But leaving them is a deliberate, user-facing decision — the frontend copy at exchange_scoping_section.rs:614 says the scope and group are 'left in place so the scoping can be re-applied'. The central claim that a later re-grant with a different group set is blocked 'until someone deletes the stale scope by hand in PowerShell' is wrong: the scope_group_mismatch message (grants.rs:245-258) directs to 'Move to managed group', and move_exchange_scope_to_managed_group (scope_group.rs:685+) repoints the scope via set_management_scope_filter inside the toolkit. What remains is an orphan-cleanup gap on decommissioning, which is a feature request, not a medium bug.

findings.title: Stale history comments and broken intra-doc links in the crate's module docs
findings.rationale: The transport has clearly been exercised live (client.rs:50-52 cites captured ExchangeOnlineManagement traffic, transport.rs:205-208 describes observed NUL-padded 403 bodies), so the 'verify during the spike' note now reads as an open question about a path that works. The line-count history is wrong since the split. The three intra-doc links resolve to nothing in this crate and produce `rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links` warnings under `cargo doc`.
findings.proposal: Replace the NOTE with a one-line statement that `beta/InvokeCommand` is the endpoint the ExchangeOnlineManagement module uses (versus the per-cmdlet `v2.0/<Cmdlet>` REST routes Microsoft documents separately). Trim the two 'lived in a 3,100-line file' paragraphs to 'moved out of the command layer so it is testable without a Tauri State'. Change the three links to plain code spans naming the module: `commands::exchange::mail_scopes::legacy_aap_scope`.
findings.verifier_notes: client.rs:26-28 NOTE reads as an open question though client.rs:50-52 and transport.rs:205-208, :42 describe observed live traffic. verdict.rs:9-10 ('~3,100 lines'), references.rs:9-10 ('2871-line'), commands/exchange/mod.rs:124 ('one 3 000-line file') are history since the split. verdict.rs:102-103 and :213-214 link [`legacy_aap_scope`] and :168-169 [`resolve_mail_scopes`], both defined in the desktop crate (mail_scopes.rs:23, :94), so they are broken intra-doc links. No `cargo doc` in justfile or CI and no rustdoc lint in [workspace.lints], so these are warnings only under a manual doc build — low is right.

findings.title: Root re-exports of targets::* are dead: callers import through the module path
findings.evidence:
pub use targets::{
    ConsolidationPlan, ExchangeTarget, NoScopablePermission, Refusal, ResourceRoles, ScopeGroups,
    UnrewritableFilter, count_member_of_group, exchange_target, filter_targets_by_value,
    group_dns_in_filter, mailbox_resources_complete, plan_consolidation, policies_safe_to_remove,
-- apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/exchange/mod.rs:26-31 imports `azapptoolkit_exchange::targets::{ExchangeTarget, Refusal, RoleStep, ...}`; mod.rs:43-46 imports aap/client items from the root; `verdict` and `references` have no root re-export at all.
findings.rationale: Three of the crate's modules are reachable two ways and two only one way, so every item has an arbitrary canonical path. `RoleStep`/`plan_role_assignments` (added later) are not in the root list, which is how the desktop ended up on the module path for targets while staying on the root for aap. Root re-exports also hide which module a symbol belongs to, which matters here because the modules are the documented seams (pure decisions vs client).
findings.proposal: Drop the `pub use targets::{...}` block (and optionally the `aap::{...}` one), keeping root re-exports only for the crate's entry types (`ExchangeClient`, `ExchangeError`, `Result`, `EXCHANGE_BASE`, `member_of_group_filter`) and the scoping constants; update mod.rs:43-46 to `azapptoolkit_exchange::aap::{...}`. Pure mechanical change, checked by `just check`.
findings.verifier_notes: lib.rs:35-41 re-exports 22 targets items; no external caller uses any via the crate root: desktop mod.rs:26-31 and graph_roles.rs import `azapptoolkit_exchange::targets::{...}`, mod.rs:43-46 takes aap/client items from the root, dto/state/audit/permission_tester use only ExchangeClient/ExchangeError/models/verdict. No `crate::<item>` (non-`crate::targets::`) use inside the crate either. RoleStep/plan_role_assignments are absent from the root list, and verdict/references have no root re-export, confirming the arbitrary-canonical-path point. Mechanical cleanup; low.

findings.title: Exchange transport classifies retries from raw status codes rather than the shared is_retryable() policy (the method itself is live via dto)
findings.rationale: The method exists for parity with the macro-generated clients, but nothing in this crate or the desktop calls it, and the transport does not route its own classification through it, so the shared `is_retryable_code` policy is not actually what governs Exchange retries. This is the same symptom as the with_retries finding: the shared policy exists but the transport bypasses it.
findings.proposal: Do not remove is_retryable. When send_core moves onto with_retries (finding 0), classify each attempt via `err.is_retryable()` so the shared policy governs, and pin agreement in the exchange error_conformance test from finding 2(b).
findings.verifier_notes: The headline claim is false: crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/lib.rs:151 `ui_error_from!(ExchangeError, hint)` expands to `retryable: err.is_retryable()` (:132), so the method runs on every ExchangeError -> UiError conversion and populates the `retryable` flag the frontend sees; removing it (the fallback proposal) breaks the dto build. The reviewer's grep missed the macro call site. The second half — transport.rs:225/:263 classify from the raw status rather than through the shared policy — is true but is finding 0 restated.

findings.title: list_all_sites drops its truncation signal, so a >5000-site tenant's Sites.Selected sweep is reported and cached as complete
findings.rationale: Every other capped tenant-wide scan in this crate (`list_applications_all`, `list_saml_sso_service_principals`, `collect_all_pages_capped`) returns `(rows, truncated)` precisely so a caller cannot present a partial view as complete. `list_all_sites` is the exception: it silently truncates to `max` and returns a bare Vec. The sweep therefore has no way to know it stopped at site 5000; it sets `total_sites = sites.len()`, `is_complete()` returns true, the result is cached for the audit TTL, and `AppSiteAccessDto::from_sweep` reads an empty match list as 'no per-site grants'. On a tenant with more than 5000 sites, an app's Sites.Selected grants on any site past the cap are invisible and the panel affirmatively says the app has none — the exact 'coverage is never overstated' invariant the surrounding code and sharepoint-selected.md promise. There is no `total_sites >= MAX_SITES_PER_SWEEP` check anywhere in the command or the frontend (grep of web-rs for MAX_SITES/5000 finds nothing).
findings.proposal: Change `list_all_sites` to return `Result<(Vec<Site>, bool)>` where the bool is `page.next_link.is_some() || pages hit MAX_PAGES` when the cap stops the walk (mirror `collect_all_pages_capped`'s tail logic, or add a scoped `collect_pages_from_capped` helper and reuse it here). In `sweep_site_permissions` bind the flag, add `truncated: bool` to `SiteSweepResult`/`AppSiteAccessDto` (additive field), fold it into `is_complete()` (`!cancelled && sites_failed == 0 && !truncated`), skip caching when truncated, and render the existing `IndexCapNotice` pattern in the Sites tab. Add a wiremock test where page 1 already exceeds `max` and assert `truncated == true`.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified. crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/sharepoint.rs:74-107: `list_all_sites(max)` loops `while out.len() < max`, then `out.truncate(max); Ok(out)` — no truncation flag, unlike `collect_all_pages_capped` (transport.rs:229-262) which returns `(Vec, bool)`. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sharepoint.rs:842-845 binds `sites`/`total = sites.len()`; :977-992 builds `SiteSweepResult{total_sites: total, cancelled, sites_failed}` and caches when `!cancelled && sites_failed == 0`; crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sharepoint.rs:130-132 `is_complete()` = `!cancelled && sites_failed == 0`. No `truncated` field exists on `SiteSweepResult`/`AppSiteAccessDto` (dto/sharepoint.rs:64-96). Frontend: web-rs/src/components/app_site_access_panel.rs:242 keys the 'no grants' wording off `is_complete()`; web-rs/src/views/resource_access/sites.rs:113-131 prints 'scanned X of Y' with only failed/cancelled qualifiers; grep of web-rs for MAX_SITES/5000 finds nothing. The only acknowledgement is the comment at commands/sharepoint.rs:756-758 ('Raise if a user legitimately hits it') — but nothing tells the user or the code that it was hit. This directly violates the repo's own stated invariants (sharepoint.rs:825-828 'coverage is never overstated'; AGENTS.md 'empty = no grants only when is_complete()'; 'a truncated run is never cached'). docs/architecture/sharepoint-selected.md never mentions the cap. `IndexCapNotice` exists (web-rs/src/components/index_cap_notice.rs:48) for reuse. Existing test `list_all_sites_follows_next_link_on_sharepoint_scope` (tests/sharepoint.rs:154) does not cover the cap. High is honest: a cached, affirmative 'no per-site grants' answer in a security-posture view on >5000-site tenants.
findings.recheck_notes: Failing path traced end to end and nothing upstream prevents it. crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/sharepoint.rs:74-107: `list_all_sites` pages `/sites?search=*&$top=200` while `out.len() < max`; on a tenant with >5000 enumerable sites page 25 brings `out.len()` to exactly 5000, the `while` condition fails, `page.next_link` (still `Some`) is dropped, `out.truncate(max)` is a no-op and a bare `Vec` of 5000 is returned with no signal. The only other exit that guards paging (`pages >= MAX_PAGES` at :96) is a hard error, not a truncation, and at 200/page it sits at 40 000 sites, so the item cap is the sole silent-truncation path. Caller apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sharepoint.rs:842-846 binds `sites`, sets `total = sites.len()` (=5000), and :977-992 builds `SiteSweepResult { total_sites: total, sites_failed, cancelled }` and caches it under `CacheKind::Audit` when `!cancelled && sites_failed == 0` — neither field is affected by the cap, so the truncated sweep IS cached for the 60-min audit TTL. `get_cached_site_sweep` (:1005) and `get_app_site_access` (:1043) then serve it; both are in `generate_handler![]` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:208-211), so this is the shipped build, not tests/demo. crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sharepoint.rs:130 `is_complete()` = `!cancelled && sites_failed == 0` returns true, and apps/desktop/web-rs/src/components/app_site_access_panel.rs:242-252 renders the affirmative empty state 'No per-site grants. This app reaches no site through the Sites.Selected model' when `complete`. The Sites tab summary (views/resource_access/sites.rs:112-135) prints 'scanned 5000 of 5000 sites' with no partial-coverage suffix. Grep of web-rs for 5000/5_000/MAX_SITES finds only the toast timeout — no frontend cap detection; `IndexCapNotice` (components/index_cap_notice.rs:47-80) is hard-wired to `sp_index_truncated` and never fires for the site sweep. The invariant this breaks is stated in docs/architecture/resource-access-and-permission-tester.md:30-34,49 ('Coverage is never overstated', 'no per-site grants is only claimed when every enumerable site was actually read') and in the command's own comment at commands/sharepoint.rs:757 ('Raise if a user legitimately hits it' — but nothing detects hitting it). The existing wiremock test (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/tests/sharepoint.rs:183-185) asserts only `capped.len() == 1` and cannot observe the dropped signal. Precondition is a tenant with >5000 team/communication sites, which is a large but realistic enterprise (Teams provisions one site per team); given the surface is a security-posture view that affirmatively asserts an app has no reach, high stands.

findings.title: Grant read-through cache is attached to the per-SP appRoleAssignments read; the tenant-wide appRoleAssignedTo read it describes is uncached
findings.rationale: The comment, the cache-key name (`assigned_to:`) and the stated motivation (audit + consent lens paying for the same full-tenant scan twice) all describe `appRoleAssignedTo` on the Microsoft Graph SP — but both real callers (`prefetch_graph_app_roles` in audit.rs:957 and the consent scan in consent.rs:197) call `list_app_role_assigned_to`, which has no cache. `appRoleAssignments` (what one SP holds) is a small per-SP list that is cheap to re-read; caching it instead brings a 60-minute staleness window to the pre-write `existing` reads in permissions.rs:666 / sharepoint.rs:307 for no measurable win. The only test that touches the key (`deleting_a_service_principal_drops_the_grant_matrices`) seeds `grants:assigned_to:sp-1` by hand, so nothing proves which method writes it. caching-and-search.md ('Page size is a wall-clock divisor') names this read as the one that dominates the audit and consent view, so the intended win is currently not realized.
findings.proposal: Move the read-through block to `list_app_role_assigned_to` (key `grants:assigned_to:{sp}`), and either drop the cache from `list_app_role_assignments` or re-key it `grants:assignments:{sp}`; both mutator families already sweep the `grants:` prefix on Ok so invalidation is unchanged. Fix the doc comments to match. Add a wiremock test with `.expect(1)` on `/servicePrincipals/sp-graph/appRoleAssignedTo` called twice, and assert the existing `a_grant_write_invalidates_the_cached_matrices` shape for it.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified. crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/roles_grants.rs:36-65: `list_app_role_assignments` (path `/servicePrincipals/{id}/appRoleAssignments`) carries the read-through cache with key `assigned_to:{sp}` and a comment describing `prefetch_graph_app_roles` and the consent lens. roles_grants.rs:70-87: `list_app_role_assigned_to` (`/appRoleAssignedTo`) has the 'heaviest paged read' comment but ends with a bare `self.collect_all_pages(page).await` — no cache. Callers confirm the mismatch: audit.rs:957 and :1030, consent.rs:197, permission_tester.rs:467, enterprise_application.rs:190 all call `list_app_role_assigned_to`; `list_app_role_assignments` is called from 18 per-SP sites (permissions.rs:406/666/943, sharepoint.rs:307/543, exchange/*, remediation.rs:350, ...) including pre-write `existing` reads. docs/architecture/caching-and-search.md:284-287 names `appRoleAssignedTo` on the Graph SP as the dominating read. Tests: tests/grants.rs:244 and :270 only exercise `list_all_oauth2_grants`; the `grants:assigned_to:sp-1` key is hand-seeded in tests/service_principals.rs:650, so nothing pins which method writes it. History is squashed (all traces to merge 06af5cc) so no rationale for the current placement is recoverable. Proposal is sound: mutators already sweep the `grants:` prefix (roles_grants.rs:30-35), so moving the block changes no invalidation.

findings.title: SharePoint resolver reports 403/429/401 on the subsite probe as 'did not resolve to a list, library or item'
findings.rationale: Only a 404 means 'not a subsite'. `get_site_by_url` rides `scoped_get_retried`, so after the retry budget a 429 still surfaces as `Throttled`; a user who lacks rights on the subsite gets `Forbidden`; an expired token gets `Unauthorized`. All three are collapsed into a `Protocol` error whose text tells the operator the URL is wrong. Downstream, `sharepoint_item_err` -> `map_sharepoint_err` only splices the capability catalog's remediation when `ui.code == "forbidden"` (graph_err.rs:26), so the 403 remediation for `sharepoint_selected_items` is bypassed too, and `retryable` is false for what was a throttle. In the multi-target grant loop (commands/sharepoint.rs:567) this becomes a warning 'could not resolve <url>' that misdirects the operator to fix the URL.
findings.proposal: Match `Err(GraphError::NotFound(_))` for the 'not a subsite' branch and `Err(e) => return Err(e)` for everything else. Add a wiremock test: site lookup returns 403 on the descent URL and the resolver must return `Forbidden`, not `Protocol`.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified. crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/sharepoint.rs:196-205: the subsite descent matches `Err(_)` and returns `GraphError::Protocol("... did not resolve to a list, library or item in this site")`; the comment ('Not a subsite either') shows 404 was the intent. `get_site_by_url` (sharepoint.rs:9-13) rides `scoped_get_retried` → `send_core_url_with`, which yields typed `Forbidden`/`Unauthorized`/`Throttled` (transport.rs:612-651, map_error_status :760-768), so all of these are collapsed. Downstream: commands/sharepoint.rs:164-176 `map_sharepoint_err` splices the catalog remediation only via `forbidden_remediation`, which requires `err.code == "forbidden"` (commands/graph_err.rs:26-30) — a Protocol error (`ui_code` = `protocol_error`, core/http_error.rs:134) bypasses it. The multi-target grant loop at commands/sharepoint.rs:566-572 turns it into a warning 'could not resolve <url>'. Note the first, site-collection lookup (sharepoint.rs:167-169) propagates with `?`, so only the descent probe is affected. tests/sharepoint.rs has no error-path test for `resolve_sharepoint_resource` (only :211, :274, :298 happy paths). Proposal (match `NotFound` only) is minimal and correct.

findings.title: Scoped writes (group membership, site/list/item grants, claims policies) bypass the retry loop entirely, so a 429 with Retry-After fails immediately where the identical unscoped write would be replayed
findings.rationale: The 'one-shot configuration write' rationale no longer holds: `add_group_member` is called from the DR restore loop over every restored SP, and `grant_list_permission`/`grant_list_item_permission`/`grant_site_permission` run inside the multi-target grant loop. `RetryReason::Throttled` is explicitly documented in http_retry.rs as safe to replay for any verb ('the service rejected the request before doing any work'), and `send_core_url_with` already takes an explicit provider plus `RetryClass::NonIdempotent` — the scoped GET family (`scoped_get_retried`) already made this move. Today a write that rides `write_token` gets its 429 honored exactly per Retry-After; the same PATCH/POST on `sharepoint_token` or `group_member_token` fails on the first 429 and the restore/grant loop records a failure the operator has to redo. AGENTS.md's 'one definition per policy' rule for the retry budget is what this violates.
findings.proposal: Reimplement `scoped_send_core` on `send_core_url_with(token, retry_class_for(&method), method, url, &[], false, body_value, None)` — derive the class from the verb (as `send_core_url` does at transport.rs:449-461 and as the `repo_invariants/trust.rs:135` invariant expects) rather than hardcoding `RetryClass::NonIdempotent`, so scoped DELETEs (`remove_site_permission`, `remove_list_permission`, `remove_group_member`, claims-policy unassign) stay idempotent-replayable while POST/PATCH are replayed only after a 429. Update the doc comments at transport.rs:78-82 and the sharepoint/policies callers' expectations; keep `scoped_get` one-shot (pinned by tests/transport.rs:306). Add the two wiremock tests as proposed (429 Retry-After:0 then 201 succeeds; 502 on a scoped POST hits `.expect(1)`).
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified. crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/transport.rs:120-155 `scoped_send_core` does a single `req.send()` and maps the status with `map_error_status`; the rationale at :78-82 ('one-shot configuration writes, not high-volume reads') predates the loops that now call it: `add_group_member` (directory.rs:216-224) is invoked per restored SP in commands/restore.rs:709-716; `grant_list_permission`/`grant_list_item_permission` (sharepoint.rs:475-516, both `scoped_send_json`) run inside the dedupe_targets loop at commands/sharepoint.rs:566-600 (added in cf32c3d, 2026-08-28). core/http_retry.rs:113-114 documents `Throttled` as safe to replay for any verb, and `send_core_url_with` already takes an explicit provider + class (transport.rs:472-482). The only test pinning one-shot behaviour is for the scoped GET (`list_synchronization_jobs`, tests/transport.rs:306-333), not the write family, so no pinned decision is contradicted. Rides the AGENTS.md 'one definition per policy' rule: these writes bypass `core::http_retry` entirely and never notify the throttle observer. One refinement to the proposal: hardcoding NonIdempotent would downgrade the scoped DELETEs that today would be Idempotent under `retry_class_for`.

findings.title: Advanced-query flag is inconsistent between page 1 and continuations: collect_all_pages defaults to eventual, the SP index does the reverse
findings.rationale: Of the 12 `collect_all_pages` callers, only two (`list_service_principal_groups`, `list_tenant_app_role_resources`) issue page 1 with `ConsistencyLevel: eventual`; the other ten (owners, oauth2 grants, appRoleAssignedTo, federated credentials, managed identities, application templates, batch overflow continuations) issue page 1 without the header and every later page with it, so a multi-page collection is served half from the primary store and half from the eventually-consistent index. The SP index inverts it: `$count=true` + eventual on page 1, plain on pages 2+; per Microsoft's advanced-query doc the `$count=true` that rides the nextLink is then 'silently ignored', and `total_count` has no reader here anyway (the comment's justification — 'keeps the response shape identical to the prior index calls' — is not a functional reason; `list_application_index_named` already dropped `$count` for exactly the reasons applications.rs:244-249 lists). The transport's own history (transport.rs:307-316) shows page-1/page-2 header drift producing a silent wrong answer once already.
findings.proposal: Delete the defaulted `collect_all_pages` wrapper (or default it to `false`) and make every call site pass the same flag it used for page 1 — mechanical, ten sites become `collect_all_pages_with(page, false)` and two become `true`. Drop `$count=true`/eventual from `list_service_principals_index` so page 1 matches its continuation (or, if there is a reason the index must be an advanced query, pass `true` to `collect_all_pages_capped` and document it). Add a wiremock regression for the transport.rs:307 bug: `list_applications_all` with `$expand` must have `header_is_missing("consistencylevel")` on the `page=2` mock — no test currently asserts that.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified by enumerating callers. transport.rs:175-181 `collect_all_pages` hardcodes `collect_all_pages_with(page, true)`. Of its 12 callers, only directory.rs:174 (`list_service_principal_groups`) and service_principals.rs:149 (`list_tenant_app_role_resources`) issue page 1 with `true`; the other ten (applications.rs:387 owners, :573 templates via `get_json_prefer` which passes `false`, batch.rs:172 `finish_paged_batch`, credentials.rs:82 federated creds, roles_grants.rs:62/:85/:182/:202, service_principals.rs:118/:406) issue page 1 with `false` and then page with `eventual`. The SP index inverts it: service_principals.rs:168-183 sends `$count=true` + `eventual` on page 1 and `collect_all_pages_capped(page, SP_INDEX_MAX, false)` at :203-205; its stated reason (:161-164, 'keeps the response shape identical to the prior index calls') is not functional, and `total_count` is dropped (the fn returns `Vec<ServicePrincipal>`). Microsoft's paging doc (learn.microsoft.com/graph/paging, point 5; graph/query-parameters#skiptoken) states the ConsistencyLevel header 'isn't included by default in subsequent page requests. It must be set explicitly' for advanced queries — so the SP index's `false` continuation is the clearly wrong half, while the ten `false→true` sites read pages 2+ from the eventually-consistent index store, which can miss a just-written grant on a security-posture read. No test asserts the page-2 header: tests/applications.rs:365-405 `list_applications_all_follows_next_link` has no header matcher, and `header_is_missing("consistencylevel")` appears only on page-1 mocks (:37, :63). The transport's own history (transport.rs:307-316) shows this exact drift produced a silent wrong answer once. Proposal (drop the defaulted wrapper, pass the page-1 flag at every site) is mechanical and matches applications.rs:219-228's single-predicate rule.

findings.title: Inner $batch 5xx sub-responses are terminal while the same GET alone is retried — one transient 503 sub-response marks the whole site sweep incomplete/uncached and strands a DR backup object
findings.rationale: The single-request transport retries every 5xx (transport.rs:613-651: anything not 4xx falls to `Attempt::Retry`), but inside a batch a 502/503/504 on one sub-request is mapped straight to `Server` and never re-batched. So the same object read has two retry policies depending on whether it travelled batched or alone — for the DR backup that means a transient 503 on one sub-request becomes a permanently 'skipped' object in the backup manifest, and for the audit prewarm a cold lean-SP entry. Microsoft's throttling guidance for batching says to retry each failed request from the batch individually; the machinery (`pending`/`throttled` index list + `RetryBudget`) is already there for 429.
findings.proposal: Extend the re-batch predicate at batch.rs:281 to `matches!(sub.status, 429 | 502 | 503 | 504) && budget.may_retry()`, notifying the throttle observer for 429 only; `budget.wait(max_retry_after)` already falls back to jittered exponential backoff when no inner Retry-After exists (core/http_retry.rs:265-269), so no new backoff code is needed. Add a wiremock test mirroring `batch_get_json_retries_inner_429_then_surfaces_throttled` with an inner 503 that succeeds on the second POST, and one where an inner 503 that exhausts the budget still surfaces as `Server`.
findings.verifier_notes: Core premise verified: batch.rs:279-289 re-batches only `sub.status == 429`; :72-74 maps 5xx straight to `GraphError::Server`; the single-request path retries every non-4xx (transport.rs:612-621 `_ => None` → `Attempt::Retry`). Two parts are overstated or stale: (1) the cited Microsoft guidance (learn.microsoft.com/graph/throttling#throttling-and-batching) says to retry each *throttled* (429) request from a batch individually — it does not speak to 5xx sub-responses; (2) the 'audit prewarm cold lean-SP entry' example is stale — the batched lean prewarm was replaced by the SP index scan (commands/audit.rs:190-199). The real consumers are the DR backup, where a `Server` sub-error becomes a recorded `SkippedObject` (commands/backup.rs:397-441, 811) — honest, but a re-run is needed — and, unmentioned by the reviewer, the site sweep, where `batch_list_site_permissions` (sharepoint.rs:45-63) sub-errors are folded into `sites_failed`, which makes the whole 5000-site sweep incomplete and uncached (commands/sharepoint.rs:975-992). Enhancement, not a correctness bug, since both paths degrade honestly; medium is defensible because of the sweep cost.

findings.title: No graph-level regression test that a non-idempotent POST is NOT replayed after a 502 / connection reset (the addPassword double-mint bug)
findings.rationale: Commit 8fb1ac7 fixed `POST .../addPassword` being replayed up to three times after a 502, minting orphaned client secrets the operator never saw. The policy now lives in `core::http_retry::with_retries` (unit-tested there), but the graph-side mapping that decides the class — `retry_class_for` plus the explicit `RetryClass::Idempotent` override on the `$batch` POST — has no test in this crate. A future edit that routes a POST through `send_core_url_with(.., RetryClass::Idempotent, ..)` or changes `retry_class_for` would pass the whole suite. The module header claims 'the behavioral contracts (retry budget, CAE single re-mint, origin guard, ...) are unchanged and pinned by tests/transport.rs' — the retry-class contract is not.
findings.proposal: Add three wiremock tests in tests/transport.rs: (1) `add_password` against a 502 mock with `.expect(1)` returns `Err(GraphError::Server{..})` and is not re-sent; (2) `get_organization` 502-then-200 succeeds (Idempotent replays); (3) `batch_get_json` 502-then-200 on `/$batch` succeeds (explicit Idempotent override). Also pin the CAE once-only guard: a provider whose `bearer_with_claims` returns a token that is still challenged must yield `Unauthorized` after exactly two requests.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified. transport.rs:770-783 `retry_class_for` and the explicit `RetryClass::Idempotent` override on the `$batch` POST (batch.rs:248-263) have no behavioural test in this crate: grep of crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/tests for `502`/`NonIdempotent`/`Idempotent` returns nothing; the only 5xx mock is tests/transport.rs:137 (a page-2 500 in a cap test). tests/transport.rs:11 covers only the 429 replay path. What does exist and the reviewer did not mention: the core unit test `a_non_idempotent_request_is_not_replayed_after_a_transient_failure` (core/http_retry.rs:404-420) pins the policy, and the source-scanning invariant `every_retry_call_site_derives_its_idempotency_class` (src-tauri/tests/repo_invariants/trust.rs:121-189) requires files calling `with_retries(` to contain `retry_class_for(` or an explicit Idempotent + `Method::` literal — but it would not catch `retry_class_for` returning Idempotent for POST, nor a new write call site passing Idempotent in a file that already contains `retry_class_for(`, so the end-to-end gap the reviewer names is real. The CAE test (tests/transport.rs:362-419) covers only the happy re-mint; the once-only guard (transport.rs:657-660 `if cae_retried { return Err(Unauthorized) }`) is unpinned despite the module header's claim at transport.rs:4-6. CHANGELOG.md:504-515 confirms the addPassword double-mint incident. Proposal is feasible with the existing `make_client`/`StaticTokenProvider` helpers.

findings.title: Zero wiremock coverage for the scoped batch continuation, the SP signing-cert password sweep, the Prefer-header gallery fetch and several other client methods
findings.rationale: Each of these encodes a non-obvious contract that was learned the hard way and is documented in a block comment: the scoped bearer must ride page 2 of a batched site read (a real 403 bug), `remove_service_principal_key_credential` must drop the paired `passwordCredentials` entry by `customKeyIdentifier` or strand a PFX password forever, `list_all_application_templates` must send `Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=2800` on the first request only, `get_application_backup_json` must `$select` the exact `APP_BACKUP_SELECT` projection and `$expand=owners` without the advanced-query header, `patch_application_expose_api`/`set_application_app_roles` must sweep the `resource:` prefix (only the SP-side twin is tested), and a `$batch` envelope missing an id must yield `Protocol`. None has a test, so each can regress silently.
findings.proposal: Add one focused wiremock test per contract in the matching tests/*.rs module: (a) `batch_list_site_permissions` whose sub-response carries a nextLink and a `page=2` mock that requires `Authorization: Bearer sp`; (b) `remove_service_principal_key_credential` with a Sign/Verify pair plus a passwordCredential sharing the thumbprint, asserting the PATCH body drops all three and keeps unrelated entries; (c) `list_all_application_templates` with `header("prefer", "odata.maxpagesize=2800")` on page 1 and `header_is_missing("prefer")` on page 2; (d) backup JSON `$select`/`$expand` + `header_is_missing("consistencylevel")`; (e) `patch_application_expose_api` clears a seeded `tenant-test|resource:...` key; (f) batch envelope with a missing id -> `Protocol`.
findings.verifier_notes: Counts verified with a literal grep over crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/tests/ (12 files): batch_list_site_permissions 0, finish_paged_batch_scoped 0, list_saml_sso_service_principals 0, list_all_application_templates 0, get_application_backup_json 0, remove_service_principal_key_credential 0, list_federated_credentials( 0, search_applications_by_name 0, find_application_by_app_id 0, patch_application_expose_api 0, set_application_app_roles 0, 'missing batch response' 0, 'odata.maxpagesize' 0, APP_BACKUP_SELECT 0. Searched for differently-named tests (saml/signing/pfx/customKeyIdentifier/prefer/backup_json/expose_api): only `add_token_signing_certificate_returns_thumbprint` (tests/credentials.rs:195) and the SP-side `publishing_app_roles_drops_the_cached_resource_definitions` (tests/service_principals.rs:677) exist, matching the reviewer's 'only the SP-side twin is tested'. Each named contract is documented as hard-won in a block comment: batch.rs:180-192 (scoped page-2 token, CHANGELOG.md:516-520 records the 403 bug), credentials.rs:236-250 (three objects per cert, stranded PFX password), transport.rs:370-374 (Prefer on first request only), batch.rs:302-308 ('missing batch response' → Protocol). Medium is fair for a cluster of untested, regression-prone contracts.

findings.title: Two hand-rolled nextLink loops duplicate collect_pages_from (same_origin + MAX_PAGES + append)
findings.rationale: `collect_pages_from` exists precisely to be the one origin-guarded, page-bounded follower for scoped reads (`list_conditional_access_policies`, `list_site_permissions`, `list_site_drives`, ... all use it). The sign-in-activity report and the site enumeration re-implement it inline, so the origin guard and the page cap are maintained in three places; `list_all_sites` additionally needs the capped/truncated shape (finding 1). Five copies of `MAX_PAGES` can drift.
findings.proposal: Route `list_service_principal_sign_in_activities` through `collect_pages_from(first, |u| self.scoped_get(token, &u))` (it already uses `scoped_get` per page, so behaviour is unchanged). Add `collect_pages_from_capped(first, max, fetch) -> Result<(Vec<T>, bool)>` next to it and use it for `list_all_sites`, which also delivers finding 1's truncation flag. Hoist `MAX_PAGES` to a single `pub(crate) const` in transport.rs.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified. directory.rs:310-340 hand-rolls the origin guard + MAX_PAGES + append loop around `scoped_get`; sharepoint.rs:84-104 repeats it with an item cap; transport.rs:269-300 `collect_pages_from` already implements the same shape and is used by `list_conditional_access_policies` (directory.rs:82-84), `list_site_permissions` (sharepoint.rs:26-30) and `finish_paged_batch_scoped` (batch.rs:200-204). `const MAX_PAGES: usize = 200` is declared five times (transport.rs:192, :238, :279; directory.rs:310; sharepoint.rs:84). Routing the sign-in report through `collect_pages_from` is behaviour-preserving: `beta_base()` derives from `base_url` (client.rs:337-341) so the `same_origin(&self.base_url, next)` check inside the helper matches the inline one, and the per-page fetch stays `scoped_get`. The proposed `collect_pages_from_capped` is the natural home for finding 0's flag. Low is right — maintenance duplication, no live defect.

findings.title: Five copies of the 'GET single object, 404 -> Ok(None)' match; two raw-JSON app readers differ only in $select
findings.rationale: The 404-to-None mapping is the crate's convention for 'object vanished between index read and detail read', and it is restated verbatim in five methods (the batched variant `batch_get_service_principals` has a sixth spelling). A single `get_json_optional<T>(path, query)` in transport.rs would make the convention one line per caller and make a future change (e.g. also treating a specific 400 `Request_ResourceNotFound` body as None) a one-place edit.
findings.proposal: Add `pub(crate) async fn get_json_optional<T: DeserializeOwned>(&self, path: &str, query: &[(&str,&str)]) -> Result<Option<T>>` to transport.rs and collapse the five call sites; optionally fold `get_application_sso_fields`/`get_application_auth_fields` into `get_application_fields_raw(object_id, select)` with two thin public wrappers so callers and tests are untouched.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified. The identical `match get_json::<_>(..) { Ok(v) => Ok(Some(v)), Err(GraphError::NotFound(_)) => Ok(None), Err(e) => Err(e) }` appears at applications.rs:457-470 (`get_application_sso_fields`), :480-496 (`get_application_auth_fields`), :503-517 (`get_application_expose_api`), service_principals.rs:520-535 (`get_service_principal_by_object_id`), :570-584 (`get_service_principal_sso_fields`); `batch_get_service_principals` (:547-560) restates it over batch results. `get_application_sso_fields` and `get_application_auth_fields` differ only in the `$select` literal. No `get_json_optional`-style helper exists in the crate (grep for `_optional` returns nothing). Low-severity refactor, correctly rated; the optional fold of the two raw readers keeps callers/tests untouched as stated.

findings.title: list_conditional_access_policies pages without $top, contrary to the 'every paged read sends $top' invariant
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md states 'Every paged read sends `$top` (`client::MAX_PAGE_SIZE`)' and caching-and-search.md explains why (serial paging, default page of 100). This read follows nextLink to exhaustion but sends no `$top`; Microsoft's 'List policies' reference lists `$top` among the supported parameters for `/identity/conditionalAccess/policies`. Most tenants have well under 100 CA policies so the cost is usually one round trip, but large/MSP tenants do exceed it and the read rides the one-shot `scoped_get` that does not retry, so each extra page is another unretried chance to fail the whole tab.
findings.proposal: Build the URL with `?$top={MAX_PAGE_SIZE}` (Graph clamps an over-ask silently, matching the crate's stated rule), and extend `conditional_access_policies_parse_and_follow_paging` to match `query_param("$top", "999")` on page 1.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified. directory.rs:78-95 builds `{base}/identity/conditionalAccess/policies` with no `$top` and pages via `collect_pages_from` over the one-shot `scoped_get` (transport.rs:20-47, no retry). AGENTS.md ('Every paged read sends `$top`') and docs/architecture/caching-and-search.md:271-282 state the rule. Microsoft's 'List policies' reference (learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/conditionalaccessroot-list-policies?view=graph-rest-1.0) lists `$skip, $top, $count, $filter, $orderby, $select` as supported, so the fix is valid. The existing test `conditional_access_policies_parse_and_follow_paging` (tests/directory.rs:186-202) matches page 1 with `query_param_is_missing("page")`, so adding `query_param("$top", "999")` is a one-line extension. Low is honest: most tenants fit in one page.

findings.title: upsert_admin_oauth2_grant_in fabricates a Graph 500 for a client-side invariant instead of using Protocol
findings.rationale: `GraphError::Protocol` exists for exactly this ('Client-side contract violation', http_error.rs). Reporting a synthetic `Api { status: 500 }` surfaces as ui_code `graph_error` and reads in logs and the UI as though Graph returned a server error, sending an operator (or a support engineer reading the trace) after a Graph outage that never happened.
findings.proposal: Replace with `GraphError::Protocol("existing oauth2PermissionGrant has no id".into())`; no caller matches on `Api{status:500}` for this path.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified. roles_grants.rs:339-346 returns `GraphError::Api { status: 500, body: "existing grant missing id" }` for a client-side invariant (an `existing_grants` element without an id). `GraphError::Protocol` is documented for exactly 'Client-side contract violation' (core/http_error.rs:96-101) and maps to `ui_code` `protocol_error` (:134), whereas `Api` maps to the client's `$api_code` (:125) and reads as a Graph-returned status. Nothing matches on `Api { status: 500 }` for this path (grep: only activity.rs:361 in a test and arm/error.rs:99, unrelated). Low, correctly rated.

findings.title: remove_key_credential / remove_service_principal_key_credential PATCH the unchanged array and report success when the key id is absent — and the remediation counts it as a removal
findings.rationale: Both fetch-modify-PATCH removers write the full collection back even when nothing matched `key_id` (another admin already removed it, or the audit's cached finding is stale). The write is a no-op on Graph but the caller sees `Ok(())`, so the audit's one-click 'remove expired credentials' Fix and bulk remove report a removal that did not happen, and the command layer then busts `apps_pairing`/detail/audit caches for nothing. `remove_password` (the `removePassword` action) gets a real 404 from Graph in the same situation, so the two credential kinds behave differently.
findings.proposal: In both removers, detect an empty match (compare lengths, or `find` the entry first) and return `Err(GraphError::NotFound(format!("keyCredential {key_id}")))` without sending the PATCH. Then adjust the callers, because none of them currently handles NotFound as 'already gone': `remediate_remove_expired_credentials` (commands/remediation.rs:69-79) should treat NotFound from either `remove_password` or `remove_key_credential` as already-removed (skip, do not increment `removed_*`, do not abort the loop) rather than surfacing it as a failure; `remove_certificate_credential` (commands/applications/credentials.rs:236-247) and the SSO retire path (commands/sso/mod.rs:960-963) can let NotFound propagate. Add the wiremock test asserting no PATCH is sent for an unknown key id.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: credentials.rs:198-209 filters `live_key_credentials` by `keyId` and PATCHes whatever remains, returning `Ok(())` even when nothing matched; credentials.rs:251-300 (`remove_service_principal_key_credential`) has the same shape (with a `thumbprint` of `None` the filter is a no-op and the PATCH is still sent). The remediation at commands/remediation.rs:77-82 then increments `removed_certificates` and busts caches via `invalidate_app_credentials` (:91-93). What is overstated: the reviewer says 'Callers already map NotFound for the password path' — they do not; remediation.rs:69-73 breaks and returns the error on any `remove_password` failure, and there is no 'already gone' handling anywhere on these paths (grep for NotFound/already in remediation.rs and applications/credentials.rs returns nothing). So the proposal as written would turn a concurrently-removed certificate from a silently-counted success into a hard remediation failure; the caller change above is needed for the fix to be an improvement. The `remove_password` 404 claim is plausible (Graph's `removePassword` action rejects an unknown keyId) but is not something the repo pins. Low is right.

findings.title: Crate-level docs misstate the retry set and claim ConsistencyLevel is added automatically
findings.rationale: This is the first thing a contributor (or an agent) reads about the transport. It undersells the retry set (any 5xx, plus the RetryClass split introduced in 8fb1ac7 is not mentioned at all), overstates jitter (an explicit Retry-After is honored verbatim per http_retry.rs), and the 'automatically' claim would lead someone to omit the `eventual` flag on a new `$count` query and get a silently-ignored `$count` (per Microsoft's advanced-query doc).
findings.proposal: Rewrite the two bullets: 'Retries 429 (Retry-After honored exactly), any 5xx and network errors under `core::http_retry`; POST/PATCH are replayed only after a 429 (`RetryClass`)'; 'Callers opt into advanced queries per request via the `consistency_eventual` flag — the header is never inferred from the query string.'
findings.verifier_notes: Verified. crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/lib.rs:5-10 says retries cover '429 w/ Retry-After, 503, 504, network' with 'exponential backoff + jitter', and that `ConsistencyLevel: eventual` is added 'automatically for $search / $count queries'. Actual behaviour: transport.rs:612-651 classifies every non-4xx status (`_ => None` → `Attempt::Retry`), i.e. 500/502 too; core/http_retry.rs:66-87 and :263-269 honor an explicit Retry-After verbatim with no jitter (jitter only on the no-header path); the `RetryClass` split (transport.rs:770-783, CHANGELOG.md:504-515) is not mentioned; and the header is sent only when a caller passes `consistency_eventual: true` to `get_json`/`send_core_url_with` (transport.rs:494-496) — `is_advanced_query` in applications.rs:228-230 is a per-call-site decision, nothing inspects the query string. The 'automatically' claim is the kind that leads to the silent `$count`-ignored failure Microsoft documents. Doc-only, low; proposed wording is accurate.

findings.title: `atScope()` is documented as excluding inherited assignments; Azure defines it as "at or above the scope" — the Key Vault reverse lookup labels inherited subscription/RG roles as direct vault grants
findings.rationale: The doc comment, the sweep's module doc, the DTO doc and two user-facing strings all assert the opposite of the documented ARM semantics. `atScope()` at a vault path returns the vault's own assignments PLUS every assignment inherited from its resource group, subscription, management group and root — the very "inherited subscription Owner" rows the comment says are excluded. The operator is told these are explicit vault grants and the panel's empty-state text claims inherited-only vaults "won't appear here", so the least-privilege picture is misreported (a subscription Owner is shown as a per-vault grant; a vault that is only reachable via inheritance shows rows anyway). `high_privilege` flags then fire on rows the user was told are direct.
findings.proposal: Keep the `atScope()` query (it is the correct single call) but stop calling the rows direct: in `sweep_key_vault_access` compare `props.scope` to the vault `id` case-insensitively and either drop non-matching rows or add `inherited: bool` to `KeyVaultAccessRow` and render an "inherited from <scope level>" badge. Rewrite the doc comment at client.rs:90-94 to "at or above `scope`", fix keyvault_rbac.rs:5 / dto keyvault.rs:16 / the two UI strings (keyvault.rs:245, 354), and add a wiremock test in client.rs where one assignment's `scope` is the subscription and assert the consumer classifies it as inherited. Expected effect: the panel answers the question it claims to answer, and the "direct" label stops being wrong for every inherited Owner.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified against Microsoft Learn (RoleAssignments list filter docs): '$filter=atScope() returns all role assignments at or above the scope' — i.e. it INCLUDES inherited assignments and excludes only child scopes. crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/client.rs:90-94 asserts the opposite ('excludes assignments inherited from ancestor scopes'); the consumer keyvault_rbac.rs:266-268 does `props.scope.unwrap_or_else(|| vault_id.clone())` with no scope==vault comparison, so an RG/subscription/MG Owner is emitted as a row for every vault under it. Module doc keyvault_rbac.rs:5, DTO doc dto/keyvault.rs:16 ('One direct Azure-RBAC role assignment'), UI copy web-rs views/resource_access/keyvault.rs:245 and :354 all repeat the wrong semantics, and the panel table (keyvault.rs:365-410) has Vault/Principal/Role columns only — the row's real `scope` is never shown (only the CSV export carries it), so the operator cannot see provenance. The only test (client.rs:501-535) asserts the query param, not the semantics. Severity downgraded from high: the principals listed genuinely hold the role over the vault (inherited or not), so the access picture is complete and not false — what is wrong is the provenance labelling and the 'inherited-only vaults won't appear' claim. Proposal (keep atScope(), add `inherited: bool` by comparing `props.scope` to the vault id case-insensitively, render a badge, fix the five strings, add a wiremock test with a subscription-scoped `scope`) is sound and small.

findings.title: Log Analytics `PartialError` responses (HTTP 200 + `error`) are treated as complete results — the granted-vs-used analysis can be built on truncated/failed query output
findings.rationale: `usage.rs::get_app_graph_usage` turns the first table into `GraphUsageResult` and the UI uses it to recommend permission downgrades ("only GETs observed → Downgrade applies"). A runaway/timeout/truncation on a large 90-day `summarize` yields 200 with partial rows and an `error.code == "PartialError"`; the model discards `error`, so the panel shows fewer call patterns than exist and the operator may strip a permission the app actually uses. The DTO already models coverage honesty for `truncated` but has no channel for this case.
findings.proposal: Add `#[serde(default)] pub error: Option<LogsErrorInfo { code: String, message: String }>` to `LogsQueryResponse`; in `LogAnalyticsClient::query` return `Err(ArmError::Protocol(format!("partial result: {code}: {message}")))` when `error` is present (or return `(table, partial: bool)` and thread a `partial` flag into `GraphUsageResult` beside `truncated` so the panel warns instead of failing). Add a wiremock test with `{"tables":[...],"error":{"code":"PartialError",...}}`. Effect: a degraded query can no longer read as an all-clear usage picture.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified against Microsoft Learn 'Azure Monitor Log Analytics API response format': a non-fatal error returns 200 OK with `tables` plus an `error` property whose code is `PartialError`; the Kusto partial-query-failures page says the consumer should ignore the whole result. crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/models.rs:44-48 `LogsQueryResponse` has only `tables` (no `error`), loganalytics.rs:67-73 returns `tables[0]` unconditionally, and apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/usage.rs:257-267 builds `GraphUsageResult` with only `truncated` (dto/usage.rs:28-30) as its coverage-honesty channel. No handling anywhere (grep PartialError → none). This is the same class the repo pins elsewhere ('a cancelled/truncated/degraded run is never shown as all-clear', AGENTS.md). Severity lowered from high to medium: the trigger (runaway/truncation on a per-app 90-day summarize with `take 200`) is uncommon, and the Downgrade action is presented as admin-judged, not automatic. Proposal (add `error: Option<LogsErrorInfo>` with `#[serde(default)]`, surface as `ArmError::Protocol` or a `partial` flag beside `truncated`, wiremock test) is correct and small.

findings.title: Key Vault `retry_class_for` doc comment contradicts itself about `setSecret` (a PUT) — clarify the deliberate same-value replay rather than reclassify PUT
findings.rationale: `setSecret` is the PUT this function routes to `Idempotent`, yet the doc comment cites `setSecret` as the example of a write that must not be replayed. Key Vault's SET operation always appends a version, so a 502/connection reset after the service committed is replayed up to `MAX_RETRIES` times and leaves duplicate versions of the rotated client secret in the vault (and, on final failure, `rotate_app_credential` removes the app secret while a vault version already holds it). Same class of defect the core `RetryClass` doc records for `addPassword`. The repo invariant in `tests/repo_invariants/trust.rs:167` only requires the file to contain `retry_class_for(`, so a Key Vault-specific mapping is compliant.
findings.proposal: Rewrite the doc comment at crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/client.rs:261-266 to state the actual trade-off: Key Vault `PUT /secrets/{name}` appends a version on every call, so a replay after an unknown outcome can produce a second version — but the replay carries the identical value, so the current version is always correct and the only cost is a duplicate same-value version. Optionally add a wiremock test (502 then 200) asserting both PUT bodies are byte-identical and the call succeeds. Do NOT route PUT to `NonIdempotent` for this crate: that would fail the rotation on a pre-commit transient 502 and, on a post-commit one, `rotate_app_credential` (commands/keyvault.rs:123-128) would remove the freshly minted app secret while the vault already holds it — a dead value in the vault is worse than a duplicate live one.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is real: client.rs:263-266 names `setSecret` as the POST/PATCH hazard example while line 269 routes PUT (which `set_secret` at client.rs:102-106 uses) to `Idempotent`; Key Vault SET does always create a new version; repo_invariants/trust.rs:150-190 only requires a `retry_class_for(` helper so a per-crate rule would be compliant. But the impact is overstated: unlike `addPassword` (core http_retry.rs:120-130, where each replay mints a DIFFERENT secret the operator never sees), the KV replay re-sends the same plaintext, so the duplicate version holds the correct value and no credential is orphaned. The proposed fix makes the rotation flow strictly more fragile (analysis above), so only the documentation half survives. Severity low.

findings.title: `principalId eq` returns assignments "at, above or below" each subscription, so a management-group/root assignment is returned once per subscription and rendered as N duplicate rows
findings.rationale: The client doc says "at or below" but ARM also returns assignments *above* the subscription (management groups, tenant root). A managed identity with Reader on a management group over 20 subscriptions appears 20 times in `list_managed_identity_azure_roles`, each row labelled with a different `subscription` display name, inflating the Azure RBAC footprint and the high-privilege count the operator sees. `readiness.rs` is unaffected (collects into a `HashSet` of GUIDs).
findings.proposal: Fix the doc comment to "at, above or below" and dedupe in the consumer by `RoleAssignment.id` (a `HashSet<String>` before `flat`), labelling above-subscription rows with the scope rather than the subscription that surfaced them. Add a unit test with two subscriptions returning the same MG-scoped assignment id and assert one row. Effort small; effect: no phantom duplicate roles.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified against Microsoft Learn (same filter docs): '$filter=principalId eq {id} returns all role assignments at, above or below the scope' — so a management-group or root-scoped assignment is returned by every subscription under it. crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/client.rs:55-57 doc says only 'at or below'. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/managed_identity.rs:251-258 flattens per-subscription lists with no dedupe and labels each copy with that subscription's display name (AzureRoleDto.subscription, dto/managed_identity.rs:87-88); `scope_level` at :412-428 already classifies '/providers/Microsoft.Management' scopes, confirming such rows are expected. An MG-scoped assignment's `id` is the same absolute path regardless of which subscription surfaced it, so dedupe by `RoleAssignment.id` (models.rs:73-75) works. readiness.rs:206-250 is unaffected (collects `role_id_tail` into a HashSet). Inflated row and high-privilege counts in an RBAC-footprint view justify medium. Proposal is correct.

findings.title: `SecretItem`/`KvSecretItemDto` drop Key Vault's `managed` attribute, so certificate-backed secrets are indistinguishable in the secret browser
findings.evidence:
crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/models.rs:6-16
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SecretItem {
    /// Full resource id: `https://{vault}.vault.azure.net/secrets/{name}`.
    pub id: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub attributes: Option<SecretAttributes>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub tags: Option<std::collections::HashMap<String, String>>,
    #[serde(default, rename = "contentType")]
    pub content_type: Option<String>,
}

Microsoft Learn, Key Vault SecretProperties.managed: "True if the secret's lifetime is managed by key vault. If this is a secret backing a certificate, then managed will be true."

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/keyvault.rs:35-47 maps only name/id/enabled/expires/content_type into `KvSecretItemDto`.
findings.rationale: Every Key Vault certificate materialises a `managed: true` secret in `GET /secrets`. The browser lists them like any other secret, and the rotation dialog's secret-name field can be pointed at one; Key Vault refuses `set` on a managed secret, so the operator gets a raw `vault error (400/403)` after the new app secret was already minted (then rolled back). Surfacing `managed` costs one field and lets the UI badge/exclude those rows. The list response also carries `attributes.recoveryLevel`/`recoverableDays`, useful for the same panel.
findings.proposal: Add `#[serde(default)] pub managed: Option<bool>` to `SecretItem` (crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/models.rs:6-16) and `managed: Option<bool>` to `KvSecretItemDto` (dto/keyvault.rs:51-58), map it in `kv_list_secrets` (commands/keyvault.rs:35-48), and render a 'certificate-backed' badge in `key_vault_view.rs`. For rotation, the secret name is a free-text `<Input>` (credentials_tab.rs:1095) pre-filled from tenant defaults/bindings (credentials_tab.rs:313-342), not a picker over existing secrets, so 'filter managed names out of the picker' does not apply; instead either pre-check the typed name against the vault's managed secrets before minting, or map Key Vault's managed-secret rejection to a typed, actionable UiError. Add a wiremock fixture with `"managed": true`.
findings.verifier_notes: The attribute exists and is server-populated (Microsoft Learn SecretProperties.managed: 'True if the secret's lifetime is managed by key vault. If this is a secret backing a certificate, then managed will be true'). models.rs:6-16 omits it and commands/keyvault.rs:35-48 maps only name/id/enabled/expires/content_type — premise holds for the browser. Overstated: there is no 'rotation target picker' to filter (the field is free text), and the failure mode is already handled — `rotate_app_credential` rolls back the minted secret on a store failure (commands/keyvault.rs:123-128) and surfaces a typed `vault_error`. Enhancement, not a bug; severity low.

findings.title: `KeyVaultResource` drops `properties.enableRbacAuthorization`, so the RBAC sweep cannot tell a legacy access-policy vault from one with no assignments — the UI admits both "produce no rows"
findings.rationale: The ARM vault list already returns `properties.enableRbacAuthorization` on every item; discarding it means the sweep's coverage numbers (`vaults_scanned`) count access-policy vaults as scanned-and-empty, when in fact their access model is invisible to `roleAssignments`. For a security posture surface that is a silent gap: an operator sees 40 scanned vaults and 12 with rows and cannot tell which of the other 28 are governed by access policies (a finding in itself — AGENTS/capabilities treat legacy mode as a problem).
findings.proposal: Add `properties: Option<KeyVaultResourceProperties { enable_rbac_authorization: Option<bool> }>` to `KeyVaultResource`; in `sweep_key_vault_access` skip the roleAssignments read for `false` vaults, count them in a new `vaults_access_policy_mode` field on `KeyVaultSweepResult`, and show it beside `vaults_failed` in the panel (optionally as a Security-tab finding "vault uses legacy access policies"). Wiremock test for the property.
findings.verifier_notes: crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/models.rs:97-108 `KeyVaultResource` deserializes only `id`/`name`; the ARM vault list (`Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults` at subscription scope) returns full `Vault` objects whose `properties.enableRbacAuthorization` is available. `sweep_key_vault_access` (keyvault_rbac.rs:150-200) counts every vault as `vaults_scanned` and the DTO (dto/keyvault.rs:40-49) has no access-policy-mode counter. Two corrections to the framing: (1) the gap is not silent — the UI empty-state at web-rs views/resource_access/keyvault.rs:354 explicitly names legacy access-policy vaults as a known limitation, and core capabilities.rs:326 already warns about RBAC mode; (2) RBAC role assignments are control-plane objects that exist regardless of the vault's permission model, so an access-policy vault with a direct assignment WILL produce rows — the flag is needed to annotate that those rows do not confer data-plane access, not merely to explain empties. Useful enhancement for a posture surface; low severity.

findings.title: The permissions catalog carries no permission data, leaving `lookup_permission`, the catalog rung of the resolution ladder, and the permission entry types as dead code
findings.rationale: The crate deliberately became a 6-row resource directory (module doc says so), but it still ships `AppRoleEntry`, `ScopeEntry`, `allowed_member_types` with a comment about "older catalog snapshots", `CatalogRoot.generated/version` that nothing reads, a `lookup_permission` that can only return `None` (and is pinned by a test to do so), a 34-line unreachable "1. Catalog" branch in `resolve_one_permission`, and `list_catalog_resources` reporting `role_count`/`scope_count` that are always 0 (the picker ignores them and uses `list_resource_permission_counts`). This is exactly the docs-in-code-contradicts-code smell: a reader of `permissions_resolve.rs` believes a bundled fallback exists offline.
findings.proposal: Pick one direction. (a) Honest directory: rename the type to `ResourceDirectory`, delete `AppRoleEntry`/`ScopeEntry`/`lookup_permission`/`CatalogRoot.generated|version`, remove ladder step 1 and the `role_count`/`scope_count` fields from `list_catalog_resources` (or fill them from the live counts). (b) Real catalog: add a `just permissions-refresh` recipe that regenerates `catalog.json` from `GET /servicePrincipals?$filter=appId in (…)` and keep the ladder. (a) is the smaller, lower-risk change and matches the crate's current intent.
findings.verifier_notes: All evidence verified: crates/azapptoolkit-permissions/data/catalog.json has six `{appId, displayName}` entries and no roles/scopes; `lookup_permission` (lib.rs:106-127) can only return `None` and lib.rs:167-179 pins that; the '1. Catalog' branch at apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/applications/permissions_resolve.rs:25-58 is therefore unreachable and its doc (:8-11) advertises a bundled rung that does not exist; `list_catalog_resources` (commands/permissions.rs:16-26) reports `role_count`/`scope_count` that are always 0 and the picker ignores them — permission_picker.rs:167-180 labels from `list_resource_permission_counts` instead; `CatalogRoot.generated`/`version` (lib.rs:26-32) are read nowhere; `ResourceEntry {` is constructed nowhere outside the crate, so the lib.rs:10-11 rationale ('same type can hold a live SP's data') is unused too. Option (a) is right. One nuance for the proposal: `CatalogResourceSummary.role_count`/`scope_count` are genuinely used by `list_app_role_resources` and `list_resource_permission_counts`, so drop only the catalog command's population (or return 0 explicitly with a comment), not the DTO fields. Cleanup with real reader-misdirection value; low.

findings.title: AGENTS.md, the Claude rules file, README and the Permissions tab header describe a bundled permissions catalog with Graph fallback "for unknown resources"; the code resolves every permission live and bundles only six resource names
findings.rationale: Four documents tell agents and users that permission names come from a bundled catalog and that Graph is a fallback for unknown *resources*; the crate doc and code say the opposite (names come from Graph for every resource; the bundle only seeds the dropdown). An agent following AGENTS.md would look for permission GUIDs in `data/` to add a rule; a user reading the README expects offline permission browsing. Staleness surfaces to users as an unexplained empty picker when Graph is unreachable.
findings.proposal: Reword AGENTS.md:112 and rules:29 to "`azapptoolkit-permissions` bundles only a resource *directory* (six first-party appIds/names) for the picker dropdown; every permission definition is resolved live via `resolve_resource_sp()` and cached under `CacheKind::Permissions`." Fix README.md:75-77 and the permissions_tab.rs header accordingly.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: AGENTS.md:112 and .claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:29 ('Permissions catalog is bundled ... unknown resources fall back to resolve_resource_sp()'), AGENTS.md:48 repo-map line ('bundled permissions catalog (data/) + Graph fallback'), README.md:75-77 ('bundled catalog (with Graph fallback for unknown resources)'), and web-rs views/tabs/permissions_tab.rs:1-3 ('resolved server-side via the bundled catalog (PermissionsCatalog::lookup_permission)') all describe a permission catalog with Graph as fallback. The crate (permissions/src/lib.rs:1-11) and commands/permissions.rs:99-105 state the opposite: a six-entry resource directory only, every permission resolved live via `resolve_resource_sp` and cached under `CacheKind::Permissions`. Proposal wording is accurate; also include AGENTS.md:48. Docs-only, so low.

findings.title: Residue of the deliberately removed `kv_set_secret` command (DTOs, binding args, phantom `delete_secret`) and an over-granting operator role doc remain
findings.rationale: Half-built plumbing (a request DTO with redacted Debug, a metadata response DTO, a binding args struct) sits behind a `#![allow(dead_code)]` and a doc comment naming a command that never existed, and the recommended custom Azure role grants `deleteSecret` for an operation the app cannot perform. An Entra admin who lands a rotated secret in a vault has no way to create a plain secret or clean one up from the toolkit — the crate is one PUT/DELETE away from both.
findings.proposal: Take the removal path only: delete `KvSetSecretInput`/`KvSecretMetadataDto` and their redaction test half (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/keyvault.rs:83-116, :174-182), the `SetArgs` struct and the two re-exports in apps/desktop/web-rs/src/bindings/keyvault.rs:8-11,58-63; fix crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/lib.rs:10 to list `list_secrets`, `get_secret`, `set_secret`; reword docs/operator-rbac/OPERATOR-ROLES.md:31 from 'full secret CRUD' to 'list/get/set (rotation)', and drop `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets/deleteSecret/action` from `DataActions` in docs/operator-rbac/azure-custom-role.json:19 (and the table row at OPERATOR-ROLES.md:53) — the app has no delete path, so the least-privilege role currently over-grants.
findings.verifier_notes: The residue is real (dto/keyvault.rs:83-116, bindings/keyvault.rs:58-63 hidden by bindings/mod.rs:1 `#![allow(dead_code)]`, lib.rs:10 names a `delete_secret` that `grep` finds nowhere, lib.rs:131-134 registers only four kv commands). But the reviewer did not engage with docs/CHANGELOG-archive.md:1883-1890, which records the deliberate removal of `kv_set_secret` as unreachable, untested surface duplicating `rotate_app_credential` on a security-critical boundary. 'Implement it' therefore contradicts a documented decision; only the cleanup option stands. The OPERATOR-ROLES/azure-custom-role.json `deleteSecret` grant is the most substantive bit: a least-privilege role granting a DataAction the app never uses. Severity low.

findings.title: Key Vault and ARM transports duplicate the same status→variant mapping closure; a shared generic transport is now feasible because both enums come from `http_error_enum!`
findings.evidence:
crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/client.rs:216-225

                    401 => Some(KeyVaultError::Unauthorized),
                    403 => Some(KeyVaultError::Forbidden(body_text.clone())),
                    404 => Some(KeyVaultError::NotFound(body_text.clone())),

crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/transport.rs:83-90

                401 => Some(ArmError::Unauthorized),
                403 => Some(ArmError::Forbidden(body_text.clone())),
                404 => Some(ArmError::NotFound(body_text.clone())),
