(both files also duplicate `retry_class_for` verbatim: keyvault client.rs:267-272, arm transport.rs:128-133)

crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/http_error.rs:5-8 "three hand-maintained enums with byte-for-byte identical variants ... these enums are the copies it did not reach."
findings.rationale: The workspace already spent two PRs collapsing retry loops and error enums onto core precisely because "a policy re-derived in N places is one that can silently diverge" — and the Key Vault PUT-replay finding above is a divergence that lives in one of these copies. Because both `KeyVaultError` and `ArmError` are generated by `http_error_enum!`, the macro can also emit the constructors a generic transport needs, removing ~180 lines and making future fixes (e.g. honouring `x-ms-error-code`, capping body size) one-place changes.
findings.proposal: If pursued: add a small `core::http_error::HttpClientError` constructor trait emitted by `http_error_enum!` and a `core::http_transport::send_with_retry<E>` holding the one status-mapping closure; make ARM's transport.rs a thin wrapper and Key Vault's `send_core_url` the origin check + api-version query + one call. Keep Graph's transport separate (CAE re-mint, throttle observer, `$batch`). Keep one `retry_class_for` per crate only if `repo_invariants/trust.rs` continues to require it; otherwise it can move to core too since all three copies are identical.
findings.verifier_notes: Duplication is real: crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/client.rs:147-251 and crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/transport.rs:24-120 are near byte-identical, and `retry_class_for` is copied verbatim in keyvault client.rs:267-272, arm transport.rs:128-133 and graph transport.rs:779-784. However the reviewer overlooked the documented seam: core http_retry.rs:5-11 and :141-144 deliberately leave per-attempt status→variant classification in each crate ('mapping an HTTP status to a crate's own error enum is genuinely per-crate'). The reviewer's best counter (the enums are now macro-generated, so the mapping is no longer per-crate) is fair, which is why this is partially rather than refuted. Two overstatements: (1) 'Key Vault's PUT rule differs' is false — all three `retry_class_for` bodies are identical, so there is no divergence today; (2) the PUT-replay finding [2] is not evidence of drift between copies. Pure refactor with moderate risk on a transport path; low.

findings.title: Key Vault client tests skip the paths that matter most: `nextLink` paging, the off-origin refusal, `exp`/`nbf` serialisation on the rotation write, the 1000-page cap, and PUT replay behaviour
findings.evidence:
crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/client.rs tests module (285-392) contains exactly:
    async fn list_secrets_returns_items()
    async fn set_secret_puts_value()
    async fn get_secret_reads_value()
    async fn retries_on_429()
    async fn unauthorized_surfaces_typed_error()

contrast crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/client.rs:315-365 which has `follows_next_link_across_pages` and `refuses_off_origin_next_link`

crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/models.rs:150-163 `optional_unix_timestamp_ser` (used by `SecretAttributesRequest.expires`) has no test; commands/keyvault.rs:109-116 sends `expires: Some(e)` on every rotation.
findings.rationale: The origin guard at client.rs:155-160 ("refusing to follow nextLink to a different origin") protects the vault bearer and is untested in this crate; a regression would send a Key Vault token off-host silently. The rotation path's only wire-format detail — `exp` as Unix seconds under `attributes` — has no serialisation test, so a serde rename slip would set no expiry on every rotated secret (Key Vault treats a missing `exp` as forever) without any test noticing. Neither crate tests the `MAX_PAGES` guard added in the paging fix.
findings.proposal: Add wiremock tests in keyvault client.rs: (1) two-page `nextLink` list returns 2+1 items and the second request carries no `api-version`; (2) off-origin `nextLink` → `Protocol` with only the host in the message and no second request received; (3) `set_secret` with `attributes.expires = Some(ts)` matches `body_json` `{"value":..,"attributes":{"enabled":true,"exp":<secs>}}`; (4) a self-referencing `nextLink` mock hits the page cap → `Protocol`. In arm client.rs add a `list_log_analytics_workspaces` test asserting `properties.customerId` is read. Mirror (4) in ARM.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: the tests module at crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/client.rs:274-393 contains exactly `list_secrets_returns_items`, `set_secret_puts_value`, `get_secret_reads_value`, `retries_on_429`, `unauthorized_surfaces_typed_error`. There is no test for `nextLink` paging (client.rs:72-91), the `check_origin` refusal at client.rs:155-160 (core::net has `same_origin` unit tests at net.rs:41-64, but the KV wiring — that `send_core_absolute` passes `check_origin = true` — is unpinned), the `MAX_PAGES` cap, or `exp`/`nbf` serialisation of `SecretAttributesRequest` (models.rs:109-125 via `optional_unix_timestamp_ser` at :150-163; the only models test, :194-206, sends `attributes: None`). `rotate_app_credential` always sends `expires: Some(e)` (commands/keyvault.rs:109-116), so a rename slip would silently produce never-expiring vault versions. ARM's client.rs:316-365 does cover paging and off-origin, but neither crate tests `MAX_PAGES` and ARM has no `list_log_analytics_workspaces`/`customerId` test. Concrete, cheap wiremock additions on a bearer-protecting guard; medium is fair.

findings.title: Role-definition name resolution is copy-pasted between the MI and Key Vault sweeps and cached per subscription-prefixed path; two high-privilege lists live outside `core::azure_roles`
findings.rationale: Built-in role definitions (`Owner`, `Reader`, `Key Vault Secrets Officer`…) share one GUID across every subscription but each subscription-prefixed path is a distinct cache key, so a 30-subscription estate resolves `Owner` 30 times per sweep and stores 30 cache entries. The 30-line block is copy-pasted, so the caching rules ("only a real name is cached") can drift between the MI view and the vault sweep; the two hard-coded privilege name lists overlap and neither lives with the role knowledge in core.
findings.proposal: Extract `commands/arm_roles.rs::resolve_role_names(arm, cache, tenant_id, ids)` used by both keyvault_rbac.rs and managed_identity.rs. Key the cache (and the fan-out dedupe) by `azure_roles::role_id_tail(id)` but fetch each GUID via the first absolute path seen for it, not the tenant-level `/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions/{guid}` path — that path resolves built-in roles only; custom roles are defined at a subscription/management-group scope and 404 at tenant level, and `get_role_definition` (client.rs:138) requires an absolute path anyway. Move `HIGH_PRIVILEGE_ROLES` (managed_identity.rs:27-32) and `KV_HIGH_PRIVILEGE_ROLES` (keyvault_rbac.rs:41-51) into `core::azure_roles` as one table with a context parameter, keeping the existing `high_privilege_roles_flagged_exactly` expectations.
findings.verifier_notes: Duplication verified: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/keyvault_rbac.rs:220-249 and managed_identity.rs:267-304 are the same 30-line block; both key the cache as `{tenant}|arm_roledef|{full path}` (grep shows exactly these two sites), and ARM returns built-in role definition ids as subscription-prefixed paths, so the same Owner GUID is fetched and cached once per subscription. `core::azure_roles::role_id_tail` (azure_roles.rs:51-56) already exists. The proposal's 'prefer the tenant-level path for built-ins' is unsafe for custom roles without a fallback, hence partially. Low.

findings.title: `LogAnalyticsClient::query` and the ARM list calls splice server-supplied ids (`customerId`, `subscriptionId`) into URL paths with no structural check, unlike `get_role_definition` which refuses the same class
findings.rationale: The crate's own reasoning treats ARM response fields as attacker-influenced and refuses `?`/`#`/authority tricks for `role_definition_id`, but `customerId` and `subscriptionId` (also ARM output) reach `format!` unchecked: `?`/`#` would inject or truncate the query and `../` segments are normalised by `url`, redirecting the call to a different same-origin path. Severity is low because the value follows a `/`, so the authority cannot change and the bearer stays on-origin; the exposure is path/query rewriting with the operator's own token.
findings.proposal: Add `fn require_guid(s: &str) -> Result<()>` (36 chars, hex + hyphens) in `azapptoolkit-arm` and apply it to `workspace_customer_id`, every `subscription_id` parameter, and `principal_id` (currently only quote-escaped), returning `ArmError::Protocol`. Unit-test with `sub?api-version=x`, `../providers/…`, and a valid GUID.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/loganalytics.rs:51-54 splices `workspace_customer_id` (from `ws.properties.customer_id`, an ARM response field, usage.rs:129) into the path; client.rs:63-66, :82-85, :115-118 splice `subscription_id` (from `list_subscriptions`, an ARM response) with no check; `list_role_assignments_at_scope` (client.rs:96-100) splices `scope` = `vault.id` from ARM with only trim — a further instance the reviewer did not list. By contrast `get_role_definition` (client.rs:133-151) refuses non-absolute ids, `?`/`#`, and off-origin authority, and its doc (:126-132) explicitly frames ARM response fields as attacker-influenced. The inconsistency with the crate's own stated threat model is real; practical exploitation requires attacker-controlled ARM responses and cannot move the bearer off-origin (value follows a `/`), so low is honest. `require_guid` for customerId/subscriptionId/principalId plus an absolute-path check for `scope` is small and consistent with existing guards.

findings.title: `Subscription` drops the `state` field, so Disabled/Warned/Deleted subscriptions are fanned out to and their failures counted as coverage gaps (`skipped`) or logged as warnings
findings.rationale: ARM's `/subscriptions` returns `state` (Enabled, Warned, PastDue, Disabled, Deleted). Reads against a Disabled/Deleted subscription fail, so every sweep (`list_managed_identity_azure_roles`, `sweep_key_vault_access`, `list_available_key_vaults`, `enumerate_azure_role_ids`, `discover_workspace`) pays a round trip, logs a warning, and reports the subscription as a coverage failure the operator cannot act on. Filtering up front makes `skipped`/`vaults_failed` mean what their docs say.
findings.proposal: Add `#[serde(default)] pub state: Option<String>` to `Subscription`; in the five consumers, partition out `state != Some("Enabled")` before the fan-out and report them separately (e.g. `subscriptions_inactive: usize`) instead of counting them as failures. One-line wiremock assertion in `lists_subscriptions`.
findings.verifier_notes: The premise — 'Reads against a Disabled/Deleted subscription fail' — is contradicted by Microsoft Learn 'Azure subscription states': Disabled, Warned, Expired and Past Due subscriptions all explicitly allow GET ('Your resources are still available, so you can retrieve or delete them (GET, DELETE)'; only PUT/PATCH/POST are blocked), and Deleted subscriptions have their resources removed and are not a persistent listing state. So the fan-outs in managed_identity.rs:223-246, keyvault_rbac.rs:113-131, keyvault.rs:204-227, readiness.rs:220-250 and usage.rs:90-115 do not pay failed round trips for non-Enabled subscriptions, and `skipped`/`vaults_failed` are not inflated by them. Worse, the proposal to partition out `state != "Enabled"` would HIDE genuine role assignments and vaults on disabled subscriptions — grants that become live again on reactivation — which is a regression for a security-posture tool. Adding `state` to `Subscription` (models.rs:14-20) as display metadata would be harmless but has no coverage-accuracy benefit.

findings.title: ARM 409 `RoleAssignmentExists` on `create_role_assignment` reaches the operator as a raw `arm error (409): {json}`
findings.rationale: Re-assigning a role the identity already holds at that scope is the most common operator slip in this dialog; ARM answers 409 with `{"error":{"code":"RoleAssignmentExists",...}}`, and the user sees a JSON blob under the generic `arm_error` code with no retry/no guidance. The client exposes enough (`Api{status:409, body}`) to classify it.
findings.proposal: In `assign_managed_identity_azure_role`, match `ArmError::Api { status: 409, body }` whose body contains `RoleAssignmentExists` and return `UiError::validation("already_assigned", "This identity already holds that role at this scope.")` (or treat as success and refresh the list). Add a unit test on the mapping. Optionally have the ARM client parse the `error.code` field into `Api` for all 4xx so callers stop substring-matching JSON.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/transport.rs:83-92 maps every non-429 4xx (including 409) to `ArmError::Api { status, body }` with the raw JSON body; `assign_managed_identity_azure_role` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/managed_identity.rs:397-407) specialises only `forbidden`; grep for `409`/`RoleAssignmentExists`/`already_assigned` across src-tauri and web-rs finds nothing. ARM does answer a duplicate assignment with 409 `RoleAssignmentExists`, so the operator sees `arm error (409): {…json…}` under the generic `arm_error` code. Proposal is small and reasonable; treating it as success and refreshing is defensible since the desired end state already holds. Low.

findings.title: Stale Key Vault crate comments: header claims no shared retry code while importing `core::http_retry`, `lib.rs` lists a nonexistent `delete_secret`, and `get_secret`'s `version` is unvalidated and never used by any caller
findings.rationale: The header contradicts the very imports beneath it (the loop was moved to core in the PR the module-level docs elsewhere cite), the crate doc advertises an operation that does not exist, and `version` is a path segment that skips the `validate_secret_name`-style guard the module doc says exists for "anything that flows into request URLs" — harmless today only because no caller passes it.
findings.proposal: Rewrite client.rs:3-6 to say the loop is `core::http_retry::with_retries` and only per-attempt status mapping is local; fix lib.rs:10; either drop the `version` parameter or validate it (32 lowercase hex chars) in `validate.rs` with a test. Also drop the unused `Serialize` derive on `Paged<T>` (models.rs:165).
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/client.rs:3-6 says 'We don't share code across crates (the Graph retry is tied to GraphError)' while lines 16-18 import `azapptoolkit_core::http_retry::{Attempt, RetryClass, RetryReason, parse_retry_after_seconds, with_retries}` and line 175 calls `with_retries`; ARM's header (client.rs:1-2) already says the opposite. lib.rs:9-10 lists `delete_secret`, which no file defines (grep). `get_secret(name, version)` (client.rs:93-100) validates `name` via `validate_secret_name` but splices `version` unvalidated, contrary to validate.rs:1-6's stated rule for path segments; the sole caller (commands/keyvault.rs:59) passes `None`. `Paged<T>` (models.rs:165-170) is `pub(crate)`, only ever deserialized, so `Serialize` is unused. All small and correct; low.

findings.title: `SecretValue` derives `Serialize` although nothing serialises it, so the redacted `Debug` can be bypassed by any future `serde_json::to_string`/JSON tracing field
findings.evidence:
crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/models.rs:40-43
/// `GET /secrets/{name}` — full value included.
#[derive(Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SecretValue {
    pub value: String,

models.rs:53-54 "/// Manual impl so a stray `{:?}` can't log the secret value"

`grep -rn SecretValue apps crates` outside the crate: only `KvSecretValueDto` (the IPC DTO) is used; no call serialises `SecretValue`.
findings.rationale: The workspace treats a derived `Debug` on a secret-bearing type as a defect and hand-writes redaction, but a derived `Serialize` gives an equally direct plaintext path (`tracing` JSON layers, `serde_json::to_string` in a future export/backup) that no test guards. Since the IPC boundary uses `KvSecretValueDto`, the derive is unused surface.
findings.proposal: Remove `Serialize` from `SecretValue` (keep `Deserialize`); if a serialiser is ever needed, implement it manually with the value redacted or gated. Consider the same for `KvSecretValueDto` if the IPC path can move to a redacted transport in future.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/models.rs:41-51 derives `Serialize` on `SecretValue`; grep for `SecretValue` outside the crate finds only comments, and inside the crate it is only deserialized (client.rs:99, :105) and mapped field-by-field into `KvSecretValueDto` (commands/keyvault.rs:60-68). The hand-written redacting `Debug` (models.rs:53-67) shows the workspace treats accidental plaintext emission as a defect; a derived `Serialize` is an equally direct path (`serde_json::to_string`, a JSON tracing layer) with no test guarding it, and removing it costs nothing. Note the workspace has no rule against `Serialize` on secret-bearing types per se (`KvSecretValueDto`, `PasswordCredential` need it for IPC), so this is a small hardening rather than a convention violation. Low.

findings.title: Both crates declare `tracing` but never use it, list `tokio` as a runtime dependency used only by `#[tokio::test]`, and pin `bytes = "1"` outside `[workspace.dependencies]`
findings.evidence:
crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/Cargo.toml:13-20
tokio = { workspace = true }
bytes = "1"
...
tracing = { workspace = true }

crates/azapptoolkit-arm/Cargo.toml:13-19 (same three lines)

`grep -rn "tracing" crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src` → no matches
`grep -rn "tokio::"` in both crates → only `#[tokio::test]` attributes (client.rs:285…, loganalytics.rs:88…), and `tokio` is already a dev-dependency in both

AGENTS.md:71 "**Workspace dependency** — add to `[workspace.dependencies]`, use `"name".workspace = true` ... Dependencies are a cost"
findings.rationale: Unused direct dependencies are noise for `cargo deny`/audit triage and contradict the workspace's stated dependency discipline; `bytes` being the only non-workspace dep in the tree is the kind of drift a future major bump silently splits.
findings.proposal: Delete `tracing` from both `[dependencies]`; move `tokio` to `[dev-dependencies]` only (it stays available transitively via reqwest at runtime); add `bytes = "1"` to `[workspace.dependencies]` and reference it with `workspace = true`. Consider a `cargo machete` step in `just verify-full`.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/Cargo.toml:13-20 and crates/azapptoolkit-arm/Cargo.toml:13-19 both declare `tokio = { workspace = true }`, `bytes = "1"`, `tracing = { workspace = true }` under `[dependencies]`; `grep -rn tracing` over both crates' `src/` returns nothing, and `tokio` appears only as `#[tokio::test]` (already covered by the `[dev-dependencies]` tokio entry in both manifests). AGENTS.md:71 states the workspace-dependency convention. Minor overstatement: `bytes = "1"` is not 'the only non-workspace dep in the tree' — it is pinned identically in four crates (graph, exchange, arm, keyvault Cargo.toml:14), and auth (`keyring-core`, `webbrowser`, `windows-native-keyring-store`) and src-tauri (`tauri-plugin-*`, `rand`) also carry non-workspace deps; the fix should hoist `bytes` for all four. No `cargo machete`/udeps step exists in the justfile or CI. Low.

findings.title: Blocking keyring delete runs inline on the tokio worker (and under the refresh lock), contradicting the crate's own rule
findings.rationale: save_refresh_token (:457) and load_refresh_token (:509) are both wrapped in tokio::task::spawn_blocking with an explicit comment saying why, but delete_refresh_token is called synchronously twice: at :535 inside the refresh path while the refresh mutex is held (exactly the scenario the :503-506 comment warns about), and at :564 in sign_out. delete_chunks performs one OS keyring round trip per chunk (Windows Credential Manager; Linux secret-service over D-Bus via zbus), so an invalid-grant purge or a sign-out stalls the async worker and every other tokio task for the duration. The clippy `unused_async` hit on sign_out is the symptom that led here.
findings.proposal: Wrap both calls the same way as save/load: `let (t, oid) = (tenant.tenant_id.clone(), tenant.account_oid.clone()); tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || delete_refresh_token(&t, &oid)).await.map_err(|e| AuthError::Keyring(format!("keyring delete task failed: {e}")))??;` at :564, and the `let _ =` form of the same at :535. Consider a private `async fn delete_refresh_token_blocking(&self, tenant)` helper so a third caller cannot regress. Effect: no tokio worker stall during sign-out or refresh-token purge; sign_out's `async` becomes genuine and the lint goes away.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is real. crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:457 (save) and :509 (load) wrap the keyring call in tokio::task::spawn_blocking with the explicit rationale at :503-506 ('otherwise it stalls other tokio tasks while this holds the refresh lock'); :535 calls delete_refresh_token inline while the refresh mutex (:485-486) is still held, and :564 calls it inline in sign_out, which is a Tauri command (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/auth.rs:49). token_cache.rs:376-396 shows delete_refresh_token -> delete_chunks does one keyring_core::Entry::delete_credential round trip per chunk. No comment, CHANGELOG entry, or docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md line justifies the asymmetry, and AuthError::Keyring(String) exists (auth/src/error.rs:45) so the proposed map_err shape compiles. Severity downgraded to low, not medium: both paths are rare (once per sign-out; once per InvalidGrant purge, where the keyring was just unlocked by the load at :509), Tauri's multi-thread runtime confines the stall to one worker rather than 'every other tokio task', and the lock held at :535 only delays refreshes for that same tenant/scope set which would wait anyway. Still a real consistency bug worth the small fix; the private helper suggestion is the right shape.

findings.title: AuthService::tenants() is dead public API
findings.evidence:
mod.rs:679-681:
    pub async fn tenants(&self) -> Vec<TenantContext> {
        self.known_tenants.lock().values().cloned().collect()
    }
$ grep -rn 'tenants()' --include=*.rs apps crates | grep -v 'fn tenants'
  -> only crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:670 (a comment: "`tenants()` / consent lookups read `known_tenants`.")
clippy (nursery): warning: unused `async` for function with no await statements --> crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:679:5

findings.title: Six unused dependencies confirmed across five manifests
findings.evidence:
$ cargo-machete (repo root):
azapptoolkit-arm -- ./crates/azapptoolkit-arm/Cargo.toml: thiserror, tracing
azapptoolkit-graph -- ./crates/azapptoolkit-graph/Cargo.toml: thiserror
azapptoolkit-keyvault -- ./crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/Cargo.toml: thiserror, tracing
azapptoolkit-exchange -- ./crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/Cargo.toml: url
desktop -- ./apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml: anyhow, thiserror
azapptoolkit-web-rs -- ./apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml: tracing
Confirmed by grep (word match over src/, build.rs, tests/): arm `tracing` 0 files; keyvault `tracing` 0 files; exchange `url::`/`Url` 0 hits (only local variables named url); desktop `anyhow` 0 files, `thiserror` 0 files; web-rs `tracing` 0 files.
Manifest lines: crates/azapptoolkit-arm/Cargo.toml:19 `tracing = { workspace = true }`; crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/Cargo.toml:20 `tracing = { workspace = true }`; crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/Cargo.toml:18 `url = { workspace = true }`; apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:42-43 `anyhow = { workspace = true }` / `thiserror = { workspace = true }`; apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml:63 `tracing = "0.1"`.
The three `thiserror` hits on arm/graph/keyvault are FALSE POSITIVES: the macro they consume expands `#[derive(Debug, ::thiserror::Error)]` (core/src/http_error.rs:65), so the dependency is required.
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md says "Dependencies are a cost: prefer std + existing crates", yet six declared dependencies are never referenced. They are harmless at link time (all are elsewhere in the graph) but they mislead readers about what each crate does (e.g. `url` in exchange suggests URL parsing that does not happen), they are extra surface for audit/deny churn, and in web-rs a direct `tracing = "0.1"` with zero call sites is pure noise.
findings.proposal: Remove: arm `tracing`, keyvault `tracing`, exchange `url`, desktop `anyhow` + `thiserror`, web-rs `tracing`; regenerate both lockfiles in the same commit (all verify gates run `--locked`). Leave `thiserror` on arm/graph/keyvault (see the macro finding) or add `[package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored = ["thiserror"]` there with a one-line comment pointing at http_error.rs:65.
findings.verifier_notes: Manifest lines are exact: arm/Cargo.toml:19 tracing, keyvault/Cargo.toml:20 tracing, exchange/Cargo.toml:18 url, src-tauri/Cargo.toml:42-43 anyhow + thiserror, web-rs/Cargo.toml:63 tracing = "0.1". Word-match greps over each crate's src/, tests/ and build.rs return zero hits for all six (exchange's only 'url' hit is a local variable at src/client/transport.rs:67; UiError lives in crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/lib.rs, so src-tauri never names thiserror; src-tauri does not invoke http_error_enum!). The thiserror false-positive analysis for arm/graph/keyvault is correct (core/src/http_error.rs:65 expands `::thiserror::Error`) — and per finding 4 that dependency is permanently required, so the machete-ignore metadata is the right fix there. No repo_invariants test, doc or comment defends any of the six. Severity lowered from medium to low: every crate is already elsewhere in both lockfiles, so this is hygiene with no security, build-time, or audit/deny surface impact.

findings.title: No unused-dependency gate anywhere in CI or the justfile
findings.evidence:
$ grep -rn 'machete\|udeps' .github justfile docs/DEVELOPMENT.md
  -> (no output)
justfile:329: verify-full: _verify-core audit web-audit deny web-deny web-itest web-itest-size
ci.yml:264-290 run only `just audit`, `just web-audit`, `just deny`, `just web-deny`.
And the consequence, from cargo-machete at the repo root: six unused deps across arm, keyvault, exchange, desktop, web-rs (see the deps finding).
findings.rationale: The repo already runs four dependency-policy gates (audit/deny for both trees) and pins their tool versions in CI, but nothing detects a dependency that is declared and never used. Six such deps accumulated silently. cargo-machete is fast (no compile), needs no network, and is a one-liner to add.
findings.proposal: Add a `machete` recipe (`cargo machete` at the root and `cd apps/desktop/web-rs && cargo machete`, both treating findings as failures) to `verify-full` and to the CI `deps` job next to cargo-deny (install pinned like cargo-deny is). Add `[package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored = ["thiserror"]` to arm/graph/keyvault (or fix the macro so it is not needed). Effect: an unused dep fails CI at the PR that introduces it.
findings.verifier_notes: grep for 'machete' or 'udeps' across .github/, justfile, docs/, deny.toml and all Cargo.toml files returns nothing; justfile:329 `verify-full: _verify-core audit web-audit deny web-deny web-itest web-itest-size` and ci.yml:250-290 (audit and deny jobs) confirm only audit/deny run. The deny job already installs pinned tools through taiki-e/install-action (ci.yml:283-285 `tool: just,cargo-deny@0.20.2`), so adding cargo-machete there is the one-liner the finding says. Feasibility caveat the finding half-states: the thiserror ignore on arm/graph/keyvault is not a stopgap 'or fix the macro' choice — finding 4 shows the macro cannot be fixed, so `[package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored = ["thiserror"]` is the permanent form. Severity lowered to low: the six deps it would have caught are harmless, so this is a hygiene gate, not a correctness or supply-chain one.

findings.title: http_error_enum! consumers must carry an unnamed `thiserror` dependency — document it at the macro and in the manifests rather than trying to re-export it
findings.rationale: Because the macro resolves `::thiserror` in the consumer's namespace, arm/graph/keyvault must each carry a dependency they never name in source. That makes cargo-machete (and any future reader) report three false positives, and a crate that adopts the macro later will fail to compile with a confusing "unresolved crate thiserror" error until it copies the dep. The standard fix is the `$crate` re-export idiom.
findings.proposal: Keep `thiserror = { workspace = true }` in arm/graph/keyvault. Add one sentence to the http_error_enum! doc comment (core/src/http_error.rs ~:36) stating that a consumer crate must depend on `thiserror` directly because thiserror's derive expands hard-coded `::thiserror::__private` paths, and a one-line `# needed by core::http_error_enum!` comment beside each of the three manifest lines. If cargo-machete is adopted (finding 3), add `[package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored = ["thiserror"]` to those three crates as a permanent, not temporary, entry.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise true: crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/http_error.rs:65 derives `::thiserror::Error`, core/src/lib.rs has no thiserror re-export, and arm/graph/keyvault never name thiserror in source (only exchange does, error.rs:1). Proposal refuted on two counts. (1) 'core already depends on it' is false: crates/azapptoolkit-core/Cargo.toml:10-26 lists no thiserror (TokenError at core/src/token.rs:25 derives Debug/Clone/PartialEq/Eq with a manual Display at :57). (2) More importantly, the $crate re-export idiom does not work for thiserror: thiserror-impl's derive hard-codes absolute paths into the expansion — `::thiserror::#private::Var` (thiserror-impl-2.0.21/src/fmt.rs:149), `::thiserror::#private::Error` / `AsDynError` (expand.rs:39,43,49,67-68) — so even with `#[derive($crate::thiserror::Error)]` the generated code still resolves `::thiserror::__private` in the CONSUMER crate, and arm/graph/keyvault would fail to compile without their own direct dependency. The three manifests must keep thiserror.

findings.title: Exchange's hand-rolled ExchangeError::ui_code / is_retryable has no conformance test: Token passthrough and the retryable set are unpinned
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md's "One definition per policy" rule is pinned by four tests in arm and keyvault (retryable set is exactly throttle/server/network; Token keeps its re-auth-fatal code; 403 hint comes from the capabilities catalog). Graph, the highest-volume client, has none of them, and exchange — the ONE client whose ui_code is hand-rolled rather than macro-generated (its Forbidden is a struct variant the macro cannot express) — is precisely "the part a hand-rolled re-implementation would get subtly wrong" that arm's own test header says is worth pinning. If someone flattens ExchangeError::Token to "token_error", every Exchange fan-out would again warn its way through a dead session, and no test would notice. The arm header's claim that graph has "a dedicated tests/ tree" is also false (graph's tests are in-crate under src/client/tests/), which is how the gap went unnoticed.
findings.proposal: Add crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/tests/error_conformance.rs mirroring arm's file with the three assertions that apply: (a) for every variant is_retryable() == http_retry::is_retryable_code(ui_code()) and the retryable set is exactly [throttled, server_error, network_error]; (b) every REAUTH_FATAL_CODES entry survives ExchangeError::Token(...) as ui_code() and is not retryable; (c) Forbidden{had_diagnostics:true}.ui_hint() == capability("exchange_rbac").remediation and had_diagnostics:false returns Some(_). Skip the graph file (or add a two-line comment in graph/src/error.rs noting its policy is pinned by the macro's other instantiations). Reword arm's header (arm/tests/error_conformance.rs:7-8) to 'graph's tests live in-crate under src/client/tests/'.
findings.verifier_notes: Exchange half confirmed: `ls crates/*/tests` shows only arm and keyvault have tests/error_conformance.rs; crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/error.rs:64-81 is a hand-written ui_code table whose Token arm (:76-78) is the passthrough, and its inline tests (:179-264) cover only is_missing_object, the membership body matchers and the two Forbidden hint branches — nothing pins the retryable set or that REAUTH_FATAL_CODES survive Token. This is load-bearing: fan-outs call `session.note_code(err.ui_code())` (commands/sharepoint.rs:926, backup.rs:351, restore.rs:412) and repo_invariants/fanout.rs:105-113 records that flattening to `token_error` once made is_reauth_fatal unfirable; no test elsewhere (grep for passthrough_code/ExchangeError::Token in src-tauri tests) covers it. Graph half overstated: GraphError (graph/src/error.rs:10-16) is a pure http_error_enum! instance with no `extra` variants and no per-crate ui_hint, so its is_retryable/ui_code are byte-identical to the expansion arm's and keyvault's tests already exercise; a hand-written `is_retryable` override would be a duplicate-inherent-method compile error, and the fourth (Forbidden → capability hint) test has no graph analogue since graph 403 remediation is spliced in the desktop layer (`graph_err::forbidden_remediation`). A graph conformance file therefore adds near-zero protection. Arm header nit: graph does have a `tests` directory (src/client/tests/, 10 modules), so 'dedicated tests/ tree' is imprecise rather than false. Severity kept medium for the exchange half only.

findings.title: CI clippy runs only the default set; a curated, mostly advisory pedantic pass would have caught the blocking keyring call and ~100 mechanical clones
findings.evidence:
justfile:236-237:
clippy: _stub-frontend-dist
    cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
justfile:273-274 web-clippy: cargo clippy --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --all-targets --features test-support -- -D warnings
Cargo.toml:75-76 has only `[workspace.lints.rust] unsafe_code = "deny"` (no [workspace.lints.clippy]).
Pedantic+nursery tally, libraries (exit 0 at default level):
  8 future cannot be sent between threads safely | 7 deriving PartialEq and can implement Eq | 4 unused `async` | 4 Option<&T> instead of &Option<T> | 1 redundant clone | 1 `format!(..)` appended to existing String | 1 unnecessarily wrapped by Option | 1 unused `self` | 1 casting u64 to i64 may wrap
Pedantic+nursery tally, web-rs (wasm target, exit 0 at default level):
  99 redundant clone | 42 this argument is passed by value, but not consumed | 46 map(..).unwrap_or* on Option | 9 `format!(..)` appended to existing String | 20 large argument passed by value (468/624 bytes)
Examples: src/components/aap_migration_report.rs:53 `let unattempted = report.unattempted.clone();` | src/components/app_site_access_panel.rs:68 `let tenant_id = t.tenant_id.clone();` | src/components/audit_dashboard.rs:127 `let tenant_id = t.tenant_id.clone();` | src/components/bulk_action_bar.rs:1006-1120 seven needless_pass_by_value hits.
findings.rationale: The repo treats `-D warnings` as a gate but only on clippy's default set, so mechanical waste accumulates unnoticed: 99 clones of Strings/Vecs on their last use in view code that ships in the wasm bundle, 42 owned parameters never consumed, and in the libraries the `unused_async` that exposed the blocking keyring call. Each of these lints is high-precision (the counts above are small in the libs and mechanical in web-rs), so enabling them as "warn" (== error under -D warnings) is cheap once the existing sites are fixed.
findings.proposal: Add a non-gating `just clippy-pedantic` recipe (both trees) with an explicit allow-list so the tally is one command away. Gate only the low-false-positive subset via `[workspace.lints.clippy]` mirrored in web-rs (`unused_async`, `ref_option`, `format_push_string`, `unnecessary_wraps`, `unused_self`, `cast_possible_wrap` = "warn") after fixing the handful of existing sites, and extend repo_invariants/release.rs to diff `[lints.clippy]` alongside `[lints.rust]`. Leave `redundant_clone`, `needless_pass_by_value`, `derive_partial_eq_without_eq`, `map_unwrap_or` and `future_not_send` advisory.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise true: justfile:236-237 and :273-274 run the default clippy set with -D warnings; Cargo.toml:75-76 has only `[workspace.lints.rust] unsafe_code = "deny"`; no clippy.toml or .cargo/config.toml exists; repo_invariants/release.rs:27-45 diffs only the `[lints.rust]` bodies. The cited example sites are real (aap_migration_report.rs:53 — `report` is never used after :53 so the clone is genuinely redundant; app_site_access_panel.rs:68; audit_dashboard.rs:127; bulk_action_bar.rs:1006-1120 are plain `parse_*` helpers taking owned Bulk*Result values). The tallies cannot be verified read-only and are plausible. Overstated: (1) 'bundle-size waste' — a redundant String/Vec clone is a runtime allocation, not meaningful wasm code size; (2) the only real defect this surfaced is finding 0; (3) gating under -D warnings is not a safe default for several of the listed lints: `redundant_clone` and `future_not_send` are nursery precisely for false positives, `derive_partial_eq_without_eq` was demoted to nursery for FP/semver reasons, `needless_pass_by_value` fights Leptos's by-value prop and closure-capture style, and `map_unwrap_or` is a style preference. The finding's own alternative (a non-gating recipe) is the sound part.

findings.title: Transport helpers bound `B: Serialize + ?Sized` without `Sync`, so Send-ness of every write future depends on each call site
findings.evidence:
transport.rs:86-96:
    pub(crate) async fn scoped_send_json<B, T>(
        &self,
        token: &Arc<dyn BearerProvider>,
        method: Method,
        url: &str,
        body: &B,
    ) -> Result<T>
    where
        B: Serialize + ?Sized,
clippy (nursery, 8 sites): warning: future cannot be sent between threads safely — "has type `&B` which is not `Send`, because `B` is not `Sync`" at transport.rs:92, :111, :126, :397, :417; applications.rs:587 (patch_application_web); service_principals.rs:618 (patch_service_principal); keyvault/src/client.rs:118 (send_json).
findings.rationale: Tauri `#[tauri::command] async fn`s must return Send futures, so today every call compiles only because each concrete body type happens to be Sync. A future caller passing a body holding a `Cell`/`Rc`/`RefCell` (or a `dyn Serialize` without `+ Sync`) would fail deep inside `generate_handler!` with an opaque "future is not Send" error rather than at the helper. All eight warnings share this single root cause.
findings.proposal: Add `+ Sync` to the `B` bound on the eight generic helpers (`B: Serialize + ?Sized + Sync`). No call site changes (all current bodies are Sync). Effect: Send-ness becomes a signature-level guarantee; the eight nursery warnings disappear, which also makes `future_not_send` enableable on the libraries if desired.
findings.verifier_notes: Bounds verified: crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/transport.rs:93, :111, :126, :398, :417 all read `B: Serialize + ?Sized` with no Sync; applications.rs:583 `patch_application_web<B: serde::Serialize>` and service_principals.rs:614 `patch_service_principal<B: serde::Serialize>` likewise; keyvault/src/client.rs:118-120 same. Each takes `body: &B` / `Option<&B>` across an `.await`, so the future is Send only if B: Sync. The other capture is fine (`BearerProvider: Send + Sync`, core/src/token.rs:76). Tauri async commands must produce Send futures, so the premise about where a non-Sync body would fail (inside generate_handler!, opaquely) holds. Adding `+ Sync` is a zero-cost tightening with no call-site change (all current bodies are typed structs, `serde_json::Value`, or slices). Low severity is honest: no current caller is affected.

findings.title: `just check` type-checks the frontend without the test harness that `web-clippy` gates, so a GUI-harness compile error skips the inner loop
findings.evidence:
justfile:243-246:
# The inner loop while iterating: type-check BOTH trees (the root workspace incl.
# every test target, and the wasm frontend) with no codegen and no tests. Not a
# CI gate — `verify` is — but it catches the compile error `verify` would take
# minutes to reach, ...
justfile:249-251:
check: _stub-frontend-dist
    cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets
    cargo check --locked --manifest-path apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
justfile:273-274:
web-clippy:
    cargo clippy --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --all-targets --features test-support -- -D warnings
findings.rationale: The recipe's stated purpose is to catch, in seconds, the compile error `verify` would reach minutes later, and for the root tree it does pass `--all-targets`. For the frontend it omits `--all-targets --features test-support`, so `src/test_support/`, `src/ipc_mock/` and the four gui_N.rs shards (the only behavioural gate for the frontend) are not type-checked until `just verify` reaches web-clippy. A signature change in a view that breaks a GUI test helper passes `just check`.
findings.proposal: Change line 251 to `cargo check --locked --manifest-path apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --all-targets --features test-support` (the flags web-clippy already uses; the wasm check with those flags completed here in well under a minute on warm artifacts). Effect: the inner loop matches what CI compiles.
findings.verifier_notes: justfile:249-251 `check` runs `cargo check --locked --manifest-path apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` with neither `--all-targets` nor `--features test-support`, while :273-274 `web-clippy` uses both. apps/desktop/web-rs/tests/ holds gui_1..4.rs, gui/, and demo_fixture_coverage.rs, and web-rs/src/lib.rs:30/:36 gate `ipc_mock` and `test_support` behind the `mock-ipc`/`test-support` features, so none of that is type-checked by `just check`. The recipe's own comment (justfile:243-246) promises 'every test target' but only delivers it for the root tree. Proposal is feasible (web-clippy already compiles exactly this configuration). One nuance to carry into the change: with `--features test-support` the inner loop no longer checks the shipped feature set's `cfg(not(feature))` paths, the same trade-off web-clippy already makes and `web-build` in `verify` covers; update the :243-246 comment accordingly.

findings.title: proc-macro-error2 2.0.1 triggers a future-incompatibility hard error (E0365) in the wasm build; the pinned toolchain hides it until the next MSRV bump

$ grep -rn 'future-incompat' .github justfile docs -> (no output)
findings.rationale: rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.98.1, so today this is only a warning. But the repo's MSRV-bump procedure ("Bump intentionally in lockstep") has no step that surfaces future-incompat reports, and this one sits under leptos_macro — the proc-macro every view in the frontend expands through. When the lint becomes a hard error, the first sign will be the wasm build failing on a toolchain bump PR with an error in a transitive crate, and the fix (leptos releasing a version off proc-macro-error2 2.0.1, or a `[patch]`) is not local.
findings.proposal: Add `cargo report future-incompatibilities` (both trees) to the MSRV/toolchain-bump checklist in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md and/or a non-gating CI step that prints the report so a new entry is visible in the run log. Track leptos 0.9 (beta today), which is the likely path off proc-macro-error2 2.0.1; if the toolchain bump lands first, a `[patch.crates-io] proc-macro-error2 = { git = ... }` to a fixed fork is the fallback. Effect: no surprise hard error on the next toolchain bump.
findings.verifier_notes: apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.lock:1361-1362 pins proc-macro-error2 2.0.1 (absent from the root Cargo.lock); the registry source /root/.cargo/registry/src/*/proc-macro-error2-2.0.1/src/lib.rs:494 is `pub use proc_macro;`; and the existing local report apps/desktop/web-rs/target/.future-incompat-report.json records exactly `warning[E0365]: extern crate proc_macro is private and cannot be re-exported ... issue #127909 ... will become a hard error` for proc-macro-error2@2.0.1, reachable via leptos_macro 0.8.17 / reactive_stores_macro / syn_derive (lock :1020, :1501, :1514, :1856). rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.98.1 with 'Bump intentionally in lockstep with the workspace MSRV', docs/DEVELOPMENT.md has no bump checklist (only :20 mentions the pin), and grep finds no 'future-incompat' step in .github/, justfile or docs/. The 'latest version' and 'leptos 0.9 drops it' claims could not be checked offline and are appropriately hedged. Nit: the anchor web-rs/Cargo.toml:22 is `unsafe_code = "deny"`; the relevant line is :28 (`leptos = { version = "0.8" ... }`). The proposal (docs checklist item + non-gating CI print, [patch] as fallback) is proportionate; low is the right severity since the pinned toolchain makes this a visible failure on a deliberate bump PR, not a silent regression.

findings.title: tauri-sys git pin predates an upstream workaround for a reported (open, unconfirmed) wasm-bindgen function-table exhaustion in event deserialization
findings.evidence:
apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml:31-33:
# Pinned to an exact rev (not the `v2` branch) so WASM builds are reproducible —
# a branch pin silently absorbs whatever upstream pushes. Bump deliberately.
tauri-sys = { git = "https://github.com/JonasKruckenberg/tauri-sys", rev = "289bd29fcbce1ee86c45089477898dbdf23f8fca", features = ["core", "event"] }

Pinned rev source (~/.cargo/git/checkouts/tauri-sys-*/289bd29/src/core.rs:126):
    let _ = tx.unbounded_send(serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value(raw).unwrap());
(same at core.rs:14 `swb::from_value(value).unwrap()` and :25-26 for every invoke result/error)

Upstream v2 branch (fetched): 289bd29 dated 2026-05-08; 4 newer commits incl. 1ffc6fa 2026-09-08 "Update conversion of `JsValues` (#113)" whose PR text says it addresses wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen#5324 and bumps to 0.2.5. Issue #5324 title: "WASM function table exhaustion with repeated `serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value()` in closures" — "A Tauri + Leptos application crashes with 'RuntimeError: Out of bounds table access' after deserializing multiple events".

Our consumption: apps/desktop/web-rs/src/bindings/events.rs:19 `listen::<AuditProgress>("audit-progress")` (8 such streams: audit, bulk, backup, restore, site-sweep, keyvault-sweep, mailbox-probe, updater); backend has 30 `.emit(` sites, e.g. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/bulk.rs:993 `progress.emit(BulkProgress {`. crates.io: "crate `tauri-sys` does not exist" — git is the only channel, and dependabot.yml:72-83 cannot advance a git rev.
findings.rationale: The reported failure mode (Tauri + Leptos, many events deserialized through serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value inside the listener closure) is exactly this app's progress-stream path, and a tenant-wide audit or bulk remediation emits one event per app across thousands of apps. Upstream shipped a workaround four commits after the pinned rev; the pin comment says "bump deliberately" but there is no crates.io release for Dependabot to track and no reminder mechanism, so the pin silently rots. Not reproduced in this repo — probability scales with event volume — but a webview crash mid-bulk-run is severe and the fix is upstream already.
findings.proposal: Bump apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml:33 to upstream v2 rev 1ffc6fa (or head 571cef4), regenerate web-rs/Cargo.lock, and run `just web-itest`. Blast radius is small: the diff only adds `T: 'static` bounds on invoke/invoke_result, a new `error::Deserialize` type, and `serde_json`/`tracing` deps (serde_json 1.0.151 and log 0.4.34 are already in the web-rs lock; wasm-bindgen 0.2.129 satisfies the new 0.2.127 floor). Note the upstream change also stops panicking on an undeserializable event (now `log::error!`, which no web-rs subscriber prints) — record that behaviour change next to the pin. Add a review date to the pin comment and, if desired, a `just deps-git-status` recipe (`git ls-remote` + commits ahead of the rev); the existing informal practice is the release-time check recorded in docs/CHANGELOG-archive.md:127.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence verified. Pinned checkout (~/.cargo/git/checkouts/tauri-sys-*/289bd29) has `serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value(raw).unwrap()` inside the listener Closure at src/event.rs:137 and :184, and in core.rs:14,25-26,126. A bare clone of upstream v2 shows exactly four commits after the pin; 1ffc6fa (2026-09-08, 'Update conversion of JsValues (#113)', bumps 0.2.4→0.2.5) adds lib.rs `from_value` that does `js_sys::JSON::stringify` + `serde_json::from_str` with the comment 'must serialize and deserialize to prevent overflowing wasm method table, see wasm-bindgen/issues/5324'. Fetched issue #5324: title matches, OPENED 2026-09-06, still OPEN, Tauri+Leptos+tauri-sys, error 'RuntimeError: Out of bounds table access'; the root-cause claim ('from_value creates a new WASM function for every field') is the reporter's own analysis with no maintainer comment, and wasm-bindgen 0.2.129's CHANGELOG (our lock) has no fix. Our exposure is real: 8 `listen::<..>` streams in web-rs/src/bindings/events.rs:19-77, consumed via hooks/use_progress_stream.rs for the component's lifetime, and the backend emits once per app (audit.rs:346,419; bulk.rs:993). Overstated: severity 'high' for an unreproduced, single-reporter, still-open issue whose mechanism the wasm-bindgen maintainers have not confirmed; 'the fix is upstream' (it is a workaround in tauri-sys, not a fix); and 'no reminder mechanism' (the pin is re-checked at release time, see CHANGELOG-archive.md:127, just not automated). Dependabot's inability to bump a git rev was not verifiable offline. The pin comment itself ('Bump deliberately') makes a deliberate bump on-convention.

findings.title: [workspace.dependencies] keyring-core alias names a package cargo cannot resolve, and no member uses it
findings.evidence:
Cargo.toml:43:
keyring-core = { package = "keyring_core", version = "1.0" }

crates/azapptoolkit-auth/Cargo.toml:20 (the only consumer, NOT via workspace):
keyring-core = "1.0"

Cargo.lock:2655-2657:
name = "keyring-core"
version = "1.0.0"
source = "registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"

Resolution test in a scratch manifest with `package = "keyring_core"`:
error: no matching package found
searched package name: `keyring_core`
perhaps you meant:      keyring-core
findings.rationale: The workspace entry is dead (auth declares its own requirement) and wrong (the crate on crates.io is `keyring-core`; cargo does not normalise underscores in `package =`). The moment anyone follows AGENTS.md's rule and switches auth to `keyring-core = { workspace = true }`, resolution fails with a confusing error. It also breaks the workspace's own convention that shared deps are workspace-managed.
findings.proposal: Change Cargo.toml:43 to `keyring-core = "1.0"` (drop the bogus `package = "keyring_core"`) and crates/azapptoolkit-auth/Cargo.toml:20 to `keyring-core = { workspace = true }`. No lockfile change results (same crate, same version).
findings.verifier_notes: Cargo.toml:43 `keyring-core = { package = "keyring_core", version = "1.0" }` is real; the only consumer, crates/azapptoolkit-auth/Cargo.toml:20, declares `keyring-core = "1.0"` directly, so the workspace entry is dead (introduced with PR #219, commit 06af5cc). Reproduced the resolution failure offline in a scratch manifest: `cargo metadata` with `package = "keyring_core"` → 'no matching package found / searched package name: `keyring_core` / perhaps you meant: keyring-core' (cargo does not normalise `-`/`_` in `package =`). Cargo.lock:2655 holds `keyring-core 1.0.0`. Nothing pins workspace-dependency consistency (tests/dependency_policy.rs only checks advisory-ignore sync). Severity lowered from medium: nothing is broken today, and the failure mode is loud and self-diagnosing at resolve time; it only fires when someone follows the AGENTS.md workspace-dependency rule.

findings.title: System-proxy support for all Graph/Exchange/KeyVault/ARM traffic depends on tauri-plugin-updater's default features, not our reqwest declaration
findings.evidence:
Cargo.toml:29:
reqwest = { version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["rustls", "json", "query", "form"] }

reqwest-0.13.5/Cargo.toml [features]:
default = ["default-tls", "charset", "http2", "system-proxy"]
system-proxy = ["hyper-util/client-proxy-system"]

`cargo tree --locked -p desktop -e features -i reqwest`:
└── reqwest feature "system-proxy"
    └── tauri-plugin-updater feature "system-proxy"
        └── tauri-plugin-updater feature "default"

tauri-plugin-updater-2.12.0/Cargo.toml:
default = ["rustls-tls", "system-proxy", "zip"]

No proxy configuration anywhere in our code (grep -i proxy over crates/*/src and src-tauri/src finds only comments about proxies answering with text/html).
findings.rationale: Corporate Entra admins commonly sit behind a proxy configured in Windows Internet Settings or macOS System Configuration (not env vars). Today the shipped binary honours those settings only because the updater plugin happens to enable reqwest's `system-proxy` and features unify. Trimming the updater's defaults (e.g. to drop `zip`), a plugin default change, or a build variant without the updater would silently make every Graph call fail behind such proxies — and no test or comment records that this feature is load-bearing for the app's own clients.
findings.proposal: Add "system-proxy" to the workspace reqwest feature list in Cargo.toml:29 with a one-line comment ("OS proxy discovery for corporate Windows/macOS deployments; enabled here on purpose, not inherited from the updater plugin"). Zero cost today (already unified in); it makes the dependency explicit and survives any updater-plugin change. Optionally add a repo_invariants test that greps the feature in Cargo.toml.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified with `cargo tree --locked --offline -p desktop -e features -i reqwest`: `reqwest feature "system-proxy"` is reached only through `tauri-plugin-updater feature "system-proxy"` ← `tauri-plugin-updater feature "default"`; the workspace declaration (Cargo.toml:29) lists only rustls/json/query/form, and reqwest-0.13.5's `default` (dropped by `default-features = false`) is what would otherwise carry `system-proxy`. tauri-plugin-updater-2.12.0 `default = ["rustls-tls", "system-proxy", "zip"]` confirmed. None of our seven `reqwest::Client::builder()` sites (graph/client.rs:163, exchange/client.rs:74, keyvault/client.rs:54, arm/client.rs:36, arm/loganalytics.rs:27, auth/service/mod.rs:93, sso/mod.rs:1282) sets or disables a proxy, so OS-proxy discovery is indeed inherited. No doc, comment or test records this. The proposal is zero-cost (feature already unified in) and fits the repo's habit of stating feature choices explicitly (see the oauth2/base64 blocks). Severity lowered from medium: it is a latent fragility, not a present defect, and the trigger (someone trimming the updater's defaults or a plugin default change) is speculative; the value is that the regression would be invisible to CI.

findings.title: src-tauri declares anyhow and thiserror but uses neither; anyhow is then unused workspace-wide
findings.evidence:
apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:42-43:
anyhow = { workspace = true }
thiserror = { workspace = true }

`grep -rn 'anyhow\|thiserror' apps/desktop/src-tauri/src apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests apps/desktop/src-tauri/build.rs` → no output.

Cargo.toml:51:
anyhow = "1"
(`cargo tree -i anyhow` shows `desktop` as the only workspace consumer; every other edge is tauri/tauri-build/tauri-utils.)
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md says "Dependencies are a cost: prefer std + existing crates" and the app's error taxonomy is deliberately typed (`UiError`, `core::http_error_enum!`). A declared-but-unused `anyhow` invites the next contributor to reach for `anyhow::Result` in a command handler, undoing that design; the phantom `thiserror` masks that `UiError` is hand-rolled. Neither removal drops a crate from the lockfile (tauri pulls anyhow; auth/exchange pull thiserror), so this is about intent and manifest honesty.
findings.proposal: Delete lines 42-43 from apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml and `anyhow = "1"` from Cargo.toml:51 (no member would remain). If a future command genuinely needs an untyped error, add it back deliberately with a comment.
findings.verifier_notes: apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:42-43 declare anyhow and thiserror; `grep -rn 'anyhow\|thiserror'` over src-tauri/src, tests and build.rs returns nothing, and src-tauri does not invoke `http_error_enum!` (callers are only arm/graph/keyvault error.rs:10), so neither is needed even via macro expansion. `cargo tree -i anyhow --depth 1` confirms `desktop` is the only workspace member depending on anyhow (other edges are tauri, tauri-build, tauri-plugin, tauri-plugin-fs, tauri-utils), so Cargo.toml:51 `anyhow = "1"` can go too. UiError is a hand-rolled struct in crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/lib.rs:45 (dto has no thiserror dep). No lockfile change results. Severity lowered from medium to low: manifest hygiene with no runtime or build effect.

findings.title: tracing declared but never used in azapptoolkit-keyvault, azapptoolkit-arm and web-rs
findings.evidence:
crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/Cargo.toml:20:
tracing = { workspace = true }
crates/azapptoolkit-arm/Cargo.toml:19:
tracing = { workspace = true }
apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml:63:
tracing = "0.1"

`grep -rn tracing crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src` → no output.
`grep -rn tracing apps/desktop/web-rs/src apps/desktop/web-rs/tests apps/desktop/web-rs/build.rs` → no output.
findings.rationale: Three manifests advertise instrumentation that does not exist. For web-rs it is doubly misleading: no tracing subscriber is installed in the WASM bundle, so even a future `tracing::info!` would be a silent no-op — anyone adding one would assume it reaches the backend log. For keyvault/arm the sibling crates (graph, exchange) do log; the asymmetry hides that these two clients emit nothing on 429/5xx.
findings.proposal: Remove the three declarations (crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/Cargo.toml:20, crates/azapptoolkit-arm/Cargo.toml:19, apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml:63). Do NOT add tracing::warn! calls to the keyvault/arm transports: both already route every request through `azapptoolkit_core::http_retry::with_retries` (keyvault/src/client.rs:175, arm/src/transport.rs:43), which emits the `tracing::warn!(attempt, label, retry_after_secs, "transient failure; retrying")` at core/src/http_retry.rs:207 — adding per-crate logging would duplicate the one shared retry policy. For web-rs, if browser-side tracing is ever wanted, add a console subscriber deliberately and document it in frontend-workspace.md.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise true: `grep -rn tracing` over keyvault/src, arm/src, web-rs/src, web-rs/tests and web-rs/build.rs returns nothing, and no subscriber is installed in the WASM bundle. Overstated rationale: 'the asymmetry hides that these two clients emit nothing on 429/5xx' is wrong — Key Vault and ARM (control plane and Log Analytics) use core's `with_retries`, which logs throttles/5xx centrally, so their silence is by design under AGENTS.md's 'one definition per policy' rule. The 'better' half of the proposal would therefore re-implement logging that already exists. Removing web-rs's line changes nothing in its lockfile (leptos pulls tracing anyway).

findings.title: No unused-dependency gate in verify-full/CI; five dead declarations slipped through
findings.evidence:
justfile:354-355:
deny:
    cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources
justfile:334-335:
audit:
    cargo audit

`grep -n -i 'udeps\|machete\|shear\|outdated' justfile .github/workflows/ci.yml` → no matches.

Dead declarations found by hand in this review: anyhow + thiserror (apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:42-43), tracing (crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/Cargo.toml:20, crates/azapptoolkit-arm/Cargo.toml:19, apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml:63).
findings.rationale: The repo gates advisories, licenses, sources, yanked crates and even the sync of two ignore lists, yet nothing checks that a declared dependency is used. cargo-machete is stable-toolchain, sub-second, and needs no build, so it fits `verify-full` and the existing `deny` CI job without touching the compile matrix.
findings.proposal: Add a `just udeps` recipe running `cargo machete --with-metadata` over the root and `apps/desktop/web-rs`, wire it into `verify-full` AND the `deny` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml (the `verify_full_runs_every_gate_ci_runs` test pins the two to each other), pinning the tool version via taiki-e/install-action like cargo-deny@0.20.2. Ship it with `[package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored = ["thiserror"]` in graph/arm/keyvault from day one — the re-export refactor in finding [6] cannot be taken (thiserror's derive hard-codes `::thiserror::__private` paths), so those three declarations are permanently macro-only and will always read as unused.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise true: `grep -i 'udeps\|machete\|shear'` over justfile, ci.yml, docs/, AGENTS.md and .claude/ finds nothing; justfile:334-355 gate only audit/deny; ci.yml:268-290 `deny` job installs `just,cargo-deny@0.20.2`. The dead-declaration count is 5 unique manifest lines (anyhow+thiserror in src-tauri, tracing ×3), not 6. Feasible: async-trait is imported as `use async_trait::async_trait;` (core/src/token.rs:9) and every web-rs dep has textual `name::` use, so false positives are limited to the macro-expanded thiserror in the three `http_error_enum!` callers. Severity lowered from medium: the gate would only catch low-severity hygiene items, and the repo's existing dependency gates cover the security-relevant classes (advisories, yanked, licenses, sources, bans).

findings.title: http_error_enum! expands to ::thiserror::Error, so its three callers must declare thiserror with no textual use — undocumented in their manifests
findings.rationale: Macro hygiene convention is `$crate::__private::dep` so the defining crate owns the dependency. Here the crate that owns the taxonomy does not declare thiserror while three callers must — and their manifests give no hint why (a grep of their src shows nothing using it). Any unused-dependency cleanup (manual or via cargo-machete, which this review recommends) removes those lines and the build fails inside a macro expansion with a confusing `::thiserror` path error.
findings.proposal: Keep `thiserror = { workspace = true }` in graph/arm/keyvault (it is genuinely required) and add a one-line comment at each (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/Cargo.toml:21, arm:18, keyvault:19): 'no textual use — required by the derive `azapptoolkit_core::http_error_enum!` expands to; do not remove'. Add the same note to the macro's doc comment in core/src/http_error.rs. Optionally add `thiserror = { workspace = true }` to core so the crate owning the taxonomy also declares it. If cargo-machete is adopted (finding [5]), add `[package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored = ["thiserror"]` to the three callers.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: core/src/http_error.rs:65 `#[derive(Debug, ::thiserror::Error)]`, core's Cargo.toml has no thiserror, and graph/arm/keyvault (error.rs:10 each) declare it with no other use. But the proposed `$crate::thiserror::Error` re-export does NOT work: thiserror-impl 2.0.x's expansion hard-codes absolute `::thiserror::__private::...` paths in the generated code (registry thiserror-impl-2.0.18/src/expand.rs:212 `impl ... ::thiserror::#private::Error for #ty`, :68 `use ::thiserror::#private::AsDynError`, :39/:49 inferred bounds), and thiserror has no crate-path attribute (none in thiserror-impl/src/attr.rs). Since expansion happens in the caller's crate, each caller must have `thiserror` in its extern prelude regardless of how the derive is named — dropping the lines would fail exactly as the finding fears, and the refactor would too. The phantom dependency is a thiserror limitation, not a hygiene lapse; the actionable part is documentation.

findings.title: bytes declared in four crates outside [workspace.dependencies]
findings.evidence:
crates/azapptoolkit-graph/Cargo.toml:14:    bytes = "1"
crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/Cargo.toml:14: bytes = "1"
crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/Cargo.toml:14: bytes = "1"
crates/azapptoolkit-arm/Cargo.toml:14:      bytes = "1"

Cargo.toml:24-68 [workspace.dependencies] has no `bytes` entry.

AGENTS.md, Common patterns: "Workspace dependency — add to `[workspace.dependencies]`, use `"name".workspace = true`".

(Similarly crates/azapptoolkit-auth/Cargo.toml:26 `webbrowser = "1"` is not workspace-managed, though it has a single consumer.)
findings.rationale: Four identical inline requirements for the same crate are exactly what the workspace table exists to centralise; today a bump to `bytes = "1.x"` minimum or a feature change would need four edits and can drift. It also contradicts the repo's own documented pattern.
findings.proposal: Add `bytes = "1"` under `# HTTP` in Cargo.toml [workspace.dependencies] and switch the four manifests to `bytes = { workspace = true }`. Optionally do the same for `webbrowser` for uniformity.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: `bytes = "1"` at crates/azapptoolkit-{graph,exchange,keyvault,arm}/Cargo.toml:14, used as `bytes::Bytes` return types in each transport (graph/transport.rs:126,438,455,494,520,537; exchange/transport.rs:154; keyvault/client.rs:136; arm/client.rs:242, arm/transport.rs:32); no `bytes` entry in Cargo.toml:24-68 `[workspace.dependencies]`. Four identical inline requirements is what the AGENTS.md 'Workspace dependency' pattern and .claude/rules/release-and-dependencies.md exist to centralise; the change is mechanical with no lockfile effect. The `webbrowser` aside is optional: the rule does not require single-consumer deps to be workspace-managed (src-tauri keeps rcgen, aws-lc-rs, p12-keystore, rand and time inline by design), so treat that as uniformity, not a rule violation.

findings.title: time dependency is undocumented and leaks across the cert.rs boundary into a chrono-only codebase
findings.rationale: `time` is genuinely required: rcgen 0.14's `CertificateParams.not_before/not_after` are `time::OffsetDateTime`. But the manifest gives no hint, so the next reviewer asks the same "two time crates?" question, and `GeneratedCert` exposes `time::OffsetDateTime` publicly, pushing the second date library (and a manual unix-timestamp round-trip) into a command layer that otherwise uses chrono exclusively.
findings.proposal: Add a one-line comment at Cargo.toml:88 ("rcgen's validity fields are time::OffsetDateTime; chrono everywhere else"), and convert inside cert.rs so `GeneratedCert.not_after` is `chrono::DateTime<Utc>` — making `time` a private detail of the one module that needs it and removing the conversion at credentials.rs:140-141.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:88 `time = "0.3"` sits under the heavily-commented crypto block (rcgen, aws-lc-rs, p12-keystore each carry rationale) with no comment; cert.rs:22 `use time::{Duration, OffsetDateTime}`, :54 `pub not_after: OffsetDateTime`, :119-121 sets rcgen's `not_before`/`not_after`; credentials.rs:140-141 round-trips through `unix_timestamp()` into chrono. The only other consumer of `GeneratedCert.not_after` is the unit test at cert.rs:261 (`> OffsetDateTime::now_utc()`), which would move to chrono trivially. chrono is already a src-tauri dep (Cargo.toml:39). `time 0.3.55` stays in the graph via rcgen/x509-parser/cookie regardless, so this is about manifest clarity and keeping the second date library private to cert.rs. No architecture doc mentions the `time` crate (grep of docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md). Proposal feasible and low-risk.

findings.title: parking_lot and std::sync locks are mixed with no rule, and the std sites exist only to recover from poisoning parking_lot doesn't have
findings.rationale: Same file (token_cache.rs) uses parking_lot::RwLock at line 11 and std::sync::Mutex at line 239. The two std sites each carry a paragraph explaining poison recovery via `unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())` — behaviour that parking_lot gives for free (no poisoning, const `new`). Either the codebase wants poisoning semantics (then the parking_lot sites silently lack them) or it doesn't (then the std sites are extra code plus prose).
findings.proposal: Pick one and write it down in AGENTS.md Coding fundamentals: given parking_lot is already a workspace dep and in the graph via tao, use `parking_lot::Mutex`/`RwLock` at the four std sites (dropping the poison-recovery closures and their comments), or the reverse if poisoning is wanted. Either way it is a mechanical change with no lockfile impact.
findings.verifier_notes: Sites verified: token_cache.rs:11 `use parking_lot::RwLock` vs :239 `static CHUNK_SET_LOCK: std::sync::Mutex<()>` + :246-248 poison-recovery guard; core/settings.rs:116-120 std Mutex with poison-recovery prose; src-tauri/commands/throttle.rs:37 std Mutex while state.rs:12 uses parking_lot; parking_lot RwLock at graph/client.rs:143. Feasibility checked: core's `parking_lot` is gated `cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))` (core/Cargo.toml:23) and `settings` is gated the same way (core/src/lib.rs:29-30), so it is available there; parking_lot 0.12's `Mutex::new` is const, so both `static` sites can switch. `cargo tree -i parking_lot` confirms tao keeps it in the graph, so nothing is gained by going the other way either. No AGENTS.md rule or comment explains the split. Honest severity is low: no bug, purely consistency plus deleting two paragraphs of poison-recovery rationale that parking_lot makes moot.

findings.title: Workspace tokio feature set is the union; library crates inherit net/io-util/rt-multi-thread/macros they don't use
findings.rationale: Feature unification means the shipped binary is unaffected, so this is precision, not size: the manifests claim every client crate needs a multi-thread runtime and raw TCP, which is false and hides that the OAuth loopback listener is the single place raw sockets are opened — a fact worth being visible in a credential tool. It also slightly inflates `just test-crate <lib>` builds.
findings.proposal: Set the workspace entry (Cargo.toml:26) to `features = ["sync", "time"]`. In crates/azapptoolkit-auth/Cargo.toml add `features = ["net", "io-util", "rt"]` — `rt` is required by the non-test `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` at service/mod.rs:457 and :509, not only the loopback listener — and add `[dev-dependencies] tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["macros", "rt"] }` (auth currently has no tokio dev-dep and its 7 `#[tokio::test]`s in loopback.rs and service/mod.rs ride the workspace `macros`/`rt-multi-thread`). In apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml add `features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread"]` (tokio::join! at enterprise_application.rs:131, backup.rs:368,519, readiness.rs:76, sso/mod.rs:466; tokio::spawn in five commands). graph/exchange/keyvault/arm/core already carry `macros`/`rt` dev-deps and use only tokio::sync/time in src.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: Cargo.toml:26 enables macros, rt-multi-thread, sync, time, net, io-util; only auth uses tokio::net/io (loopback.rs:7-8, service/mod.rs:34); no `Runtime::new`/`#[tokio::main]` anywhere (runtime is Tauri's); graph/exchange/keyvault/arm src use no tokio API beyond what tests need; core uses only tokio::time (http_retry.rs, cache). Overstated/incomplete: the proposal's auth feature set omits `rt`, which `spawn_blocking` (auth/service/mod.rs:457,509 — keyring I/O deliberately moved off the async worker) needs, and omits the dev-dependency auth would need for its `#[tokio::test]`s; as written the trim would break auth's build and tests. Value is precision only (feature unification leaves the shipped binary unchanged), so low.

findings.title: The futures facade's default `executor` feature pulls futures-executor into Windows/macOS builds for nothing
findings.evidence:
crates/azapptoolkit-graph/Cargo.toml:23: futures = { workspace = true }
apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:38: futures = { workspace = true }

Usage (grep over graph/src + src-tauri/src): futures::future::join_all ×6, futures::future::try_join ×7, futures::future::join ×2, futures::join! ×2, futures::stream::* ×6 — e.g. crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/batch.rs:138 `let results = futures::future::join_all(` — all of which live in futures-util.

`cargo tree -i futures-executor`:
futures-executor v0.3.34
├── futures v0.3.34
│   ├── azapptoolkit-graph
│   ├── desktop
│   └── wiremock [dev-dependencies]
└── glib v0.18.5   (Linux-only GTK stack)
findings.rationale: On the two platforms the release actually ships (Windows/macOS per release-updater-demo.md), `futures` and `futures-executor` are compiled solely because of the facade; everything used is in futures-util, which tauri already depends on. Small win, but the repo's stated posture is that unused code in a credential tool is liability, and this one is free to remove. (web-rs gets no benefit: tauri-sys itself depends on the facade.)
findings.proposal: Change the workspace entry (Cargo.toml:27) to `futures = { version = "0.3", default-features = false, features = ["std", "async-await"] }`. futures-0.3.34's `default = ["std", "async-await", "executor"]` and `executor = ["std", "futures-executor/std"]`, so dropping the default removes futures-executor with ZERO source changes — every item used (future::{join, join4, join_all, try_join}, stream::{self, StreamExt, FuturesUnordered}, `join!`, future::abortable) is re-exported by the facade under std+async-await. Confirm with `cargo tree -e normal,build -i futures-executor --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` (today it prints `futures-executor ← futures` only). Rewriting ~30 `futures::` paths to `futures_util::` buys nothing extra.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: `cargo tree --locked --offline -i futures-executor` → `futures v0.3.34` (← azapptoolkit-graph, desktop, and wiremock dev-only) plus `glib v0.18.5` (Linux GTK); with `-e normal,build --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` futures-executor is present solely via `futures`. All 25 use sites in graph/src/client/batch.rs:138 and src-tauri commands are futures-util items. Overstated: the switch-to-futures-util proposal is far more churn than needed; the facade's own feature flags achieve the same drop, matching how the repo already handles oauth2/base64/reqwest (`default-features = false` + explicit features with a comment). web-rs is correctly excluded (tauri-sys depends on the facade with defaults). Gain is one small pure-Rust crate on two targets, so low.

findings.title: reqwest http2 is off, so every Graph/Exchange fan-out multiplexes over HTTP/1.1 connections
findings.evidence:
Cargo.toml:29:
reqwest = { version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["rustls", "json", "query", "form"] }

reqwest-0.13.5 default = ["default-tls", "charset", "http2", "system-proxy"] — `http2` is dropped by default-features = false and nothing re-enables it:
`cargo tree --locked -p desktop -e features -i reqwest` lists: __rustls, __rustls-aws-lc-rs, __tls, form, json, query, rustls, rustls-no-provider, stream, system-proxy (no http2).
`cargo tree -i h2 --target all` → "nothing to print" (h2 is not in the graph on any target).
findings.rationale: Graph, Exchange Admin and Key Vault endpoints negotiate h2 via ALPN. With HTTP/1.1 only, a `ConcurrencyThrottle` fan-out at N in-flight requests holds N TLS connections per host; with h2 it multiplexes streams over one connection, cutting handshakes and connection-pool churn behind corporate proxies. Benefit is unmeasured here and `$batch` already reduces request count, so this is a measure-first item, not a defect.
findings.proposal: Add `"http2"` to the workspace reqwest features (adds the `h2` crate), run an existing fan-out (e.g. the site sweep or audit on a large tenant) with `RUST_LOG=hyper_util=debug` before/after to count connections and wall time, keep it if it wins. Record the result next to the opt-level bench in Cargo.toml so it is not re-asked.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: Cargo.toml:29 omits `http2`; reqwest-0.13.5's `default = ["default-tls","charset","http2","system-proxy"]` is dropped by `default-features = false`; `cargo tree --locked --offline -p desktop -e features -i reqwest` lists no `reqwest feature "http2"` (only __rustls, __rustls-aws-lc-rs, __tls, form, json, query, rustls, rustls-no-provider, stream, system-proxy). Nuance on the h2 claim: with dev-deps included, `cargo tree -i h2` shows h2 ← hyper (feature "http2" via hyper "full"/hyper-util) ← hyper-rustls ← reqwest, which is why Cargo.lock:2033 contains h2; with `-e normal,build --target all` it is absent, so for the SHIPPED binary the reviewer's 'h2 not in the graph' and 'adds the h2 crate' both hold. No comment, doc or CHANGELOG entry records HTTP/1.1-only as deliberate (grep of Cargo.toml, docs/architecture). The finding is correctly framed as measure-first: `$batch` + ConcurrencyThrottle already bound request count, reqwest pools HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections, and the auth crate already special-cases TLS-intercepting proxies (service/mod.rs:160,188) whose behaviour h2/ALPN can change — so the proposal to benchmark, decide, and record the result next to the opt-level bench is the right shape. Low, as stated.

Section bytes: Quick reference 2204 · Repo map 2850 · Canonical commands 649 · Conventions & gotchas 10263 · Verification playbook 925 · Keeping this file up to date 533.

Duplicated text (line → bytes → where it already lives):
- L20 Quick-reference "Verify" row (243 B): "`just verify` = the CI gates in CI order, plus the browser GUI tests when Chrome + chromedriver are present (LOUD skip otherwise). `just verify-ui` makes them mandatory; `just verify-full` adds the audit/deny gates" — restated by L172-173 (Verification playbook steps 1-2) and by the Canonical commands paragraph.

- L180 (500 B) "Keeping this file up to date" paragraph.
- L103 tail (~75 B) "Pinned per call site in `repo_invariants/{cancel,fanout}.rs`" — caching-and-search.md:330-332.
findings.rationale: At 19 998/20 000 the next one-sentence invariant (which the file's own "Keeping this file up to date" section mandates for every new command/cache/CSP/cancel rule) fails `repo_invariants/release.rs` and trips `staleness-check.sh`, so contributors are pushed to shorten an unrelated rule under pressure. findings.proposal: (1) Delete the Quick-reference "Verify" row (-243 B) — the Verification playbook is the canonical home. (2) Replace L176 with "Browser GUI tests are the frontend's only behavioural gate → [frontend-workspace.md#browser-gui-tests]" (-~200 B). (-~250 B). (5) Move L103's pin clause to .claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md L19 (-~75 B). (6) Trim Repo-map annotations for self-explanatory entries (`docs/CHANGELOG-archive.md`, `.github/workflows/`, `scripts/`) (-~150 B). findings.verifier_notes: Numbers verified: `wc -c AGENTS.md` = 19998; apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/repo_invariants/release.rs:115 `const BUDGET: usize = 20_000` (asserted at :124); .claude/hooks/staleness-check.sh:68-69 warns past 20000.
