findings.title: No network/proxy/TLS guidance for enterprise deployments; Requirements omit the updater hosts
findings.evidence:
README.md Requirements: "Outbound network access (at runtime) to `login.microsoftonline.com`, `graph.microsoft.com`, and — only when you use those features — `*.vault.azure.net` ..., `outlook.office365.com` ..., `management.azure.com` ..., and `api.loganalytics.azure.com`" — github.com is not listed, yet apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:47-48 `"endpoints": ["https://github.com/tiredithumans/azapptoolkit/releases/latest/download/latest.json"]` (asset downloads redirect to `objects.githubusercontent.com`).
`grep -n -i 'proxy|firewall|allowlist|TLS inspection|certificate store' README.md docs/DEVELOPMENT.md docs/operator-rbac/OPERATOR-ROLES.md` → no matches.

What the binary actually does (undocumented): reqwest 0.13.5 src/async_impl/client.rs:310 `auto_sys_proxy: true,` and :417-418 `if config.auto_sys_proxy { proxies.push(ProxyMatcher::system()); }`; hyper-util 0.1.21 matcher.rs:101-102 "This checks the same environment variables as `from_env()`, and if not set, checks the system configuration for values for the OS", :704-718 reads Windows `ProxyEnable`/`ProxyServer`/`ProxyOverride` (no `AutoConfigURL`/PAC handling in the file); Cargo.lock hyper-util deps include `system-configuration` and `windows-registry`. TLS roots come from the OS store: Cargo.lock:3937 reqwest → `rustls-platform-verifier`. crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:188 already classifies "NOT Entra: a TLS-intercepting proxy, WAF or captive portal".
findings.rationale: The README targets MDM/Group Policy rollouts (MSI section, `AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE` for "MDM/Group Policy deployments") — exactly the environments with egress allowlists, explicit proxies and TLS inspection. Today an admin cannot learn from the docs that (a) auto-update needs github.com/objects.githubusercontent.com, (b) `HTTPS_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` and the OS static proxy are honoured but PAC/WPAD is not, (c) TLS inspection works only if the inspecting CA is in the OS trust store, or (d) what the "a proxy answered" sign-in error means.
findings.proposal: Add a "Network requirements" subsection under Requirements: the full host allowlist per feature plus the two updater hosts; a "Behind a proxy" note (env vars, OS static proxy, no PAC, how `NO_PROXY` interacts with the 127.0.0.1 loopback redirect); a "TLS inspection" note (OS trust store via rustls-platform-verifier; certificate pinning is not used); and a troubleshooting bullet for the text/html-from-login-host error. Sovereign clouds: list the per-cloud hosts already in the CSP (tauri.conf.json:25).
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: README.md:292-298 host list omits github.com although apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:47-48 sets the updater endpoint to github.com/.../latest.json (asset downloads redirect to objects.githubusercontent.com); grep for proxy/firewall/allowlist/TLS inspection across README, DEVELOPMENT.md and OPERATOR-ROLES.md returns nothing. Behaviour claims check out against the vendored sources: reqwest-0.13.5 src/async_impl/client.rs:310 `auto_sys_proxy: true` and :417 pushes ProxyMatcher::system(); hyper-util-0.1.21 matcher.rs:704-708 reads ProxyEnable/ProxyServer only (no AutoConfigURL/PAC); Cargo.lock reqwest depends on rustls-platform-verifier (OS trust store); crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:183-192 already classifies the TLS-intercepting-proxy case. The README's MSI/Intune/Group-Policy audience makes medium fair. One overstatement to drop: the NO_PROXY/127.0.0.1 loopback note is moot — the loopback redirect is an inbound browser→listener hop, not an outbound reqwest call; the proxy guidance should cover the Microsoft and GitHub hosts only.

Locally you can build for your own host with the per-platform recipes below." followed by :155 "`just build-macos-updater` runs `cargo tauri build --target aarch64-apple-darwin --config updater-build.json ...`" and :169 "`just build-linux-updater` ...".

justfile:380-382 "# Requires the updater signing key in TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY[_PASSWORD] (`tauri build` fails without it when createUpdaterArtifacts is on); kept separate from `build-windows` so local/test packaging needs no signing key." — but the only keyless recipe is justfile:375-378 `build-windows` (`cargo tauri build --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -- --locked`); justfile:401-414 define only `build-macos-updater` and `build-linux-updater`.
AGENTS.md Canonical commands: "`just build-{windows,macos,linux}-updater` need `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`; `build-windows` is keyless".
findings.rationale: A macOS or Linux contributor who wants a local .dmg/.AppImage to test install/Gatekeeper/updater-disable behaviour has no recipe that works without the release private key, and the doc tells them the recipes below are for exactly that. `cargo tauri build` by hand is what AGENTS.md forbids.

Update AGENTS.md Canonical commands accordingly (fits inside the budget headroom from the AGENTS.md finding).
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:109-112 says 'Locally you can build for your own host with the per-platform recipes below', and the macOS (:155) and Linux (:169) subsections name only `build-macos-updater` / `build-linux-updater`; justfile:377 build-windows is the only keyless recipe, and justfile:380-382 documents that the -updater variants fail without TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY; no build-macos/build-linux recipe exists (grep ^build-). AGENTS.md says build-windows alone is keyless and forbids hand-typed cargo, yet DEVELOPMENT.md:72 itself offers '(or `cargo tauri build` for your host target)' — a second inconsistency worth fixing in the same pass. findings.title: CHANGELOG.md has no title and no pointer to the archived releases
findings.evidence:
CHANGELOG.md:1 `## [Unreleased]` (no `# Changelog` heading, no preamble); version headers end at :367 `## [0.27.0] - 2026-08-28`; the last lines of the file are the 0.27.0 body ("...The doc header listed only \"(Graph, Key Vault, ARM)\", which is how the gap stayed invisible."). The only mention of the archive is inside a 0.30.0 entry: :169 "`docs/CHANGELOG-archive.md`, and editing this file no longer recompiles the frontend."

docs/CHANGELOG-archive.md:1-5 "# Changelog archive — azapptoolkit 0.26.3 and earlier ... Split out of the main [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md)" — the link is one-directional.
release-updater-demo.md:29-31: the notes extractor matches "`^##\s+\[$version\]`" and "pulls the lines between this version's header and the next `## [` header" — content above the first `## [` is never extracted.
findings.rationale: Anyone reading CHANGELOG.md on GitHub (the README's "Status: pre-release" badge links to it) sees history start at 0.27.0 with no hint that 0.1.0-0.26.3 exist; the archive's rationale ("Nothing depends on this file") is fine, but discoverability was not preserved.
findings.proposal: Prepend `# Changelog` plus one line: "Releases 0.26.3 and earlier live in [docs/CHANGELOG-archive.md](docs/CHANGELOG-archive.md). Format: Keep a Changelog headers `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD` (parsed by release.yml and web-rs/build.rs)." Placing it above `## [Unreleased]` keeps both parsers untouched; verify with the `the_running_versions_changelog_section_is_baked_in` test.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: CHANGELOG.md:1 is `## [Unreleased]` with no title; the oldest header is `## [0.27.0]` at :367 and the file ends with that body; the only archive mention is inside the 0.30.0 entry (:169). docs/CHANGELOG-archive.md:1-4 links back but nothing links forward. Both parsers tolerate a preamble: apps/desktop/web-rs/build_support.rs:16-29 `section_for` uses skip_while on the `## [version]` header (its own test fixture at :35-38 starts with '# Changelog'), and .github/workflows/release.yml:232-239 iterates lines and only starts collecting at the matching `## [` header. So the proposal is safe and the cited test would confirm it.

findings.title: Mailbox advisory and scope gate omit the newer RBAC-scopable Graph mailbox permissions (MailboxItem.*, MailboxFolder.*, Mail-Advanced.*) — a documented but audit-relevant gap
findings.rationale: The comment justifies the 10-entry map by the AAP migration ("never AAP-scopable"), but the same map is the gate for every non-AAP path: `is_scopable_exchange_resource_permission` (scoping.rs:126-131) decides whether the Grant-access wizard and the Scope fix offer confinement, and `is_mailbox_reaching_permission` decides membership in the audit's mailbox advisory. `MailboxItem.ReadWrite.All` (read/write/delete every item in every mailbox) and `MailboxItem.ImportExport.All` (common in third-party backup apps) do not start with `Mail.`, so an org-wide grant of them produces no mailbox finding, no high-risk points, and no Scope action, even though Exchange documents a scoped role for each. That is the direction a least-privilege audit must not be wrong in. The name-shaped fallback's own doc comment claims it catches permissions "this build's graph_mail_role table doesn't know yet" but the prefix list cannot match `Mailbox`- or `Mail-`-prefixed names.
findings.proposal: Extend `graph_mail_role` with the Graph-resource roles only (MailboxFolder.Read/ReadWrite.All, MailboxItem.Read/ReadWrite/Export/ImportExport.All, Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All, MailboxConfigItem.Read/ReadWrite, MailTips.ReadBasic.All), citing the Learn table in the existing table-driven test `every_confinable_graph_mail_permission_reaches_mailboxes`; map `SMTP.SendAsApp` on the Office 365 Exchange Online resource next to `EWS_FULL_ACCESS_AS_APP` (scoping.rs:112-114) and extend `unscopable_legacy_exchange_spares_the_live_protocol_roles` accordingly, or leave it unmapped. Widen `mailbox_named` to `Mailbox`/`Mail-` prefixes and fix the doc comment at scoping.rs:200-203. Add `MailboxItem.ReadWrite.All`, `MailboxItem.ImportExport.All`, `Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All`, `MailboxFolder.ReadWrite.All` to HIGH_RISK and the read variants to MEDIUM_RISK in audit/permissions.rs with the CHANGELOG note exchange-scoping.md:48-49 already requires; keep `aap.rs` on the 11-value AAP set (it is the migration parity contract) and update exchange-scoping.md:46-50.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise holds: crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/scoping.rs:77-92 maps only the 11 AAP-era values; `mailbox_named` (scoping.rs:194-198) tests `Mail.`/`MailboxSettings.`/`Calendars.`/`Contacts.` so `MailboxItem.*`, `MailboxFolder.*`, `Mail-Advanced.*` never satisfy `is_mailbox_reaching_permission` on Graph (scoping.rs:204) and never get a Scope fix; the fallback doc comment at scoping.rs:200-203 ('a Graph permission this build's table doesn't know yet still reports reach') is therefore inaccurate for Mailbox*-prefixed names. Learn's 'Supported Application Roles' table (fetched) confirms `Application MailboxItem.ReadWrite` → `MailboxItem.ReadWrite.All`, `MailboxItem.ImportExport.All`, `MailboxFolder.*`, `Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All`, `MailboxConfigItem.*`, `MailTips.ReadBasic.All`, `SMTP.SendAsApp`. HOWEVER this is a documented, deliberate gap the reviewer did not engage with: docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md:46-50 ('Not mapped, on purpose ... RBAC-scopable today but never AAP-scopable ... adding one is additive, but it widens is_scopable_exchange_permission and therefore the audit's scoped-mail weighting, which needs a CHANGELOG note') and scoping.rs:74-76. That rationale only justifies AAP-migration parity, not the audit/advisory blind spot, so the finding is real but is a known/accepted limitation rather than an unnoticed bug — 'high' is overstated. Proposal defect: `SMTP.SendAsApp` is an appRole on Office 365 Exchange Online (00000002-…), not Microsoft Graph; putting it in `graph_mail_role` would make `is_unscopable_legacy_exchange_permission` (scoping.rs:153-155) flag it and break the pinned test `unscopable_legacy_exchange_spares_the_live_protocol_roles` (scoping.rs:628-645). Also `verdict.rs` already handles the broader role list on the read side (composite roles, verdict.rs:47-51), so only the map/advisory/risk-list side needs work.

findings.title: SSO wizard hardcodes the global-cloud application template id and login host; sovereign clouds fail
findings.rationale: The rest of the backend resolves Graph, Exchange, ARM, Key Vault and Log Analytics hosts through `CloudEnvironment`, so the product advertises sovereign-cloud support, yet the SSO wizard's `POST /applicationTemplates/{id}/instantiate` will 404 in US Gov and China (wrong template GUID) and the SAML/OIDC URLs handed to app owners point at the commercial login host.
findings.proposal: Add `CloudEnvironment::custom_app_template_id() -> &'static str` returning the three documented GUIDs (DoD shares the US Gov id), replace `CUSTOM_TEMPLATE_ID` with `state.auth.cloud().custom_app_template_id()` at mod.rs:167/313, and replace `LOGIN_HOST` with `state.auth.cloud().login_authority_root()` at mod.rs:90-100. Add a unit test in cloud.rs pinning the three ids.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sso/mod.rs:41 `CUSTOM_TEMPLATE_ID` and :44 `LOGIN_HOST` are hardcoded, used at :90/:93/:100 (URLs) and :167/:313 (instantiate). `CloudEnvironment::login_authority_root()` exists at crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/cloud.rs:85-91 and `state.auth.cloud()` is the established accessor (state.rs:476, 503, 519; federated.rs:78). README.md:414-420 advertises US Gov/DoD/China support and says the cloud switch covers 'Entra login, Microsoft Graph, Exchange Online, Key Vault, and ARM endpoints' — the SSO wizard is the outlier. Learn (New-EntraApplicationFromApplicationTemplate) confirms the three non-gallery template ids exactly as quoted: global 8adf8e6e-…, US Gov 4602d0b4-…, China 5a532e38-…; DoD is not listed separately so 'DoD shares US Gov' is an inference to mark as such. Two additions: the SAML issuer at mod.rs:89 (`https://sts.windows.net/{tenant}/`) is also cloud-specific for China (sts.chinacloudapi.cn) and should ride the same `CloudEnvironment` method; and the unit tests at mod.rs:1832-1847 pin the commercial strings, so `saml_summary_urls`/`oidc_summary_urls` need a cloud parameter plus tests per cloud. Not handled anywhere else (grep for the GUIDs/hosts finds only this file and the auth service's own authority).

findings.title: Group-membership token requests only GroupMember.ReadWrite.All; Learn documents that adding a servicePrincipal member also requires Application.ReadWrite.All
findings.rationale: The member the app always adds is a service principal, which is exactly the row the docs single out. The dedicated token is minted from a single-scope request, so whether the resulting `scp` also carries `Application.ReadWrite.All` depends on the tenant having previously consented the write bundle for this client, not on anything the code asserts. The readiness checklist probes `consent_scopes_for("group_membership")` and reports the scope half as satisfied with only GroupMember consented, while the POST can still be rejected. Because outcomes vary with consent history, this is a latent 403 that the catalog cannot explain.
findings.proposal: Change `default_graph_group_member_scopes` to `graph_scopes(&["GroupMember.ReadWrite.All", "Application.ReadWrite.All"])`, list both in the `group_membership` capability `scopes`, and mention the pair in its remediation string. Add a scopes.rs test mirroring `write_scopes_cover_mutations`.
findings.verifier_notes: Learn 'Add members' permissions table (fetched) reads: servicePrincipal | GroupMember.ReadWrite.All and Application.ReadWrite.All | Not supported | GroupMember.ReadWrite.All and Application.ReadWrite.All. Repo requests only the first: crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/scopes.rs:79-81, minted into the dedicated adapter at state.rs:465-468 and used by `add_group_member`/`remove_group_member` (graph client/directory.rs:216-230). The catalog row lists only GroupMember (capabilities.rs:307) and the readiness scope probe uses `consent_scopes_for("group_membership")` (readiness.rs:58, 273 → state.rs:542), so the scope half reads 'have' with a scope set Learn says is insufficient for the only member type the app ever adds. Not documented as deliberate: docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md:41 explains why not `Group.ReadWrite.All` but never addresses the SP-member pair. Caveat: Graph's runtime enforcement cannot be verified offline and the reviewer's 'depends on consent history' mechanism is speculative (v2 tokens carry only the requested scopes), but the remedy is the same either way and `Application.ReadWrite.All` is already in the write bundle (scopes.rs:150), so requesting it here widens nothing.

findings.title: Claims-mapping policy assign/list ride a Policy-only token; Learn requires Application.ReadWrite.All AND a Policy.* scope
findings.rationale: Creating the policy (`POST /policies/claimsMappingPolicies`) genuinely needs only `Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration`, but the two `$ref` operations on the service principal are documented as needing `Application.ReadWrite.All` in the same token. As with the group-member token, success today depends on Entra folding previously consented write scopes into a single-scope request. Listing assigned policies is also a read that could ride `Policy.Read.All` + `Application.ReadWrite.All` rather than forcing the admin-consent-only write scope on a read path.
findings.proposal: Mint the policy-write token with `["Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration", "Application.ReadWrite.All"]`; consider routing `list_assigned_claims_mapping_policies` through the existing `policy_token` (Policy.Read.All) plus the write bundle so a browse-only SSO view never requests the write scope. Document the pair in a new capability entry (see the catalog-gap finding).
findings.verifier_notes: Learn 'Assign claimsMappingPolicy' and 'List assigned claimsMappingPolicy' (both fetched) require, delegated: least privileged `Application.ReadWrite.All and Policy.Read.All`, higher `Application.ReadWrite.All and Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration`; only `POST /policies/claimsMappingPolicies` is Policy-scope-only. Repo: crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/policies.rs:26-58 and :62-74 ride `policy_write_token`, minted with the single scope at scopes.rs:55-57 / state.rs:449-452, so the `$ref` assign/list/remove calls carry no `Application.ReadWrite.All`. The browse path `get_sso_config` (sso/mod.rs:455-470) calls the list on every SSO-tab open and only degrades. Nuance on the second half of the proposal: routing the list through `policy_token` (Policy.Read.All, state.rs:441) still needs `Application.ReadWrite.All` in the same token per Learn, so a 'browse-only view never requests the write scope' is not achievable — the gain is only avoiding `Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration` on reads. Runtime enforcement unverified offline, same caveat as finding 2.

findings.title: Capabilities catalog has no entry for the `policy_write` (claims mapping) and `sync` (provisioning) on-demand scopes
findings.evidence:
capabilities.rs:1-2: "Authorization-capability catalog: the single source of truth mapping each privileged feature area to the role(s) and delegated OAuth scope(s) it needs."
CAPABILITIES (lines 125-404) `scope_feature` values: "write", "audit_log", "policy", "sharepoint", "group_membership", "keyvault", "arm", "log_analytics", "exchange" — no entry with Some("policy_write") or Some("sync").
state.rs:534-543:
    pub fn consent_scopes_for(&self, feature: &str) -> Option<Vec<String>> {
            "sync" => self.auth.default_graph_sync_scopes(),
            "policy_write" => self.auth.default_graph_policy_write_scopes(),

Microsoft Learn, List synchronization jobs (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/synchronization-synchronization-list-jobs?view=graph-rest-1.0): least privileged delegated `Synchronization.Read.All`; supported roles "Application Administrator, Cloud Application Administrator, Hybrid Identity Administrator".
findings.rationale: Both features are admin-consent-only and role-gated, so a 403 on the provisioning tab or on SAML claim customization has no `forbidden_remediation` hint, no `RequiresRole` label, and no readiness row — exactly the drift the catalog header says it exists to prevent.
findings.proposal: Add two `Capability` rows: `saml_claims_mapping` (Plane::EntraDirectory; roles Application Administrator / Cloud Application Administrator / Global Administrator; scopes per the claims-mapping finding; scope_feature Some("policy_write")) and `provisioning_status` (roles Application Administrator / Cloud Application Administrator / Hybrid Identity Administrator with template ids; scopes ["Synchronization.Read.All"]; scope_feature Some("sync")). Add a test asserting every `consent_scopes_for` key except "write" has a catalog row, and splice `forbidden_remediation` into the SSO claims and provisioning commands.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: CAPABILITIES (capabilities.rs:125-404) has `scope_feature` values write/audit_log/policy/sharepoint/group_membership/keyvault/arm/log_analytics/exchange only; `consent_scopes_for` (state.rs:534-552) also serves "sync" and "policy_write". `check_readiness` builds its probe list from catalog `scope_feature`s (readiness.rs:55-60), so neither scope is ever probed or shown. `forbidden_remediation` call sites (grep) are enterprise_application.rs:315 (group_membership), sharepoint.rs:166, managed_identity.rs:402, permission_tester.rs:1026, keyvault_rbac.rs:66 — none for the provisioning read (enterprise_application.rs:332) or the SSO claims writes (sso/mod.rs:158, 1637). Learn 'List synchronization jobs' (searched) confirms least-privileged delegated `Synchronization.Read.All` and supported roles Application Administrator / Cloud Application Administrator / Hybrid Identity Administrator (template 8ac3fc64-6eca-42ea-9e69-59f4c7b60eb2). Note the proposed test should simply assert every `consent_scopes_for` key has a catalog row — "write" already has rows, no exclusion needed. Severity is honest as a catalog-drift finding since capabilities.rs:9-12 promises all three feedback mechanisms read from this one table.

findings.title: Exchange client rides the undocumented `adminapi/beta/{tenant}/InvokeCommand` gateway while comments and doc links present it as the documented Admin API
findings.rationale: The route the app depends on for every scoping mutation is the ExchangeOnlineManagement module's private transport, not the documented (preview) REST surface, and the documented surface does not expose any RBAC-for-Applications cmdlet. That is a legitimate engineering choice, but the repo currently (a) carries a pre-launch "verify during the live transport spike" note on production code, (b) cites the v2.0 get-started page as the contract for an endpoint that page does not describe, and (c) nowhere records the support risk or the trigger for migrating (RBAC cmdlets appearing under `adminapi/v2.0`).
findings.proposal: Replace the stale NOTE with a paragraph stating that `InvokeCommand` is the EXO PowerShell module's transport (unsupported for third parties), that the documented Admin API is `adminapi/v2.0/{tenant}/{Endpoint}` with `Exchange.ManageV2` and today covers none of the cmdlets in `rbac.rs`, and name the watch condition. Add the same note to docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md. Keep the pagination link but scope its wording to "the same nextLink/POST-continuation contract the documented API uses".
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real: crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/client.rs:22-30 carries the 'NOTE (verify during the live transport spike)' on `ADMIN_API_VERSION = "beta"` / `INVOKE_ENDPOINT`; client/transport.rs:42 cites admin-api-get-started#pagination; scopes.rs:106-108 records that the gateway rejects `ManageV2` with a bodyless 403 — which shows the live spike already happened, so the NOTE is stale. Learn get-started (fetched) documents `POST <BaseUrl>/adminapi/v2.0/<TenantID>/<EndpointName>` with `Exchange.ManageV2`, marked Preview; the endpoints reference (fetched) lists only AcceptedDomain, DistributionGroupMember, DynamicDistributionGroupMember, Mailbox, MailboxFolderPermission, OrganizationConfig — none of the RBAC cmdlets in client/rbac.rs. docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md has no mention of InvokeCommand, the beta path, or the support risk (grep). Premise and proposal hold, but this is a comment/architecture-doc fix with no functional impact, so medium overstates it; the pagination link is still fair since the continuation contract described at transport.rs:30-42 matches the documented API.

findings.title: Key Vault control-plane api-version 2023-07-01 is retired on 2027-02-27; other ARM/KV versions are merely behind
findings.rationale: AUTHORIZATION_API and SUBSCRIPTIONS_API are current. KEYVAULT_API (control plane) is three stable releases behind and Microsoft has an active control-plane API-version retirement for Key Vault; LOG_ANALYTICS_WORKSPACES_API is four behind; the data-plane 7.4 predates the switch to date-based versions. Old versions keep working until retired, but the retirement page is the signal that this cannot stay unreviewed indefinitely, and the constants carry no review date or source link.
findings.proposal: Bump `KEYVAULT_API` (arm/client.rs:22) to `2026-02-01` — the only stable version that survives the announced retirement — and confirm the vault-list response shape is unchanged (read-only GET; the 2026-02-01 access-control default change affects only new vaults). Optionally bump `LOG_ANALYTICS_WORKSPACES_API` to 2025-02-01 or later and `DEFAULT_API_VERSION` (keyvault/client.rs:25) to 2025-07-01; leave AUTHORIZATION/SUBSCRIPTIONS as-is. Add a `// Source: <url>, reviewed YYYY-MM` comment per constant and note the 2027-02-27 date in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md or the ARM crate header. Wiremock tests at arm/client.rs:266-509 reference the constants and follow automatically.
findings.verifier_notes: Constants confirmed at crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/client.rs:19-22 and crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/client.rs:25. Learn: AUTHORIZATION 2022-04-01 and SUBSCRIPTIONS 2022-12-01 are current; Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces has stable 2023-09-01, 2025-02-01, 2025-07-01, 2026-03-01 after 2022-10-01; Microsoft.KeyVault control plane has 2024-11-01, 2025-05-01, 2026-02-01 after 2023-07-01; the Get Secret REST reference is at data-plane 2025-07-01. The premise is understated in one respect and the proposal is wrong in one: the fetched 'Update the Azure Key Vault API version you use' page states 'All Key Vault control plane API versions before 2026-02-01 retire on February 27, 2027 ... you can manage them only with control plane API version 2026-02-01 or later. There's no exception or extension.' So `KEYVAULT_API = "2023-07-01"` (used by the vault listing at arm/client.rs:86, wiremock at :479) has a hard break date, and the reviewer's suggested target 2024-11-01 would be retired too. Data-plane 7.4 is explicitly unaffected ('Stable data plane API versions aren't affected'), so that bump is optional hygiene. No repo doc records an api-version review policy (grep of docs/ finds none).

findings.title: Readiness checklist cannot recognise the custom Entra role the repo itself recommends
findings.evidence:
capabilities.rs:428-451 `matched_directory_role` matches only `role_template_id` against the built-in TID_* constants or the catalog display names:
    for role in active_roles {
        if let Some(tid) = role.role_template_id.as_deref()
            && let Some((name, _)) = cap.directory_roles_any.iter()
                .find(|(_, want)| want.is_some_and(|w| w.eq_ignore_ascii_case(tid)))
directory.rs:116-123 reads `/me/transitiveMemberOf/microsoft.graph.directoryRole`.
docs/operator-rbac/OPERATOR-ROLES.md:19: "So: **two custom roles + one built-in role**." and ships `entra-custom-role.ps1`; grep of that file for "checklist|readiness|detect" returns nothing.

Microsoft Learn, List Microsoft Entra role assignments (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/view-assignments#list-microsoft-entra-role-assignments): "GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments?$filter=principalId+eq+'<object-id-of-principal>'" and "List role assignments with app registration scope ... $filter=directoryScopeId+eq+'/<app object id>'".
findings.rationale: An operator following OPERATOR-ROLES.md holds a custom role whose template id is tenant-specific, so every DirectoryRole-detected capability reads "Role missing" for them; the doc does not warn about this. The unified RBAC API can return the operator's role assignments with their definitions (`allowedResourceActions`), which is what the catalog actually cares about, and it also exposes app-scoped assignments (`directoryScopeId eq '/<appObjectId>'`) that neither the checklist nor the app detail (owners only) shows today.
findings.proposal: Add an optional `required_actions: &[&str]` per capability (e.g. `microsoft.directory/applications/credentials/update`) and a second detection path via `roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments?$filter=principalId eq '{me}'&$expand=roleDefinition` (RoleManagement.Read.Directory, or fall back to the existing directoryRole read); report a custom role whose actions cover the set as "have (custom role X)". Separately, surface app-scoped role assignments on the app detail next to Owners. Document the current limitation in OPERATOR-ROLES.md in the meantime.
findings.verifier_notes: `matched_directory_role` (capabilities.rs:428-451) matches only catalog `roleTemplateId`s (the TID_* built-ins at :109-122) or catalog display names; readiness reports 'Activate one of: …' / Missing otherwise (readiness.rs:147-156). docs/operator-rbac/OPERATOR-ROLES.md:19 ('two custom roles + one built-in role') and section 2 recommend a custom Entra role via entra-custom-role.ps1, and neither that doc nor readiness.rs / readiness_view.rs mention that the checklist cannot recognise it (grep for custom role/checklist/readiness returns nothing). Learn confirms custom `unifiedRoleDefinition.templateId` is caller/tenant-defined and recommends the unified RBAC API over `directoryRoles` ('Microsoft recommends that you use the unified RBAC API instead'). Feasibility of the proposal is fine and can even avoid a new scope: keep the existing `/me/transitiveMemberOf/microsoft.graph.directoryRole` read (directory.rs:116-127) and resolve unknown template ids through `roleManagement/directory/roleDefinitions/{id}` to compare `rolePermissions.allowedResourceActions` against a per-capability action set; the app-scoped assignment surfacing is a separate, larger item. Effort L is right; severity medium is fair because the repo's own recommended operator setup renders the checklist wrong for every DirectoryRole row.

findings.title: Adopt appCredentialSignInActivities (same AuditLog.Read.All token) for per-credential last-used and an unused-credential finding
findings.rationale: The app already pays for the token, roles, and licence this report needs and already caches the sibling SP report per tenant. Per-key last-used lets the credential dashboard and the audit distinguish a live secret from a stale one, turns the "remove expired credentials" fix into a safe "remove never-used / long-unused credentials" fix, and tells rotation flows which of two overlapping secrets is still in use before revoking. Beta-only and Global-cloud-only, so it must degrade like the SP report.
findings.proposal: Add `list_app_credential_sign_in_activities()` next to the SP report (same beta_base, same cache bucket with its own key, same MAX_PAGES/origin guards), join on `keyId` into the credential DTOs, add an audit rule "credential unused for N days" gated on `sign_in_report_available`, and surface last-used in the Credentials tab. Note national-cloud unavailability in the capability description.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: the only sign-in signal is per-app `last_sign_in` (audit.rs:1287-1289; audit/types.rs:539) fed by the beta SP report at graph client/directory.rs:291-320; no reference to appCredentialSignInActivities anywhere (grep). Learn (searched) confirms `GET /reports/appCredentialSignInActivities` is beta, least-privileged delegated `AuditLog.Read.All`, roles Reports Reader / Security Reader / Security Administrator (exactly the existing `audit_reports` capability, capabilities.rs:200-218), returns keyId/keyType/keyUsage/credentialOrigin/expirationDateTime/signInActivity, supports $top/$filter, and is Global-cloud only (US Gov L4/L5 and China ❌). The proposal follows the repo's existing pattern (same token, same per-tenant cache bucket, origin-checked nextLink, degrade to 'report unavailable'). Downgraded to low: it is a feature request, not a defect, and beta-only.

findings.title: Read tenant/app management policies (v1.0) to pre-validate secret lifetimes and explain policy-driven 400s
findings.rationale: Tenants increasingly enable `passwordAddition`/`passwordLifetime` restrictions; today the app discovers them only as an opaque Graph 400 after the operator has chosen a lifetime. The app already has an on-demand `Policy.Read.All` token (`policy_token`, used for Conditional Access), so reading the default policy and any `appManagementPolicies` applied to the app is one extra GET with no new consent. It also gives the audit a tenant-posture signal ("secret creation not blocked tenant-wide").
findings.proposal: Add `get_default_app_management_policy()` and `list_app_management_policies_for(app_id)` on `policy_token` (degrade to None like CA), compute the effective max lifetime / addition block, clamp or warn in the add-secret dialog before the POST, map the Graph policy-violation error code to that explanation, and add an audit posture card when the tenant default is disabled.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: `add_password` (graph client/credentials.rs:32-40) posts whatever lifetime the caller chose; no appManagementPolicy/passwordLifetime/maxLifetime handling in crates or src-tauri (grep). Learn 'Get tenantAppManagementPolicy' (searched) confirms `GET /policies/defaultAppManagementPolicy`, least-privileged delegated `Policy.Read.All`, Global Reader is the least privileged role, and the restriction model (`passwordAddition`, `passwordLifetime`, `keyCredentials.maxLifetime`, `restrictForAppsCreatedAfterDateTime`). The app already mints `Policy.Read.All` as `policy_token` (state.rs:441-448) with the graceful-degradation contract, so no new consent is needed. Feature, not a defect; low.

findings.title: UI and audit text call Application Access Policies "deprecated"; Microsoft's current wording is "legacy, replaced, deprecation to be announced"
findings.evidence:
groups.rs:63-64:
        title: "Legacy Application Access Policy scoping",
        blurb: "Mailbox access confined by an Application Access Policy — deprecated, per-app, and blind to anything granted through Exchange RBAC. ..."
scope_badge.rs:270: "// Legacy Application Access Policy: genuinely scoped, but deprecated —"
commands/exchange/mod.rs:3: "//! These replace the deprecated Application Access Policy flow"

Microsoft Learn, Application Access Policies (legacy) (https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/permissions-exo/application-access-policies): "App Access Policies has been replaced by Role Based Access Control for Applications ... New access configuration should not use Application Access Policies since this feature will have deprecation announced in the future which will require migration."
findings.rationale: There is no announced deprecation or retirement date yet; telling operators the mechanism is deprecated overstates urgency (and a future announcement with a real date will need distinct wording). The architecture doc (exchange-scoping.md) already uses "legacy" consistently; the UI strings drifted.
findings.proposal: Reword to 'legacy (replaced by RBAC for Applications; Microsoft has said deprecation will be announced)' in groups.rs:64 AND the scorer recommendation at audit/scoring.rs:383, and align the comments at scope_badge.rs:270, exchange/mod.rs:3, audit/types.rs:168/384/588; check web-rs tests for the old blurb text; add a CHANGELOG line for the two user-visible strings.
findings.verifier_notes: Learn AAP page (fetched) is titled 'Application Access Policies (legacy)' and says 'has been replaced by Role Based Access Control for Applications ... this feature will have deprecation announced in the future' — i.e. not yet deprecated. Repo operator-facing strings say 'deprecated': web-rs/src/views/audit_view/groups.rs:64 (blurb), scope_badge.rs:270 (comment), commands/exchange/mod.rs:3 (comment), and additionally the audit recommendation text at crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/audit/scoring.rs:383 ('deprecated per-app gate') which the reviewer missed, plus doc comments in audit/types.rs:168/384/588 and filter.rs:79/508. docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md consistently says 'legacy'. Fine as a low docs/wording item; note the GUI tests (AGENTS.md: renaming on-screen text a test references fails CI) if the blurb is referenced.

findings.title: `admin_consent` capability omits Application Administrator / Cloud Application Administrator, which Learn lists as supported for non-Graph app-role grants
findings.evidence:
capabilities.rs:176-198:
        key: "admin_consent",
        directory_roles_any: &[
            ("Privileged Role Administrator", Some(TID_PRIVILEGED_ROLE_ADMIN)),
            ("Global Administrator", Some(TID_GLOBAL_ADMIN)),
        ],
        remediation: "... A custom or Cloud Application Administrator role is not sufficient for sensitive permissions."

Microsoft Learn, Grant an appRoleAssignment to a service principal (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/serviceprincipal-post-approleassignments?view=graph-rest-1.0#permissions): supported roles include "Privileged Role Administrator - the least privileged role supported for Microsoft Graph and Azure AD Graph app roles", "Application Administrator", "Cloud Application Administrator".
findings.rationale: The readiness checklist marks the role half "Missing" for a Cloud Application Administrator, yet that operator can legitimately grant app roles exposed by the tenant's own APIs, SharePoint, or Exchange Online — the resources the Grant-access wizard lists via `list_tenant_app_role_resources`. Only Microsoft Graph / AAD Graph app roles require PRA.
findings.proposal: Add ("Application Administrator", TID_APPLICATION_ADMIN) and ("Cloud Application Administrator", TID_CLOUD_APPLICATION_ADMIN) to `directory_roles_any`, and reword description/remediation to state the PRA/GA requirement applies to Microsoft Graph (and AAD Graph) app roles specifically; optionally have the consent command splice a resource-aware hint when the target resource is Graph.
findings.verifier_notes: capabilities.rs:176-198 lists only Privileged Role Administrator / Global Administrator for `admin_consent`, consumed by the proactive label at web-rs/src/views/tabs/permissions_tab.rs:481 (whole Declared-permissions header, including the non-Graph resources the wizard offers) and the 403 splice at commands/permissions.rs:372-380. Learn 'Grant an appRoleAssignment to a service principal' (fetched) lists Application Administrator and Cloud Application Administrator as supported roles with PRA 'the least privileged role supported for Microsoft Graph and Azure AD Graph app roles'; Learn 'Grant tenant-wide admin consent' confirms Cloud/Application Administrator can consent 'for any API, except Microsoft Graph app roles'. The existing remediation string already half-acknowledges this ('not sufficient for sensitive permissions'), and OPERATOR-ROLES.md:132-136 states the Graph-specific gate, so the catalog row is the odd one out. The repo has a precedent for keeping such a row honest via the description (sharepoint_selected_items, capabilities.rs:284-296). Low: readiness/label over-report of 'Missing' for non-Graph grants, no functional block.

findings.title: Exchange role-assignment list renders administrative-unit-scoped assignments as '(org-wide)'
findings.evidence:
models.rs:36-47:
pub struct ExoRoleAssignment {
    #[serde(rename = "Name", default)] pub name: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "Role", default)] pub role: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "RoleAssigneeName", default)] pub role_assignee_name: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "CustomResourceScope", default)] pub custom_resource_scope: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "Identity", default)] pub identity: Option<String>,
}
rbac.rs:229-231: "/// Assigns an Exchange application `role` ... optionally constrained to a management scope. `custom_resource_scope = None` grants org-wide."

Microsoft Learn, RBAC for Applications (https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/permissions-exo/application-rbac#configuration-instructions): "New-ManagementRoleAssignment ... -CustomResourceScope <Management Scope> (or -RecipientAdministrativeUnitScope)"; Example Two: "New-ManagementRoleAssignment -App ... -Role \"Application Mail.Read\" -RecipientAdministrativeUnitScope 4d819ce9-...".
findings.rationale: The verdict path uses `Test-ServicePrincipalAuthorization` and treats any non-Organization `ScopeType` as confined (verdict.rs tests at 358-385), so effective-scope answers stay right; but the assignment listing (`get_role_assignments` -> grants.rs:446) projects only `CustomResourceScope`, so an assignment an admin created with an administrative-unit scope displays with no scope, which the docstring equates with org-wide.
findings.proposal: Add `RecipientAdministrativeUnitScope` (and, if present on the wire, `RecipientWriteScope`) to `ExoRoleAssignment` after confirming the property names from a live `Get-ManagementRoleAssignment` envelope; carry them through `ExchangeRoleAssignmentDto` (azapptoolkit-dto/src/exchange.rs:61) and render 'Administrative unit <id>' instead of '(org-wide)' in exchange_scoping_section.rs:663-667. Leave `roles_already_scoped` (targets.rs:274) keyed on `custom_resource_scope` — an AU-scoped role is not the toolkit's group scope. Update exchange-scoping.md:49-52 to say the listing now shows AU scopes.
findings.verifier_notes: Model gap is real: crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/models.rs:36-47 has only `CustomResourceScope`; the list command projects only that field (commands/exchange/grants.rs:446) and the UI renders `custom_resource_scope.unwrap_or_else(|| "(org-wide)")` (web-rs/src/components/exchange_scoping_section.rs:663-667), so an AU-scoped assignment is literally displayed as '(org-wide)' — slightly worse than the reviewer stated. Learn confirms `New-ManagementRoleAssignment … -CustomResourceScope (or -RecipientAdministrativeUnitScope)` and `Get-ManagementRoleAssignment -RecipientAdministrativeUnitScope`. Overstated/misread parts: (1) this is a documented, deliberate limitation — docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md:49-52 says AU scoping is 'a read-only capability here: an AU-scoped assignment is read correctly (is_org_wide_auth_row won't call it org-wide; the enrich step simply finds no management scope), but the grant paths only build MemberOfGroup management scopes' — so the effective-scope verdict is correct, as the reviewer also concedes; (2) the cited docstring at client/rbac.rs:229-231 describes the write parameter of `new_role_assignment`, which the toolkit always calls with a management scope, not the read model, so 'the docstring equates None with org-wide' does not apply to the listing. The exact JSON key emitted by the InvokeCommand transport for the AU scope must be checked against a live response before adding the serde field.

findings.title: Adopt servicePrincipalRiskDetections (v1.0) to flag risky workload identities in the audit
findings.rationale: A least-privilege audit that scores every SP but is blind to Entra's own "leaked credentials" or "malicious application" detections misses the highest-signal finding available; the endpoint is GA in v1.0 and follows the same optional-scope, graceful-degradation pattern as the CA and audit-log tokens.
findings.proposal: Add an on-demand `IdentityRiskEvent.Read.All` token (`consent_scopes_for("risk")`) with a catalog row, fetch detections once per audit run (cache like the SP sign-in report), join on `servicePrincipalId`, and add a top-severity finding "Entra ID Protection flags this workload identity (riskEventType)" that is never cached when the read fails.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: the SP-only scoring path (commands/audit.rs:1271-1297) folds in only sign-in and legacy-policy signals; no riskDetection/IdentityRiskEvent references in crates or src-tauri (grep). Learn (searched) confirms `GET /identityProtection/servicePrincipalRiskDetections` is v1.0, requires a Microsoft Entra Workload ID Premium license, is available in Global/US Gov L4/L5 but not China, and exposes riskEventType (leakedCredentials, anomalousServicePrincipalActivity, …), riskLevel, riskState. Fits the repo's optional-scope pattern (auth-and-consent.md 'Optional on-demand extra-scope tokens') and would need a catalog row like `audit_reports`. Constraint the proposal must respect: AGENTS.md 'no Grant consent on audit surfaces' — the `IdentityRiskEvent.Read.All` consent must be requested from readiness/settings, not from the Security tab, and a failed read must leave the run marked degraded rather than all-clear. Feature request, licence-gated; low.

findings.title: SAML SSO does not expose `requestSignatureVerification` (signed AuthnRequest enforcement), a v1.0 application property
findings.rationale: The SSO tab already manages SAML signing certificates and claims; the one hardening control it cannot show or set is whether Entra must verify signed AuthnRequests (and whether RSA-SHA1 is still tolerated). Surfacing `isSignedRequestRequired=false` on a SAML app is also a natural audit signal.
findings.proposal: Add `requestSignatureVerification` to `get_application_sso_fields`'s `$select` and to `ApplicationSsoPatch`, render a toggle plus the weak-algorithm allowance in the SAML SSO summary, and consider a low-weight audit rule for SAML apps that allow `rsaSha1`.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: `get_application_sso_fields` selects only `id,appId,identifierUris,web,spa` (graph client/applications.rs:457-462); `ApplicationSsoPatch` (applications.rs:105-117) has no `requestSignatureVerification`; no occurrence anywhere in crates, src-tauri or web-rs (grep). Learn (searched) confirms `requestSignatureVerification` is a v1.0 property of `application` with `isSignedRequestRequired` (Boolean) and `allowedWeakAlgorithms` (rsaSha1 | unknownFutureValue). The SSO tab already manages signing certs and claims (sso/mod.rs), so surfacing the toggle is a small additive PATCH field; the proposed audit rule is optional and would need a CHANGELOG note under the scoring-rule convention. Feature, not a defect; low.

findings.title: Bulk-delete confirmation says 'cannot be undone' although Entra soft-deletes for 30 days (single-app dialog already says so); no in-app 'Recently deleted' list or restore
findings.rationale: TOP-5 #1. Entra soft-deletes application objects for 30 days (`GET /directory/deletedItems/microsoft.graph.application`, `POST /directory/deletedItems/{id}/restore`, `DELETE /directory/deletedItems/{id}` for permanent removal). The toolkit ships `delete_application` and `bulk_delete_applications` (the latter seeded by multi-select and 'Fix all N' flows) yet has no view of, or route back from, the recycle bin, and both the bulk bar and the CHANGELOG-described single-app dialog tell the operator the action is irreversible. That is the wrong message for the one moment an admin most needs the true one: after a mis-targeted bulk delete they will reach for PowerShell (`Restore-MgDirectoryDeletedItem`) — exactly what this app exists to replace — or assume the app is gone and recreate it, which mints a new appId and breaks every consumer. The read needs only `Directory.Read.All` (already the sign-in scope); restore/permanent-delete ride the existing `write` scope feature (`Application.ReadWrite.All`). Restoring also re-creates the SP link, so the existing `invalidate_app_lists` + pairing index refresh is the only cache work.
findings.proposal: (1) S: reword only bulk_action_bar.rs:817 to match the single-app dialog's existing wording (restorable from the Entra recycle bin for 30 days). (2) M: as proposed — `commands/applications/deleted.rs` with list/restore/purge over `/directory/deletedItems/microsoft.graph.application` (paged with `$top`), registered in `generate_handler![]`, bindings, a 'Recently deleted' surface with restore, `invalidate_app_lists` on Ok, `demo::register_fixtures` entries, and an 'Undo (restore N)' action on the bulk-delete toast.
findings.verifier_notes: Bulk copy is real: apps/desktop/web-rs/src/components/bulk_action_bar.rs:817 says 'Permanently delete ... This cannot be undone.' and `delete_application` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/applications/mod.rs:403-411) is a plain DELETE /applications/{id}, which Entra soft-deletes. No `deletedItems` code exists anywhere (only docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:59 mentions soft-delete for MIs). BUT the single-app dialog is already correct: apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/application_detail_pane.rs:269 body reads 'Deletion can be undone from the Entra admin center within 30 days.' — so 'both ... dialogs tell the operator the action is irreversible' is half wrong; only the bulk bar misinforms. The bulk completion toast (bulk_action_bar.rs:1187) has no undo path. Recycle-bin list/restore is a genuine absence.

findings.title: Build the file-bridged posture snapshot + drift report (#109) — every seam it names exists and is unblocked
findings.rationale: TOP-5 #2. The owner's 2026-08-04 comment on #109 retired the blocker (backup/export already established the file-bridged, user-initiated persistence posture) and wrote a full design: `PostureSnapshot` = cached `AuditItem`s + `AppPermissionGrantDto`s + coverage + `sign_in_report_available`, a pure `audit::drift::diff`, five commands, a Drift sub-tab. I verified each precondition in the tree: `save_backup_to_file`/`load_backup_from_file` plumbing exists (backup.rs:305-312), `list_app_role_assigned_to` exists (roles_grants.rs:71), `AuditItem` fields are `#[serde(default)]`, and — the two correctness hazards the design calls out — `list_app_permission_grants` really does degrade a failed resource to zero rows (so a naive diff would print 'every Exchange grant removed'), and the finding classifier `matches_finding` really is frontend-only, so the backend diff cannot bucket by stable marker without the §6 move into `azapptoolkit-core::audit`. `AppPermissionGrantDto` still lacks the `resource_app_id` diff key the design requires. Nothing has landed. For an admin this is the difference between 'here is today's posture' and 'here is what changed since the last attestation' — the attestation/trend question is what audit committees actually ask.
findings.proposal: Implement the owner's design as written: (a) additive `resource_app_id: Option<String>` on `AppPermissionGrantDto` and a per-resource `grant_coverage` record emitted by `list_app_permission_grants` in place of the silent `Vec::new()`; (b) move `matches_finding` to `azapptoolkit_core::audit::classify_finding` and have `filter.rs` delegate (keep its characterization tests); (c) `azapptoolkit-dto/src/snapshot.rs` + pure `core::audit::drift::diff` with the fail-closed rules (suppress removals for uncovered resources, omit the unused dimension unless both sides have the report, refuse tenant/cloud mismatch and newer schema, refuse a cancelled run as baseline); (d) `commands/snapshot.rs` with capture/save/load/diff/save-drift riding `export::save_export_via_dialog`; (e) a read-only Drift sub-tab in `SecurityView` (`security_view.rs:74-79`) with the baseline on `TenantScopedUi` + `reset()` line + pinning assertion. Expected effect: 'N new high-risk grants since the last snapshot' and a CSV/JSON trend export, with no new scopes, Graph calls or persistence policy.
findings.verifier_notes: Every cited precondition verified. GitHub issue #109 comments (2026-08-04, owner) retire the blocker and lay out exactly the PostureSnapshot / core::audit::drift / five-command / Drift sub-tab design the reviewer summarises. Nothing has landed: no snapshot.rs or drift module (grep snapshot|drift over crates/apps finds only unrelated cache/lockstep comments). `AppPermissionGrantDto` (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/consent.rs:9-19) still lacks `resource_app_id`; `list_app_permission_grants` degrades a failed resource to `Vec::new()` with a warn (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/consent.rs:184-201); `matches_finding` is frontend-only (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/audit_view/filter.rs:102) and docs/architecture/audit-findings-and-remediation.md:281-283 confirms classification lives there; `load_backup_from_file`/`blocking_pick_file` exist (backup.rs:305-312); `list_app_role_assigned_to` exists (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/roles_grants.rs:71); `AuditItem` carries `#[serde(default)]` fields (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/audit/types.rs:514+). Proposal is the owner's own design; effort L is right.

findings.title: Conditional Access tab ignores `conditions.clientApplications`, so workload-identity CA policies targeting the service principal are never shown
findings.rationale: TOP-5 #3. Entra has two CA axes for an app: policies whose *target resource* is the app (`conditions.applications.includeApplications`) and Conditional Access for workload identities, where the *subject* is the service principal itself (`conditions.clientApplications.includeServicePrincipals` / `excludeServicePrincipals` / `servicePrincipalFilter`, gated on Workload Identities Premium). The model only deserializes `applications`, and `to_dto` returns `None` when it is absent, so a policy that blocks this SP from untrusted locations, or one that ties it to service-principal risk, renders as 'no policies apply'. For a tool whose subject matter is the service principal (Enterprise Applications, managed identities, the SP-only audit rows), the workload-identity axis is the one an admin hardening app identities cares about — and a tab that says nothing when a block policy exists actively misleads a troubleshooting session ('why does this app get AADSTS53003?'). The candidate list in the task ('Conditional Access for workload identities') is confirmed absent. The fetch already returns whole policy objects with no `$select` (directory.rs:78-95), so this is a model + classifier change with no new Graph call or scope.
findings.proposal: Add `client_applications: Option<CaClientApplications>` (include/exclude SP ids + `servicePrincipalFilter {mode, rule}`) to `CaConditions`; extend `to_dto`/`applies_reason` to take the SP object id and emit distinct reason codes (`workloadIdentity`, `workloadIdentityFilter`) with exclude-wins semantics; add a target-axis field to `ConditionalAccessPolicyDto`; extend the existing `ConditionalAccessPanel` prop from `app_id` to `(app_id, sp_object_id)` so the already-mounted enterprise-pane instance (panels.rs:133) can pass the SP id; table tests mirroring `all_matches_unless_excluded`; README:130 wording.
findings.verifier_notes: Model gap is real: `CaConditions` deserialises only `applications` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/models.rs:612-617), `to_dto` returns None when it is absent (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/conditional_access.rs:56-61), and `applies_reason` only compares appIds (:79-110); no `clientApplications`/workload-identity handling anywhere (grep 0 hits). The fetch returns whole policy objects (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/directory.rs:78-95), so no new call/scope. HOWEVER the claim 'today it lives only on the app-registration pane' is false: `ConditionalAccessPanel` is already mounted on the enterprise pane at apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/enterprise_application_detail_pane/panels.rs:133 (import at mod.rs:36). What is missing there is that the panel takes only `app_id` (conditional_access_tab.rs:28), so the SP object id needed for the workload-identity axis is not passed. Tests to mirror exist (`all_matches_unless_excluded`, conditional_access.rs:176). Workload-identity CA is Workload Identities Premium-gated, which tempers the reach.

findings.title: Enterprise-app (SP-only) audit rows skip the ownership rule even though SP owners live in this tenant
findings.rationale: TOP-5 #4. The documented rationale for dropping rules 14-18 on SP-only rows is that the data lives in the home tenant. That is true for credentials and the manifest, but not for owners: `servicePrincipals/{id}/owners` is a local property, the detail pane already reads it (`list_service_principal_owners`), and `add_enterprise_app_owner` (enterprise_application.rs:461) already writes it. Foreign-tenant multi-tenant apps and gallery SaaS apps are precisely the principals that most often end up ownerless in a directory (the consenting admin left; nobody in-tenant is accountable), and they are the rows the audit already scores for org-wide mail/SharePoint reach. Today the 'Missing or single owner' group and the ownerless-app campaign (`bulk_add_owner` → app registrations only) cannot see them. This is an 'ownerless-app campaign' gap the task asked to evaluate; the rationale in the code does not cover the owner axis.
findings.proposal: Add `owner_count: Option<usize>` to `SpAuditInput` (scoring.rs:1022), resolve it in `run_audit`'s phase-2 candidate build (`sp_audit_candidates`, audit.rs:1312) via the same batched `$expand=owners($select=id)` trick the app index uses (audit.rs:175-187) or a `$batch` of `/servicePrincipals/{id}/owners?$select=id&$top=2`, run Rule 14 for SP rows, and emit `RemediationKind::AddOwner` with `principal_kind` routing to a new `bulk_add_sp_owner` core that wraps `add_enterprise_app_owner` (SP-only rows must never enter `bulk_add_owner`, per the existing invariant in `findings.rs:231`). Table tests: foreign SP with 0/1/2 owners; SP rows with owners unresolved (`None`) must not fire. CHANGELOG entry (ranking shifts). Expected effect: ownerless enterprise apps appear in the ownership group and are fixable in bulk.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise holds: SP owners are a local property the detail pane already reads (`list_service_principal_owners`, apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/enterprise_application.rs:131-133) and writes (`add_enterprise_app_owner`, :461), while `score_service_principal` passes `None` for owner_count with the bare note 'SP owners aren't audited' (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/audit/scoring.rs:1067-1078) and the documented rationale (:1036-1043) covers only credentials/manifest. Corrections: (a) the cited invariant `findings.rs:231` does not exist (no such file); the actual pins are crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/audit/scoring/tests.rs:775 ('SP-only rows never get AddOwner') and docs/architecture/audit-findings-and-remediation.md:184-188. (b) The proposal ignores first-party Microsoft SPs: `sp_audit_candidates` (audit.rs:1298-1305) only drops *grantless* first-party SPs, so Microsoft-owned SPs holding app roles would all be flagged ownerless — an exclusion on `appOwnerOrganizationId` (Microsoft tenants) is required or the group becomes noise. (c) The ownership rule deliberately carries no points (docs:288-289), so 'ranking shifts' is overstated; it is a user-visible finding-group change only. Severity lowered: zero-point advisory rule on a group the docs already note is large.

findings.title: No visibility of tenant app-management policies (credential lifetime / type enforcement); audit and Credentials tab cannot explain a policy-rejected secret add
findings.rationale: TOP-5 #5. Entra's app management policies (`/policies/defaultAppManagementPolicy`, `/policies/appManagementPolicies`, `/applications/{id}/appManagementPolicies`) are the tenant control that *prevents* the findings this audit reports after the fact: `passwordAddition` blocks new client secrets, `passwordLifetime`/`symmetricKeyLifetime` cap durations, `customPasswordAddition` blocks portal-set secrets, `keyCredential` restrictions require asymmetric keys, `nonDefaultUriAddition` blocks URI hijack. The audit's Rules 7 and 17 ('Long-lived secrets (>1 year)', 'Uses client secret(s)') and the per-app Credentials tab give no hint whether the tenant already enforces a policy, whether this app is exempted by a custom policy, or why an `add_password` just failed with a policy violation. The read scope is `Policy.Read.All` (the existing `policy` feature; the same scope already gates the CA tab) and the write scope is `Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration` (the existing `policy_write` feature used for claims mapping), so no new consent surface is needed. For an admin managing apps at scale this is the difference between remediating each app and turning the tap off once.
findings.proposal: Phase 1 (M, read-only) as proposed for the three `GraphClient` reads and a best-effort `TenantAppPolicyDto` in the audit prefetch — but keep `LONG_LIVED_SECRET_DAYS` as the legacy floor and add the effective `passwordLifetime` as an *additional* advisory comparison (with a CHANGELOG entry), plus the Credentials-tab `Callout` and a Home posture line. Add the `capabilities.rs` entry. Phase 2 (writes) as proposed behind `policy_write`.
findings.verifier_notes: App-management-policy absence confirmed: grep appManagementPolic|passwordAddition|passwordLifetime over crates/apps/docs = 0 hits; crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/policies.rs is claims-mapping only (75 lines); `policy`/`policy_write` scope features exist (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/state.rs:539-540). But the framing 'audit hardcodes a 365-day threshold' presents a deliberate legacy port as a defect: `LONG_LIVED_SECRET_DAYS` cites `Credential-Analysis.ps1:169` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/audit/permissions.rs:28-29), and AGENTS.md requires scoring rules to cite the PowerShell origin. Replacing the constant with a policy-derived value is a ranking change (CHANGELOG-gated) and must not silently remove the legacy floor. No policy-violation mapping for `add_password` exists in graph_err.rs (only Policy.Read.All remediation hints at :141,:152), so the 'explain a rejected add_password' part is real. Severity lowered: additive visibility feature, nothing currently misleads.

findings.title: Readiness reports a PIM-eligible role as 'Missing' with no way to tell it from 'not assigned', and no activation link
findings.rationale: The checklist deliberately treats an eligible-but-inactive role as absent (documented, and correct as a nudge). But 'Missing' currently conflates two states with different remedies: eligible (go activate, 2 minutes) versus not assigned at all (file a request with the PIM owner, days). The remediation text says 'Activate one of' even when the operator cannot. Graph exposes the eligibility set to the user for themself via `/roleManagement/directory/roleEligibilityScheduleInstances/filterByCurrentUser(on='principal')` (delegated `RoleEligibilitySchedule.Read.Directory`, or `RoleManagement.Read.Directory`), keyed by `roleDefinitionId` which equals the built-in `roleTemplateId` the catalog already matches on. The readiness page is the app's stated answer to 'why can't I do X', and 'you are eligible — activate here' is the answer it is one call short of giving. The whole page already runs three planes concurrently (readiness.rs:73), so a fourth best-effort probe fits the existing degrade-to-'?' pattern.
findings.proposal: (1) M-ish: add a `CloudEnvironment::portal_root()` helper and a PIM activation deep link in the Missing branch. (2) M: `pim` optional scope feature, `me_eligible_directory_roles()` (`roleEligibilityScheduleInstances/filterByCurrentUser`), and either a `Verdict::Eligible` variant or eligible-specific `role_detail` text; degrade to today's behaviour when unconsented; table tests beside `directory_role_absent_is_missing_and_lists_alternatives` (readiness.rs:345).
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: `role_for` returns `Verdict::Missing` with 'Activate one of: …' for any non-active role (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/readiness.rs:147-155); `Verdict` has only Have/Missing/Unknown (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/readiness.rs:18-22); directory.rs:101-104 and readiness_view.rs:188-190 document that eligible-but-inactive reads as Missing. The documented decision is about not counting eligible as Have, not about distinguishing eligible from unassigned, so the finding stands. Overstated: step (1) is not an S — there is no portal deep-link pattern anywhere in the app (only the GitHub link at apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/shell.rs:665) and `CloudEnvironment` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/cloud.rs) has no portal-host helper, so a sovereign-cloud-aware PIM link introduces a new URL surface. Step (2) needs a new consent scope feature (`RoleEligibilitySchedule.Read.Directory`) and a fourth probe. Severity lowered: an ergonomic refinement of an advisory page that already tells the user what to do.

findings.title: Switching tenants requires a relaunch by design (single-tenant-bound instance is a documented invariant); ergonomics of the switch could be improved without breaking it
findings.rationale: The 0.30.0 CHANGELOG itself names the persona: 'a consultant working several tenants had to re-point the app from outside the UI', and the fix was a Settings tab that saves the pair and relaunches. Everything below the auth service is already multi-tenant by construction — `graph_for(&tenant_id)`/`exchange_clients` are per-tenant maps, every cache key is `{tenant_id}|…`, `TenantScopedUi::reset()` and the open-items dock are keyed by tenant, and `tenant_defaults` in `settings.json` is a `BTreeMap<tenant_id, TenantDefaults>` — so the only single-tenant components are `UserSettings.{client_id,tenant_id}`, `AppState::new` resolving them once (state.rs:235-260), and `EntraAuthService::new(client_id, tenant_id)`. An MSP or multi-region admin switching between three tenants several times a day pays a full process restart, a browser round trip, and loses the audit run each time. This is the 'multi-tenant quick switch' item, verified absent.
findings.proposal: Keep one tenant per process. Cheaper, invariant-preserving form: store several saved profiles (`label, client_id, tenant_id`) in settings.json alongside the existing pair, add a 'Switch tenant…' picker in the account menu that saves the chosen pair and relaunches (reusing `set_auth_config` + `restart_app`), and preserve the last audit export path. If the maintainers want in-process switching, open a design issue that explicitly revisits backup-and-restore.md:10-13 first.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise true: `set_auth_config` persists one pair and requires a relaunch (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/config.rs:27-33), `UserSettings` holds one client_id/tenant_id (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs:27-31), `AppState::new` resolves them once (state.rs:232-257), and `sign_in` rejects a foreign `tid` (crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:313-318); CHANGELOG.md:44-45 names the consultant persona. BUT this is a documented, deliberate invariant the reviewer did not engage with: docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:10-13 — 'A running instance therefore can **never** touch two tenants. We do not change that. … This preserves the single-tenant security invariant and needs no multi-authority auth.' The whole DR shape ('file-bridged, two single-tenant instances') is built on it, and the repo's #1 footgun (cross-tenant cache leakage) is what the invariant defends. A proposal to make the auth service multi-authority overturns an architecture decision and must be raised as such, not shipped as an L feature. Frontend `set_active_tenant` (web-rs/src/state/tenant.rs:18) exists but is only ever fed one tenant per process.

findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: `list_credential_expirations` scans only `/applications` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/credentials.rs:58-68), the enterprise pane renders SP-held `password_credentials`/`key_credentials` (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/enterprise_application_detail_pane/credentials.rs:7-8), and `score_service_principal` has no credential rules (scoring.rs:1036-1043), so an SP-held secret is in no tenant-wide list. Feasibility overstated: the shared SP index projection is `id,appId,displayName,accountEnabled,servicePrincipalType,appOwnerOrganizationId,createdDateTime,alternativeNames` (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/service_principals.rs:176) and the index is pinned, capped (`SP_INDEX_MAX`) and shared by every list — adding two credential arrays to it inflates every consumer's payload, so 'one projection field set' undersells it; a separate `$select` scan or a `$batch` over candidate SPs is the right shape. findings.title: SCIM provisioning is read-only: no start / pause / restart (clear quarantine) for a job the pane already diagnoses
findings.rationale: The pane shows the job state and its quarantine reason, which is the diagnosis; the remedy an admin then performs in the portal is 'Restart provisioning' (clears quarantine and re-runs the initial cycle) or 'Pause'. Graph exposes `POST /servicePrincipals/{id}/synchronization/jobs/{jobId}/start|pause|restart` (restart with `criteria.resetScope`), delegated `Synchronization.ReadWrite.All`. The `sync` scope feature and `sync_token` plumbing already exist (state.rs:537, client.rs:291-295), so the write is a scope-set change plus three thin commands. This is the 'SCIM controls beyond status' item, verified absent.
findings.proposal: (M) Add `Synchronization.ReadWrite.All` as a `sync_write` feature (or widen `sync` on first write, mirroring the incremental-consent pattern), `start_synchronization_job` / `pause_synchronization_job` / `restart_synchronization_job(reset_scope)` in `client/directory.rs` next to `list_synchronization_jobs`, three commands + bindings, and confirm-gated buttons on the provisioning panel with the quarantine reason in the dialog body (the `subject` field). Expected effect: a quarantined job is fixed from the same pane that reported it.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: `get_enterprise_app_provisioning` is the only synchronization command and is read-only (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/enterprise_application.rs:330-349); quarantine reason is surfaced (fixture :599-601; panel apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/enterprise_application_detail_pane/panels.rs:70-98) with no buttons in that panel section; the `sync` feature is `Synchronization.Read.All` only (crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/scopes.rs:25-29; state.rs:427-430, 537; client.rs:291-295); no start/pause/restart endpoints anywhere (grep 0 hits). Proposal (a `sync_write` feature + three thin client methods + confirm-gated buttons) matches existing incremental-consent and confirm-dialog patterns.

findings.title: Risky workload identities (Identity Protection) are not part of the SP audit or the enterprise-app overview
findings.rationale: Entra ID Protection flags service principals with leaked credentials, anomalous token issuance or suspicious sign-ins (`/identityProtection/riskyServicePrincipals`, `/identityProtection/servicePrincipalRiskDetections`; delegated `IdentityRiskyServicePrincipal.Read.All`; Workload Identities Premium). A risk-scored audit that does not fold in the platform's own live risk signal ranks a leaked-secret SP the same as a clean one holding the same permissions. The audit already has the seams — a tenant-wide best-effort prefetch pattern (`prefetch_sign_in_activity`, audit.rs:1182) and an `SpAuditInput` the SP-only rows are scored from — and the same `premium_feature_err` mapping used by CA/activity handles the licence-gated 403. Lower priority than the others because it is licence-gated and the count of affected tenants is smaller; a security team that has the licence will expect it.
findings.proposal: (M) Add `list_risky_service_principals()` to the graph client under a new `identity_protection` scope feature + capability entry (Security Reader / Security Administrator); in `run_audit` prefetch it best-effort alongside sign-in activity and record a `degraded` gap when unavailable; add `risk_state`/`risk_level` to `AuditItem` (additive `#[serde(default)]`) and a Rule 21 'Identity Protection risk: {level}' with a score contribution and a `RemediationKind::DisableSignIn` pointer (already exists); a facet in the Findings pane and a chip on the Enterprise Application overview. Table tests for atRisk/confirmedCompromised/dismissed. CHANGELOG (ranking shift).
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: grep riskyServicePrincipal|servicePrincipalRiskDetection|identityProtection over crates/apps/docs = 0 hits; the seams exist — `prefetch_sign_in_activity` best-effort pattern (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/audit.rs:1182-1200), `sp_audit_candidates` (:1312), `SpAuditInput` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/audit/scoring.rs:1022-1034), `premium_feature_err` (commands/graph_err.rs:51), `RemediationKind::DisableSignIn` (types.rs:455), `AuditItem` additive `#[serde(default)]` fields (types.rs). Minor: scoring rules currently stop at Rule 18, so the new rule would be 19 (the same number this reviewer also proposes for the FIC rule in #12). Licence-gated (Workload Identities Premium), so low is honest.

findings.title: No headless/CLI mode for scheduled posture reports; audit orchestration is coupled to Tauri (extractable, but needs a new device-code auth flow)
findings.evidence:
Cargo.toml:3-13
  members = [
      "crates/azapptoolkit-core", ... "crates/azapptoolkit-arm",
      "apps/desktop/src-tauri",
  ]
(grep -l tauri crates/*/Cargo.toml → none: no library crate depends on Tauri)

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/audit.rs:127

(11 `tauri::`/`AppHandle`/`State<` references in this 2011-line file; `save_audit_to_file` at :543 is dialog-driven)
findings.rationale: Every export in the app is interactive (OS save dialog), and there is no way to run the security audit or the credential-expiry report on a schedule, in CI, or on a jump host without a desktop session. Admins who want 'email me the weekly posture' today go back to PowerShell — the tool's stated replacement target. The eight library crates already have zero Tauri dependency, so auth (device-code or the existing loopback PKCE flow), Graph, Exchange, ARM and the pure scoring in `azapptoolkit-core::audit` are reusable as-is. What is not reusable is the orchestration: `run_audit`, `prefetch_*`, `score_sp_only`, `export_audit_csv/json/html` live in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/audit.rs` and take `State<'_, AppState>` / `AppHandle` for progress and cancellation.
