findings.proposal: Step 1 (L): extract `run_audit`'s orchestration (prefetch_*, score_one, score_sp_only, exports) into a Tauri-free module taking a `ProgressSink` trait + `CancelToken`, leaving the command as a thin adapter with the repo_invariants pins on the adapter. Step 2 (L, separate): an `azapptoolkit-cli` bin only after a device-code flow lands in `azapptoolkit-auth` and headless keyring behaviour is decided; keep it out of the release matrix until it has gates.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: no library crate depends on Tauri (grep tauri crates/*/Cargo.toml = none; Cargo.toml:3-13), while `run_audit` takes `AppHandle` + `State` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/audit.rs:127-131) and the 2011-line file has 11 `tauri::`/`AppHandle`/`State<` references; exports are dialog-driven (`save_audit_to_file`, :543). No documented non-goal against a CLI was found. Overstated: (a) the auth crate has no device-code flow (grep device_code in crates/azapptoolkit-auth = 0), and the loopback PKCE flow needs a browser, so headless-on-a-jump-host means a new auth flow plus keyring behaviour on headless Linux — effort is XL, not L; (b) the README promises no scheduled reporting, so this is a new product surface rather than a gap in a stated promise; (c) the extraction must preserve the cancel/fanout repo invariants pinned per call site (repo_invariants/{cancel,fanout}.rs), which the reviewer acknowledges. Severity lowered to low.

findings.title: Audit never reads federated identity credentials, so a planted or over-broad OIDC trust is invisible in the security workbench
findings.rationale: The codebase's own module doc explains why a FIC is the most dangerous credential to miss: no secret, no expiry, silently accepted by Graph even when wrong. The audit scores secrets and certificates (Rules 5-9, 17) and even flags 'Uses client secret(s)' as a hygiene nudge toward federation, yet it never looks at the federated credentials an app already has — so an attacker-planted trust (`iss` = a GitHub org the tenant does not own, or a `sub` matching every branch via a flexible FIC `claimsMatchingExpression`), or a FIC left behind after a repo was archived, produces a clean row. The batched per-app FIC read already exists for the backup path, so the audit can reuse it at the same fan-out cost class; the validation rules in `core::federation` give the classifier.
findings.proposal: (M) In `run_audit`, fetch FICs per app through the backup's batched reader (only for apps that hold app permissions or admin-consented scopes, to bound cost), pass `federated: Vec<FederatedIdentityCredential>` into `score_application`, add advisory Rule 21: list issuers/subjects; flag `claimsMatchingExpression` present, issuers outside a per-tenant allowlist in `TenantDefaults` (e.g. `token.actions.githubusercontent.com` with an org prefix, the tenant's AKS OIDC issuer URL), and `sub` values without a ref/environment constraint. New `issue::FEDERATED_TRUST_REVIEW` marker + finding group (no one-click fix — admin-judged). CSV/JSON export columns. Table tests with the fixtures in `client/tests/credentials.rs`. Expected effect: the workbench sees the credential class its own docs call the worst case.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/federation.rs:1-19 documents why a FIC is a silently-accepted trust; the audit never reads FICs (grep federated in apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/audit.rs and core/audit = 0 hits; `score_application` takes only `&Application`, scoring.rs:871-876); backup already has `batch_list_federated_credentials` (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/credentials.rs:86-91) and backup.rs:11-13 confirms FICs are captured; `validate_federated_credential` (federation.rs:36) gives a classifier; fixtures exist in crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/tests/credentials.rs (:218+). No documented decision excludes FICs from scoring (docs/architecture/audit-findings-and-remediation.md has no mention). Minor: rules stop at 18, so it would be Rule 19; the issuer allowlist in `TenantDefaults` must be added to the exhaustive `apply_tenant_defaults` destructure per AGENTS.md. Medium is fair for a security workbench blind to the credential class its own docs call the worst case.

findings.title: Observed-activity panel promises a 'GETs-only → Downgrade' verdict but renders raw rows with no method roll-up (a gate-safe partial of #110)
findings.rationale: Issue #110 is correctly gated: mapping `(method, path-family) → permission-family` without live data risks a confidently wrong 'safe to downgrade'. But the method axis alone is not guesswork — a KQL `summarize` by `RequestMethod` is a fact, and the panel's own header text promises exactly the 'only GETs observed' reading while leaving the operator to eyeball up to 200 rows. Surfacing 'N calls: 100% GET, 0 write methods observed over 90 days (long tail truncated)' is a factual hint that stays inside the gate (no path buckets, no permission verdict), and it is the observation that makes `downgrade_application_permission` (already a command) worth clicking. It should be labelled as an observation, not a verdict, to honour the issue's reasoning.
findings.proposal: (S) Add `method_totals: Vec<(String, u64)>` to `GraphUsageResult` (computed from the rows, or a second cheap `summarize by RequestMethod` in the same query) and render a one-line roll-up above the table: 'Write methods observed: none' / 'POST 12, PATCH 3, DELETE 1' with a `Callout tone=info` that explicitly says this is not a permission verdict and links to the Downgrade action only when zero non-GET calls were seen AND `truncated == false`. Leave the path-family map to #110.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: both headers promise the GET-only reading (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/tabs/usage_panel.rs:4-6; apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/usage.rs:9-10), the summary is a bare count (usage_panel.rs:132-141), `GraphUsageResult` has no method totals (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/usage.rs:22-31), and the KQL already summarises by `RequestMethod, Path` (usage.rs:186). Issue #110 is indeed walkthrough-gated on the *path-family → permission* map; a method-only roll-up is factual and stays inside that gate. One nuance the reviewer already handles: rows are capped by `USAGE_ROW_CAP`, so a roll-up computed from rows is incomplete when `truncated` — the 'only when truncated == false' gate (or a second `summarize by RequestMethod` in the same query) is required, as proposed.

findings.title: Credential-expiry dashboard has no owner data, so an 'expiring in 7 days' row cannot be turned into a notification
findings.evidence:
crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/credentials.rs:13-25
  pub struct CredentialRowDto {
      pub app_object_id: String,
      pub app_id: String,
      pub app_display_name: String,
      pub credential_name: String,
      pub kind: CredentialKind,
      ... days_to_expiry, status
  }

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/audit.rs:175-187 (owners already expanded on the same collection for the audit)
  // `$expand=owners` brings owner ids inline so the ownership audit
      .with_expand("owners($select=id)"),
findings.rationale: The dashboard answers 'what expires when' but the next step an admin performs — telling the owner to rotate — needs the owner's mail, and the row has none; the operator opens each app's Owners tab. The audit already `$expand`s owners on the same `/applications` scan, so adding `owners($select=id,mail,userPrincipalName)` to the credential scan's projection is the same shape. Full notification via Graph `sendMail` would need `Mail.Send` and is out of character for a tool that avoids new scopes; a `mailto:` handoff and a 'Copy owner emails for the expiring set' action need nothing. This is the modest, no-new-scope form of the 'credential rotation reminders and owner notifications' item.
findings.proposal: (S/M) Add `owner_emails: Vec<String>` to `CredentialRowDto`, expand owners in `list_credential_expirations` (credentials.rs:58), show an Owners column with a 'Notify…' `mailto:` (pre-filled subject naming the app and expiry date) per row and a 'Copy owner emails' action on the expiring-soon banner (`credentials_dashboard.rs:20-21` already defines the 7/30-day bands); include owners in the CSV. Keep the ownerless rows visibly marked so they route to the AddOwner flow.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: `CredentialRowDto` has no owner data (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/credentials.rs:13-25); the dashboard columns are Application/Type/Credential/Expires/Status/Open (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/credentials_dashboard.rs:53,117) with `CRITICAL_DAYS`/`WARNING_DAYS` bands (:20-21); no `mailto:` or `Mail.Send` anywhere. The audit already `$expand`s owners on the same collection (audit.rs:175-187) — note its documented 20-owner truncation, which is fine for a notification list. External links already work via `<a target=_blank rel=noopener>` (shell.rs:665), so a `mailto:` handoff is feasible. Correct that this is the no-new-scope form; S/M effort is right.

findings.title: No accessibility statement despite substantial shipped a11y work
findings.evidence:
(grep -rni accessib|screen reader|wcag README.md CONTRIBUTING.md docs/DEVELOPMENT.md docs/architecture/frontend-workspace.md → 0 hits)

CHANGELOG.md 0.30.0 Fixed:
  - **Critical badges are legible in dark mode.** Five foregrounds were hardcoded white ... about 2.8:1
  - **Spinners keep spinning with reduced motion enabled.**
  - **Finding-group severity is readable without color.**
  - **Arrow keys move between rows in the three inventory lists.**
findings.rationale: Enterprise procurement (and public-sector tenants, a stated audience via the sovereign-cloud support) routinely asks for an accessibility conformance statement. The work exists — contrast fixes, reduced-motion handling, roving tabindex, aria labelling, a shortcuts sheet (`components/shortcuts_help.rs`) — and the GUI test gate pins aria-labels and on-screen text, but nothing states the target (e.g. WCAG 2.1 AA), what is known-nonconforming, and how to report an issue. Cheap to write because the CHANGELOG already documents the substance.
findings.proposal: (S) Add `docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md` (target level, keyboard model summary pointing at the shortcuts sheet, reduced-motion/contrast/dark-mode commitments, known gaps such as the virtualized list's screen-reader row count, how to report) and link it from README under 'App experience & operator tools' and from CONTRIBUTING's pre-PR checklist as a review item.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: grep accessib|screen reader|wcag over README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md, docs/architecture/frontend-workspace.md = 0 hits (only docs/CHANGELOG-archive.md mentions WCAG); CHANGELOG.md:88,206,210,217 document the 0.30.0 a11y fixes; `components/shortcuts_help.rs` exists; CONTRIBUTING.md has a 'Before you open a pull request' section (:32) and README's 'App experience & operator tools' heading is at :148 (cited :142). Cheap and useful; low is right.

findings.title: Header docs still describe restore and the credential-dashboard cache as future or absent work that has shipped
findings.evidence:
apps/desktop/web-rs/src/state/mod.rs:55-58
  /// Disaster-recovery backup & restore: export a portable manifest of the
  /// tenant's app estate (and, in later slices, restore it into a new tenant).
  DisasterRecovery,

docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:3-4
  This subsystem lets an operator capture a tenant's app estate to a portable file
  and (in later slices) rebuild it in a **new** tenant

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/restore.rs:4  //! This slice restores **app registrations**.
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/restore.rs:292,307  // ---- Pass 4: enterprise applications ----  // ---- Pass 5: managed identities ----

apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/credentials_dashboard.rs:6-7  //! ... Data is fetched fresh on open (no cache) so a just-rotated credential is never shown as still-expiring.
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/credentials.rs:9  //! Read-through cached under `CacheKind::Lists` (`{tenant}|credential_expirations`).
findings.rationale: Four doc-in-code statements contradict the shipped behaviour: restore is registered in `generate_handler![]` (`restore_tenant`, `plan_restore`) and already runs enterprise-app and managed-identity passes, yet the view enum, the architecture deep-dive and restore.rs's own header call it a later slice / app-registrations-only; and the credential dashboard says it is uncached while the command it calls is a read-through cache busted by `invalidate_app_credentials`. Agents are told to read these docs before touching the subsystem, so stale framing costs real time and can lead a contributor to 'add' something that exists.
findings.proposal: Rewrite `ActiveView::DisasterRecovery` doc (state/mod.rs:55-57) → 'backup, plan and restore'; drop '(in later slices)' at backup-and-restore.md:4 and reconcile its 'Pass 5'/'Pass 6' (:184, :197) with restore.rs's 'Pass 4'/'Pass 5' (:292, :307) — one numbering, one source; extend restore.rs:4-14 to list passes 4-5; replace credentials_dashboard.rs:6-7 with the read-through-cache description and its two invalidators.
findings.verifier_notes: Three of four stale passages confirmed verbatim: apps/desktop/web-rs/src/state/mod.rs:55-57 ('in later slices, restore'), apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/restore.rs:4-14 (lists only passes 1-3 while :292/:307 run Pass 4 enterprise apps and Pass 5 managed identities; `plan_restore`/`restore_tenant` registered in lib.rs:55-56), and apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/credentials_dashboard.rs:6-7 ('no cache') vs credentials.rs:9-16 (read-through `CacheKind::Lists`, busted by `invalidate_app_credentials`/`invalidate_app_lists`). Overstated for docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md: only the intro sentence (:4 '(in later slices)') is stale — the doc body already documents enterprise-app (:184) and MI (:197) restore. Missed: that doc numbers them Pass 5 / Pass 6 while restore.rs numbers them Pass 4 / Pass 5 — a fourth inconsistency worth fixing in the same pass.

findings.title: Bulk create accepts only a pasted JSON array of three fields — no file picker, no CSV, no owners/permissions columns to seed a migration from a legacy inventory
findings.rationale: Teams migrating off the legacy PowerShell scripts typically hold a CSV/JSON inventory (name, audience, owners, required permissions) and today must retype it into the Bulk Actions page three fields at a time. The app has exactly one file-open path (`load_backup_from_file`) and it reads the toolkit's own `TenantBackup`. A CSV importer for `BulkCreateSpec` (plus optional owner UPNs and permission values that map onto `bulk_add_owner` / `bulk_grant_permissions`) reuses `blocking_pick_file`, the `csv_field` conventions in reverse, and the existing `validate_only` dry-run. Lower priority: the DR restore already covers the toolkit-native shape, so this is mainly onboarding ergonomics.
findings.proposal: Add `load_bulk_create_specs_from_file` (CSV `DisplayName,SignInAudience,Description,Owners,Permissions` and JSON array) beside `load_backup_from_file`, feeding the existing textarea/validate path; extend `BulkCreateSpec` additively with `owner_upns`/`permissions` wired to `bulk_add_owner`/`bulk_grant_permissions` after create; document the column contract in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md.
findings.verifier_notes: Spec shape verified (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/bulk.rs:115-119: displayName/signInAudience/description) and `load_backup_from_file` is the only `blocking_pick_file` caller (backup.rs:312). But the premise 'must retype it … three fields at a time' is false: the Bulk Actions page already takes a pasted JSON array (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/bulk_actions_view.rs:9, :145-147 `Textarea value=create_json`, parsed at :63; the DTO doc says 'Parsed from the user's JSON import'), with `validate_only` dry-run (bulk.rs:531-539). What is genuinely absent is a file picker, a CSV shape, and owner/permission columns.

findings.title: Tenant configured as a domain is accepted by the config screen but unconditionally rejected by sign_in
findings.rationale: The id_token `tid` claim is always a GUID, so when the operator follows the UI's own guidance and enters `contoso.onmicrosoft.com` (accepted by `is_valid_tenant`, persisted to settings.json, used as the authority segment), every sign-in completes in the browser and then fails locally with 'id token tid ... does not match configured tenant contoso.onmicrosoft.com'. `UserSettings::remembered_account_for` (settings.rs:171-175) does the same string compare, so restore would also never fire. No test exercises a domain-form tenant (tests use 't1'), and no code resolves a domain to its GUID (grep for well-known/openid-configuration only finds the SSO summary URL builder). README 384-401 tells users to copy the GUID, contradicting the config screen text.
findings.proposal: Prefer (a): make `is_valid_tenant` GUID-only, align config.rs:44 and config_screen.rs:125/176-177 with README, and add a service/mod.rs test with a non-GUID configured tenant asserting the tid check. If domain support is wanted instead, resolve the domain to its GUID at sign_in time (GET `{auth_root}/{domain}/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration`, issuer tid), compare `tid` to that, and persist the GUID so `remembered_account_for` matches — not in `AppState::new`, which is sync and runs before any network access.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise holds. crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:313 does a plain string compare of the id_token `tid` (always a GUID) against `self.tenant_id`, which state.rs:241-258 sets verbatim from env/settings.json/bake with no domain→GUID resolution (state.rs:128-150 `resolve`). config.rs:41-46 + 71-72 accept a dotted domain and config_screen.rs:125/176-177 tell the operator a domain is fine, so a domain-configured install fails every sign-in after the browser round trip. settings.rs:171-175 `remembered_account_for` and state.rs:377 do the same string compare, so restore never fires either. No test uses a domain tenant (mod.rs:1029 uses 't1'; config.rs:80-87 only tests the validator). README.md:384-401 says GUID, contradicting the config screen. sign_in.rs:16-19 even documents that a wrong id 'comes back as an opaque token_exchange failure'. Severity lowered from high to medium: functional first-run bug with a clear workaround (enter the GUID) and an error message naming the mismatch, not a security or data-loss issue. Feasibility note on option (b): AppState::new is synchronous and offline, so resolving the domain there adds a blocking network call at launch; resolve lazily at sign_in instead.

findings.title: Updater signing key is in the environment of the whole `cargo tauri build` (every dependency build script), not just the bundling step
findings.evidence:
release.yml:127-144:
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
      ...
      - name: Build bundles (with updater artifacts)
        env:
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_UPDATER_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_UPDATER_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: just ${{ matrix.recipe }}

justfile:392-393:
build-windows-updater:
    cargo tauri build --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --config updater-build.json -- --locked

release.yml:169-180 already signs post-build for the Authenticode case:
      - name: Refresh updater signature (NSIS)
        ...
          cargo tauri signer sign "$($exe.FullName)"
findings.rationale: The minisign key that authorizes silent code delivery to every installed copy is readable by every `build.rs` and proc-macro in the ~600-crate dependency graph during the compile phase, because the CLI only needs it after cargo finishes. A single compromised transitive crate exfiltrating `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` from the release runner defeats the whole signed-update model that the pubkey guard, SHA-pinned actions and deny.toml exist to protect. Restoring `rust-cache` into the release job additionally lets cached compiled artifacts from CI runs feed the shipped binary. The repo already has the exact post-build signing step needed (line 176-180) for one platform.
findings.proposal: Split the three `build-*-updater` justfile recipes into `cargo tauri build --no-bundle ... -- --locked` (no signing env) followed by `cargo tauri bundle --config updater-build.json [--bundles ...]`, and in release.yml scope TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY[_PASSWORD] to the bundle step only (or sign each updater artifact with `cargo tauri signer sign` as the NSIS refresh does). Optionally set `save-if: false` on the release job's rust-cache. Update DEVELOPMENT.md:290-296 to describe the compile/sign split.
findings.verifier_notes: The key-exposure premise is real: release.yml:140-144 sets TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY[_PASSWORD] on `just build-*-updater`, whose bodies (justfile:393/404/414) are a full `cargo tauri build`, so every build.rs/proc-macro in both trees (including the trunk `beforeBuildCommand`) runs with the key in env, and `cargo tauri signer sign` (release.yml:176-180) already shows the post-build alternative. Overstated: (1) Swatinem/rust-cache keys on `github.job` ('build'), while ci.yml's jobs are `rust`/`web` (ci.yml:86/132), so CI caches are not restored into the release job; a tag ref can only see caches from its own ref or the default branch, so the sole crossover is a `workflow_dispatch` release run on main — the same trusted workflow, and rust-cache excludes workspace crates' own artifacts. (2) A malicious build script already controls the binary being signed; scoping the key only limits persistence of a leak, so 'defeats the whole signed-update model' overstates the marginal gain. Severity lowered to low. Proposal is feasible (`cargo tauri build --no-bundle` + `cargo tauri bundle --config updater-build.json` exist in tauri-cli 2.x) but must land in the justfile recipes and DEVELOPMENT.md:290-296, not only the workflow.

findings.title: CSP connect-src allowlists 13 Microsoft origins the WASM frontend never contacts, contrary to the repo's own CSP rule
findings.evidence:
tauri.conf.json:25:
"csp": "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; connect-src 'self' https://graph.microsoft.com https://graph.microsoft.us https://dod-graph.microsoft.us https://microsoftgraph.chinacloudapi.cn https://login.microsoftonline.com https://login.microsoftonline.us https://login.partner.microsoftonline.cn https://*.vault.azure.net https://*.vault.usgovcloudapi.net https://*.vault.azure.cn https://management.azure.com ..."

web-rs/Cargo.toml:51 (no Request/Response/fetch features, no gloo/reqwest):
web-sys = { version = "0.3", features = ["MediaQueryList", ..., "Storage", "File", "FileList", "Blob", "HtmlInputElement", "Event"] }

.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:28:
- **CSP governs the *webview*, not backend egress.** `connect-src` in `tauri.conf.json` restricts only WASM frontend fetches; backend reqwest calls to new hosts need no CSP change.
findings.rationale: Every network call goes through backend reqwest via IPC; the frontend has no fetch binding at all (grep for fetch/Request/XmlHttpRequest/WebSocket in web-rs/src finds only unrelated words). The list is therefore dead permission that the repo's own rules say should not exist. It is not harmless: `https://*.vault.azure.net` lets any webview-side script bug exfiltrate data to an attacker-owned Key Vault hostname (Key Vault diagnostic logs record the request URI even for 401s), and the login/graph hosts give the same script a way to make authenticated-looking requests with the operator's browser cookies. Tauri appends its own IPC origins to connect-src at runtime, so `'self'` is sufficient.
findings.proposal: Set `connect-src 'self'` in tauri.conf.json:25 (verify IPC + updater splash under `just dev`), add a repo_invariants test asserting connect-src contains no `https://` origin, and note in AGENTS.md / .claude/rules that the list is intentionally `'self'` only.
findings.verifier_notes: Dead permission is real: tauri.conf.json:25 lists 13 remote origins; web-rs/Cargo.toml:51 enables no fetch/Request web-sys features and tauri-sys is used with `core`+`event` only (Cargo.toml:33), so the webview never contacts them. The repo's own rules say connect-src covers only frontend fetches (AGENTS.md:111, .claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:28, docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md:56 'add the origin to the CSP only if the *frontend* fetches it'), so the list contradicts them. Overstated impact: sign-in happens in the system browser (loopback.rs `open_system_browser`), and the Tauri webview has its own cookie jar, so 'authenticated-looking requests with the operator's browser cookies' does not apply; and any script-execution bug in the webview already has IPC access to every backend command, which dwarfs a connect-src exfil path. Severity lowered to low (hygiene / defense in depth). Proposal to reduce to `'self'` is sound (Tauri appends its IPC origins automatically); the invariant test is simpler as an exact assertion that connect-src is `'self'` only.

findings.title: SAML/OIDC summary URLs and the federation-metadata probe hard-code the commercial login host, ignoring CloudEnvironment
findings.rationale: The app advertises sovereign-cloud support (`AZAPPTOOLKIT_CLOUD`, per-cloud Graph/Exchange/KV/ARM/Log Analytics hosts, a `cloud` field in backups that refuses cross-cloud restores), yet the SSO tab's copy-paste 'Login URL / Logout URL / Metadata URL' and the OIDC authority/discovery URL (`oidc_summary_urls`, line 100) are commercial-only. Microsoft Learn (authentication-national-cloud) confirms Gov and China use `login.microsoftonline.us` / `login.partner.microsoftonline.cn`. In a GCC-High tenant an operator configuring a service provider from these values gets a broken IdP, and `probe_federation_metadata` fetches the wrong host so every staged rollover reads as 'couldn't check'. `app_id` is also interpolated into the query unvalidated (no `is_guid` call anywhere in sso/mod.rs).
findings.proposal: Thread `state.auth.cloud()` into `saml_summary_urls`/`oidc_summary_urls` and use `login_authority_root()`; add `CloudEnvironment::saml_issuer_root()` (commercial/Gov `https://sts.windows.net`, China `https://sts.chinacloudapi.cn`) next to the other per-cloud getters; validate `app_id` with `guid::is_guid` before building the metadata URL. Add a test asserting the Gov cloud yields `login.microsoftonline.us` URLs.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence verified: sso/mod.rs:44 `LOGIN_HOST` is commercial-only; saml_summary_urls (88-96) and oidc_summary_urls (99-103) use it; probe_federation_metadata (829) fetches the resulting metadata URL, so in a sovereign tenant every probe reads as 'couldn't check'; tests at 1829-1848 pin the commercial hosts only. core/cloud.rs:85-90 already has `login_authority_root()`, and state.rs:476-685 threads `self.auth.cloud()` into every other host, so this is the one host left hard-coded. README.md:414-420 advertises US Gov/DoD/China support. Microsoft Learn (authentication-national-cloud) confirms login.microsoftonline.us / login.partner.microsoftonline.cn. Minor: `app_id` at line 274 comes from the Graph SP `appId`; only the probe (829) takes it from the frontend — with a fixed host it can only reshape the query, so the `is_guid` addition is a small hygiene item, not part of the bug. Verify the China SAML issuer host (`https://sts.chinacloudapi.cn/`) against Microsoft docs before adding `saml_issuer_root()`; US Gov keeps `sts.windows.net`.

findings.title: `TokenResponse` derives Debug with plaintext access, refresh and id tokens — the one secret-bearing type without a redacted Debug
findings.rationale: No call site Debug-prints it today (grep for `?token`/`{token:?}` in the auth crate is empty), so this is latent — but the repo has explicitly elevated 'derived Debug on a secret' to a defect class and hand-wrote Debug for AccessToken, PasswordCredential, SecretValue, SecretSetRequest, GeneratedCert(ificateResult), RegeneratedSecret and KvSecretValueDto. The refresh token is the most valuable secret the process ever holds and this struct is the only type that carries it in plaintext; one future `tracing::debug!(?token, ...)` while debugging AAD responses writes it to the 14-day rolling log.
findings.proposal: Replace the derive with a hand-written `Debug` that prints `<redacted>` for the three token fields (keep `expires_in`/`scope`), and add a test mirroring `a_generated_private_key_and_pfx_are_redacted_in_debug`. Optionally add a repo-invariant test that greps for `derive(...Debug...)` on structs with fields named `*_token`/`secret*`/`*password*`.
findings.verifier_notes: wire.rs:13-23 derives Debug on TokenResponse with plaintext access/refresh/id tokens. The convention is real and repeatedly applied: hand-written redacting Debug on AccessToken (token_cache.rs:107-110), PasswordCredential (core/models.rs:273), SelfSignedCertificate (models.rs:940), SecretValue/SecretSetRequest (keyvault/models.rs:57/95), KvSecretValueDto/KvSetSecretInput (dto/keyvault.rs:72/106), RegeneratedSecret (dto/backup.rs:486), OidcSsoSummary (dto/sso.rs:252), GeneratedCertificateResult (dto/applications.rs:255), GeneratedCert (cert.rs:66), each with a `<redacted>` test. No current call site Debug-prints TokenResponse (grep for `?token`/`{:?}`/`dbg!` in the auth crate is empty), so latent; no repo_invariants test guards derived Debug on secret-bearing structs. Low severity is honest. `TokenErrorBody` (wire.rs:25) needs no change.

findings.title: Loopback listener aborts the whole sign-in on a foreign `state` or `error` query from any local process, and serves the success page before validating
findings.rationale: The listener already loops past favicon/preconnect noise, but a request carrying `?error=x` or `?code=x&state=forged` — which any unprivileged local process can send to the ephemeral port during the 300 s window — terminates the flow, so the real redirect that arrives moments later is lost and the operator sees 'state mismatch — possible CSRF' or the raw attacker-chosen `error` string in the toast. RFC 8252 loopback guidance is to ignore requests that do not match the outstanding state. The 200 'sign-in complete' page is also written before the state check, so a forged request gets a success page.
findings.proposal: Validate `state == expected_state` before writing any response; on mismatch (or an `error` without a matching state) answer 400, log at warn, and `continue` the accept loop. Only after the state matches, branch on `error` vs `code` and write the success/failure page; constrain the surfaced `error` to `[a-z_]+`. Update `state_mismatch_is_rejected` to assert the genuine redirect is still delivered afterwards, and accept that a real mismatch now surfaces as the 300 s timeout.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: loopback.rs:86-99 writes the 200 'sign-in complete' page before any validation, then 100-106 returns on any `error` or mismatched `state`, so one forged request to the ephemeral port aborts the flow; dto/lib.rs:153-175 maps AuthError::Authorization via `err.to_string()`, so the attacker-chosen `error` text does reach the UI message. Existing test `state_mismatch_is_rejected` (loopback.rs:245-257) pins the current abort behaviour. Overstated: RFC 8252 discusses loopback interception risk but does not literally prescribe ignoring mismatched-state requests; the practical impact is a local DoS of one sign-in attempt by a process that knows the ephemeral port within the 300 s window. Trade-off the proposal omits: continuing the loop on mismatch means a genuine CSRF/mismatch now waits out the 300 s timeout instead of failing fast — acceptable, but it should be a deliberate choice with a warn! log.

findings.title: Graph/ARM/Key Vault error bodies flow raw and uncapped into errors, logs and the UI, unlike the Exchange client's sanitized bodies
findings.rationale: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md 'Token & secret security model' says response bodies are 'control-char-stripped and length-capped ... never a raw body that could carry token material', but only the Exchange client does this. The Graph, ARM and Key Vault clients put the full body into `Forbidden/NotFound/Api/Server`, which `?err` logs write to disk verbatim (audit.rs:1497, consent.rs:187/200, keyvault_rbac.rs:120/192, managed_identity.rs:238, keyvault.rs) and `UiError::from` shows in toasts. A proxy/WAF block page (the case post_token explicitly guards against) or a multi-MB HTML error lands unbounded in the 14-day log.
findings.proposal: Move `sanitize_error_body` into `azapptoolkit-core` (next to `http_retry`/`http_error`) and call it at the four body-capture sites (graph transport.rs:597, arm/transport.rs, keyvault client.rs `let body_text = resp.text()...`, exchange keeps its own call). Add a shared unit test and update DEVELOPMENT.md to name the core helper.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: graph transport.rs:597-618 captures the raw body into Forbidden/NotFound/Api; arm/transport.rs:77-113 and keyvault/client.rs:213-244 do the same; only exchange transport.rs:293-324 sanitizes. The shared `http_error_enum!` Display (core/http_error.rs:70-81) interpolates the body, so `UiError::from` (dto/lib.rs:140-153, `err.to_string()`) shows it in toasts and `?err` logs (e.g. audit.rs:1497) write it to the rolling file verbatim. Nuance: DEVELOPMENT.md:348-351 and .claude/rules/auth.md:23 explicitly scope the sanitization claim to Exchange bodies, so this is a consistency gap in the 'never a raw body' rule rather than a doc contradiction; graph_err.rs:64-79 rewrites 403 bodies only on the scoped-feature paths. Moving the helper to core matches the 'one definition per policy' convention. Low severity is honest.

findings.title: Log (and config) directory is created with the process umask while every file the app writes is owner-only
findings.rationale: The rolling logs carry tenant ids, the signed-in scope set, authorize endpoint, app display names (audit.rs:1497), correlation ids, Graph error bodies (see previous finding) and panic backtraces, and settings.json was made 0600 for a weaker class of content ('config-sensitive'). `tracing_appender` creates files with default 0644 under whatever mode `create_dir_all` gives the directory, so on a shared Linux/macOS workstation with a 755 home the 14 days of logs are world-readable.
findings.proposal: On unix create both `log_directory()` and `config_directory()` with `DirBuilder::new().recursive(true).mode(0o700)` and `set_permissions(0o700)` afterwards to tighten an existing directory; document the Windows ACL inheritance as private_file.rs does, and add a one-line note to DEVELOPMENT.md's security model.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: lib.rs:339-340 `create_dir_all(&log_dir)` (and lib.rs:32 for the config dir) leave the mode to the umask, while private_file.rs:12-16/71-75 makes settings.json and exports 0600 with an explicit rationale. Overstated: on macOS `~/Library` is 0700 by default, so `~/Library/Application Support/azapptoolkit/logs` is already owner-only there; on Linux many distros now create homes 0750 (Ubuntu >= 21.04), so exposure is limited to 755-home setups. tracing_appender files remain 0644, but a 0700 directory is sufficient. No doc or test covers log-directory permissions. Severity low holds.

findings.title: Webview capability grants `updater:default` and `dialog:allow-save` that no frontend code invokes
findings.evidence:
capabilities/default.json:6-12:
  "permissions": [
    "core:default",
    "core:window:default",
    "core:app:default",
    "updater:default",
    "dialog:allow-save"
  ]

commands/updater.rs:26-27 (backend drives the plugin, needs no capability):
pub async fn check_for_update(app: AppHandle) -> Result<Option<UpdateInfo>, UiError> {
    let updater = app.updater().map_err(updater_err)?;

commands/export.rs:86-91:
        let chosen = app_handle
            .dialog()
            .file()
            .add_filter(filter_name, &[ext])
findings.rationale: Capabilities gate what the webview may `invoke` on plugins. Grep of web-rs/src for `plugin:` finds only the mock bridge's `plugin:event|*` routes; every save/open dialog and every update check/download goes through a `#[tauri::command]` in the backend, which uses `AppHandle` APIs that are not capability-gated. `updater:default` in particular lets webview-side code call `plugin:updater|download_and_install` directly — the silent-install path AGENTS.md says must never be reintroduced — so a compromised webview could bypass the interactive splash. Least privilege says grant only what the frontend uses.
findings.proposal: Remove `updater:default` and `dialog:allow-save` from capabilities/default.json, run `just dev` and exercise an export, backup load, and update check to confirm nothing regresses; add a `repo_invariants` test asserting the capability file lists only `core:*` permissions unless `web-rs/src` contains a matching `plugin:<name>|` invoke.
findings.verifier_notes: capabilities/default.json:10-11 grants `updater:default` and `dialog:allow-save`. The frontend uses tauri-sys with only `core` + `event` features (web-rs/Cargo.toml:33) and every `tauri_sys::` use is `core`/`event`; the only `plugin:` routes anywhere in web-rs are the mock bridge's `plugin:event|*` (ipc_mock/mod.rs:125/146). The backend drives both plugins through Rust APIs (updater.rs:26-27 `app.updater()`, export.rs:86-91 `app_handle.dialog().file()`), which are not capability-gated, so removing both permissions is safe; `core:default` already covers events. `updater:default` does expose `plugin:updater|download_and_install` to webview code, which is the silent-install path AGENTS.md says must not return. No doc or test pins the capability file. Low severity is honest; the invariant test is simpler as an exact assertion of the permission list.

findings.title: Release-note markdown links render any `href` scheme, and the update splash feeds it the unsigned `latest.json` `notes` field
findings.rationale: The minisign signature covers the downloaded bundle, not `latest.json`; its `notes` field is trusted only via TLS to github.com. Anyone who can edit the release asset (repo/CI compromise without the signing key) can therefore inject `[Update](javascript:...)` or a custom-scheme link that renders as a clickable anchor inside the privileged webview. Today `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` blocks `javascript:` navigation, so this is defense in depth rather than an exploitable hole — but it is the only remote-content-to-DOM path in the app and a one-line allowlist closes it independently of CSP.
findings.proposal: In `parse_link` (or `render_inline`) accept only `https://` (optionally `http://`) hrefs and render anything else as plain text; add a unit test with `javascript:` and `file:` inputs next to the existing `parse_inline` tests. Mention in release-updater-demo.md that `notes` is unsigned content.
findings.verifier_notes: changelog_notes.rs:376-383 accepts any href and :402 renders it as an anchor; update_splash.rs:82 feeds it `UpdateInfo.notes`, which updater.rs:32 fills from `update.body` (latest.json `notes`). The minisign signature covers the bundle, not latest.json, so `notes` is TLS-trusted content only; release-updater-demo.md:30-51 documents the notes contract without saying it is unsigned. Mitigations the reviewer already credits hold: `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` blocks `javascript:` navigation, and no opener/shell plugin is registered (lib.rs:24-25). release_notes.rs:52 also routes the build-time (trusted) notes through the same component, so an allowlist affects both harmlessly. Defense in depth; low is honest.

findings.title: Log Analytics `workspace_customer_id` from an ARM response is interpolated into the request path unvalidated, unlike the sibling `get_role_definition` guard
findings.rationale: `usage.rs::discover_workspace` passes `properties.customerId` straight from `list_log_analytics_workspaces` into this path with the Log Analytics bearer attached. The ARM client's own doc comment classifies values echoed from ARM responses as attacker-influenced and validates them structurally before composing a URL; this second consumer of the same class has no check, so a value containing `/`, `?`, `#` or `..` reshapes the request (`?` would let a second query override `timespan`, `..` walks the path). The host is fixed so this is not SSRF, but it is an inconsistency in a documented invariant and a GUID check costs one line.
findings.proposal: Reject `workspace_customer_id` that is not a canonical GUID (reuse the shape check from `commands/guid.rs::is_guid`, or add a tiny `is_guid` to core so both crates share it) and return `ArmError::Protocol`, mirroring `get_role_definition`'s error text; add a wiremock test that a `../x?y` id is refused before any request is sent.
findings.verifier_notes: loganalytics.rs:45-54 interpolates `workspace_customer_id` into the path unvalidated; usage.rs:129-137 passes `ws.properties.customer_id` straight from the ARM workspace listing into it with the Log Analytics bearer attached. The sibling guard at arm/client.rs:139-152 explicitly classifies ARM-echoed ids as attacker-influenced and validates shape + origin, so this is a real inconsistency within a documented invariant. Host is fixed, so impact is path/query reshaping, not SSRF — low is honest. `is_guid` lives only in apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/guid.rs:37, unreachable from the arm crate, so the fix needs a small `core` helper (the proposal already allows this). Wiremock test scaffolding exists at loganalytics.rs:81-139 to host the refusal test.

findings.title: `just setup` panics on a fresh clone: `cargo check` runs before any frontend dist exists
findings.evidence:
scripts/setup.sh:131-136
  info "cargo check --workspace"
  cargo check --workspace
  ok "Rust workspace compiles"
  info "Frontend build (apps/desktop/web-rs)"
  ( cd apps/desktop/web-rs && trunk build )

scripts/setup.ps1:73-79 (same order): `cargo check --workspace` ... `Push-Location apps/desktop/web-rs; try { trunk build } ...`

justfile:212-217: "Tauri's `generate_context!` ... validates at COMPILE time that the frontendDist dir (apps/desktop/web-rs/dist) exists, and panics otherwise. clippy/test compile the desktop crate but do NOT build the frontend, so on a fresh checkout ... the dir is absent and the macro panics." — and `check: _stub-frontend-dist` (justfile:249) depends on the stub for exactly this reason.

~/.cargo/registry/.../tauri-codegen-2.6.3/src/context.rs:189: "The `frontendDist` configuration is set to `{path:?}` but this path doesn't exist"

`git ls-files | grep -E '(^|/)dist/'` → (empty); .gitignore:32 `dist/`
findings.rationale: `just setup` is the first command CONTRIBUTING.md, README and DEVELOPMENT.md tell a new contributor to run. On a clean clone `apps/desktop/web-rs/dist` does not exist (gitignored, not committed), `cargo check --workspace` expands `generate_context!` and the desktop crate panics before the script ever reaches the `trunk build` that would have created the directory. The justfile already solved this for `check`/`clippy`/`test` via `_stub-frontend-dist`; the setup scripts predate that and were never routed through it. Both scripts also drop `--locked`, unlike every other recipe.
findings.proposal: In both setup scripts replace the hand-typed `cargo check --workspace` with `just check` (which depends on `_stub-frontend-dist`, adds `--locked --all-targets`, and also type-checks web-rs for wasm32), and run it AFTER the `trunk build` smoke step, or swap the order so the frontend build lands first. Change `trunk build` to `trunk build --locked` for the same supply-chain pin every other recipe enforces. Expected effect: `just setup` succeeds on a fresh clone on all three OSes.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise holds end to end. tauri-codegen-2.6.3/src/context.rs:178-191 skips the frontendDist existence check only when `dev` is true; tauri-macros-2.6.3/src/context.rs:155 sets `dev: cfg!(not(feature = "custom-protocol"))`, and apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:99 has `default = ["custom-protocol"]`, so every default build (incl. `cargo check`) runs the check and panics when apps/desktop/web-rs/dist is absent. dist is gitignored (.gitignore:32), not tracked (`git ls-files | grep dist` empty) and absent in this checkout. scripts/setup.sh:131-136 (`set -euo pipefail`, line 4) and scripts/setup.ps1:73-79 (`$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'`) run `cargo check --workspace` BEFORE `trunk build`, so both abort. History: `_stub-frontend-dist` already existed in the justfile before 7b63ab3 extracted the inline setup body (pre-extraction justfile:207 stub, :496-497 `cargo check --workspace`), so setup was never routed through it. CONTRIBUTING.md:16 and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:18,42,358 make `just setup` the first command on a fresh clone. Proposal is sound: `just check` (justfile:249-251) already depends on the stub and adds `--locked`; `trunk build --locked` matches `web-build` (justfile:57). Only softening: the panic text names the missing path, so it is diagnosable — but it still fails the documented bootstrap on all three OSes. Related stale comment: justfile:195 calls dist a 'committed' stub; it is not committed.
findings.recheck_notes: Failing path traced end to end from source; nothing upstream prevents it. (1) apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:99-100 sets `default = ["custom-protocol"]` -> `tauri/custom-protocol` -> `tauri-macros/custom-protocol` (tauri-2.11.6/Cargo.toml:82, tauri-macros-2.6.3/Cargo.toml:48). (2) tauri-macros-2.6.3/src/context.rs:155 computes `dev: cfg!(not(feature = "custom-protocol"))`, so under default features `dev == false`. (3) tauri-codegen-2.6.3/src/context.rs:178 only skips the asset step when `dev && dev_url.is_some()`; with dev=false the `devUrl` in tauri.conf.json:9 is irrelevant and it falls to the `FrontendDist::Directory` arm at :182-189, which does `if !assets_path.exists() { panic!("The `frontendDist` configuration is set to ... but this path doesn't exist") }` for `../web-rs/dist` (tauri.conf.json:10). (4) apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:227 calls bare `tauri::generate_context!()` (no `assets` override), and `cargo check` compiles+executes proc macros, so the panic surfaces as a compile error. (5) `dist/` is gitignored (.gitignore:32), `git ls-files | grep dist/` is empty, and the dir is absent in this checkout; tauri-build's create_dir calls (tauri-build-2.6.3/src/lib.rs:51,142,164) are for resource copies, not frontendDist. (6) scripts/setup.sh:132 runs `cargo check --workspace` under `set -euo pipefail` (line 4) BEFORE `trunk build` at :136; scripts/setup.ps1:74 does the same with `$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'` (:3) before :79. So the script aborts before the only step that would create dist. (7) The repo already knows this: justfile:212-218 documents the exact panic and routes `check`/`clippy`/`test`/`test-crate` (justfile:236,240,249,257) through `_stub-frontend-dist`; the setup scripts were extracted in commit 7b63ab3 and never routed through it. CONTRIBUTING.md:16 and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:18-42,358 make `just setup` the first command on a fresh clone. Could not reproduce end-to-end on this box only because gdk-3.0 dev libs are missing (cargo check dies earlier in gdk-sys), which does not weaken the trace. Severity kept high as an unconditional onboarding blocker on all three OSes, with the mitigation that the panic message names the missing dir and the fix (run `trunk build` / `just check`) is trivial. Proposal is sound: swap order or call `just check` after `trunk build --locked` (matches justfile:57 `web-build`).

findings.title: Docs-only CI detector skips the very tests that pin AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md and the commit hook
findings.rationale: Five tests exist precisely to catch a malformed `## [X.Y.Z]` header, an AGENTS.md over its 20 000-byte budget, a scope added to AGENTS.md but not the hook (or vice versa), and a newest-CHANGELOG-header/version mismatch. Every one of those files is classified docs-only, so a PR that changes only one of them merges green with `just test` skipped, and the failure surfaces on the next unrelated code PR (or, for the CHANGELOG header, at release time as fallback updater notes). The `.claude/*` rule also skips the test that pins `conventional-commit-validator.sh` to AGENTS.md — the scan job only shellchecks it.
findings.proposal: Add an exceptions arm ahead of the docs globs in the `case`: `AGENTS.md|CHANGELOG.md|.claude/hooks/*) code=true ;;` (optionally `.claude/settings.json` too, since the hooks it wires are part of the contract). Update the `changes` job comment and `.claude/rules/release-and-dependencies.md:23` ("Docs-only changes (`*.md`, `docs/`, `.claude/`) skip the compile jobs") to name the exceptions. Expected effect: the pinned invariants run on exactly the PRs that can break them; docs/ and README-only PRs stay fast.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real: ci.yml:74-77 classifies `*.md` and `.claude/*` as non-build; the rust job's test step is gated on `code == 'true'` (ci.yml:128-130). release.rs pins exactly those files: CHANGELOG.md at :55, :179, :323; AGENTS.md at :119, :217; conventional-commit-validator.sh at :228. Nothing else runs them: the scan job (ci.yml:222-223) only shellchecks hooks, and the staleness-check hook is local-only for Claude Code users. db600f0 is a real docs-only CHANGELOG commit (CHANGELOG.md + docs/CHANGELOG-archive.md). .claude/rules/release-and-dependencies.md:23 documents the rule the reviewer wants amended. No AGENTS.md/doc rationale claims these files are exempt; the `changes` job comment (ci.yml:34-39) simply did not consider pinned-by-test docs. Proposal (`AGENTS.md|CHANGELOG.md|.claude/hooks/*) code=true ;;` ahead of the docs arm) is minimal and correct; `.claude/rules/*.md` can stay docs-only (not pinned).

findings.title: pages.yml never redeploys the demo when web-rs's path-dependency crates (or the root manifest they inherit from) change
findings.evidence:

  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "apps/desktop/web-rs/**"
      - "justfile"
      - ".github/workflows/pages.yml"

apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml:25-26
  azapptoolkit-core = { path = "../../../crates/azapptoolkit-core" }
  azapptoolkit-dto = { path = "../../../crates/azapptoolkit-dto" }

apps/desktop/web-rs/build.rs:25: `let changelog = repo_root(&manifest).join("CHANGELOG.md");` (bakes the "What's new" panel)
findings.rationale: The demo bundle compiles `azapptoolkit-core` (audit scoring, scoping, thumbprints, settings types) and `azapptoolkit-dto` into the wasm, and bakes the current version's CHANGELOG section. A merge to main that changes only those crates — e.g. a new audit finding or a DTO field the demo fixtures already carry — leaves https://tiredithumans.github.io/azapptoolkit/ showing the previous behaviour until some unrelated web-rs file changes. The CI web job does rebuild on such changes (its detector is path-agnostic), so the drift is Pages-only and silent.
findings.proposal: Extend `paths:` with `crates/azapptoolkit-core/**`, `crates/azapptoolkit-dto/**` and the root `Cargo.toml` (core inherits `[workspace.*]`/`[workspace.dependencies]` from it, crates/azapptoolkit-core/Cargo.toml:3-7). Leave CHANGELOG.md out: web-rs/build.rs:26-35 bakes only the CURRENT version's section and deliberately ignores changelog churn, so `[Unreleased]` edits on main never reach the bundle and a version bump already touches web-rs/Cargo.toml; adding it would redeploy Pages on every user-visible change for no visible difference (only a rare post-release edit of the released section would be missed).
findings.verifier_notes: Core/dto half confirmed: apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml:25-26 path deps; 49 files under web-rs/src import `azapptoolkit_core` (scoping, audit::CredentialStatus, models, thumbprint). pages.yml:10-13 lists only web-rs/justfile/pages.yml. CHANGELOG half overstated per build.rs:26-35 (no rerun-if-changed by design; baked section changes only with a version bump). Severity lowered: the demo's audit items are pre-scored fixtures delivered by the mock IPC, so most core-only changes (e.g. a scoring rule) do not alter what the demo displays; drift is real but narrow.

findings.title: Release guard re-runs cargo-audit but not cargo-deny, so `yanked = "deny"` is unenforced on the shipping lockfile
findings.evidence:
.github/workflows/release.yml:74-85
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@... # v2.87.17
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-audit
      # main-branch CI runs `just audit` per-merge, but an advisory filed after
      # the last merge (or against this tag's exact lockfile) would otherwise
      # ship unscanned — gate it here so a new advisory fails the release.
      - name: audit (workspace)
        run: just audit
      ...
      - name: audit (web-rs lockfile)
        run: just web-audit

deny.toml:8-9: `version = 2` / `yanked = "deny"`
justfile:346-351: "omitting the check meant that block was config nobody executed — `yanked` was never enforced by anything"
findings.rationale: The guard's own rationale ("filed after the last merge ... would otherwise ship unscanned") applies equally to a crate yanked after the last merge and to the `[bans]`/`[sources]` policy — but only `cargo audit` runs, which reports yanked crates as warnings, not failures. The repo went to some length (justfile:346-351, `both_deny_recipes_run_the_advisories_check`) to make `yanked = "deny"` a real gate in CI; the release path is the one place it still is not.
findings.proposal: Add `cargo-deny@0.20.2` to the guard's `install-action` tool list and two steps `run: just deny` / `run: just web-deny` after the audit steps (mirror the ci.yml deny job's version-pin comment). Expected effect: a yank or new advisory/source/ban violation between merge and tag fails the release before any build minutes are spent, matching the guard's stated intent.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real: release.yml:74-85 installs `just,cargo-audit` and runs only `just audit` / `just web-audit`; deny.toml:8-9 `version = 2` / `yanked = "deny"`; .cargo/audit.toml has no `[output] deny = ["yanked"]`, so cargo-audit reports yanked crates as warnings only. justfile:346-351 and docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md:180 ("`yanked = "deny"` as a required check") show the repo treats it as a gate, and the guard's own comment (release.yml:77-79) states the between-merge-and-tag rationale that applies equally to yanks. No doc argues for omitting deny at release. Severity lowered from medium: a yank in the merge→tag window is rare and a `--locked` build still compiles a yanked crate, so this is consistency with stated intent rather than a shipping risk. Proposal detail: keep the `cargo-deny@0.20.2` pin (ci.yml:286) because `web-deny`'s `--config` placement depends on the 0.20 CLI (justfile:359-361).

findings.title: tauri-cli `=2.11.5` is hand-pinned in three places with no test keeping them in agreement or within the locked `tauri` runtime

        # runtime (Cargo.lock) ... Bump in lockstep with the crate. --locked pins its deps.

scripts/setup.ps1:35:    cargo install tauri-cli --locked --version "=2.11.5"

Severity low: the literal changes a few times a year and CHANGELOG.md:10 shows the last bump was done in lockstep by hand; the release matrix's failure mode is a build-time install error, not a shipped defect.

findings.title: No rustdoc gate anywhere: 588 intra-doc links are never checked
findings.evidence:
justfile:293: `_verify-core: fmt-check clippy test web-fmt-check web-clippy web-test web-build`

`grep -rn 'cargo doc\|RUSTDOCFLAGS\|rustdoc' .` → (no hits anywhere in the repo)

`grep -rhoE '^\s*//[/!].*\[`[A-Za-z_:]+`\]' crates/*/src apps/desktop/src-tauri/src | wc -l` → 588
crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/http_error.rs:15: [`crate::http_retry`] [`crate::reauth`]

findings.rationale: This codebase leans on doc comments as its architecture record (AGENTS.md points every agent at them), and it uses intra-doc links heavily. A renamed item or module silently breaks those links; `clippy -D warnings` does not run rustdoc, so nothing in `verify` or CI notices. The workspace already passes `-D warnings` for clippy, so a `-D warnings` rustdoc gate is a small increment.
findings.proposal: Add `[workspace.lints.rustdoc] broken_intra_doc_links = "deny"` to the root Cargo.toml (Cargo's `[lints.rustdoc]` table — no RUSTDOCFLAGS, so no Windows env-var portability problem) and mirror it into web-rs's `[lints.rustdoc]`, extending `web_rs_lint_block_matches_the_workspace_block` (release.rs:28) to compare that table. Add a `doc` recipe (`cargo doc --locked --workspace --no-deps`) that depends on `_stub-frontend-dist` — rustdoc expands `generate_context!`, and per the `custom-protocol` default (src-tauri/Cargo.toml:99) the frontendDist check runs in every build — wire it into `_verify-core` and the ubuntu leg of ci.yml; `verify_full_runs_every_gate_ci_runs` (release.rs:374) then requires it in verify-full automatically.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: 588 intra-doc links in crates/*/src + src-tauri/src (777 incl. web-rs); `grep -rn 'cargo doc\|RUSTDOCFLAGS\|rustdoc'` finds nothing outside target/; justfile:293 `_verify-core` has no doc step; Cargo.toml `[workspace.lints.rust]` only has `unsafe_code`. Clippy does not run rustdoc lints, so the links are genuinely unchecked. Whether any are currently broken is unverified (cannot run cargo doc here), so the honest claim is 'never checked', not 'broken'. Severity lowered to low: it is a hygiene gate with no user-facing effect, and it costs CI minutes (ubuntu only is the right scope).

Nothing documents that `verify-full` is effectively Unix-only, and the rust job does run on windows-latest, so Windows contributors exist.
findings.proposal: Either (a) mark `web-itest-size` `[unix]` and add a `[windows]` twin with the same LOUD-skip text `web-itest-auto` uses (justfile:124-129), plus a `[windows] verify-full` that depends on `web-itest-auto` instead of `web-itest`/`web-itest-size` — keeping the `[unix]` `verify-full:` header first so `verify_full_runs_every_gate_ci_runs` (release.rs:382 takes the first `verify-full:` line) still reads the full list; or (b) state in AGENTS.md:20/89/173, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:90 and .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md:57 that the browser + shard-size gates are Unix/CI only and Windows contributors rely on CI for them.

However this is a documented, deliberate decision inside the justfile (:141-142 'Unix/CI only', :122-123 'On Windows the GUI tests stay a CI/Unix gate (matching web-itest-size)'), and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:324-326 already says the browser gates + shard ceiling run 'on Linux' in CI — so 'bug' overstates it. The real gap is that AGENTS.md and DEVELOPMENT.md:90 advertise verify-full as CI parity with no OS caveat. Severity low.

findings.title: DEVELOPMENT.md says `just setup` warns about a missing C toolchain; neither setup script checks for one
findings.evidence:
docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:27-30
  System dependencies that no `cargo`/`rustup` command can install — `just setup` detects and warns about
  these, but you provide them via your OS package manager:
  - A C toolchain: MSVC on Windows, Xcode CLT on macOS, gcc/clang on Linux

scripts/setup.ps1:39-45 (the only system-dep check on Windows)
  Write-Info "Checking WiX Toolset (required only for MSI packaging)"
  if (Get-Command candle -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { ... }

`grep -n -i 'link.exe\|cl.exe\|xcode\|gcc\|clang\|cc ' scripts/setup.sh scripts/setup.ps1` → none
findings.rationale: The most common first-build failure on Windows is `linker 'link.exe' not found` (MSVC Build Tools missing) and on macOS `xcrun: error: invalid active developer path`. The doc promises `just setup` detects these; it does not — it only checks apt packages on Debian-family Linux and WiX on Windows — so the contributor hits an opaque linker error from `cargo check` (after this fix lands, from `just check`) with no pointer to the remedy.
findings.proposal: Add a cheap probe to each script before the smoke build: Windows `Get-Command link.exe` / `cl.exe` (or `where.exe link`) → warn with the Visual Studio Build Tools link; setup.sh `command -v cc || command -v clang || command -v gcc` and on Darwin `xcode-select -p` → warn with `xcode-select --install`. Keep them warnings (non-fatal) like the existing package checks. Alternatively soften DEVELOPMENT.md to say only Linux apt packages and WiX are detected.
findings.verifier_notes: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:27-30 promises `just setup` 'detects and warns about' a C toolchain (MSVC / Xcode CLT / gcc-clang). scripts/setup.sh checks only Debian apt packages (:29-46) and scripts/setup.ps1 only WiX (:39-45); `grep -i 'link.exe\|cl.exe\|xcode\|gcc\|clang\|cc ' scripts/*` finds nothing. So the doc overstates what setup does. Severity lowered from medium: rustup's own Windows installer prompts for the MSVC Build Tools, and the linker error is a common, searchable failure; the fix is either a cheap non-fatal probe (as proposed) or a one-line doc correction. Both are small; the doc correction alone is sufficient to make the claim honest.

findings.title: dependabot.yml sha2 rationale is stale: the root lockfile already carries both sha2 0.10 and 0.11
findings.evidence:
.github/dependabot.yml:39-41
      # digest on aws-lc-rs, the backend rcgen already signs with. Bumping the
      # lock entry to 0.11 would not remove the 0.10 line those three pin; it
      # would add a second crypto major to the graph of a credential tool.

Cargo.lock:4478-4479: name = "sha2" / version = "0.10.9"
Cargo.lock:4489-4490: name = "sha2" / version = "0.11.0"
Cargo.lock:4228: "sha2 0.11.0"  (a dependency of `secret-service 5.2.0`)

.claude/rules/release-and-dependencies.md:21: "`sha2` (transitive-only) still qualifies: oauth2 5 + Tauri 2 hold the 0.10 line, and 0.11 is Linux-only via the keyring store."

The rules file was updated to say so; dependabot.yml, which is where AGENTS.md sends readers for the rationale, was not. A future reader checking the claim against `cargo tree` will conclude the comment is wrong and may drop the ignore for the wrong reason.
findings.proposal: Rewrite the sha2 ignore comment to match the rules file: the 0.10 line is pinned by oauth2/p12-keystore/tauri-codegen, 0.11 is already present Linux-only via `secret-service`, and the ignore exists so Dependabot does not churn a transitive-only dep; drop condition unchanged. Keep `.claude/rules/release-and-dependencies.md` and `docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md` as the single narrative and have dependabot.yml point at it rather than restate.
findings.verifier_notes: Cargo.lock:4478-4479 `sha2` 0.10.9 and :4489-4490 `sha2` 0.11.0 both present; :4214-4229 `secret-service` 5.2.0's dependency list includes `"sha2 0.11.0"`. .github/dependabot.yml:38-40 still says a bump 'would add a second crypto major to the graph', which is no longer the reason the hold stands. docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md:156-166 and .claude/rules/release-and-dependencies.md:21 already describe the accurate state (0.11 reached the Linux-only keyring path via secret-service 5.2.0; moving a declared dep to 0.11 would add the second major to the Windows/macOS graphs where artifacts ship). So only dependabot.yml lags; AGENTS.md and the rules file both send readers to dependabot.yml for the rationale. Rewrite should carry the nuance the architecture doc already has (hold justified by the shipped Windows/macOS graphs), not merely 'already present'.

findings.title: secrets-scanner's gitleaks path ignores SCAN_SCOPE (always a full-history scan) and labels every gitleaks failure as 'secrets detected'
findings.evidence:
.claude/hooks/secrets-scanner.sh:7-8, 26-31
  #   SCAN_MODE=warn|block   (default warn)  warn = print and exit 0; block = exit 2
  #   SCAN_SCOPE=diff|all    (default diff)  diff = changed/staged/untracked; all = whole tree
  ...
  if command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if ! output=$(gitleaks detect --no-banner --redact 2>&1); then
      emit_and_exit "$output"
    fi
    exit 0
  fi

.claude/settings.json:62: `"command": "SCAN_MODE=warn SCAN_SCOPE=diff ... secrets-scanner.sh"` with `"timeout": 30`
findings.rationale: `gitleaks detect` with no arguments scans the whole git history regardless of `SCAN_SCOPE`, so a contributor who installs gitleaks (as the scan job and the header encourage) turns the 30-second SessionEnd hook into a full-history scan on every session end — on a large history it hits the timeout and the hook silently produces nothing, which is the opposite of what the diff scope promises. Separately, gitleaks exits 1 for findings but other non-zero codes for errors (bad flag, deprecated-subcommand removal in a future version, unreadable repo); the hook prints all of them under "Potential secrets detected", and in CI (SCAN_MODE=block) a tooling error is indistinguishable from a leak.
findings.proposal: Branch on `$scope` in the gitleaks path: `all` → `gitleaks git --no-banner --redact .` (what CI wants, ci.yml:213-216); `diff` → `gitleaks git --pre-commit --staged --no-banner --redact` plus `gitleaks dir` over the untracked/unstaged file list. Keep fail-closed on ANY non-zero exit, but word the message honestly ('gitleaks reported leaks or failed (exit N)') — gitleaks documents exit 1 for 'leaks OR error encountered', so `$? == 1` cannot distinguish findings from tooling errors as the original proposal assumes. Moving off the deprecated `detect` alias is a fair future-proofing note for the 8.30.1 pin (ci.yml:229).
findings.verifier_notes: Scope half confirmed: .claude/hooks/secrets-scanner.sh:26-31 runs `gitleaks detect` regardless of `$scope` (declared :7-8); settings.json:62 runs it as SessionEnd with SCAN_SCOPE=diff and a 30 s timeout. It is a superset scan, and ci.yml:215 explicitly relies on `detect` reading the log. The timeout claim is speculative for this repo: 161 commits, 3.1 MB .git — gitleaks finishes in seconds. Exit-code half is refuted: gitleaks' documented codes are 0 (clean), 1 (leaks or error), 126 (unknown flag), so the proposed 'exactly 1 = findings' discrimination does not work. Net: a real but small hygiene fix.

findings.title: branch-switch-guard lets `git switch -` / `git checkout -` through; `git stash && git checkout X` is a documented false positive
findings.evidence:
.claude/hooks/branch-switch-guard.sh:65-75
        args = tokens[i + 2:]
        # `-- <path>` anywhere = path checkout, not a branch switch.
        if "--" in args:
            continue
        if any(a in NEW_BRANCH_FLAGS for a in args):
            continue
        targets = [a for a in args if not a.startswith("-")]
        if targets:
            print(targets[0])
            sys.exit(0)
findings.rationale: `-` (the previous-branch shorthand) starts with `-`, so `git switch -` and `git checkout -` produce no target and the guard allows the switch on a dirty tree — the exact hazard the hook exists for, and the shorthand an agent is likely to use after a `git checkout -b` detour. Conversely the segment split means `git stash && git checkout main` is evaluated at PreToolUse time with the tree still dirty, so the hook blocks the one compound form that handles the dirty state correctly, teaching the agent to reach for the `AZAPP_ALLOW_BRANCH_SWITCH=1` override.
findings.proposal: In branch-switch-guard.sh:71 treat a bare `-` as a target (e.g. `targets = [a for a in args if a == '-' or not a.startswith('-')]`). Optionally skip the block when an earlier `&&`/`;` segment of the same command is `git stash` (not `pop`/`apply`) or `git commit`. `@{-1}` needs no change — it does not start with `-` and is already returned as a target. Any regression table should be a bash self-test the scan job can run (ci.yml:222 already shellchecks hooks), not a Rust repo_invariants test that would have to shell out to bash+python3 on windows-latest.
findings.verifier_notes: `-` gap confirmed by reading :71 (`not a.startswith('-')` drops `-`) → `switch_target` empty → :79 exits 0 with a dirty tree. `@{-1}` claim overstated (it passes the filter). The stash-combo block is real (:55-75 evaluate each segment against the current dirty state, :86-87) but the hook header (:10-11) and block message (:92 'Commit or `git stash` first') document the two-step flow as the intended path, so it is a known false positive rather than the hazard. Low severity: advisory hook, fail-open design (:33-37).

findings.title: changelog-check nudges about the previous commit when the `git commit` it saw actually failed
findings.evidence:
.claude/hooks/changelog-check.sh:36-40
  # The command mentioned `git commit` but may have failed; if HEAD is
  # unreadable there is nothing to inspect.
  subject=$(git log -1 --format=%s 2>/dev/null)
  [ -z "$subject" ] && exit 0

.claude/hooks/changelog-check.sh:47-49
  printf '%s\n' "$files" | grep -qE '^(crates/|apps/desktop/)' || exit 0
  printf '[changelog-check] HEAD (%s) touches app code but not CHANGELOG.md ...' "$subject" >&2
findings.rationale: HEAD is essentially never unreadable — after a failed commit (nothing staged, a pre-commit hook rejection, `--amend` on a protected state) HEAD is simply the *previous* commit, so the hook prints a CHANGELOG nudge about a commit the agent did not just make. A stale nudge is worse than none: it invites an `--amend` onto the wrong commit.
findings.proposal: Only nudge when HEAD is fresh: `age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct) )); [ "$age" -le 120 ] || exit 0`. Optionally also skip when the payload's `tool_response` indicates a non-zero exit (the PostToolUse payload carries the Bash result for the harness versions that expose it).
findings.verifier_notes: .claude/hooks/changelog-check.sh:36-39 only guards an unreadable HEAD; after a failed `git commit` HEAD is the previous commit and :44-49 nudges about it by subject. Premise true and the age heuristic (`git log -1 --format=%ct`; committer date, so `--amend` counts as fresh) is a sound, dependency-free fix. Severity is honestly low: the hook never blocks (:9) and the nudge names the subject, so the harm is a misleading reminder rather than a wrong amend by itself. Relying on `tool_response` exit codes is harness-dependent — keep it optional as the proposal does.

findings.title: The release bump is hand edits plus hand-typed `cargo update`; a `just bump VERSION` recipe would remove the last hand-typed cargo from the release skill
findings.evidence:
.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md:23-29, 37-40
  ## 1. Bump the 3 guarded manifests
  - `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` — `"version"`
  - root `Cargo.toml` — `[workspace.package] version`
  - `apps/desktop/web-rs/Cargo.toml` — `version`
  ...
  cargo update --workspace                                # root Cargo.lock
  (cd apps/desktop/web-rs && cargo update --workspace)    # web-rs Cargo.lock (workspace-excluded)

AGENTS.md → Canonical commands: "Every build/dev/verify command is a `just` recipe (...; never hand-type `cargo`)"
repo_invariants/release.rs:138-139: "correctness of the bump was delegated to a release *ritual* rather than to any check."
findings.rationale: The repo's own test comment calls the bump a ritual, and the release skill then instructs the agent to hand-type `cargo update` — the one thing AGENTS.md says never to do — because no recipe exists. Three manifests (two TOML, one JSON) plus two lockfiles plus a CHANGELOG header edit is the highest-stakes, lowest-frequency sequence in the repo; the guard catches drift only after a tag push (a full re-cut cycle).
findings.proposal: Add `bump VERSION` with `[unix]`/`[windows]` variants (sed vs PowerShell) or a tiny Rust helper that rewrites the three literals (tauri.conf.json `"version"`, root `[workspace.package] version`, web-rs `version`), then runs `cargo update --workspace` in both trees (NOT `--locked` — that flag makes `cargo update` refuse to rewrite the lockfile, so the original proposal is self-defeating), then `just test-crate desktop -- release` so `every_manifest_states_the_same_version` runs immediately. Point release SKILL.md §1-2 at it.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise true: .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md:23-29 lists three hand edits and :37-40 hand-typed `cargo update`; AGENTS.md's 'never hand-type `cargo`' rule; release.rs:139 calls the bump a 'ritual'. Overstated: `every_manifest_states_the_same_version` (release.rs:152-201) runs under `just test`, which is a required check on the release PR (SKILL.md:66), so a partial bump fails PR CI — not 'only after a tag push (a full re-cut cycle)'. The `--locked` in the proposal is wrong as noted. Net: a convenience recipe, low severity.

findings.title: `rust` matrix job boots three runners on docs-only changes just to echo; other jobs skip at job level
findings.evidence:
.github/workflows/ci.yml:86-103
  rust:
    name: Rust workspace (${{ matrix.os }})
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    ...
      - uses: actions/checkout@...
      - name: Skip notice (docs-only change)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.code != 'true'
        run: echo "Docs-only change — backend build/test skipped."

.github/workflows/ci.yml:134-137 (web job)
    # Skipped on the weekly cron (audit/deny only) and on docs-only changes. A
    # skipped job reports its required check as satisfied, so the merge gate stays
    # green without running the WASM build / GUI tests.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule' && needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'
findings.rationale: Two different mechanisms achieve the same required-check outcome: the rust job runs on ubuntu, windows AND macos (checkout + 7 conditional steps each, ~1 min of macOS runner per docs PR) while web/actionlint/audit/deny use a job-level `if` whose comment states that a skipped job satisfies the required check. The `changes` job header (lines 34-39) describes only the rust-job mechanism, so the file contradicts itself about how skipping works.
findings.proposal: Move the rust job to the same job-level `if: github.event_name != 'schedule' && needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'`, drop the per-step `if:`s and the notice step, and update the `changes` job comment to describe the job-level skip. Expected effect: zero runner minutes on docs-only PRs for the matrix, one consistent pattern.
findings.verifier_notes: ci.yml:86-130: rust job has job-level `if: github.event_name != 'schedule'` only, then a checkout, a 'Skip notice' step (:101-103) and six per-step `if: needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'` guards across a 3-OS matrix; web (:137), actionlint (:184), audit (:250) and deny (:272) use a job-level `if` whose comments (:134-136, :182-183, :249, :271) state that a skipped job satisfies the required check — the same GitHub semantics the rust job could use. The `changes` job comment (:34-39) describes only the per-step mechanism, so the file is internally inconsistent about how skipping works. No documented reason for the asymmetry. Cost is real but small (three runner boots, one macOS, per docs-only PR); severity low.

findings.title: `verify`'s closing summary omits `web-itest-size` from the gates it did not run
findings.rationale: The size gate is `cargo test --no-run` for wasm32 plus `wc -c` — it needs neither Chrome nor network, yet only `verify-full` runs it, and `verify`'s closing message lists only the network gates as "NOT run", so a contributor reasonably believes `verify` covers everything a browserless box can check. A shard drifting past 52 MB is exactly the CI-only, opaque-timeout failure the recipe was written to pre-empt (justfile:131-139).
findings.proposal: Make the summary at justfile:304 honest: list `web-itest-size` alongside the network gates as not run (with `just verify-full` as where it runs). Optionally run `web-itest-size` from the `[unix]` `web-itest-auto` only AFTER a successful `web-itest`, where the shard objects are hot and the recipe is a relink (justfile:155-156). Do not add it to the skip path: without a prior `web-itest`, `cargo test --no-run --target wasm32 --features test-support` is a full ~45-50 s codegen build of four shards (justfile:22-25) on top of `web-clippy`'s check-only pass.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise true: verify (justfile:302) runs `_verify-core web-itest-auto`; `web-itest-size` (justfile:146-185) needs no browser or network; the summary (:304) names only audit/deny as skipped. But 'near-free' holds only when web-itest just ran; on the skip path it is a real build. It is also a documented decision: justfile:141-142 scopes it as a Linux CI gate, docs/architecture/frontend-workspace.md:227-228 says 'It runs in CI and in `just verify-full`', and shard size only drifts when GUI test modules are added or moved. Low severity: the honest summary line is the genuine fix.

findings.title: aria-expanded bound to a bare bool in FilterToggle and the account-menu trigger (the documented boolean-attribute bug, two new instances)
findings.evidence:
filter_toggle.rs:24:            aria-expanded=move || open.get()
shell.rs:343:                                aria-expanded=move || menu_open.get()

docs/architecture/frontend-workspace.md:71-73: "**`aria-selected` must be a *string*** ... bound to a bare `bool`, Leptos renders a boolean attribute — `aria-selected=""` when true, absent when false — and neither is a valid ARIA value."
tab_bar.rs:193-199 and application_list.rs:526-529 carry the same warning and use `.to_string()`.
findings.rationale: Both bindings render `aria-expanded=""` when open and omit the attribute when closed, so a screen reader hears no expanded/collapsed state for the list filter drawer or the account menu (the latter also declares aria-haspopup="menu", so AT expects the state). The repo already fixed this class of bug three times (tab_bar, global_search, permission_tester, application_list) but nothing pins it, so it keeps recurring.
