findings.title: List Refresh bumps the resource before the cache invalidation is awaited, so it can refetch the cached list
findings.rationale: Nothing orders the two IPC calls: the resource re-run is scheduled first and the backend's cache-hit path is fully synchronous (no await before `return Ok(cached)`), so `list_applications_with_pairing` can be served from the very cache `invalidate_list_cache` is about to drop. The Refresh button then spins and shows the same stale rows. The detail pane's own Refresh (application_detail_pane.rs:70-73) does it correctly: `invalidate_application_detail(...).await; reload.update(...)`. enterprise_application_list.rs:114-122 has the same shape, so the fix should land in both.
findings.proposal: In `on_refresh`, move `reload.update(...)` inside the spawned task after the `invalidate_list_cache(...).await` (mirroring application_detail_pane.rs:70-73), and do the same in enterprise_application_list.rs. Optionally add a GUI test in tests/gui/application_list.rs whose mock records call order (invalidate before list).
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is real: apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/application_list.rs:244-251 bumps `reload` and only then spawns `invalidate_list_cache`; enterprise_application_list.rs:114-123 is the same shape. Backend `list_applications_with_pairing` (src-tauri/src/commands/applications/mod.rs:136-148) returns the cached Vec synchronously with no await before it, and `invalidate_list_cache` (commands/diagnostics.rs:52-81) is a sync command. Nothing orders the two IPCs, so the outcome is a scheduling race (frontend task order vs. tokio spawn of the async list command vs. the sync invalidate on the IPC thread) — it may often resolve favourably in practice, but nothing guarantees it and the comment's 'next tick' rationale is unproven. The repo already has the correct order in three siblings: application_detail_pane.rs:70-74, managed_identities/mod.rs:110-121 and managed_identities/detail_window.rs:195-206 all `await` the invalidate before bumping. The only test (tests/gui/application_list.rs:196-214, and the enterprise twin at :116) asserts the invalidate call happened, not its order relative to the list fetch. No AGENTS.md/architecture note documents bump-first as deliberate.

findings.title: Permissions tab consent/downgrade outcome notes are set right before `on_changed` unmounts the tab; consent failures never reach the operator
findings.rationale: `bump_reload` re-runs the pane's `LocalResource`; the `Suspend` closure in application_detail_pane.rs:136-148 builds a fresh view (new `detail_signal`, new tab components) so every local signal in PermissionsTab is discarded. The `consent_result` Callout (763-779, the only place `r.role_assignments_skipped.len()` and `r.failures.len()` are shown) and the `scope_note` Callout (759-761, the only report of the downgrade outcome, e.g. "narrower permission was already in place" / "was already gone") therefore flash at most for the refetch duration. The success toast omits `failures`, so a partial consent (`GrantResult.failures: Vec<GrantFailure>`, dto/permissions.rs:72) reads as an unqualified success. The comment at 205-206 is also stale: line 342 closes the chooser.
findings.proposal: Follow the credentials tab's documented pattern: report via the session toast stack before `on_changed`. For consent, `toast_error` when `!r.failures.is_empty()` naming the count (and ideally the first failure message), `toast_success` otherwise; drop the `consent_result` Callout. For downgrade, `session.toast_success(note)` and drop `scope_note`. Fix the stale comment. Longer term, see the detail-pane remount finding.
findings.verifier_notes: Code matches: permissions_tab.rs:110-117 toasts only created/upserted counts, sets `consent_result`, then `on_changed.run(())`; the downgrade path at :341-343 sets `scope_note`, closes the chooser (`pending_downgrade.set(None)`) and calls `on_changed`. The pane's `Suspend` (application_detail_pane.rs:136-148) rebuilds the whole subtree on reload, and credentials_tab.rs:470-475 documents exactly this ("anything held here is unmounted before it can be read"). The `consent_result` Callout (:763-779) is the only place `failures.len()` appears, and backend `grant_admin_consent_core` (src-tauri/src/commands/permissions.rs:348, :425-555) collects partial failures into `Ok(GrantResult.failures)` rather than erroring, so a partial consent really does read as an unqualified success toast. The comment at :205-206 is stale — :342 closes the chooser. Downgraded from high to medium: after the reload the permissions table shows live per-row consent state, so the operator is not left believing a permission is granted when it is not; what is lost is the explicit failure count/message (`GrantFailure.message` is not surfaced anywhere even today, only counted). No GUI test covers either note (grep of tests/gui for Downgrade/Grant admin consent finds nothing).

findings.title: SharePoint sites section (app-reg and enterprise panes) is gated on the bare `Sites.*` value instead of the resource-aware `is_sharepoint_orgwide_permission`
findings.rationale: The row-level gate `row_scope_kind` (lines 70-81) and the `has_mail` gate three lines earlier (781-786, `is_exchange_scopable_on(Some(&p.resource_app_id), v)`) are resource-aware; this section gate is not. An app holding `Sites.Read.All` only on Office 365 SharePoint Online (or any third-party API exposing a `Sites.*` role) gets the `SharePointSitesSection`, which reads Graph per-site grants and will report "no grants" for a permission that section cannot describe. The repo invariant (`the_resource_blind_mailbox_gates_are_not_reintroduced`) only pins the Exchange forms, so nothing catches this.
findings.proposal: Gate both call sites (permissions_tab.rs:808-814 and enterprise_application_detail_pane/permissions.rs:253-258) on `is_sharepoint_orgwide_permission(Some(&p.resource_app_id), v) || (v == "Sites.Selected" && resource is Graph or SPO)` — i.e. accept Graph + Office 365 SharePoint Online and reject other resources — or add a `is_sharepoint_site_grant_resource_permission` helper in core::scoping with that exact semantics and a unit test. Decide explicitly (doc comment on `SharePointSitesSection`, lines 7-11) whether SPO-resource apps keep the section; do not silently narrow to Graph-only. Optionally extend the repo invariant's GONE list to bare `is_sharepoint_orgwide(` calls outside core and scope_badge.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise holds: permissions_tab.rs:808-814 gates `SharePointSitesSection` on the bare value (`v == "Sites.Selected" || is_sharepoint_orgwide(v)`), unlike the row gate `row_scope_kind` (:70-81) and `has_mail` (:781-786); the enterprise pane has the identical bare gate at enterprise_application_detail_pane/permissions.rs:253-258, and the invariant at src-tauri/tests/repo_invariants/commands.rs:130-133 pins only the three Exchange names. But the impact and the proposal are overstated. The core already has a resource-aware classifier the reviewer did not engage with: `is_sharepoint_orgwide_permission(resource_app_id, value)` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/scoping.rs:377-388) deliberately treats BOTH Microsoft Graph and Office 365 SharePoint Online as SharePoint reach and rejects other resources — so a Graph-only gate would hide the section for SPO-resource apps, which the repo's own reach classification (and sharepoint-selected.md:13-15, 'only per-site via the SharePoint site access section') does not call for; the Graph-only limit in `is_scopable_sharepoint_resource_permission` (scoping.rs:406-410) is about offering the *conversion fix*, not about showing the per-site grant list. The realistic false positive is a third-party API exposing a `Sites.`-prefixed role, and the cost is an extra collapsible section, not a wrong verdict.

findings.title: `pending_app_tab` leaks to the next opened app when the deep-link target is already open
findings.rationale: The pane consumes `pending_app_tab` only in its constructor. If the credential dashboard's "Open" (credentials_dashboard.rs:114) or an audit row (audit_view/row.rs:179) targets an app that is already in the workspace, `open_item` just refocuses it, no pane mounts, and the flag stays `Some("credentials")`. The next unrelated app the operator opens from the list lands on Credentials instead of `last_app_tab`, with no visible cause. The MI variant's comment acknowledges an already-open window keeps its tab, but nobody clears the flag. The only test (state/mod.rs:456-487) covers the tenant-switch reset.
findings.proposal: In `open_app_on_tab` / `open_enterprise_on_tab`, check `self.is_open(kind, &id)` first: if open, don't set the pending flag (or set a per-open-item `requested_tab` the pane observes via an Effect so the live pane actually switches tab). Add a unit test asserting `pending_app_tab` is `None` after deep-linking to an already-open item.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified end to end. navigation.rs:108-110 sets `pending_app_tab` unconditionally then calls `open_item`; open_items.rs:70-74 early-returns (retitle + `focus_item`) when `(kind, entity_id)` is already open; the workspace mounts a pane for EVERY open item (`<For each=move || session.open_items.get()>` at components/open_items_workspace.rs:138) and merely toggles `display:none` for non-shown panes (:236), so re-focusing never remounts and the only consumer (application_detail_pane.rs:81-86) never runs. The flag is cleared only by `TenantScopedUi::reset` (state/mod.rs:264), and the sole test (state/mod.rs:456-488) covers that reset. `open_enterprise_on_tab` (navigation.rs:117-122) with its consumer at enterprise_application_detail_pane/mod.rs:185-193 has the identical leak. The MI comment at navigation.rs:127-129 acknowledges the already-open case keeps its tab but not that the pending flag then leaks to the next unrelated app.

findings.title: Every mutation rebuilds the whole detail pane and remounts all visited tabs (root cause of the deferred-reload workarounds)
findings.rationale: `bump_reload` re-runs the resource, the Suspend closure yields a brand-new view, and with `Suspense` (not `Transition`; no `<Transition` exists in web-rs) the skeleton flashes first. The keep-alive latch preserves state across tab switches but not across saves, so removing one owner re-runs `list_federated_credentials`, `get_expose_api`, `get_application_authentication`, the Activity audit query + sign-in lookup, the CA list, the Exchange mail-scope lookup and resets the usage panel for every tab that was visited — and discards half-typed forms in other tabs. It also forces the credentials tab's three "defer on_changed until the dialog is dismissed" dances (390-397, 578-584, 600-608) and causes the lost-notes bug in the permissions tab.
findings.proposal: Keep a long-lived `RwSignal<Option<Arc<ApplicationDetail>>>` on the pane, update it from an Effect over the resource (or in the Suspend on success), and mount `DetailHeader` + `TabBar` + the keep-alive tabs once outside the Suspend, passing `Signal<Arc<ApplicationDetail>>` derived from that signal; show `DetailSkeleton` only while the signal is `None`. Tabs then survive `on_changed`, the reveal-dialog deferrals become unnecessary, and per-tab sub-resources only re-run when their inputs change. Interim cheap step: switch `Suspense` to `Transition` to remove the skeleton flash.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is accurate: application_detail_pane.rs:129-135 uses `Suspense` (fallback = `DetailSkeleton`), :136-148 rebuilds header, `TabBar` and every `keep_alive` tab inside the `Suspend` on each resource re-run; the `keep_alive` comment (:94-99) explains tab-switch survival only. `grep -rn Transition web-rs/src` returns nothing, so the skeleton flash claim stands. The three credentials-tab deferrals exist at credentials_tab.rs:390-397, 578-584 and 600-608, and the browser test `the_reveal_defers_the_detail_reload_until_it_is_dismissed` (tests/gui/certificate_reveal.rs:279) pins the workaround — the refactor must keep or adapt that test. The long-lived `RwSignal<Option<Arc<ApplicationDetail>>>` + Effect proposal is feasible in Leptos 0.8 and would also remove the root cause of finding 1. Effort L is honest; medium severity fits a refactor whose symptoms are already visible as separate bugs.

findings.title: OwnersTab and AddOwnerButton hand-roll the directory search that DirectorySearch/OwnerPicker exist to replace, reintroducing the 'No matches under an untouched box' bug
findings.rationale: owners_tab.rs:36-67 + 449-536 and add_owner.rs:42-62 + 213-261 each carry their own 300 ms debounce, 2-char gate, Suspense + "Searching…" spinner and `.candidates` markup. Because the resource returns `Ok(Vec::new())` for short queries and the render only checks `filtered.is_empty()`, the Owners tab shows "No matches." beneath an empty search box on first paint — exactly the drift the primitive was extracted to end. Both files also duplicate the add-default-owners loop (owners_tab.rs:127-150 vs add_owner.rs:125-159) with slightly different `existing` sources. There is no backend `add_default_owners` command (grep of src-tauri/src/commands finds none).
findings.proposal: Replace both search blocks with `OwnerPicker`/`DirectorySearch` (`exclude` = current owners or staged set, `action_label` = "Add"/"Stage", `row_disabled` for the in-flight id, `clear_on_pick=false` + own `query` for the add path that clears on success). Move the default-owners loop into one backend command (`add_default_owners(tenant_id, object_id) -> {added, failures}`) or one shared frontend helper, and have both call sites use it.
findings.verifier_notes: owners_tab.rs:36-67 and :449-536 and dialogs/add_owner.rs:42-62 and :213-261 each carry a 300 ms `use_debounced`, a 2-char gate returning `Ok(Vec::new())`, and their own results markup. The owners tab's `Suspend` checks only `filtered.is_empty()` (:482-484) so an untouched box renders "No matches." — the exact bug frontend-workspace.md:85-86 says `DirectorySearch` was extracted to end (add_owner.rs:222-228 gates on the debounced, not raw, query so it renders nothing but still drifts). The default-owners loop is duplicated at owners_tab.rs:127-150 vs add_owner.rs:125-159 with different `existing` sources, and `grep add_default_owners src-tauri/src/commands` finds no backend command. `DirectorySearch` already exposes `exclude`, `query`, `action_label`, `action_appearance`, `row_disabled`, `clear_on_pick`, `show_no_matches` (components/directory_search.rs:60-130), so the replacement is feasible; one caveat: the Owners tab's Stage/Add label flips with `replacing`, and `action_label` is a plain `String`, so either a `Signal` prop or two instances under a `Show` is needed. directory_search.rs:1-10 and frontend-workspace.md:77-86 list the four folded consumers; neither owners surface is documented as a deliberate exclusion.

findings.title: 'Rotate & remove existing' deletes every client secret with no confirmation and no count
findings.evidence:
<Button
                        class="button--danger"
                        appearance=Signal::derive(|| ButtonAppearance::Primary)
                        on_click=Box::new(move |_| do_rotate(true))
                        disabled=Signal::derive(move || cmd_rotate.busy.get())
                    >
(lines 512-516) let remove_key_ids: Vec<String> = if remove_existing { secrets.with(|list| list.iter().map(|s| s.key_id.clone()).collect()) } else { Vec::new() };
findings.rationale: Removing one secret goes through `ConfirmDialog` with the credential named as subject (1132-1146), and the expired sweep is confirm-gated too (1162-1177), but the rotate dialog's primary danger button strips all N secrets, active ones included, on a single click. The dialog body says only "optionally removes the existing secret(s)" and the button label carries no count, so an operator cannot see they are about to break every other caller of the app.
findings.proposal: Label the button with the live count ("Rotate & remove {n} existing"), and either route `do_rotate(true)` through a `ConfirmDialog` (subject = app name, body naming the count) or require `require_keyword` when `n > 1`. Also surface `r.warnings` content (currently "see the log", line 539) in the toast or an expandable Callout, since the log is not reachable from the UI.
findings.verifier_notes: credentials_tab.rs:1112-1127: the `button--danger` Primary button calls `do_rotate(true)` directly; :512-516 collects every `key_id` in `secrets` (active included); the dialog body (:1089) says only "optionally removes the existing secret(s)". Per-row removals (:1130-1160) and the expired sweep (:1162-1177) go through `ConfirmDialog` with a named subject, so the inconsistency is real. Warnings come from src-tauri/src/commands/keyvault.rs:133-182 ("failed to remove {key_id}: {e}") but the UI only shows a count with "see the log" (:539), and a grep of web-rs/src for any log viewer/open-log affordance finds none. Proposal (live count in the label, ConfirmDialog or `require_keyword` when n>1, surface warning text) is consistent with the repo's existing ConfirmDialog usage.

findings.title: Lifetime/validity inputs are silently coerced (garbage → default, out of range → clamp) instead of validated
findings.evidence:
let days = rotate_lifetime
            .get()
            .parse::<u32>()
            .unwrap_or(180)
            .clamp(1, 730);
(lines 570-574) let days = gencert_validity.get().parse::<u32>().unwrap_or(365).clamp(1, 1095);
(lines 125-128) /// Resolves the Expires controls ... Mirrors the backend's validation (end after start, 24-month cap) for friendlier, pre-submit errors
findings.rationale: The new-secret dialog validates and reports (`resolve_expiry_fields` returns `Err("Secret lifetime cannot exceed 24 months.")`), but the rotate and generate-certificate dialogs accept "abc", "0", "3650" or "90 days" and mint a credential with a lifetime the operator did not type (180/365 days, or the cap), with no message. A certificate valid for 1095 days when 3650 was requested, or a rotated secret expiring in 180 days when "18" was a typo for "180", is a silent divergence from intent on a security-critical object. Neither path has a unit test.
findings.proposal: Extract `fn parse_days(raw: &str, min: u32, max: u32) -> Result<u32, String>` returning a message ("Enter a whole number of days between 1 and 730."), surface it via the shared `error` signal before dispatch like `resolve_expiry_fields`, and add table tests. Consider `<Select>` presets for both dialogs, matching the new-secret dialog.
findings.verifier_notes: Both controls are free-text `<Input>`s (credentials_tab.rs:935 `gencert_validity`, :1098 `rotate_lifetime`, defaults at :279/:349). :507-511 does `parse::<u32>().unwrap_or(180).clamp(1, 730)` and :570-574 `unwrap_or(365).clamp(1, 1095)` with no error path, unlike `resolve_expiry_fields` (:125-140) which returns `Err` for the new-secret dialog. Backend: rotate also clamps (commands/applications/credentials.rs:82, MAX_SECRET_LIFETIME_DAYS=730) so the frontend clamp is redundant but the parse-failure→default is silent; `generate_self_signed_certificate` uses `validity_days.unwrap_or(365)` with no cap (credentials.rs:136), so the frontend 1095 clamp is the only cap and a typed 3650 becomes 1095 with no message. The four unit tests in credentials_tab.rs (:1199-1275) cover presets/custom expiry and secret-name sanitising, not these two paths.

findings.title: Identifier-URI add/remove replays the tab's stale snapshot as a full replace (lost-update), contradicting the module doc
findings.rationale: `uris` is a `StoredValue` captured from the DTO at mount (line 100). Scopes and pre-authorized clients are re-read live by the backend before their PATCH, but `set_identifier_uris` writes whatever list the client sends. If another admin (or the SSO wizard, which also edits identifierUris) added a URI after this tab loaded, Add or Remove here silently drops it. The module doc claims live re-read for every mutation, so a maintainer would not expect this.
findings.proposal: Either add `add_identifier_uri` / `remove_identifier_uri` backend commands that GET the live `identifierUris`, apply the delta, validate and PATCH (like `upsert_api_scope`), or have the frontend call `get_expose_api` immediately before computing the new list. Update the module doc either way.
findings.verifier_notes: expose_api_tab.rs:100 snapshots `dto.identifier_uris` into a `StoredValue` at mount; :123-139 (add) and the remove path (~:145-155) mutate that snapshot and call `set_identifier_uris(&list)`. Backend `set_identifier_uris` (src-tauri/src/commands/expose_api.rs:253-284) validates and PATCHes the client-supplied list with no live read — its own doc says "The editor loads the current list and sends the complete desired set" — whereas `upsert_api_scope` re-reads live (`fetch_expose_api`, expose_api.rs:296). The tab module doc (:6-9) claims the backend re-reads live state before every write, which is false for URIs. The SSO wizard also writes `identifier_uris` (commands/sso/mod.rs:199). The window is narrower than implied — the tab refetches after each of its own saves (:61-65) and the whole pane remounts on `on_changed` — but it is a real lost-update on a security-relevant field with a misleading doc. Either proposed fix (delta commands re-reading live like `upsert_api_scope`, or a `get_expose_api` immediately before computing the list) fits the repo's 'full-collection PATCH: re-read live, mutate, write back' convention.

findings.title: Tab-level load failures render red text with no Retry instead of the DetailLoadError primitive
findings.rationale: A transient 429/network failure on `get_expose_api`, `get_application_authentication`, `list_federated_credentials` or `list_resource_permissions` leaves the operator with a dead red line; the only recovery is the pane-level Refresh (which remounts everything) or reopening the wizard. Activity and Conditional Access tabs (activity_tab.rs:83-91, conditional_access_tab.rs:70-78) already use `DetailLoadError` with `on_retry` bumping their `reload`, so this is drift, not design.
findings.proposal: Replace the four `Body1.form-error` branches with `<DetailLoadError error=e on_retry=Callback::new(move |_| reload.update(|n| *n += 1)) />` (the picker can re-set `resource_app_id` to retrigger its resource). The `web-test-strings-check.sh` hook will flag nothing since no test references these strings.
findings.verifier_notes: All four cited branches exist verbatim (expose_api_tab.rs:81-83, authentication_tab.rs:66-69, federated_tab.rs:557-559, permission_picker.rs:243-248) and the drift is larger than stated: sharepoint_sites_section.rs:319, enterprise_application_detail_pane/app_roles.rs:263 and enterprise_application_detail_pane/permissions.rs:222 are the same hand-rolled `Body1.form-error` on a load failure. activity_tab.rs:83-91 and conditional_access_tab.rs:70-78 already use `DetailLoadError` with an `on_retry` that bumps `reload`, and frontend-workspace.md / .claude/rules/frontend.md name `DetailLoadError` as the single load-failure primitive, so this is a documented-invariant violation rather than a taste call. Medium is fair given AGENTS.md's 'one primitive per UI pattern' rule; the fix is mechanical.

findings.title: Authentication form has no Reset or dirty state; Overview Save round-trips an empty PATCH (and busts list caches) when nothing changed
findings.evidence:
<div class="actions-row">
                <Button
                    appearance=Signal::derive(|| ButtonAppearance::Primary)
                    on_click=Box::new(save)
                    disabled=Signal::derive(move || cmd.busy.get())
                >
(overview_tab.rs:84-88) move |tenant_id| { let mut patch = UpdateApplicationInput::default(); let dn_t = dn.trim(); if dn_t != app.display_name { patch.display_name = Some(dn_t.to_string()); }
(overview_tab.rs:158-159) on_click=Box::new(save) disabled=Signal::derive(move || cmd.busy.get())
findings.rationale: The Authentication tab is a full-replace write of three URI lists plus five flags, yet the only control is Save: after mangling rows the operator has no way back short of refreshing the whole pane, and there is no indication that anything differs from the loaded DTO. The Overview edit computes the diff only inside the async closure, so an unchanged form still round-trips a `{}` PATCH and shows a spinner, and Save is never disabled for a clean form. Neither form warns when the open item is closed with unsaved edits.
findings.proposal: Derive a `dirty: Signal<bool>` for each form (compare `to_uris()`/flags with the loaded DTO in AuthenticationForm; compare the four fields with `app` in OverviewTab), disable Save when clean, add a Reset to the Authentication form that rebuilds the `UriListState`s from the DTO, and have Overview's `save` short-circuit with a toast when the patch is empty so `update_application` is not called (avoids the needless `invalidate_app_lists`). An unsaved-changes guard on `close_item` is optional follow-up, not part of this fix.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise mostly true: authentication_tab.rs:184-196 renders only Save (disabled on busy), no Reset/dirty state; overview_tab.rs:84-111 computes the diff inside the async closure so a clean form still dispatches, and backend `update_application` (commands/applications/mod.rs:383-400) PATCHes whatever it receives and then `invalidate_app_lists` — so an unchanged save costs a Graph PATCH *and* a list-cache bust. `grep -rn dirty|unsaved web-rs/src` finds nothing. Overstated: the Overview edit DOES have a Cancel (`cancel` at overview_tab.rs:113-116), so 'no Cancel' applies to the Authentication tab only; and the pane-level Refresh is an existing (if heavy) way back. This is a UX enhancement with a workaround, so low rather than medium.

findings.title: Browser GUI tests do not exercise the Owners, Expose an API or Permissions tab actions, nor rotate/new-secret/federated flows
findings.rationale: The detail pane has four smoke tests, the certificate reveal and authentication tab are well covered, but the three most mutation-heavy tabs have no behavioural coverage: revoke/remove-declaration confirm routing (three always-mounted dialogs keyed on `PendingRevoke`), the downgrade chooser, the Application/Delegated filter toggles, Replace-all-owners staging and apply, default-owner addition, scope add/edit/delete and pre-authorized client editing, the new-secret dialog + `SecretRevealDialog`, and the rotate-into-Key-Vault dialog prefill. Regressions such as the lost consent/downgrade notes or a mis-wired `PendingRevoke` arm would pass CI.
findings.proposal: Add `tests/gui/owners_tab.rs`, `expose_api_tab.rs` and `permissions_tab.rs` modules (sharded by the detail-pane subtree per frontend-workspace.md) with mocked IPC: assert the confirm dialog names the row's subject and the mocked command receives the right ids; assert the downgrade chooser lists `downgrade_alternatives` and the outcome is reported; assert Replace-all sends exactly the staged ids; assert the new-secret flow shows the reveal and only reloads on Done. Reuse the `certificate_reveal.rs` mount helpers.
findings.verifier_notes: tests/gui/ has application_detail.rs (4 smoke tests), authentication_tab.rs, certificate_reveal.rs and credential_sweep.rs; per-string greps confirm no GUI test mentions Downgrade, Grant admin consent, Revoke, Replace all, Add Default Owners, Add a scope or New secret, and 'Rotate' matches only a notes fixture string (application_detail.rs:35). permissions_tab.rs has 5 `#[test]`s of pure helpers, owners_tab.rs and expose_api_tab.rs have 0. AGENTS.md states the browser GUI tests are the frontend's only behavioural gate, so the mutation-heavy tabs are indeed ungated. Note for the proposal: the detail-pane modules live in tests/gui_1.rs and `just web-itest-size` enforces a per-shard ceiling, so new modules may need a new shard (frontend-workspace.md sharding rules).

findings.title: Stale doc comments reference a deleted TSX frontend and the removed thaw TabList
findings.rationale: `apps/desktop/` contains only `src-tauri` and `web-rs`; the `.tsx` files referenced in application_detail_pane.rs:3, application_list.rs:2, owners_tab.rs:2, create_app_dialog.rs:3, tabs/mod.rs:1, views/mod.rs:1, hooks/mod.rs:1 and state/tenant.rs:17 no longer exist, and `AppTab`/`EnterpriseTab` still describe themselves in terms of thaw's `Tab`/`TabList`, which the architecture doc says was removed. A new contributor following these pointers finds nothing.
findings.proposal: Delete the "Mirrors …tsx" sentences (or replace with the one-line purpose) and reword app_tab.rs:59 / enterprise_tab.rs:27,64 to reference `components::ui::TabBar`. A repo-invariant test asserting no source mentions `apps/desktop/web/` would keep it that way.
findings.verifier_notes: `grep -rn 'apps/desktop/web/' web-rs/src` returns exactly the eight cited references (application_detail_pane.rs:3, application_list.rs:2, owners_tab.rs:2, create_app_dialog.rs:3, tabs/mod.rs:1, views/mod.rs:1, hooks/mod.rs:1, state/tenant.rs:17) and `ls apps/desktop` shows only src-tauri and web-rs. app_tab.rs:59 and enterprise_tab.rs:27,64 still cite Thaw's `Tab`/`TabList`, while components/ui/tab_bar.rs:19-20 documents that `TabList` was replaced app-wide. Purely a docs fix; a repo-invariant scan is cheap and consistent with the existing source-scanning tests.

findings.title: Shared helpers exist but are still bypassed: no_tenant(), copy_text(), MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID, sign-in-audience list
findings.rationale: `util::no_tenant()` was introduced to end the duplication its own doc describes, yet application_detail_pane.rs:44-50 and permission_picker.rs:130-135 still inline the struct. `util::copy_text` exists ("Shared by the detail panes and the SSO summary") but credentials_tab.rs:972-982 and secret_reveal_dialog.rs:21-29 re-implement the clipboard call. `azapptoolkit_core::scoping::MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID` is already imported by permissions_tab tests, but permission_picker.rs redefines it. create_app_dialog.rs:88-97 hard-codes the four sign-in audiences that overview_tab.rs:12-26 keeps in `SIGN_IN_AUDIENCES`.
findings.proposal: Use `no_tenant()` in both resources; use `copy_text` (or `CopyIconButton`) in the two dialogs; re-export core's `MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID` from the picker instead of redefining; move `SIGN_IN_AUDIENCES` to a shared module and render `create_app_dialog`'s options from it.
findings.verifier_notes: All claims check out and one is understated. `no_tenant()` (util.rs:88-96) is bypassed by inline structs at application_detail_pane.rs:44-50, permission_picker.rs:130-135, exchange_scoping_section.rs:173 and enterprise_application_detail_pane/mod.rs:113. `copy_text` (util.rs:76-86) is re-implemented at credentials_tab.rs:972-982, secret_reveal_dialog.rs:21-28 AND sso_summary.rs:122-131 — even though util.rs:77 claims the SSO summary uses it — and components/ui/copy_icon_button.rs:12-16 declares `CopyIconButton` the single home of copy feedback. permission_picker.rs:31 redefines the Graph app id as a literal while core::scoping::MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID (scoping.rs:26) exists and is used by scope_wizard tests. create_app_dialog.rs:88-97 hard-codes the four audiences that overview_tab.rs:12-26 keeps in `SIGN_IN_AUDIENCES`. Small, mechanical, matches the repo's stated intent.

findings.title: Dead and duplicate IPC argument structs hidden by `#![allow(dead_code)]` on the bindings module
findings.rationale: `ResolvePermissionArgs` (applications.rs:75-81), `UpdateRequiredResourceArgs` (permissions.rs:53-59) and `SetArgs` (keyvault.rs:58-63) have no callers (grep finds only their definitions); `FederatedListArgs` (applications.rs:406-411) is field-for-field `ObjectIdArgs`; `TenantArgs` in keyvault.rs (and search.rs/sso.rs/defaults.rs) duplicates `common::TenantArg` despite common.rs existing to be the single source of truth. The crate-wide `#![allow(dead_code)]` means the compiler will never point any of this out, including a binding whose backend command is later removed.
findings.proposal: Delete the three unused structs, replace `FederatedListArgs` with `ObjectIdArgs` and the per-file `TenantArgs` with `TenantArg`, then narrow `#![allow(dead_code)]` to the specific re-exported DTO items that need it (or drop it and let clippy report genuinely dead bindings).
findings.verifier_notes: bindings/mod.rs:1 is `#![allow(dead_code)]` with no rationale comment. Greps confirm `ResolvePermissionArgs` (applications.rs:77), `UpdateRequiredResourceArgs` (permissions.rs:55) and keyvault's `SetArgs` (keyvault.rs:60) have only their definitions (defaults.rs has its own, *used*, `SetArgs` at :27/:40 — a name collision but not dead). `FederatedListArgs` (applications.rs:406-411) is field-for-field `common::ObjectIdArgs` (common.rs:22-27). `TenantArgs` is redefined in keyvault.rs:81, search.rs:22, sso.rs:180 and defaults.rs:15 despite `common::TenantArg` (common.rs:15-19) being re-exported from bindings/mod.rs:53 and used by enterprise_application.rs, sharepoint.rs, backup.rs, managed_identity.rs. Caveat on the proposal: some bindings exist only for demo fixtures/tests, so dropping the crate-wide allow may need targeted `#[cfg_attr]`/`#[allow]` rather than a blanket removal.

findings.title: SecretRevealDialog reports 'Copied' even when the clipboard write fails, and a reflex Escape dismisses the one-time secret
findings.rationale: `write_text` can reject (no focus, permission denied in some webviews); the dialog still flips to "Copied", and because `on_close` triggers `on_changed` the secret is gone for good once dismissed. Escape closes the reveal unconditionally, so an operator who habitually hits Esc after copying-that-failed loses the value. The credentials tab's `copy_pk` (972-982) gives no feedback at all, so a failed private-key copy is indistinguishable from success there.
findings.proposal: Set `copied` only on `Ok(_)` and show a Callout on `Err` ("Couldn't copy — select the text and copy manually"); for both one-time reveals gate Escape (`use_escape(|| false, ...)`) or require the explicit Done button, and reuse `CopyIconButton`/`copy_text` so the feedback is the app-wide badge.
findings.verifier_notes: secret_reveal_dialog.rs:21-28: `let _ = JsFuture::from(promise).await; copied.set(true);` flips the label regardless of rejection; :32 `use_escape(|| true, …)` closes on Escape unconditionally and `on_close` is what releases the deferred reload (credentials_tab.rs:390-397), so the value is gone. credentials_tab.rs:972-982 `copy_pk` discards the result with no feedback at all, and the gencert reveal has no `use_escape` (grep), so the two one-time reveals already behave differently. `CopyIconButton` (components/ui/copy_icon_button.rs) is the documented feedback primitive, though it too rides fire-and-forget `copy_text`, so honouring the promise result would need a small extension there.

findings.title: Permissions tab empty state points to the Entra portal and the hand-rolled kind filters can render an empty table silently
findings.evidence:
<Body1>
                            "No permissions declared. Use the Entra portal or restore from a saved manifest."
                        </Body1>
(lines 523-527) <button class=move || filter_chip_class(show_application.get()) type="button" on:click=move |_| show_application.update(|v| *v = !*v)>
(lines 484-489) <Button appearance=Signal::derive(|| ButtonAppearance::Primary) on_click=Box::new(move |_| wizard_open.set(true))> "Grant access"
findings.rationale: The empty-state copy predates the in-app "Grant access" wizard that sits two lines above it, so it sends the operator to the portal for something the tab now does. The Application/Delegated toggles are bespoke `permissions-tab__filter-chip` buttons (not `FilterChip`/`TabBar`), carry no `aria-pressed`, and with both toggled off the `<For>` renders nothing under the table header with no "no rows match" message.
findings.proposal: Reword to "No permissions declared — use Grant access to add one."; add `aria-pressed` (as a string) to the toggles or replace them with a three-value `TabBar` (All/Application/Delegated) which cannot reach the both-off state; if toggles stay, render an inline `Body1` when the filtered set is empty.
findings.verifier_notes: permissions_tab.rs:573-575 still says "Use the Entra portal or restore from a saved manifest" while the in-app `Grant access` wizard button sits at :484-489. The Application/Delegated toggles at :520-533 are raw `<button>`s styled by `filter_chip_class` (:835-841) with no `aria-pressed` (grep); note the existing `FilterChip` primitive (components/filter_chip.rs) is a single-select facet chip, also without `aria-pressed`, so a three-value `TabBar` or `aria-pressed` on the existing buttons is the right fix rather than `FilterChip`. No 'no rows match' message exists for the both-off state (grep finds none). All low-severity copy/a11y polish.

findings.title: Permission picker checkboxes share one aria-label and clone the counts map per option
findings.evidence:
<input
                            type="checkbox"
                            class="permission-picker__check"
                            aria-label="Select permission"
                            prop:checked=checked
                            on:change=on_change
                        />
(lines 172-174) let label = counts.get().get(&r.app_id)
(application_list.rs:703) let check_label = format!("Select {display_name} ({app_id_string}) for bulk actions");
findings.rationale: Microsoft Graph alone lists ~400 application permissions; every checkbox announcing "Select permission" makes the picker unusable with a screen reader, while the app-registration list already demonstrates the descriptive-label pattern. Separately, `counts.get()` inside the per-option `.map` clones the whole `HashMap` once per resource option on every render of the dropdown.
findings.proposal: Use `aria-label=format!("Select {}", r.value)` (and the same for delegated scopes at line 421); read counts with `counts.with(|c| c.get(&r.app_id).copied())`.
findings.verifier_notes: permission_picker.rs:474 and :421 both render `aria-label="Select permission"` on every option checkbox; application_list.rs:703 shows the repo's descriptive-label pattern. :172-174 calls `counts.get()` inside the per-option `.map`, cloning the whole `HashMap` per resource option on each dropdown render; `counts.with(|c| c.get(&r.app_id).copied())` is the idiomatic fix. Real but small; low is right.

findings.title: Pre-authorized client add is a GUID-only field with no directory lookup, and existing rows show the bare GUID with no display name
findings.rationale: Pre-authorizing a client skips user consent, so a mistyped or wrong GUID is a security-relevant error that today only surfaces as a Graph 400 (or silently pre-authorizes the wrong app if the GUID happens to exist). The frontend already has a tenant SP index and a `list_app_role_resources`-style picker group ("Tenant app registrations") that resolve name + appId; the row also renders the raw GUID with no display name (line 567), so the operator cannot tell which app is authorized.
findings.proposal: Add a typeahead over the tenant's app registrations/service principals (appId + display name — the SP index / `list_app_role_resources`-style catalog already resolves these) for the add path, and resolve display names for existing `pre_authorized_applications` rows from the SP index (falling back to the GUID). Client-side GUID-shape validation is optional polish since the backend already returns a validation error before Graph.
findings.verifier_notes: The 'no validation … only surfaces as a Graph 400' premise is false: backend `set_pre_authorized_app` (src-tauri/src/commands/expose_api.rs:362-373) rejects a non-GUID with `UiError::validation("invalid_client_app_id", …)` before any Graph call, and the dialog surfaces it via `pre_cmd.error`. What holds: the add path is a free-text `` (expose_api_tab.rs:741-746) with no typeahead over the tenant's app registrations, existing rows render the bare GUID (:567 `{p.app_id}`) with no display name, and a *well-formed but wrong* GUID is indeed only caught by Graph (or not at all if it exists). A feature request, low severity.

findings.title: Deep-link pending tab leaks into the next mounted pane when the target item is already open
findings.rationale: Panes are keep-alive (keyed <For> over open_items) and consume `pending_app_tab` / `pending_enterprise_tab` once on mount. When the credential dashboard or a finding calls `open_app_on_tab(id, "credentials")` for an app whose pane is ALREADY open, `open_item` dedupes and re-focuses without remounting, so the pending signal is never consumed. It stays `Some("credentials")` until the next app-reg pane mounts — i.e. the next unrelated app the operator opens from the list lands on the Credentials tab instead of their last-used tab. Same for `open_enterprise_on_tab` (line 117). The MI variant (`last_mi_tab`) is immune because it sets the persistent last-tab rather than a one-shot.
findings.proposal: In `open_app_on_tab` / `open_enterprise_on_tab`, only set the pending signal when `self.is_open(kind, &id).is_none()` (an already-open pane keeps its live tab, which is what the MI variant's doc already says is intended). Add a unit test in state/mod.rs: open app-1, call `open_app_on_tab(app-1, "credentials")`, assert `pending_app_tab` is `None`.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is real. navigation.rs:108-111 and :117-122 set `pending_app_tab`/`pending_enterprise_tab` unconditionally before `open_item`; open_items.rs:70-74 dedupes an already-open `(kind, entity_id)` by re-titling + `focus_item` and returns without a remount; the workspace mounts panes via keyed `<For>` (open_items_workspace.rs:138), so the pane's one-shot consumption at application_detail_pane.rs:80-86 and enterprise_application_detail_pane/mod.rs:188-193 never runs for an already-open item. The only other reset is the tenant switch (state/mod.rs:264-265). The MI variant (navigation.rs:129-136) is indeed immune because it writes `last_mi_tab`. Callers where re-opening an already-open item is routine exist (audit_view/row.rs:179-182, credentials_dashboard.rs:114, mailboxes.rs:73-76). The existing GUI test (tests/gui/security_findings.rs:566-585) only asserts the signal is set, never consumed. Proposal is minimal and consistent with the MI doc's stated intent.

findings.title: `/` shortcut targets the first filter input in DOM order, so it no-ops once any earlier keep-alive pane has been visited
findings.rationale: `query_selector` returns the FIRST match in document order and the code then bails if that one element is hidden, rather than searching for the first laid-out match as the comment intends. Under keep-alive the App Registrations pane (placeholder "Filter App Registrations…") precedes Enterprise Apps, Managed Identities and Security in the DOM, so after visiting App Registrations once, pressing `/` on any later view finds the hidden Apps input, sees `offset_parent() == None`, and does nothing. Also, two of the three selector alternates (`input.search-input__field`, `.search-input input`) match nothing — the only `search-input*` class in src is `search-input__clear` — so only the placeholder heuristic is live. The GUI test (tests/gui/shortcuts.rs) only covers the negative case (no fire while typing), so this is untested.
findings.proposal: Use `query_selector_all` on `input[placeholder^='Filter']` and pick the first element whose `offset_parent()` is `Some`; drop the two dead selector alternates (or give `SearchInput` a real `search-input__field` class and match that). Add a GUI test that mounts two filter inputs with the first inside `display:none` and asserts `/` focuses the second.
findings.verifier_notes: use_shortcuts.rs:53-70 does `query_selector` (first match in document order) then bails when that single element has no offset parent — the comment's 'first filter input that is actually laid out' is not what the code does. keep_alive (util.rs:45-47) hides inactive panes with `display:none` and mounts them in declaration order (lib.rs:260-274: Home, Apps, EnterpriseApps, ManagedIdentities, Security…). Apps' input has placeholder 'Filter App Registrations by name or appId…' (application_list.rs:304), so after one visit to Apps, `/` on any later view finds the hidden Apps input and returns false. The two dead selector alternates are confirmed: SearchInput wraps Thaw `Input` (search_input.rs:21), which renders `.thaw-input__input` (thaw-0.5.0-beta src/input/mod.rs:182), and the only `search-input*` class in src is `search-input__clear`. The Global Search input's placeholder starts with 'Search' (global_search.rs:212) so it does not collide. tests/gui/shortcuts.rs has no positive `/` test (only the no-fire-while-typing case). Proposal (query_selector_all + first laid-out) is the right fix.

findings.title: `CommandState::run` (inline-error path, 24 call sites) never offers the dead-session Re-authenticate recovery
findings.rationale: `run` was taught to raise the consent toast because 'the inline message can never resolve' a missing consent — but a dead session (`refresh_missing` / `not_signed_in`) is exactly as unresolvable inline, and the sink's own doc says inline-affordance surfaces must call `report_if_session_dead` first. Every form modal / tab mutation using `cmd.run(...)` (24 sites) on an expired session shows only the raw backend message in red with no Re-authenticate action; the operator's only route is to find the topbar Refresh-token button.
findings.proposal: In `run`'s `on_err`, call `session.report_if_session_dead(&e)` before `report_consent_required` (keep setting the inline `error` text as well), mirroring `report_command_error_for`'s ordering. Add a host unit test: `run` with an op returning `refresh_missing` pushes a toast whose `action_label == Some("Re-authenticate")`.
findings.verifier_notes: use_command.rs:85-105: `run`'s on_err calls only `report_consent_required` then sets `error`; `run_toast_err` (:121-131) routes through `report_command_error_for`, which at errors.rs:167-175 tries `report_if_session_dead` first. The sink's own doc (errors.rs:54-57) says surfaces with their own inline affordance must call `report_if_session_dead` first. Outside dr.rs (6 sites) and bulk_action_bar.rs, no `cmd.run(` caller (23 sites in src) reports a dead session, so form modals show a raw `refresh_missing`/`not_signed_in` message with no Re-authenticate action. AGENTS.md's 'a dead session forces re-auth in place' rule and the sink doc both support the proposal; the existing host tests (errors.rs:188-224) give the pattern for the requested unit test.

findings.title: Sign-in recovery hints point at 'Settings → Tenant connection', which the file itself says is unreachable before sign-in
findings.rationale: These two AADSTS hints are shown ON the sign-in card, where Settings cannot be reached; the module doc says so explicitly, and the card already renders the correct escape hatch (`Signing in to {tenant} · Change`). An operator who follows the hint looks for a Settings page that does not exist yet. The `recovery_hint` tests assert the text contains 'tenant doesn't resolve' but not the destination.
findings.proposal: Reword the 90002/900023 and 700016/700054 hints to point at the card's own affordance ('select Change above to correct the tenant/client ID'), and extend `an_aadsts_code_beats_the_generic_code_hint` to assert the hint does not mention Settings. Consider passing a `where_to_fix: &'static str` into `recovery_hint` so the same table can serve Settings → Tenant connection post-sign-in.
findings.verifier_notes: sign_in.rs:190-198 hints point at 'Settings → Tenant connection'; the same file's `on_reconfigure` doc (sign_in.rs:21-24) and lib.rs:205-212 say that surface is unreachable before sign-in, and the card renders the real escape hatch ('Signing in to {tenant} · Change', sign_in.rs:69-82) which reopens the 'Configure your tenant' form (config_screen.rs:42) holding both IDs. `recovery_hint`/`aadsts_hint` have no other callers, so the hints only ever render on the sign-in card. The nearby comment (sign_in.rs:187-189, 'the ids are editable there') is a deliberate choice built on a wrong premise, not a sound rationale. Test at sign_in.rs:270-274 asserts only 'tenant doesn't resolve'. Severity downgraded to low: the correct affordance and raw AADSTS code are on the same card, so this is a misleading sentence in a failure path, not a blocked recovery.

findings.title: Toast stack neither dedupes identical recovery toasts nor protects sticky ones from the drop-oldest cap
findings.rationale: A dead session fails every in-flight command at once (dr.rs alone has six `report_if_session_dead` call sites; the bulk bar and every `run_toast_err` route here too), so the stack fills with N identical 'Your session has expired' toasts. Worse, `drain(0..overflow)` is blind to stickiness: the sixth error evicts the first sticky Re-authenticate toast while transient 5-second successes survive. ToastHost's own rule ('errors with a retry action are sticky') is undone by the cap.
findings.proposal: In `push_toast`: (1) if a toast with the same `kind`, `message` and `action_label` is already present, return its id instead of pushing; (2) when over cap, evict non-sticky toasts (no action) first, oldest-first, and only then sticky ones. Add two host tests next to the existing toast tests.
findings.verifier_notes: toasts.rs:9-35: no dedupe, and `drain(0..overflow)` evicts by position regardless of `action`, while ToastHost (toast.rs:129-131) makes 'Error + action' sticky — so the cap can indeed evict a sticky Re-authenticate/Grant-consent toast while auto-dismissing successes survive. `report_if_session_dead` (errors.rs:58-70) pushes a fresh toast per call with no guard; grep confirms no dedupe anywhere and no MAX_TOASTS test. The burst scenario is overstated: list/dashboard resources fail into `DetailLoadError` (not toasts), the bulk bar stops on the first re-auth-fatal code, and the six dr.rs sites are separate handlers — so N identical toasts needs N operator actions, which is plausible but not automatic. Downgraded to low; proposal (dedupe on kind+message+label, evict non-sticky first) is sound and small.

findings.title: List refetch after a mutation remounts the whole `LoadedApps` subtree (Suspense), losing scroll position
findings.rationale: The rationale ('the old offset pointed into a different list') is right for a search/facet change but wrong for the other trigger the comment lists — a refetch. After any mutation that bumps `apps_reload` / `enterprise_apps_reload` (delete, remove-expired, add owner from the pane, 'Fix' from a finding), the list resource yields a new `Arc<Vec>`, `items` changes, and the operator triaging row 3,800 of a 10k list is thrown back to row 0. This is the core 'work down a long list' workflow and the one place the frontend loses scroll state.
findings.proposal: Either (a) switch the list body to `<Transition>` and feed `LoadedApps` a signal of rows so the component instance survives a refetch, then clamp `scroll_top` on an `items` change instead of snapping; or (b) lift the scroller offset out of `VirtualList` into an optional `scroll_top: RwSignal<f64>` prop owned by the view (or `tenant_ui`) and restore it on mount. Also amend the virtual_list.rs:132 comment: 'refetch' does not reach that effect today.
findings.verifier_notes: The snap-to-top effect at virtual_list.rs:132-144 exists as quoted, but it is not the mechanism that loses scroll on a refetch. application_list.rs:315-357 renders the loaded body via `<Suspense>` + `Suspend::new(async move { apps.await … <LoadedApps …/> })`, and the comment at :317-320 says it re-runs on every refetch (tenant switch / reload bump). A bump of `apps_reload` (tracked at :228) therefore shows the skeleton fallback and re-creates `LoadedApps` — a new `use_filtered_list`, a new `VirtualList` with fresh `scroll_top = 0` and a new scroller element — so the effect's `prev.is_some()` guard never even fires for that case. The user-visible symptom (scroll lost after a list-mutating action) is real, but the proposed `reset_key` prop would not fix it: the component is gone. The same shape applies to enterprise_application_list.rs. Note also that `shown` is a `Memo<Arc<Vec<T>>>` (use_filtered_list.rs:73), so a same-content refetch would not retrigger the effect anyway.

findings.title: ~75 lines of dead CSS (command palette, owner list, MI scope panel, kbd chip, DR secret value, others) match nothing in src
findings.rationale: Global search replaced the command palette (global_search.rs owns Cmd/Ctrl-K), the enterprise owners tab no longer renders `.owner-list`, the MI pane uses `.detail-section`, the SSO wizard renders `.sso-claims` without rows, and dr.rs never renders individual secret values (only a count + 'Save the report'). None of these class names appear anywhere in Rust source or tests. Dead selectors are cheap at runtime but each is a trap for the next reader ('who uses this?') and the file is already 4,438 lines with no ownership signal.
findings.proposal: Delete the listed rules except `.dr-view__secrets` and `.dr-view__secret-name` (live at dr.rs:529/532). Add a host-side test extracting `.class` selectors from styles.css and asserting each appears in src/ literally or as a `{base}--` prefix of a `format!` modifier, with an allowlist for `thaw-*`.
findings.verifier_notes: Most of the list checks out with zero hits in src/ and tests/: `.cmd-palette*` (styles.css:2124-2171), `.mi-grant` (:1461), `.mi-scope-panel` (:1465), `.owner-list` (:1524/1532), `.dash-links`/`.dash-link` (:1822-1840), `.checkbox-list` (:2059), `.centered-pad` (:2361), `.ui-kbd` (:3122), `.sso-claims__row` (:3451, :3616; only `.sso-claims` is rendered at sso_wizard_dialog.rs:300), `.dr-view__secret-value` (:4206). But two of the cited selectors are live: `.dr-view__secrets` and `.dr-view__secret-name` are rendered at dr.rs:529 and :532, so 'dr.rs never renders individual secret values' is only true of the value span. The proposed coverage test is feasible but must allow `format!("…--{tone}")` modifiers (home_dashboard.rs:604, security_view.rs:271) and Thaw classes.

findings.title: Shortcut sheet <kbd> uses an undefined `--surface-alt` token (renders transparent) while the designed `.ui-kbd` rule sits unused
findings.rationale: `var(--surface-alt)` with no fallback and no definition makes `background` invalid-at-computed-value → `transparent`, so the key chips in the `?` sheet have a border and no fill in both themes. Meanwhile `.ui-kbd` is the finished key-chip style with the correct token and is referenced by no component.
findings.proposal: Give the `<kbd>` in shortcuts_help.rs `class="ui-kbd"` and delete the ad-hoc `.shortcuts__keys kbd` rule (or change it to `var(--bg-subtle)`). Also define or drop the other two undefined tokens used with fallbacks (`--surface-hover` at 1595, `--border-subtle` at 325) so the token set is closed.
findings.verifier_notes: styles.css:4281 uses `var(--surface-alt)` with no fallback; grep shows no `--surface-alt:` definition anywhere (only `--bg-subtle`, `--surface`, `--surface-raised` at :12-14 and :115-117), so the declaration is invalid at computed-value time and the `<kbd>` renders with a border and transparent fill. `.ui-kbd` (:3122-3134) is the finished chip with `var(--bg-subtle)` and has zero references in src/ or tests/. shortcuts_help.rs:27 renders a bare `<kbd>`. `--surface-hover` (:1595) and `--border-subtle` (:325) are undefined but carry fallbacks, so they render correctly; closing the token set is a nice-to-have. Proposal is a one-line class change plus a rule deletion.

findings.title: Two 'is the user typing?' predicates disagree: `?`/`/` are dead while a row checkbox has focus
findings.rationale: The grid hook correctly treats a bulk-select checkbox as not-a-text-field ('arrowing off it is exactly what a keyboard user expects'), but the window-level twin treats every `<input>` as typing. After Space-toggling a row checkbox, `?` (help) and `/` (focus filter) silently do nothing. The module comment forbids importing across the two hooks, but a shared leaf helper in `hooks/mod.rs` satisfies that boundary and removes the drift.
findings.proposal: Move `in_text_field` to `hooks/mod.rs` as `pub(crate) fn is_text_entry(ev)` and use it from both hooks; extend tests/gui/shortcuts.rs with a checkbox probe asserting `?` still opens the sheet.
findings.verifier_notes: use_shortcuts.rs:34-45 treats every `<input>` as typing; use_grid_keynav.rs:100-114 exempts checkbox/radio/button/submit/reset and its own doc (:96-99) forbids the surface hook from importing the window-level module — but says nothing against a shared leaf helper, and `hooks/mod.rs` already exists as that home. 19 `type="checkbox"` inputs exist in src (bulk-select rows), so after Space-toggling one, `?` and `/` no-op. No GUI test covers the checkbox case (tests/gui/shortcuts.rs uses a text probe only). Proposal is consistent with the documented boundary.

findings.title: ModalShell hardcodes one `id="modal-shell-title"`; stacked modals get duplicate ids and both close on one Escape
findings.rationale: UpdateSplash, ReleaseNotesDialog, ShortcutsHelp and every form modal share ModalShell. Pressing `?` while any modal is open (focus on a modal button is not 'typing') stacks a second ModalShell: two elements with the same id, so `aria-labelledby` resolves to whichever the browser finds first, and the next Escape fires both `use_escape` listeners, closing the underlying dialog too.
findings.proposal: Mint a per-instance id (`StoredValue<u32>` from a static counter, or `format!("modal-title-{}", id)`), and either gate the bare `?` on `document.querySelector('[role=dialog]')` being absent or make `use_escape` only act for the topmost dialog (last `.modal-backdrop` in DOM).
findings.verifier_notes: modal_shell.rs:47-54 hardcodes `id="modal-shell-title"` / `aria-labelledby="modal-shell-title"`; 8 components mount ModalShell (grep `<ModalShell`), including ShortcutsHelp (shortcuts_help.rs:15) which is always mounted in the shell (shell.rs:524). use_shortcuts.rs:163-166 toggles `show_help` on `?` with no dialog gate, and `is_typing` returns false for a focused button, so `?` from inside any open modal stacks a second ModalShell with a duplicate id. use_escape.rs:18-23 registers an independent window listener per dialog with no topmost check, so one Escape runs both `on_close`s. Other dialogs mint their own ids (scope_wizard.rs:758, add_owner.rs:187, …) so the duplicate-id half is ModalShell-only; the double-Escape half applies to any two open dialogs.

findings.title: ExportMenu (and the account menu) claim `role="menu"` without the menu keyboard contract

                <div class="export-menu__panel" role="menu">

                        view! {

(no on:keydown, no focus() on open; shell.rs:~330 `.shell__account-menu` role="menu" is the same shape)

Neither menu moves focus in or handles arrows; only Escape (via `use_escape`) is implemented. The TabBar in this same slice shows the team knows the pattern; these two menus were built as plain disclosures for a documented WebView2 reason but kept the menu roles.
findings.proposal: Either drop `role=menu/menuitem` and keep `aria-expanded` on the trigger (disclosure pattern — semantically honest for what is rendered), or add a small `use_menu_keynav(panel_ref, open)` hook: focus first item on open, Arrow/Home/End roving, and restore focus to the trigger on close (reuse `use_focus_return`).

The module doc (export_menu.rs:5-10) documents the plain-DOM disclosure as a deliberate WebView2 workaround for the *overlay*, not for dropping the menu keyboard contract; shell.rs:470-473 shows the roles were kept intentionally for AT visibility, which plain `<button>`s in a disclosure also provide. No GUI test queries `menuitem`/`role=menu`, so either proposal is feasible without test churn.

findings.title: `use_debounced` leaks one `Closure::once_into_js` per cancelled timer (every keystroke that resets the debounce)
findings.rationale: wasm-bindgen's `Closure::once_into_js` frees the Rust closure only when JS invokes it; a closure whose timer is cleared before firing is leaked for the life of the page. With a 300 ms debounce on every list filter, a fast typist cancels the pending timer on nearly every keystroke, leaking a boxed closure plus the captured `String` each time. Small per event, unbounded over a long session in a keep-alive app that never unmounts its lists. (`CopyIconButton` and `pairing.rs` also use `once_into_js`, but their timers always fire.)
findings.proposal: Keep a `StoredValue<Option<Closure<dyn FnMut()>>, LocalStorage>` alongside the handle and drop it in `clear_pending` (dropping a `Closure` invalidates the JS side), or create one persistent `Closure` per hook instance that reads the latest value from `source.get_untracked()` when it fires.
findings.verifier_notes: use_debounced.rs:16-22 clears the pending timeout and :35-38 creates each callback with `Closure::once_into_js`. wasm-bindgen's own doc (closure.rs:685-688) states: 'If the JavaScript function is never called then the FnOnce and everything it closes over will leak.' With `LIST_FILTER_DEBOUNCE_MS = 300` (constants.rs:26) and keep-alive lists, every keystroke inside the window cancels and leaks one boxed closure + the captured `String`. Minor correction to the parenthetical: toast.rs also clears timers on manual dismiss (:123, :150) and so leaks the same way, as can global_search.rs:222 / permission_tester_view.rs:310; the debounce is simply the high-frequency case. Proposal (own the `Closure` in a `StoredValue` and drop it on cancel, or one persistent closure per hook) is correct.

findings.title: Shell's refresh-token fallback duplicates `Session::spawn_reauth` and the two have already drifted (readiness reload)
findings.rationale: Same IPC call, same two toast strings, but the shell path bumps `readiness_reload` after a successful re-auth and the toast-action path (`report_if_session_dead` → `spawn_reauth`) does not — so re-authenticating from the recovery toast leaves a mounted Access Readiness checklist stale, while the topbar button refreshes it. A new post-re-auth side effect will have to be remembered in two places.
findings.proposal: Give `spawn_reauth` the `bump_readiness_reload()` on success and an optional `on_done: impl FnOnce(bool)` (for the shell's `reauthing` flag), then have `on_refresh_token`'s fatal branch call `session.spawn_reauth(...)` instead of re-implementing it. One home for the re-auth round trip, as the AGENTS.md 'one definition per policy' rule asks.
findings.verifier_notes: shell.rs:126-142 and errors.rs:24-38 both call `bindings::auth::reauthenticate(&tenant)` and emit the identical success/failure strings, but only the shell path calls `session.bump_readiness_reload()` on success — so the toast-action route (`report_if_session_dead` → `spawn_reauth`) leaves a mounted Access Readiness checklist stale, while the topbar button refreshes it (state/mod.rs:306-309 documents the Refresh-token control as the only re-check trigger). The `spawn_reauth` doc (errors.rs:22-23) even names the Refresh button's fallback as a caller, which it is not. Proposal (add the bump to `spawn_reauth`, optional `on_done` for the `reauthing` flag, and have the shell delegate) matches the 'one definition per policy' rule.

findings.title: Stale, redundant `#![allow(dead_code)]` / `unused_imports` in icon.rs, toast.rs and ui/mod.rs; two `IconName` variants (`More`, `ExternalLink`) are unused
findings.rationale: toast.rs's justification ('not every kind/helper has a call site yet') is no longer true — Info is used by the eviction and update toasts, Success/Error everywhere — so the allow now only masks future rot. ui/mod.rs's `unused_imports` allow is unnecessary today. icon.rs's allow hides two dead variants (`More`, `ExternalLink`); an icon catalog is a reasonable place to keep spares, but that should be an explicit per-variant `#[allow(dead_code)]` with a comment, not a file-wide blanket that also hides a dead helper fn.
findings.proposal: Delete the three module-level allows as dead weight and the toast.rs justification comment (its premise is no longer true). Remove `IconName::More` and `IconName::ExternalLink` (or annotate them as intentional spares) by hand — the lint cannot prove this because the enum is public API through `pub mod components`.
findings.verifier_notes: The allows exist as quoted (icon.rs:6, toast.rs:1-3, ui/mod.rs:5) and `IconName::More` / `IconName::ExternalLink` have zero uses outside icon.rs. But the premise that the allows 'hide' them is wrong: `components/mod.rs` declares `pub mod icon`, `pub mod toast`, `pub mod ui`, and lib.rs:20 makes `components` pub, so these are exported API of a lib crate and `dead_code` never fires on them regardless of the allow — removing the allows would not make `just web-clippy` (justfile:274, `-D warnings`) flag the two variants. There is also no dead helper fn in icon.rs: `paths` (:79) is called by `Icon` (:60). Every `pub use` in ui/mod.rs has ≥6 external uses, so that allow is redundant rather than harmful.

findings.title: Crate-wide `#![allow(private_interfaces)]` could be narrowed to the test-mountable modules
findings.rationale: The only consumers of the `pub` modules are the `tests/gui_*.rs` shards (25 `views::` imports), compiled with `--features test-support`; `main.rs` calls `run()` only and `demo` is in-crate. The shipped Trunk bundle therefore exports a public API nobody uses, and the crate-wide allow also silences the lint for any future accidental leak of a private type through a genuinely public item.
findings.proposal: If anything, move the allow from the crate root onto the `pub mod views;` / `pub mod components;` items (the only modules that need it) and leave the module visibility alone; skip the `#[cfg(feature = "test-support")]` module duplication. Correct the evidence: `Route`/`Destination` are both private and are not an instance of the lint.
findings.verifier_notes: lib.rs:13 is a crate-wide `#![allow(private_interfaces)]` and lib.rs:19-25 exposes the modules `pub`, with the rationale written out at lib.rs:7-12 — a deliberate, documented decision the finding acknowledges but does not defeat: the crate is a lib consumed only by main.rs (`run()`), the gui shards behind `test-support` (Cargo.toml:77) and the in-crate `demo`, so there is no 'genuinely public item' for a future leak to reach, and pub-but-unused items in a wasm bin bundle cost nothing at runtime (linker/wasm-opt DCE). The cited 'real instance' is wrong: global_search.rs:408 `enum Route` is a field of the private `struct Destination` (:426), not a private type in a public signature. The cfg-doubled module tree is churn for lint hygiene only.

findings.title: `APPS_HARD_CAP` hand-mirrors the backend's `APPS_MAX` while the SP lists already read their cap from `get_directory_index_status`
findings.rationale: web-rs is outside the root workspace and cannot depend on src-tauri, so nothing pins the two 10_000s together; a backend change to `APPS_MAX` would silently make the App Registrations cap notice fire at the wrong count (or never). The Enterprise/MI lists already solved this by reading `sp_index_cap` from `get_directory_index_status`. (The comment's path is also stale: `commands/applications/mod.rs`.)
findings.proposal: Add `app_index_cap: usize` to the backend `DirectoryIndexStatus` (commands/applications/mod.rs:88) and its bindings mirror (bindings/applications.rs:24), populate it from `APPS_MAX`, and have application_list.rs:448/:576 read it like `IndexCapNotice` does; or, cheaper, move the single `10_000` into azapptoolkit-dto (shared by both trees) and reference it from both `APPS_MAX` and the frontend. Fix the stale `commands/applications.rs` path either way.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise holds: constants.rs:20-22 hand-mirrors `APPS_MAX` (src-tauri commands/applications/mod.rs:75), nothing pins the two (no hit for `APPS_HARD_CAP`/`10_000` under src-tauri/tests or web-rs/tests), the comment path `commands/applications.rs` is stale, and the SP side already solved it via `sp_index_cap` (backend mod.rs:88-95: 'so the notice can name the number without the frontend keeping its own copy in sync'; index_cap_notice.rs:245-266). The proposal's location is wrong: `DirectoryIndexStatus` is not in azapptoolkit-dto — it is a `serde::Serialize` struct in the backend (applications/mod.rs:86-95) mirrored by a `Deserialize` twin in web-rs bindings/applications.rs:22-27. Also `app_index_truncated` would require the status command to read the apps list cache, not just the SP index.

findings.title: Saved views snapshot only facet + search; the drawer's date range is neither saved nor cleared on apply
findings.rationale: The drawer presents saved views and the created-on range as one filter set, but 'Save view' captures only two of the three inputs. A view like 'Disabled, created this quarter' cannot be saved, and applying any saved view leaves whatever date range is currently set still active — the `FilterToggle` badge keeps counting it — so the applied view shows fewer rows than when it was saved with no visible reason.
findings.proposal: Extend `SavedView` with `#[serde(default)] after: Option<NaiveDate>, before: Option<NaiveDate>` (backward-compatible with existing localStorage payloads), thread the two range signals from `ListScaffold` into `SavedViews`, write them on save and set them (including to `None`) on apply.
findings.verifier_notes: saved_views.rs:12-16 `SavedView { name, facet, search }` and :58-62 snapshot only those two signals; `created_after`/`created_before` are view-local `RwSignal<Option<NaiveDate>>` (application_list.rs:185-186, enterprise_application_list.rs:54-55) passed to `DateRangeFilter` in the scaffold's `drawer` slot (application_list.rs:309-311) and counted in the FilterToggle badge (:201-202) — the same drawer that hosts `SavedViews` (list_scaffold.rs:42-46). So a saved view cannot capture a date range and applying one leaves the current range active. Proposal (`#[serde(default)]` optional dates threaded from `ListScaffold`, set including to `None` on apply) is backward-compatible with stored payloads and feasible; the MI list has no date range and would pass nothing.

findings.title: Restored working set is not clamped to `MAX_OPEN_ITEMS`
findings.rationale: The cap is an invariant of the in-memory set, but the snapshot is trusted as-is. A snapshot written by a build with a larger cap (or a hand-edited/corrupted-but-valid JSON) restores >8 chips, and because `open_item` evicts exactly one per open, the dock stays over cap indefinitely. Cheap to close and keeps the 'restore cannot violate the model' property the module otherwise enforces.
findings.proposal: After decoding: dedupe by `(kind, entity_id)` keeping the higher `focused_at`, then while `len() > MAX_OPEN_ITEMS` remove the entry with the smallest `focused_at` (preserving Vec/dock order rather than sorting), then `set`. Add a test that a 9-item snapshot restores 8 and drops the least recently focused.
findings.verifier_notes: open_items.rs:221-241 decodes the snapshot and `set`s it with no length clamp or `(kind, entity_id)` dedupe; the cap is enforced only in `open_item` (:76-96) and evicts exactly one per push, so a >8 snapshot stays over cap. The existing tests (state/mod.rs:523-568 cap, :571-627 restore) never feed an oversized snapshot. One wrinkle in the proposal: `Vec` order is the dock order that `step_open_item` walks (use_shortcuts.rs:75-77 'the dock's own (open order), not focus recency'), so sorting by `focused_at` would reorder the dock.

findings.title: SSO tab renders an unreadable claims policy as an empty editor; Save then detaches the real policy
findings.rationale: `SsoConfigDto.claims_policy` is `None` both when no policy is assigned AND when the read failed (the DTO doc at crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sso.rs:297-299 says so). Because `list_assigned_claims_mapping_policies` requires `policy_write_token()`, every operator who has not yet consented `Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration` sees an EMPTY "Attributes & claims" editor for an app that has a custom policy. Clicking "Save claims" (e.g. to add one claim) triggers the consent flow, then `set_claims_mapping` detaches every existing policy and recreates one from the empty/partial editor — silently deleting the app's configured claims. Nothing in the UI warns that the current state was never loaded.
findings.proposal: Add a discriminator to `SsoConfigDto` (e.g. `claims_policy_unavailable: bool` or `claims_read_error: Option<UiError>`) set in `get_sso_config`'s `Err` arm. In `SsoEditor`, when it is set: render a `Callout tone="warn"` ("Couldn't read the current claims policy — grant consent to load it before editing") with a "Load claims" button that calls `request_scope_consent(.., "policy_write")` and bumps `reload`, and disable "Save claims" until a successful read. Add a GUI test: mock `get_sso_config` with the flag set and assert Save is disabled and no `set_claims_mapping` call happens. Expected effect: no path from an unread policy to a detach.
findings.verifier_notes: All evidence real. sso/mod.rs:466-468 joins get_service_principal_sso_fields with list_assigned_claims_mapping_policies; policies.rs:51 shows the READ takes policy_write_token(); mod.rs:510-513 collapses Err into (None, None); dto/sso.rs:297-299 documents that None means either 'no policy' or 'read skipped'. sso_tab.rs:543 seeds ClaimsEditorState from unwrap_or_default() (include_basic=true, empty schema) with no discriminator. set_claims_mapping (mod.rs:1643-1661) detaches every assigned policy before create, and an empty policy yields None (no replacement). The consent path makes it worse: grant_consent (sso_tab.rs:675-685) does NOT bump reload, so even after consent the editor still shows the never-loaded state and the 'Save again' toast walks the operator straight into the detach. No AGENTS.md/architecture rationale covers the data-loss path; auth-and-consent.md only justifies not prompting on read. Proposal is consistent with repo conventions (Callout primitive, request_scope_consent 'policy_write' already used at sso_tab.rs:682).
findings.recheck_notes: Failing path is reachable end to end in the shipped build, not just tests/demo. (1) apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/state.rs:449-481: `graph_for` ALWAYS installs a `policy_write_token` ScopedTokenAdapter, so `policy_write_token()` (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client.rs:317) never returns the `Forbidden("... not configured")` short-circuit; the read in crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/policies.rs:51 goes to `bearer()` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/token_adapter.rs:70) → `access_token_inner` silent refresh, which for an un-consented `Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration` returns `AuthError::ConsentRequired` without any interactive prompt (crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:540-546; per AGENTS.md this scope is never in the sign-in bundle, so first-time operators always hit it). (2) apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sso/mod.rs:466-468 and 498-513: `get_sso_config` swallows that Err (and ANY other error — transient 5xx, 403 from a missing directory role) into `(None, None)`; `SsoConfigDto` has no discriminator (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sso.rs:297-302). (3) apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/enterprise_application_detail_pane/sso_tab.rs:543 seeds `ClaimsEditorState::from_dto(&ClaimsPolicyDto::default())` — an empty editor with `include_basic_claim_set=true`, rendered with no warning; `Save claims` (sso_tab.rs:797-803) is only disabled while `cmd.busy`. (4) First Save → `set_claims_mapping` (sso/mod.rs:1636-1639) returns `consent_required`; the `grant_consent` handler (sso_tab.rs:675-685) clears `needs_consent`, toasts 'Save again to apply your claims' and deliberately does NOT bump `reload`, so the editor keeps the never-loaded state. (5) Second Save → `ensure_policy_write_token` OK → `list_assigned_claims_mapping_policies` now succeeds → every assignment is removed (sso/mod.rs:1643-1655) → `policy.is_empty()` (dto/sso.rs:150-155) is true for the untouched editor so NO replacement is created (or a partial one containing only the operator's added rows). Result: the app's live custom claims are silently detached. Mitigating detail (does not lower severity): only the SP assignment is removed, the claimsMappingPolicy object itself survives in `/policies/claimsMappingPolicies`, so an admin can re-attach it out of band — but nothing in the app tells them it happened, and SAML sign-in for that app changes/breaks immediately. No repo_invariants test or GUI test pins this: the only SSO GUI test (apps/desktop/web-rs/tests/gui/sso_rollover.rs) uses a fixture with `claims_policy: None` and never exercises `set_claims_mapping`. Proposal is sound; would add: also bump `reload` after successful consent so the editor re-seeds from the real policy.

findings.title: "Rotate and activate immediately" reveals the show-once certificate, then the reload it triggers tears the reveal down
findings.rationale: Bumping the outer `reload` refetches `config`, the Suspense drops the current `SsoEditor`, and a fresh one is built with `rotated_cert = None` — so the `<pre class="secret-reveal">` at lines 766-774 is gone before the operator can copy it. This is the big-bang path where sign-in is already broken until the app owner installs the new certificate, and the base64 is exactly what they need. The staged path does not have this bug because `SigningCertRolloverPanel` bumps its own `reload` and `staged_pem` lives outside that Suspense. No GUI test covers the rotate reveal (grep for "Rotate and activate" in tests finds nothing).
findings.proposal: Lift `rotated_cert` (and `cert_subject`) to `SsoContent` and pass them into `SsoEditor`, or stop bumping the outer `reload` on rotate and instead bump a rollover-panel reload exposed via a shared `RwSignal<u32>` prop (the rotation only changes SP key state, which the rollover panel re-reads). Render the reveal through the shared `CopyBlock` (see the separate finding). Add a `sso_rollover.rs` GUI test: mock `rotate_saml_signing_certificate` with `base64: Some(..)`, click the button, assert `pre.secret-reveal` still contains it after the mocked reload resolves.
findings.verifier_notes: Mechanism verified: rotate_cert (sso_tab.rs:618-624) sets rotated_cert then bumps the OUTER reload; SsoContent's config LocalResource tracks reload (sso_tab.rs:19) and its Suspend re-renders <SsoEditor cfg=cfg reload=reload/> (line 45), and rotated_cert is RwSignal::new(None) inside SsoEditor (line 541) — so the <pre class="secret-reveal"> at 766-774 is gone once the refetch resolves. The staged path is immune because staged_pem lives in SigningCertRolloverPanel with its own reload (lines 66,70). tests/gui/certificate_reveal.rs:53-59 documents this exact teardown class for the credentials tab, so the repo treats it as a real bug pattern. No GUI test covers rotate (grep confirms). Severity downgraded from high to medium: unlike a private key, the SAML public signing certificate is recoverable out of band from the federation metadata URL shown in SamlSummaryView (Entra publishes it; probe_federation_metadata even returns published_certs), so the loss is of the in-app convenience copy, not of an irrecoverable secret. Proposal (lift rotated_cert to SsoContent or stop bumping the outer reload) is sound.
