findings.evidence:
sso_tab.rs:759-765
                <Button
                    appearance=Signal::derive(|| ButtonAppearance::Secondary)
                    on_click=Box::new(rotate_cert)
                    disabled=Signal::derive(move || cmd.busy.get())
                >
                    "Rotate and activate immediately"

Contrast mod.rs:373-385 (delete SP: ConfirmDialog + typed DELETE for foreign SPs), access.rs:270-286, permissions.rs:315-332, app_roles.rs:453-464 — all stage a ConfirmDialog.

docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md:191-193: "because the superseded certificate *is* the rollback, retiring is what ends the ability to revert, so it stays an explicit action."

An operator who mis-clicks rotate breaks SSO for every user of that app; the frontend-workspace.md guidance reserves the un-confirmed treatment for reversible actions (Disable sign-in).

Keep Remove-expired one-click (dead weight, documented). Update the sso_rollover GUI tests to click through the dialog.
findings.verifier_notes: sso_tab.rs contains no ConfirmDialog (verified by reading the whole file); rotate (759-765) and retire (473-479) fire directly via cmd.run_toast_err. Siblings do stage ConfirmDialog: mod.rs:373-385 (delete SP, typed DELETE for foreign), access.rs (remove/assign/add-to-group), owners.rs. Backend doc calls rotate a big-bang that stops sign-in for static-cert apps (also the UI's own Callout at 753-755). One correction: the cited frontend-workspace.md:98-104 passage is about button--danger STYLING ('Reversible actions stay un-reddened'), not about confirmation dialogs, and auth-and-consent.md:191-193 'stays an explicit action' means a dedicated button rather than automatic removal — neither doc mandates a confirm. The finding stands on the in-pane inconsistency and outage risk. Proposal is feasible; note the existing GUI test staging_a_certificate_does_not_activate_it clicks '.cert-rollover button' (first = Stage), which the change would not disturb.

findings.title: Certificate reveals are a bare <pre> with no copy/save; the existing CopyBlock is private and hand-rolls the clipboard call
findings.rationale: The staged/rotated public certificate is the artefact the app owner must receive, and the UI asks the operator to "upload this to the application" while offering no copy button, no label and no file save. `sso_summary::CopyBlock` is the codebase's primitive for exactly this (label + hint + pre + Copy) but is `fn` (private), and it duplicates the clipboard code `util::copy_text` claims to centralise. There are 12 `save_*_to_file` commands but none for a certificate, so an operator has to paste base64 into a file by hand to produce the `.cer` most SaaS admin consoles expect.
findings.proposal: Make `CopyBlock` `pub` and use it for both reveals in sso_tab.rs (label "New signing certificate (Base64)", hint about uploading). Route `CopyBlock`'s copy through `util::copy_text` (extend it to return the `JsFuture`/accept an on-done callback so the "Copied" state still works). Add a backend `save_certificate_to_file(base64, suggested_name)` command writing PEM (`[PEM BEGIN CERTIFICATE]`, 64-col wrapped) via the OS save dialog, exposed as a "Save as .cer" button beside Copy.
findings.verifier_notes: sso_tab.rs:395-406 and 766-774 render bare <pre class="secret-reveal"> with no copy affordance (the rotate one has no label/hint). sso_summary.rs:113-145: CopyBlock is a private `fn` and hand-rolls navigator.clipboard().write_text via spawn_local, duplicating util::copy_text (util.rs:76-85) whose doc claims to be the shared copier — though CopyBlock needs a completion callback for its 'Copied' state, which copy_text lacks, so extending copy_text is required as the proposal says. Minor correction to the evidence: there IS a certificate save command, save_generated_certificate_pfx (lib.rs:98, credentials_tab.rs:1000-1064 'Save .pfx…'), for app-registration generated certs; none exists for the SAML signing public cert. Proposal is reasonable and matches the one-primitive rule.

findings.title: Opening the SSO tab runs the SP→app→app-SSO Graph chain twice and reads the SP a third time
findings.rationale: `get_sso_config` is get_service_principal_sso_fields + list_assigned_claims_mapping_policies + find_application_by_app_id + get_application_sso_fields (3-4 serial Graph calls). `get_sso_summary` re-runs all of it just to wrap the same fields in `SamlSsoSummary`/`OidcSsoSummary`, whose extra fields (`saml_summary_urls`, `oidc_summary_urls`) are pure functions of tenant id + app id. The rollover panel then fetches the SP fields a third time. Every SSO tab open is therefore ~8 Graph requests for data the tab already holds, and the summary crosses IPC as an untagged `serde_json::Value` that the frontend re-deserialises and swallows on mismatch.
findings.proposal: Either (a) have `get_sso_config` return the summary (or the `SigningCertRolloverDto`) as fields of `SsoConfigDto`, so one command feeds the whole tab, or (b) build the summary client-side from `SsoConfigDto` + the static URL formulas (move `saml_summary_urls`/`oidc_summary_urls` into `azapptoolkit-dto` so both trees share them). Delete `get_sso_summary` (and its binding) or type it as `#[serde(tag = "protocol")] enum SsoSummary { Saml(..), Oidc(..) }`. Expected effect: ~2x fewer Graph calls per SSO tab open and no double parse.
findings.verifier_notes: sso/mod.rs:1738-1745: get_sso_summary calls get_sso_config again, then only wraps fields plus oidc_summary_urls/saml_summary_urls (pure functions of tenant/app id). get_sso_config = SP fields ∥ claims read, then find_application_by_app_id, then get_application_sso_fields (mod.rs:466-486). findings.title: Enterprise Credentials expiry badge truncates days ("0d left" for an expired credential) and is the fourth independent expiry helper
findings.rationale: `Duration::num_days()` truncates toward zero, so a credential that expired anywhere in the last 24h yields `days == 0`, misses the `< 0` arm and renders "0d left" — the exact misread the architecture doc says the backend was fixed to avoid. The enterprise pane's `cred_status`, the app-reg `credentials_tab::days_until`, `application_list.rs` and the two dashboards each carry their own copy of the thresholds and formatting, so the fix has to be made in five places and "Expiring Soon" can drift between boards (the auth doc's stated reason for reusing `EXPIRY_WARNING_DAYS`).
findings.proposal: Add one `util::days_until(end) -> Option<i64>` using `(end - now).num_seconds().div_euclid(86_400)` and one `components::ui::expiry_badge(days: Option<i64>)` that imports `azapptoolkit_core::audit::EXPIRY_WARNING_DAYS` (and a new `EXPIRY_CRITICAL_DAYS = 7` in core). Replace `cred_status`, `credentials_tab::{days_until,status_label,status_badge}`, the `application_list.rs` inline format and the two dashboards' `status_badge`. Add a unit test that an `end` 12h in the past renders "Expired".
findings.verifier_notes: mod.rs:65-77 cred_status uses chrono num_days() (truncates toward zero), so end in (-24h,0) gives days==0 -> misses the <0 arm -> renders '0d left' badge--danger. auth-and-consent.md:181-184 documents that the SSO cert path was fixed with div_euclid (sso/mod.rs:1538) precisely to avoid this. Sibling copies confirmed: credentials_tab.rs:30-61 (days_until num_days, WARN_DAYS/CRITICAL_DAYS), application_list.rs:159, credentials_dashboard.rs:20-21,136, sso_certificates_dashboard.rs:29-30,300; core has EXPIRY_WARNING_DAYS (audit/permissions.rs:19). The finding UNDERSTATES scope: core::audit::credentials.rs:24,40 also uses num_days() and credential_status maps 0 -> ExpiringSoon (credentials.rs:76-82), and types.rs:110-113 likewise, so the two dashboards that take days_to_expiry/status from the backend show '0d left' for a credential expired <24h ago as well. Corrected proposal: floor in core (summarize_credentials + ListCredentialStatus) with EXPIRY_CRITICAL_DAYS there, then one frontend badge helper consuming it.

findings.verifier_notes: True: COMMON_AZURE_ROLES (managed_identity_detail_pane.rs:479-503) has eight roles and the Select (577-584) offers only those, so custom/other built-in roles cannot be assigned here; two 'Grant access' labels exist (163-168 wizard vs 385-391 ARM consent). findings.title: No way to install an operator-supplied SAML signing certificate (PFX) — only self-signed minting
findings.evidence:
sso_tab.rs:385-394
                        <Field label="Certificate subject for a staged certificate (e.g. CN=Contoso)">
                            <Input value=subject />
                        </Field>
                        <Button ... on_click=Box::new(stage) ...>

bindings/sso.rs:160-176 — `stage_saml_signing_certificate(tenant, sp, subject, lifetime_days)` is the only staging path (self-signed via `addTokenSigningCertificate`).
util.rs:100-115 `cert_payload_from_bytes` + views/dialogs/upload_certificate_dialog.rs exist for app-registration public-key uploads.
findings.rationale: Regulated tenants often require the SAML signing certificate to come from an internal CA (portal: "Import certificate" with a PFX + password on the SAML signing certificate blade). Graph supports it by PATCHing the SP's `keyCredentials` (Sign + Verify halves sharing a `customKeyIdentifier`) together with a `passwordCredentials` entry holding the PFX password, after which the existing stage → probe → activate flow applies unchanged. The rollover panel is the natural home and already dedupes the two halves.
findings.proposal: Add an `import_saml_signing_certificate(tenant, sp, pfx_base64, password)` command: parse the PFX with the already-pinned `p12-keystore`, derive the SHA-1 thumbprint via `core::thumbprint::canonical`, PATCH `keyCredentials` (Sign/AsymmetricX509Cert + Verify) and `passwordCredentials` (keyId of the Sign half), leave `preferredTokenSigningKeyThumbprint` untouched so it lands as Staged. Frontend: an "Import certificate (.pfx)" button in the rollover panel reusing the file-picker pattern from `UploadCertificateDialog`; never log or persist the password (zeroize). Cover with a repo_invariants trust test like the existing SAML cert lifetime bound.
findings.verifier_notes: Feature request, correctly scoped. Verified: sso_tab.rs:385-394 and bindings/sso.rs stage_saml_signing_certificate is the only staging path (self-signed addTokenSigningCertificate); util.rs:100-115 cert_payload_from_bytes and upload_certificate_dialog.rs exist for app-reg public-key uploads; p12-keystore is already a src-tauri dependency (Cargo.toml:85); core::thumbprint::canonical exists (thumbprint.rs:47); repo_invariants/trust.rs has the federation-trust and redirect validation scans to extend. Graph's documented custom-signing-key flow (PATCH servicePrincipal keyCredentials Sign+Verify sharing customKeyIdentifier plus a passwordCredentials entry keyed to the Sign half) matches the proposal, and auth-and-consent.md:170-173 confirms the panel already dedupes the two halves. One nuance: 'lands as Staged' assumes the imported cert is newer than the active one (CertStatus::Staged requires newer-than-active per dto/sso.rs:308-312); an older-dated import would read as Superseded. Low: no defect, a capability gap for internal-CA tenants.

findings.title: Exchange scoping section toasts "Migrated" on a `partial` AAP report (gate ignores item status, `incomplete`, `unattempted`); the audit dialog gates correctly
findings.rationale: The doc says `AapMigrationReportView`'s "one job is that a `partial` status never reads as success" and that partial means "kept the legacy policy because a grant is still org-wide". A `partial` item, an `incomplete` (cancelled / dead-session) run, or a non-empty `unattempted` list all arrive with `failures` empty, so the Permissions-tab surface toasts success, fires `on_changed` (the caller reloads and rebuilds the section) and the report is never shown. The operator walks away believing the app is migrated while the policy is the only thing still confining it. The toast noun is also wrong: `items` are per-app, not per-policy.
findings.proposal: Add `pub fn is_clean(&self) -> bool` on `AapMigrationReport` (or a free fn next to `AapMigrationReportView`) = `!dry_run && failures.is_empty() && !incomplete && unattempted.is_empty() && !items.is_empty() && items.iter().all(|i| i.status == "migrated")`; use it in both `do_migrate` and `migrate_legacy_scope.rs` so the two surfaces cannot disagree. In the section, keep `mig_result` inline unless clean. Toast "Migrated N app(s) / removed M policy(ies)" using `items.len()` and `Σ removed_policies.len()`. Unit-test `is_clean` on a partial item, an incomplete run, and an unattempted tail.
findings.verifier_notes: exchange_scoping_section.rs:324-328 gates on `dry_run || !r.failures.is_empty()` only. The backend sets `status = "partial"` while pushing to `warnings`, not `failures` (src-tauri commands/exchange/aap_migration.rs:375 and :400 — the KEPT-policy fail-closed path), and `incomplete: cancelled` / `unattempted` at :143-144, so all three arrive with `failures` empty and the section toasts success and fires `on_changed`. The report view itself says 'partial must never read as success' (aap_migration_report.rs:20, tone at :27,:43). The audit dialog gates correctly on item status (migrate_legacy_scope.rs:81-84) but also ignores `incomplete`/`unattempted`, so the shared `is_clean` predicate in the proposal is the right fix for both. Toast noun is wrong: `AapMigrationItem` is per app (dto exchange.rs:174-196, `removed_policies` per item). No existing `is_clean`/`needs_attention` helper on the DTO (grep).
findings.recheck_notes: Reachable in the shipped build with no upstream guard. Backend apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/exchange/aap_migration.rs:364-400 sets `status = "partial"` inside a *successful* `Ok(AapMigrationItem)` (policy-remove error at :375, or `policies_safe_to_remove` false at :400 with the KEPT-the-legacy-policy warning pushed into `item.warnings`, not into `report.failures`); the loop at :113-125 only pushes to `failures` on `Err`. So a single-app run (`Some(&app_id)` from the section) can return `{dry_run:false, items:[partial], failures:[]}`. The section gate at apps/desktop/web-rs/src/components/exchange_scoping_section.rs:324 (`dry_run || !r.failures.is_empty()`) is then false, so :327 toasts "Migrated 1 policy(ies).", :328 fires `on_changed` (parent reload rebuilds the section), and `mig_result` — the ONLY thing that mounts `AapMigrationReportView` (:761) — is never set, so the KEPT/UNKNOWN warning is never shown. Second path: a cancel or dead session before the first iteration (:97-104) yields `items:[]`, `unattempted:[app]`, `incomplete:true`, `failures:[]` → toast "Migrated 0 policy(ies)." Third: no matching policy at all → `items:[]` → same 0-count success toast. The sibling dialog at views/dialogs/migrate_legacy_scope.rs:81-84 gates on `all(status == "migrated") && !items.is_empty()` (still ignores `incomplete`/`unattempted`, but for a single-app run those imply empty items so it is safe), and the report view at components/aap_migration_report.rs:27,43 treats any non-`migrated` status / `incomplete` / failures as attention-needed — so the two surfaces demonstrably disagree. No GUI test covers the section's migrate path (tests/gui/security_findings.rs:477-525 exercises only the audit dialog), and repo_invariants/{cancel,fanout}.rs pin the backend, not this frontend gate. DTO doc (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/exchange.rs:242-262) and docs/architecture/audit-findings-and-remediation.md:198 both state a partial run must never read as complete; this surface violates that on a security-posture mutation. Severity high stands: the operator is told the legacy policy is gone / the app is RBAC-scoped when the org-wide grant is still in place and the AAP is the only confinement, inviting manual cleanup of the very policy still doing the confining. Proposal is correct as written; the toast noun fix (`items` are per-app per exchange-scoping.md:78-80) is also accurate.

findings.title: ScopeWizard preseed uses `scope_kind_for` while `mechanism` uses `cart_mechanism`; a held Sites.* row on Office 365 SharePoint Online reaches a scoped `scope_mode` with `mechanism == None` and a silent no-op Grant button — reachable today via HeldPermissionsPanel, not latent
findings.evidence:
484-490 (preseed): if let Some(k) = scope_kind_for(Some(&sel.resource_app_id), &sel.permission_value) { ... scope_mode.set(default_mode(k)); } selected.set(vec![sel]); step.set(1);
392-404 cart_mechanism additionally requires `item.kind == PermissionKind::Application` (returns None for Delegated)
541-546 run_apply: let plan = if mode == ScopeMode::OrgWide { Plan::OrgWide } else { let Some(kind) = mechanism.get_untracked() else { return; }; ...
604: _ => return,
734-740 review_line matches scope_mode alone: ScopeMode::Managed | Existing => "Grant {perms}, scoped to the chosen mailbox group(s)..."
findings.rationale: `scope_mode` and `mechanism` are two independent signals that must agree, and the preseed path sets one from a predicate looser than the other's. A delegated `Mail.Read` preseed (or any future caller passing an unscopable row) leaves `scope_mode = Managed` with `mechanism = None`: step 2 shows the "can't be scoped together" hint but no org-wide callout, step 3's review claims the grant is scoped and the strip warning appears, and "Grant access" returns silently at the `else { return; }` with no error. Today's three callers (permissions_tab, enterprise permissions, MI pane) gate on scopable Application rows, so the bug is latent, but the wizard is the shared shell and has no defence.
findings.proposal: Introduce `let effective_mode = Signal::derive(move || if mechanism.get().is_none() { ScopeMode::OrgWide } else { scope_mode.get() })` and read it in `run_apply`, `review_line`, `review_targets`, `strip_warning`, `targets_label`, `consent_and_retry` and the radios; in the preseed effect use `cart_mechanism(&[sel.clone()])` instead of `scope_kind_for`. Replace the two silent `return`s (546, 604) with `error.set(Some("This selection can only be granted org-wide — go back and choose Org-wide."))`. Unit-test that a delegated preseed yields `None` and the derived mode is OrgWide.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: preseed at scope_wizard.rs:481-491 sets `scope_mode` only when `scope_kind_for` is Some and otherwise leaves the initial `ScopeMode::Managed` (:424, also `reset` :456); `cart_mechanism` (:332-349) additionally requires `PermissionKind::Application`; `run_apply` returns silently at :546 (`let Some(kind) = mechanism.get_untracked() else { return; }`) and :604; review/strip/label matches are on `scope_mode` alone (:687-748). The reviewer understated reachability: `held_permissions_panel.rs:43-44` gates the Scope… button with value-only `is_sharepoint_orgwide` (scoping.rs:370), so a `Sites.Read.All` held on `OFFICE365_SHAREPOINT_ONLINE_APP_ID` (scoping.rs:38) gets the button and is seeded with that resource (:162-173); `scope_kind_for(Some(SPO), ..)` is None because `is_scopable_sharepoint_resource_permission` requires Graph (scoping.rs:406-411). That yields exactly the described state on enterprise-app and MI panes. The `effective_mode` derive plus replacing the silent returns with an error is sound and small.

findings.title: Doc claim "add a ScopeKind variant + a target panel + a Step-3 apply arm — nothing else branches on the concrete mechanism" is wrong: the wizard branches in ~10 places
findings.evidence:
docs/architecture/audit-findings-and-remediation.md ("The scope registry + the mechanism-dispatched wizard"): "**To teach the app a new mechanism**: add a `ScopeKind` variant + a target panel + a Step-3 apply arm — nothing else branches on the concrete mechanism."
scope_wizard.rs mechanism-specific branches: 83 fn default_mode(kind) match; 484-488 preseed `if k == ScopeKind::SharePoint { site_write.set(..) }`; 507 toggle `Some(ScopeKind::SharePoint) => {`; 548-604 Plan match on (kind, mode); 655 consent_and_retry match on ScopeKind; 782/819/828 three per-mechanism <Show> blocks; 687 targets_label, 698 review_targets, 722 strip_warning, 734 review_line all match ScopeMode (whose variants Managed/Existing/Sites/Items are per-mechanism); 866 hint text names each mechanism.

A contributor following the doc would add a variant and panel, get a non-exhaustive-match compile error in `default_mode` and the Plan match, and still silently miss the review strings, the consent feature key, the Step-1 Show block and the radio (see the SharePoint one-way-door finding, which is exactly this drift). The `admin_applicable() == false` seam the doc mentions for Teams RSC is not wired into the wizard at all.
findings.proposal: At minimum correct docs/architecture/audit-findings-and-remediation.md:135-136 AND the mirrored sentence in .claude/rules/scoping-and-audit.md:25 ('Adding a mechanism touches exactly three places and nothing else branches on it') to enumerate the real touch points (default_mode, preseed, toggle, Plan match, consent_and_retry feature key, the Step-1 Show block + radio, the four ScopeMode-driven review strings, the hint copy). The MechanismSpec table refactor is optional and would make the claim true.
findings.verifier_notes: Doc text is exactly as quoted (audit-findings-and-remediation.md:135-136), and the same claim is restated in .claude/rules/scoping-and-audit.md:25. The wizard branches on `ScopeKind` at scope_wizard.rs:83-89 (default_mode), :484-488 (preseed), :507 (toggle), :548-604 (Plan match), :655-659 (consent feature key), :782/:819/:828 (Step-1 Show blocks), and on the per-mechanism `ScopeMode` enum at :687,:698,:722,:734 plus the hint at :866. `ScopeKind::admin_applicable` (core scoping.rs:484) is not referenced anywhere in web-rs (grep), so the doc's 'seam' is unwired. Finding [2] is a concrete symptom of this drift.

findings.title: Fold the two remaining per-action matches (`confirm_label`, `description`) into `Spec`; splitting bulk_action_bar.rs is optional
findings.rationale: The file holds four independent concerns: the action catalog (`BulkAction`/`Spec`/`Confirm`, ~120 lines), the pure result parsing (`Parsed`, `BulkRow`, `failures_of`, `unattempted_note`, `session_dead_error`, eight `parse_*`, ~300 lines) plus ~400 lines of tests for it, `BulkProgressRow` (~80 lines), and the `BulkActionBar` component + `armed_panel` (~600 lines). The Spec comment explains why parallel matches are a hazard, yet `confirm_label` and `description` are still two of them (a new action compiles without a confirm label only because `match` is exhaustive — but the copy is scattered across 700 lines).
findings.proposal: Extend `Spec` with `confirm_label: &'static str` and a `description: fn(usize) -> String` (the danger class is already derivable from `destructive || Grant`), and remove the matches at :762-820 and :962-972. Treat the four-file split as a separate, optional cleanup; if done, note six importers (bulk_actions_view, application_list, sso_certificates_dashboard, audit_view/{findings,mod,groups}.rs), not four.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real: Spec's doc at bulk_action_bar.rs:288-293 explains why parallel matches are a hazard, yet `description` (:762-820) and `confirm_label` (:962-972) remain parallel matches. The file is 1546 lines with the seams as described (Parsed/parse_* :125-1196, BulkProgressRow :201, tests from :1198). The split is a subjective refactor with no functional gain and the repo has no rule about file length; the Spec fold is the concrete improvement. `grep -rl bulk_action_bar::` returns six files, not four.

findings.title: `ALL_ACTIONS` test table omits `StageSsoCertificate`, so the spec-coherence tests are not exhaustive-by-construction; the RemoveRedundant carve-out is unexplained
findings.rationale: groups.rs's sibling test pins every `RemediationKind` "exhaustive by construction: a new variant won't compile until it is listed"; this one silently skipped the last variant added. `every_action_has_a_coherent_spec` (label non-empty, keywords unique/uppercase) and `destructive_actions_are_keyword_gated` therefore never ran for StageSsoCertificate, and the next variant will be skipped the same way. The `RemoveRedundant` exemption from "destructive ⇒ keyword" has no comment stating why (presumably: the backend re-plans and only removes covered permissions, so it is safe-by-construction), so a reviewer cannot tell a deliberate exception from an oversight.
findings.proposal: Add `impl BulkAction { pub const ALL: [BulkAction; 9] = [...]; }` beside the enum plus a `#[test] fn all_is_exhaustive()` that `match`es every variant (non-exhaustive match = compile error on a new variant) and asserts `ALL.len()` equals the arm count; use `BulkAction::ALL` in the tests. Document the RemoveRedundant exception in `Spec` and in the test (or promote it to `Confirm::Keyword("REMOVE")`-style gating if the exception is not intended).

findings.title: Neither `UNCONFINABLE_MAILBOX`/`UNCONFINABLE_SHAREPOINT` nor `UNSCOPABLE_LEGACY_MAILBOX` belongs to a finding group, so the findings-first pane hides them
findings.rationale: The scorer deliberately splits org-wide mailbox reach into confinable (`ORG_WIDE_MAILBOX` → Fix) and unconfinable (`UNCONFINABLE_*` → remove the grant). The Findings pane — the default, "remediation-centric" view — has a group for the first and none for the second, so a principal whose only mailbox problem is a legacy Exchange Online `Mail.Read` grant (which `reconcile_orgwide_grant` treats as reaching every mailbox) is invisible there unless it also trips another rule. Advisory groups (`high_risk_perms`, `external_exposure`) already exist for exactly this "visible with Open, no bulk fix" shape.
findings.proposal: Add advisory Actionable group(s) with no bulk action/remediation kind covering the three markers — but keep the legacy-resource marker's advice separate from the UNCONFINABLE one: types.rs:575-585 says 'remove the legacy grant' is the wrong advice for UNCONFINABLE_MAILBOX, so either two groups (`legacy_orgwide_grants` → LegacyExchangeGrantsCallout advice; `unconfinable_orgwide` → review/re-declare on Graph) or one group whose Detail column quotes the matched line. Add to PostureCounts and to `issue_marker_findings_match_exactly_their_finding`.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise confirmed: filter.rs:60-95 has no arm for any of these markers; only row.rs:62-66 knows them; scoring.rs:350-355 and :433-441 emit them as their own issues with no Fix. The example is wrong, though: a legacy Exchange Online `Mail.Read` grant produces `UNSCOPABLE_LEGACY_MAILBOX` (scoring.rs:317-349), a third ungrouped marker, while `UNCONFINABLE_MAILBOX` is defined as 'for a reason OTHER than the legacy-resource one' (types.rs:575-585), and the two carry deliberately different recommendations — so a single blurb pointing at `LegacyExchangeGrantsCallout` would misadvise the UNCONFINABLE case. No doc says these should stay ungrouped (grep docs/AGENTS/CHANGELOG for UNCONFINABLE: none), so this is an omission, not a decision.

findings.title: AuditController seeds the synthetic first progress event with `in_flight_cap: 8`, duplicating the backend's `INITIAL_CONCURRENCY`; a downward change there makes the rate-limit notice fire on every scan
findings.evidence:
controller.rs 187-193: self.progress.set(Some(AuditProgress { done: 0, total: 0, current_app: None, in_flight_cap: 8, cancelled: false }));
controller.rs 72-75: Effect::new(move |_| match progress.get() { Some(p) => peak_cap.update(|peak| *peak = (*peak).max(p.in_flight_cap)), ... })
security_view.rs 203: <Show when=move || cap < peak_cap.get()> ... "Microsoft Graph is rate-limiting this scan"
src-tauri commands/audit.rs 76,133,287: const INITIAL_CONCURRENCY: usize = 8; ... FanOutMeter::attach(client.clone(), INITIAL_CONCURRENCY); ... in_flight_cap: meter.limit(),
findings.rationale: `peak_cap` is documented as a high-water mark of the backend's live cap, but the frontend pre-loads it with a literal 8 that only happens to equal `INITIAL_CONCURRENCY`. If the backend constant is ever lowered (or made tenant-adaptive), the first real event's `cap < 8` and the "Graph is rate-limiting" notice shows on a healthy scan.
findings.proposal: Seed `in_flight_cap: 0` (so `peak_cap` only tracks backend events), or make the synthetic progress carry no cap (`Option<usize>` like `BulkProgress`) and hide the cap/notice until the first backend event; the progress bar still renders from `done/total`.
findings.verifier_notes: controller.rs:187-193 seeds `in_flight_cap: 8` with no comment tying it to the backend; `peak_cap` effect at :72-75 takes the max; security_view.rs:203 shows the rate-limit notice when `cap < peak_cap`; backend `INITIAL_CONCURRENCY: usize = 8` at src-tauri commands/audit.rs:76 with the cap emitted via `meter.limit()`. Lowering the backend constant would make the notice fire on a healthy scan's first real event. Seeding 0 (or an Option) is the right fix.

findings.title: Mutation-heavy surfaces have zero GUI coverage: SSO wizard, federated credentials, Expose-an-API, create app, enterprise Access/App roles
findings.rationale: The suite is the frontend's only behavioural gate (AGENTS.md), yet the surfaces it skips are the ones that mint trust or do irreversible full-collection writes: `add/update/remove_federated_credential` (auth trusts), `set_identifier_uris`/`upsert_api_scope`/`set_pre_authorized_app` (Graph full-replaces the `api` arrays — the exact footgun AGENTS.md documents), `create_saml/oidc_sso_application` + `ClaimsEditor` (945 lines, untested), `create_application`, `assign/remove_enterprise_app_access`, `upsert/delete_enterprise_app_role`. Coverage map (direct mounts): tested = ApplicationList, EnterpriseApplicationList, ManagedIdentitiesView(+DetailWindow), ApplicationDetailPane (Overview only), AuthenticationTab, CredentialsTab (cert reveal + expired sweep only), SsoContent (rollover only), SecurityView, CredentialsDashboard, SsoCertificatesDashboard, ReadinessView, KeyVaultView, SettingsView, AppShell, OpenItemsDock/Workspace, ScopeWizard/PermissionPicker, SharePointSitesSection, OrgwideScopeCallout, GalleryDialog, ConfirmDialog, GlobalSearch, ToastHost, CopyableId, DisasterRecoveryView; smoke-only = BulkActionsView, ResourceAccessView, PermissionTesterView; untested = everything listed in evidence plus SecretRevealDialog's add_password path, PermissionsTab's remove_declared_permission/revoke_*/downgrade_application_permission.
findings.proposal: Add one GUI module per risk tier, in this order: (1) `federated_tab.rs` — mount FederatedTab with `list_federated_credentials` mocked; drive the GitHub scenario, assert `add_federated_credential` args carry the auto-built issuer/subject and that Remove goes through ConfirmDialog. (2) `expose_api_tab.rs` — assert upsert/delete scope and pre-authorized-app calls send the *whole* current state (the full-collection contract) and that a failed save leaves the form editable. (3) `sso_wizard.rs` — protocol → config → review → create for SAML and OIDC, asserting create_*_sso_application args and that the show-once summary renders. (4) `create_app.rs`, `enterprise_access.rs`, `enterprise_app_roles.rs`. Group (1)(2)(4-create) into shard 1 (they share ApplicationDetailPane's tab code), (3)/(4-enterprise) into shard 1 as well and re-measure with `just web-itest-size`; split a shard 5 if it crosses 52 MB. Component-name grep over apps/desktop/web-rs/tests/ returns zero mounts for all 17 listed components (SsoWizardDialog, FederatedTab, ExposeApiTab, CreateAppDialog, ClaimsEditor, AccessContent, AppRolesContent, PermissionsTab, ...). Extracting every command literal from src/bindings (multi-line aware) gives 183 commands, 122 with no reference anywhere under tests/gui (reviewer said 125/186 — same picture). Every mutation named in the evidence (create_saml/oidc_sso_application, set_identifier_uris, upsert_api_scope, set_pre_authorized_app, create_application, assign/remove_enterprise_app_access, upsert/delete_enterprise_app_role, add/update/remove_federated_credential, add_password, remove_declared_permission, downgrade_application_permission) has 0 hits in tests/. tests/gui/application_detail.rs only clicks the Overview copy button (line 60) and the load-error retry (line 80), so the detail tabs are linked but not exercised; claims_editor.rs is 945 lines as stated. docs/architecture/frontend-workspace.md:219 confirms the suite is the frontend's only behavioural gate and nothing in AGENTS.md or the docs records a decision to leave these surfaces uncovered. Effort L is honest; the shard-size caveat (re-measure with `just web-itest-size`, split a gui_5) is consistent with the documented grouping rule.

findings.title: Bulk Delete's keyword gate and the updater launch chain have no DOM/behavioural test (spec-level pins exist for the former)
findings.rationale: `confirm_dialog.rs` proves `require_keyword` on the shared dialog, but BulkActionBar implements its own `Confirm::Keyword` panel and is the ONLY bulk caller; nothing proves that `bulk_delete_applications` cannot fire until "DELETE" is typed, nor that the armed panel reports partial failures. Likewise AGENTS.md says auto-update is interactive ("never reintroduce a silent download_and_install"); the shell test deliberately leaves `check_for_update` unmocked, so the launch-check → toast → splash → explicit click → `perform_update` chain has no test and a regression that calls `perform_update` on launch would pass CI.
findings.proposal: (a) Add one GUI flow in security_findings.rs (SecurityView already mounts BulkActionBar) for a keyword-gated action: arm Delete, assert call_count("bulk_delete_applications") == 0 after typing a wrong-case word and after clicking, == 1 after "DELETE". The partial-failure rendering is already unit-tested via parse_delete, so a single 'failed id renders' assertion suffices. (b) For the updater, the cheapest honest pin is a repo_invariants-style source scan asserting `perform_update(` is called only from web-rs/src/components/update_splash.rs and never from shell.rs/lib.rs; a GUI test with mock_ok("check_for_update", Some(UpdateInfo)) + mock_ok("perform_update", ()) is the fuller option if a fixture is cheap.

findings.title: 13 fallible read commands are unregistered in the demo — the Federated, Expose-an-API, Conditional Access, Activity, Usage, Exchange-roles and MI mail-scope surfaces render the demo rejection, and nothing inventories unfixtured reads
findings.rationale: The demo already had to hand-patch Authentication, SSO, get_sso_summary, rollover, the grant lenses etc. after visitors hit rejections (the comments say so). The remaining gaps are systematic: in the demo the Federated credentials, Expose an API, Conditional Access, Activity and Usage tabs of an app registration, the Exchange role assignments panel, the Resource Access Sites/Key Vault panes (cached sweeps), and the MI Permissions tab's mail-scope lookup all render the DemoFriendly error. `demo_fixture_coverage` cannot see this because it only scans the infallible form, so each new read is discovered by a visitor.
findings.proposal: (1) Register fixtures for the listed reads (small typed builders in fixtures.rs: `federated_credentials()`, `expose_api()`, `conditional_access_policies()`, `sign_in_activity()`, `graph_usage()`, `exchange_role_assignments()`, `site_sweep_result()`, `key_vault_access()`; `get_cached_*` may return `None` legitimately — register `&Option::None` so the panes show their honest 'no scan yet' state instead of an error). (2) Extend demo_fixture_coverage.rs with a second test over `invoke_result` literals matching `^(list_|get_|search_|check_|find_|probe_|current_)`: every one must be registered in demo/mod.rs OR appear in a `DEMO_READS_LEFT_UNFIXTURED: &[(&str, &str)]` allowlist with a reason, mirroring the existing `NOT_DEMO_REACHABLE` honesty test. Effect: new read surfaces must be classified before they ship to Pages.
findings.verifier_notes: All 13 listed commands verified: each is an `invoke_result` in src/bindings and has zero occurrences in src/demo/mod.rs (my independent scan of read-shaped invoke_result literals finds exactly the same 13 plus check_for_update, which is correctly left unmocked). demo_fixture_coverage.rs:1-3 and :36-69 scan only the infallible form, as stated. demo/mod.rs:6 promises 'Read commands are answered from fixtures', and the file's own comments at :332-335 and :446-448 record prior hand-patching after visitors hit the rejection, so the gaps are against the demo's stated contract, not a deliberate decision. release-updater-demo.md:102-103 acknowledges 'any unfixtured read' degrades gracefully but does not name or justify these. Minor overstatement: find_mailbox_reachers, list_exchange_scope_group and list_site_permissions are on-demand searches/probes rather than tab loads, and get_cached_site_sweep / get_cached_key_vault_access legitimately return None (the reviewer already accounts for the latter). The allowlist-test proposal is feasible: it is a native source scan of the same shape as the existing test.

findings.title: The two-parser differential test re-implements section_for instead of mounting it, and build_support.rs still says nothing checks agreement
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md's claim "two parsers, pinned by test" is true in spirit, but the pin compares a hand-copied `rust_semantics` against a PowerShell port — so an edit to the real `section_for` (e.g. tolerating `##  [`) would not change the differential at all, and the test would keep passing while the baked notes and the updater notes diverge. Meanwhile build_support.rs's own header tells the next reader the check does not exist, which invites a second one.
findings.proposal: In src-tauri/tests/repo_invariants/release.rs mount the real file with `#[path = "../../../web-rs/build_support.rs"] mod build_support;` and call it from the differential. `section_for` is a private `fn` (build_support.rs:16) — a private item in a child module is not visible to its parent — so it must become `pub(crate)` (harmless for build.rs, which `include!`s the file). The `include_str!("../../../CHANGELOG.md")` in its test module resolves relative to build_support.rs itself, so no path problem arises; gating its own #[cfg(test)] tests behind a feature is unnecessary. Update the build_support.rs header (lines 4-8) to name `both_changelog_extractors_produce_the_same_notes` as the agreement check.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real: release.rs:277-289 `rust_semantics` is a verbatim hand copy of build_support.rs:16-29 `section_for`, so an edit to the real parser cannot change the differential; build_support.rs:7 still says 'nothing checks that'. lib.rs:314-316 mounts the file via #[path] exactly as the proposal suggests, proving the mechanism. The comment at release.rs:265-274 justifies keeping two implementations (Rust + PowerShell) but says nothing about a third copy. Downgraded to low: a divergence only makes the in-app 'What's new' and the updater notes show different text — cosmetic — and both are still individually tested.

findings.title: click_button / next_enabled / select_permission / has_button / focused_matches are copy-pasted across 11 test modules

findings.title: global_search_capped fixture is dead; the capped footer/IndexCapNotice DOM rendering has no GUI test (its label/flatten logic is unit-tested)

findings.title: The one hand-written JSON demo fixture contradicts the 'typed fixtures cannot drift' guarantee
findings.rationale: Every other fixture is a typed struct serialized through the same serde path the bindings deserialize with, which is what makes fixture drift a compile error. `DirectoryIndexStatus` is defined frontend-side with `Deserialize` only, so the demo fell back to `json!` — the one place a renamed field (`sp_index_cap` → something) would silently turn into a deserialize error at demo runtime rather than a build failure. The DTO comment at dto/src/search.rs:55 even notes the frontend 'keeping its own copy in sync'.
findings.proposal: Either add `serde::Serialize` to `DirectoryIndexStatus` and register `&DirectoryIndexStatus { sp_index_truncated: false, sp_index_cap: 10_000 }` via a `fixtures::directory_index_status()` builder, or move the struct into `azapptoolkit-dto` (it mirrors a backend type already) so both sides share it. Effect: zero hand-written JSON in the mock path, matching the module's stated contract.
findings.verifier_notes: demo/mod.rs:379-382 is the only `json!` in src/demo and src/ipc_mock (grep confirms), contradicting fixtures.rs:1-4 'not hand-written JSON, so they can't drift'. bindings/applications.rs:22-27 derives only Deserialize with rename_all = camelCase; crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/search.rs:55-57 explicitly notes the frontend 'keeping its own copy in sync (mirroring DirectoryIndexStatus)'. Adding `serde::Serialize` to the frontend struct (or moving it to the dto crate beside the backend type it mirrors) is a one-line change with no wire impact. Low: the field names are stable and the failure mode is a demo-only deserialize error for a notice that is hidden anyway.

findings.title: Enterprise sub-tab and SSO demo fixtures are deliberately static per SP; making them args-aware via variant_index would add per-object variety (enhancement, not a violated rule)
findings.evidence:
demo/mod.rs:450  mock_ok("get_sso_config", &f::sso_config("sp-demo", "app-demo"));
demo/mod.rs:421-427  mock_ok(
        "list_enterprise_app_assignments",
        &vec![ f::app_assignment("Sales Team", "Group"), ...
demo/mod.rs:337  "get_application_authentication",
docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md:105-108  A plain `mock_ok` returns one payload for every id — the wrong-detail bug to avoid.
findings.rationale: The demo doc names one-payload-for-all-ids as the bug to avoid, and the detail/mail-scope/held-grant/Azure-role commands honour it, but `get_sso_config`/`get_sso_summary`/`get_signing_cert_rollover` return an SP `object_id: "sp-demo"` for Datadog, Slack and GitHub alike (with identical thumbprints), every SP has the same three assignments and roles, and every app registration has Contoso CRM's redirect URIs. `variant_index` already exists for exactly this; the same three-variant pattern would make the enterprise side coherent.

But this is acknowledged as deliberate — demo/mod.rs:419 reads 'Enterprise detail sub-tabs — representative sample data shown for every SP' — and release-updater-demo.md:104-108 scopes the args-aware rule to the detail commands whose pane would otherwise not switch, which is a different failure than a sub-tab showing sample data. findings.title: Stale shard/module counts in Cargo.toml and justfile sharding comments; the two merged-size figures come from different opt-levels rather than contradicting
findings.evidence:
Cargo.toml:113-115  # The browser GUI tests (`just web-itest`) are the slowest CI step. Each of the
# ~21 integration-test binaries is a full debug wasm
Cargo.toml:132-133  # 19 MB and all 24 modules merged are 29 MB.
justfile:133-134  # A single merged test binary (~78 MB) exceeds what headless Chrome will
# instantiate, so `tests/gui_N.rs` shards exist to stay under ~52 MB each.
(actual: 4 shard binaries + demo_fixture_coverage; 36 modules under tests/gui/)
findings.rationale: The comments are the only record of why the 52 MB ceiling and the shard layout exist. Today they contradict one another — Cargo.toml says the merged suite is 29 MB at opt-level 1 (under the ceiling), the justfile says ~78 MB — and the counts (21 binaries, 24 modules) predate the current 4-shard layout. A future contributor cannot tell whether sharding is still load-bearing without re-measuring. This is not a case for un-sharding (no new evidence); it is a case for making the numbers current and checkable.
findings.proposal: Fix the counts (Cargo.toml:114 '~21 integration-test binaries' → 4 gui shards + demo_fixture_coverage; :133 '24 modules' → the current module count, 32 today) and gui_2.rs:11 ('whole-shell smoke test' → shell.rs lives in gui_4). In justfile:133 qualify '~78 MB' as the pre-opt-level-1 measurement, or replace it with a current measured figure, so the rationale for the 52 MB ceiling reads as current. Optionally have web-itest-size print the summed shard size as a 'merged estimate' and paste dated numbers into the [profile.test] comment.
findings.verifier_notes: Counts are stale as claimed: 4 shard binaries (gui_1..4.rs) and 32 modules under tests/gui/ (the reviewer's '36' is itself off), versus Cargo.toml:114 '~21' and :133 '24 modules'. The 'contradict one another' claim is overstated: Cargo.toml:115-116 '1954 MB → 78 MB stripped' is the opt-level-0 debuginfo-stripped merged binary, and :127-133 explains that opt-level 1 brought the merged suite to 29 MB — the justfile:133-134 '~78 MB' is that older opt-level-0 number, so the two comments describe different builds rather than disagreeing, though the justfile figure is now stale and does misstate why sharding is still needed. The reviewer's restraint (not proposing un-sharding without new evidence) is correct. Low.

findings.title: demo_fixture_coverage scan has two blind spots: non-recursive bindings walk and comment-insensitive registration match
findings.rationale: Both are fine today (bindings is flat; no infallible invoke outside it) but each is one refactor away from silently disabling the guard: a `bindings/sso/` subdirectory would drop its files from the scan, and a comment in demo/mod.rs like `// see "cancel_audit"` would count as a registration. AGENTS.md leans on this test as the enforcement of a page-crash invariant.
findings.proposal: Walk `src/` recursively (skip `ipc_mock/` and `demo/`) so an infallible `invoke` anywhere is caught; strip `//` line comments from demo/mod.rs before the `contains` check and require the literal to be preceded by `mock_ok(`/`mock_each(`/`mock_err(` or to sit inside the `for cmd in [` array. Add a negative unit test for each (a comment-only mention must not satisfy the scan). Effort S.

findings.title: Two near-duplicate 'current version has a CHANGELOG section' tests; the docs name only one
findings.rationale: Both fail on the same condition (manifest version has no non-empty section). The release_notes one is strictly stronger — it checks the *baked* output, so it also catches a broken build.rs path or OUT_DIR write — and it is the one the architecture doc names. The build_support copy re-parses CHANGELOG.md with `include_str!` for the same assertion.
findings.proposal: Remove `the_repos_own_changelog_has_a_section_for_the_current_version` (keep the parser edge-case tests around it), or reduce it to a one-line pointer comment to the release_notes test. Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: build_support.rs:110-118 `the_repos_own_changelog_has_a_section_for_the_current_version` asserts section_for(CHANGELOG, CARGO_PKG_VERSION).is_some(); src/components/release_notes.rs:86-95 `the_running_versions_changelog_section_is_baked_in` asserts the baked CURRENT_RELEASE_NOTES is non-empty and stops before the next header. build.rs:41-44 writes `unwrap_or_default()` (empty) when the changelog is unreadable or the section is absent, so the release_notes test fails on every condition the build_support one does, plus a broken bake path — strictly stronger, as claimed. Mild counterpoint the reviewer did not weigh: keeping the parser-side assertion gives a faster triage signal (parser vs bake) when the stronger test fails — which is why 'reduce to a pointer comment' is the better of the two options offered. Low.

findings.title: DR view tells the operator a re-run restore "recreates only what is missing" — the backend creates every app unconditionally and the Restore button stays live after a run
findings.evidence:
dr.rs:502  "...Re-authenticate and run the restore again — it recreates only what is missing."
dr.rs:366  <Show when=move || plan.get().is_some() && !cloud_blocked() && !restoring.get()>
dr.rs:368      "Restore into this tenant…"
restore.rs:195-218  // ---- Pass 1: create shells ----
    for app in &backup.app_registrations {
        ...
        match create_application_core(&client, input).await {
findings.rationale: `restore_tenant` Pass 1 iterates every `app_registrations` entry and calls `create_application_core` with no lookup for an existing app by identifier URI or display name (grep for exist/duplicate in restore.rs finds nothing on the create path). So the session-expired callout's remedy — re-run the restore — creates a second copy of every app that was already created, each with a fresh appId, paired SP and regenerated secret. Independently, `plan`/`loaded` are never cleared after `report.set(Some(r))` (dr.rs:168), so the primary Restore button remains visible after a successful run and a second click duplicates the whole estate. The confirm modal (dr.rs:415) says only that nothing is overwritten or deleted, which is true but omits that duplicates are created. docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md makes no idempotency claim; the UI does.
findings.proposal: Short term (S): change the callout to say a re-run will create the remaining apps AND re-create the ones listed above, so the operator must first delete the duplicates or edit the manifest; after `report.set(Some(r))` clear `loaded`/`plan` so the Restore button requires re-loading a file. Proper fix (M): in `restore_tenant` Pass 1, resolve each manifest app in the destination by `identifier_uris` (api://{new}) then by display name via the existing `find_application_by_app_id`/index accessors; skip a match, record it as a `ManualItem`/"already present" row, and continue wiring only the newly created ones — then the callout's promise becomes true. Add a unit test on the pure planner and a GUI test asserting the button disappears after a report renders.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise holds on every point. dr.rs:502 promises a re-run 'recreates only what is missing'; restore.rs:197-218 iterates every `app_registrations` entry and calls `create_application_core` (applications/mod.rs:329-338 — a bare POST /applications, no lookup by name/URI/marker). Nothing in restore.rs, backup.rs, CHANGELOG.md or docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md claims or implements idempotency. The Restore button gate at dr.rs:366 reads `plan.get().is_some() && !cloud_blocked() && !restoring.get()`; `plan`/`loaded` are set at dr.rs:131-132 and never cleared — `load_file` (:125-126) and `do_restore` (:155-157) clear only `report`, so the primary button survives a successful run. The GUI test dr.rs:77-95 waits for `.dr-view__result` and never asserts the button is gone. Worse than the reviewer noted: restore.rs:750-752 (MI runbook) ALSO tells the operator to 're-run the restore to re-bind its Graph app-roles', so the report itself instructs a duplicate-creating re-run. One correction to the proposal: matching by `api://{new}` is not derivable from the manifest (the rewrite target is the new appId, known only in the report); match by display name and/or stamp a source marker (e.g. `notes`/tag `azapptoolkit:source_app_id=<guid>`) at create time so a re-run can resolve it; `find_application_by_app_id` exists (graph/client/applications.rs:446) but keys on appId, which changes. High is honest: the UI's stated remedy creates a second copy of the whole estate with fresh secrets and paired SPs in a DR destination.
findings.recheck_notes:
Could not refute; every link in the chain checks out in the shipped (non-demo) build.

1. Backend creates unconditionally. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/restore.rs:196-238 (Pass 1) iterates `backup.app_registrations` and calls `create_application_core` for each with no lookup of an existing app; `create_application_core` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/applications/mod.rs:329-338) is a bare POST `/applications` (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/applications.rs:391-393). Entra does not enforce displayName uniqueness, so a second run yields a second app + fresh appId. The only dedupe on the path is `ensure_service_principal` (service_principals.rs:506-516), which keys on the NEW appId and therefore never matches the prior run's SP. Identifier-URI uniqueness cannot save it either: Pass 2 rewrites `api://{old}` -> `api://{new}` (restore.rs:419-420) so the URI is unique per run, and any verbatim URI collision is a best-effort per-app warning (module doc restore.rs:22, doc backup-and-restore.md:152-153), not a rollback of the already-created shell. `build_restore_plan` (restore.rs:125-146) reports `app_registrations_to_create: backup.app_registrations.len()` with no destination lookup, so even re-loading the file shows the full count. grep for exist/duplicate/already in restore.rs confirms nothing on the create path.

2. The session-expired path returns Ok. restore.rs:319-329: `report.session_expired = session.is_dead(); ... Ok(report)`, so dr.rs:160-168 takes the `Ok(r)` arm, toasts "Restored N app(s)" and sets `report`, and `report_if_session_dead` is never consulted (dr.rs:170-174 is the Err arm). The callout at dr.rs:500-503 then tells the operator to "run the restore again — it recreates only what is missing", which is false.

3. Restore button stays live. `do_restore` (dr.rs:149-179) never clears `plan`/`loaded`; the primary button's guard is `plan.get().is_some() && !cloud_blocked() && !restoring.get()` (dr.rs:366), so after `restoring.set(false)` (dr.rs:176) it reappears and a second click re-runs `restore_tenant` on the same `loaded` manifest. The confirm modal (dr.rs:413-417) says only that nothing is overwritten/deleted.

4. No test guards it. tests/gui/dr.rs:167-184 pins the callout wording ("Re-authenticate and run the restore again") but nothing asserts the button disappears after a report or that a re-run skips created apps; no repo_invariants test covers restore idempotency (fanout.rs:48, trust.rs only). docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:141-178 makes no idempotency claim.

Severity stays high: in the exact DR scenario the UI describes, following the on-screen remedy duplicates every already-restored app (new appId, paired SP, regenerated secret, re-granted admin consent, federated credentials), which is irreversible without manual cleanup and multiplies consented trust in the destination tenant.

findings.title: `invoke_result` unwraps the error deserialization — any rejection that is not a `UiError` JSON object panics the whole WASM app
findings.evidence:
bindings/*.rs:  use tauri_sys::core::invoke_result;   (every binding, no wrapper)
tauri-sys/src/core.rs:18-27
  pub async fn invoke_result<T, E>(command: &str, args: impl Serialize) -> Result<T, E> {
      inner::invoke_result(command, swb::to_value(&args).unwrap())
          .await
          .map(|val| swb::from_value(val).unwrap())
          .map_err(|err| swb::from_value(err).unwrap())
.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:15  "use `invoke_result()` (never bare `invoke`, which panics on a rejected promise)"
findings.rationale: The repo's rule treats `invoke_result` as the safe path, but tauri-sys `unwrap`s `from_value::<UiError>(err)`. Tauri rejects with a plain string (not `{code,message,retryable}`) for arg-shape mismatches ("invalid args `tenantId` for command …"), unknown commands, and denied plugin permissions (e.g. if `dialog:allow-save` is ever narrowed in capabilities/default.json). Any of those turns into a `console_error_panic_hook` panic (lib.rs:69) that freezes the UI with no toast — worse than the bare-`invoke` failure the rule warns about. Nothing pins binding arg names to backend param names today (`command-parity-check.sh` checks command names only), so this is one rename away.
findings.proposal: Add `bindings::ipc::invoke_result<T: DeserializeOwned>(cmd, args) -> Result<T, UiError>` that calls `tauri_sys::core::invoke_result::<T, serde_json::Value>` and maps a value that fails `UiError` deserialization into `UiError::new("ipc", value.to_string(), false)` (also catching the success-side `from_value` failure). Mechanically switch every `use tauri_sys::core::invoke_result` in bindings/ to it, and add a repo_invariants source-scan test that bindings never import `tauri_sys::core::{invoke,invoke_result}` directly. Then `report_if_session_dead`/toasts see a real error instead of a panic.
findings.verifier_notes: tauri-sys core.rs:18-27 (pinned rev 289bd29, Cargo.toml:33) does `.map(|val| swb::from_value(val).unwrap()).map_err(|err| swb::from_value(err).unwrap())`. `UiError` is a struct, so a string rejection (Tauri's shape for invalid-args deserialization failures and ACL/permission denials) fails `from_value` and panics; lib.rs:69 installs `console_error_panic_hook`, which logs and aborts the WASM instance with no toast. `.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:15` presents `invoke_result` as the safe path, so the rule is misleading. Nothing pins binding arg names: repo_invariants/ has cache/cancel/commands/fanout/release/sources/trust only, and command-parity-check.sh compares command *names*. The GUI harness cannot catch this because `ipc_mock::mock_err` (ipc_mock/mod.rs:265-267) only ever rejects with a `UiError`. Proposal is feasible: deserialize both sides to `serde_json::Value` first and map failures to a synthetic `UiError`, plus a source-scan that bindings/ never import `tauri_sys::core::{invoke,invoke_result}` directly (note `defaults::get_tenant_defaults` and the diagnostics bindings use bare `invoke` by design as infallible commands — the wrapper should cover those too or leave them explicitly allow-listed).

findings.title: Key Vault browser: listed secrets, vault name and `loaded` survive a tenant switch/sign-out — only `revealed`/`error` are wiped
findings.rationale: `set_active_tenant` (state/tenant.rs:18-42) resets `tenant_ui` and sets view=Home, which does wipe `revealed` via the view-watch — but there is no `tenant.get()` dependency anywhere in this view, so tenant A's secret names, content types and expiry dates (and A's vault name in the picker) are still on screen when tenant B opens Key Vault. Clicking Reveal there sends `kv_get_secret(tenantB, vaultA, name)`. The Resource Access panels and the mailbox probe explicitly reset on `tenant.get()` for this reason ("cross-tenant leakage", mailboxes.rs:152-159); this view is the one tenant-scoped surface that does not.
findings.proposal: Either add an `Effect` tracking `session.active_tenant` that clears `listed`, `loaded`, `vault_name`, `revealed`, `error`; or (preferred, per the AGENTS.md rule that per-list state lives on `Session.tenant_ui` and resets structurally) move `vault_name`/`listed` into `TenantScopedUi` with a `reset()` line so `tenant_switch_resets_every_tenant_scoped_field` pins it. Add a GUI test: list secrets, `set_active_tenant(other)`, assert the table is empty and the vault field is blank.
findings.verifier_notes: key_vault_view.rs:42-47 tracks only `session.view` and wipes `revealed`/`error`; `vault_name` (:23), `listed` (:24) and `loaded` (:30) have no tenant dependency. `set_active_tenant` (state/tenant.rs:18-39) resets `tenant_ui` and sets view=Home, which triggers the view-watch but leaves the table populated. `VaultPicker` (vault_picker.rs:27-30) resets its discovered `all_vaults` on tenant change but not `value`, so tenant A's vault name stays in the field. Every sibling tenant-scoped panel resets on `tenant.get()` (sites.rs:163-168, resource_access/keyvault.rs:168-173, mailboxes.rs:153-160 with the explicit 'cross-tenant leakage' comment). What leaks is secret names/content-types/expiry (metadata), not values — still a tenant-scoped surface violating the repo's #1 footgun rule. On the proposal: the lighter, sibling-consistent fix is an `Effect` on `tenant.get()` clearing all five signals; moving a `Vec<KvSecretItemDto>` into `TenantScopedUi` is heavier than what that struct holds today (filters/facets/flags), so prefer the Effect plus the GUI test.

findings.title: Dead-session recovery convention (`report_if_session_dead`) is applied in only 2 of the 9 error surfaces in this slice
findings.rationale: A `refresh_missing`/`not_signed_in` failure in the permission tester, any Resource Access panel, the Key Vault browser or the top-bar search renders a raw message with no Re-authenticate action; in global search it re-renders "Search failed: …" on every debounced keystroke. The DR view already shows the intended shape (`if !session.report_if_session_dead(&e) { error.set(...) }`). The `report_consent_required` twin is likewise unused where a consent feature applies (mailbox probe → "exchange").
findings.proposal: At each listed `Err(e)` arm, call `session.report_if_session_dead(&e)` first and only fall through to the inline banner when it returns false; in GlobalSearch render a single "Session expired — re-authenticate" row (and call the sink once per failure, not per keystroke — e.g. guard on `e.is_reauth_fatal()` and a `reported` flag reset when the query is cleared). Consider a repo_invariants scan: any `Err(e) => error.set(Some(e.message))` in web-rs/src/views must be preceded by the sink call.
findings.verifier_notes: grep confirms `report_if_session_dead` is called only in dr.rs (6 sites) and bulk_action_bar.rs:564; the sink's own doc (state/errors.rs:45-48) says surfaces with an inline banner should call it first. The listed arms are real: permission_tester_view.rs:231-235 and :259-261, sites.rs:208-211/:228, resource_access/keyvault.rs:212-215/:232, mailboxes.rs:189, key_vault_view.rs:67/:90. global_search.rs:88-101 maps the error to `e.message` (a `String`) inside the `LocalResource`, discarding the code entirely, and the debounced resource re-renders 'Search failed: …' (:284-288) on each settled keystroke — so the fix there needs the resource to carry the `UiError`. The gap is actually wider than this slice: `use_command::run` (hooks/use_command.rs:96-104) calls only `report_consent_required`, never `report_if_session_dead`, so every `run` caller with an inline error signal has the same dead-end. Proposal holds; the repo_invariants scan is optional but consistent with how the Callout rule is pinned (repo_invariants/commands.rs:21).

findings.title: Restore dry-run omits the schema-too-new blocker and the Pass 4/5 counts, so a too-new manifest is rejected only after the confirm click
findings.rationale: `plan_restore` is documented as the operator's chance to inspect before writes (backup-and-restore.md "The frontend shows it before the operator confirms"). The cloud-mismatch blocker is computed there, but the newer-schema refusal is not, so the operator loads the file, reads a plausible plan, confirms the modal, and only then gets `schema_too_new`. The plan also says nothing about Pass 4/5 (enterprise-app access re-application, MI app-role re-binding, runbook items), even though the report afterwards has whole sections for them — the dry-run under-describes what Restore will do.
findings.proposal: Add `schema_too_new: Option<String>` (or a shared blocker enum with `cloud_mismatch`) to `RestorePlan` computed from `check_manifest_schema` in `build_restore_plan`, generalise `cloud_blocked()` in dr.rs to `plan_blocked()`, and add `enterprise_apps_to_reapply` / `enterprise_apps_manual` / `managed_identities_to_rebind` counts rendered in `RestorePlanView`; extend the existing pure unit test (restore.rs:1049).
findings.verifier_notes: Premise is accurate: `plan_restore` (restore.rs:87-97) never calls `check_manifest_schema`, which runs only at restore.rs:157; `RestorePlan` (dto/backup.rs:351-368) and `RestorePlanView` (dr.rs:453-459) cover app registrations only while the report has enterprise/MI/manual sections; `load_backup_from_file` (backup.rs:305-326) deserialises a newer manifest fine because every field is `serde(default)`. Severity is overstated: the schema check fires before any write, so the cost is a wasted confirm click and a late error message, not a partial restore. Enhancement, low.

findings.title: Sites and Vault-access panels duplicate the sweep-table filtering/export/hydrate scaffolding (~120 lines each)
findings.rationale: keyvault.rs opens with "Mirrors the Sites panel" and the body is a copy with the DTO types, consent feature ("sharepoint"→"arm"), noun and three `<td>`s swapped. Both already had to receive the same fixes in lockstep (the haystack corpus, the render-window reset, the still-active hydrate guard, the export-summary rider). The next fix — e.g. the dead-session sink above, or a "scan was partial: re-scan?" callout — has to land twice, and the mailbox panel is a third partial copy.
findings.proposal: Extract a narrower hook — e.g. `use_sweep_table<Row, Res>(result, haystack: fn(&Row)->String, summary: fn(&Res,&[Row])->String) -> (filtered_rows, render_limit, summary)` plus the export wiring — matching the granularity of the existing `use_list_export` / `use_progress_stream` hooks; leave `do_run`/consent/cancel per panel (they differ in DTO, command and consent feature). Pin with a source-scan that neither panel defines its own `corpus`/`filtered_rows` memo.
findings.verifier_notes: Duplication is real and verbatim: sites.rs:55-97 and resource_access/keyvault.rs:70-107 (debounce, corpus, filtered_rows, render_limit reset), :104-136 vs :113-146 (summary), :146-155 vs :153-162 (export), :163-184 vs :168-189 (hydrate with still_active guard), :187-231 vs :191-235 (run/consent); keyvault.rs:4 says 'Mirrors the Sites panel'. But a refactor with no defect is not medium severity. The proposed all-in-one hook returning a 12-tuple would be harder to read than the two files; mailboxes.rs is only a partial copy (no corpus/filter memo, per-target probe), so the 'third copy' claim is thin.

findings.title: GUI coverage misses the Key Vault reveal wipe, the DR skipped-object notice, the Home dashboard, the cache dialog and the tester seed; Resource Access partial-sweep is covered only from the per-app side
findings.evidence:

tests/gui/key_vault.rs test fns: lists_secrets_for_named_vault / empty_vault_renders_empty_state / list_error_renders_message   (no Reveal, no wipe)

findings.title: Dead IPC leftovers hidden by `#![allow(dead_code)]`: `keyvault::SetArgs` for a non-existent `kv_set_secret`, unused `auth::is_tauri_runtime`, and six one-field tenant arg structs redeclared beside `common::TenantArg`
findings.evidence:
bindings/mod.rs:1   #![allow(dead_code)]
bindings/keyvault.rs:1   //! Azure Key Vault IPC bindings: list / get / set secrets.
bindings/keyvault.rs:58-63   struct SetArgs<'a> { tenant_id: &'a str, input: &'a KvSetSecretInput, }   (no fn uses it)
src-tauri/src/lib.rs:131-134   kv_list_secrets, kv_get_secret, rotate_app_credential, list_available_key_vaults   (no kv_set_secret)

findings.proposal: Delete `keyvault::SetArgs` and `auth::is_tauri_runtime`; fix the module doc (bindings/keyvault.rs:1) and dto/keyvault.rs:83; replace `TenantArgs` in search.rs:22, keyvault.rs:81, defaults.rs:15, sso.rs:180 plus `CheckReadinessArgs` (readiness.rs:15) and `RefreshSessionArgs` (auth.rs:39) with `crate::bindings::TenantArg`; then narrow or drop the module-wide `#![allow(dead_code)]` so `just web-clippy -D warnings` reports leftovers. Adjacent definition-only structs: `audit::ExportArgs` (audit.rs:28), `applications::ResolvePermissionArgs` (:77), `permissions::UpdateRequiredResourceArgs` (:55). `RevokeOauth2ScopeArgs` is used (permissions.rs:236/249) and `sharepoint::remove_selected_item_permission` is a binding for a registered command (lib.rs:216) with no UI caller — unused, not stale.
findings.verifier_notes: Core premise confirmed: bindings/mod.rs:1 `#![allow(dead_code)]` with no rationale anywhere (grep docs/AGENTS/.claude: none); `SetArgs` (keyvault.rs:58-63) has no constructor; lib.rs:131-134 registers kv_list_secrets/kv_get_secret/rotate_app_credential/list_available_key_vaults only; `is_tauri_runtime` has zero callers across web-rs. Overstated/incorrect details: the count is six redeclarations (sso.rs:180 was missed), `RevokeOauth` is not dead, and `remove_selected_item_permission` is an unused-but-valid binding rather than a stale one.

findings.title: Cache diagnostics offers per-kind Clear for only Lists/All although the DTO and backend support all four kinds; the toggle button does not say what it will do
findings.evidence:
cache_diagnostics_dialog.rs:195   "Toggle enabled"
cache_diagnostics_dialog.rs:199   on_click=Box::new(move |_| clear(CacheKindDto::Lists))
cache_diagnostics_dialog.rs:205   on_click=Box::new(move |_| clear(CacheKindDto::All))
dto/diagnostics.rs:40-46   pub enum CacheKindDto { ServicePrincipal, Permissions, Audit, Lists, All }
commands/diagnostics.rs:34-46   clear_cache ... CacheKindDto::ServicePrincipal => Some(CacheKind::ServicePrincipal), Permissions => ..., Audit => ...
