findings.title: audit_cancel is shared by the read-only audit, every bulk write and the AAP migration, and the UI can run them concurrently, so any Cancel button stops all of them
findings.rationale: Generation arithmetic: audit claims (current=1, token g=1), then a bulk scope-and-strip/delete claims (current=2, g=2). Pressing Cancel in EITHER the posture strip (cancel_audit) or the BulkProgressRow (cancel_bulk) runs cancel(): cancelled = max(0, 2) = 2, and both 2>=1 and 2>=2 hold, so both runs stop. The reverse start order gives the same result. There is no ordering in which cross-kind collateral cancellation does not happen. Consequences: (1) the operator cancels a read-only scan and a tenant WRITE (bulk delete, scope mailbox/SharePoint access, add owner, disable sign-in, AAP migration) halts mid-selection, reporting 'N app(s) were never attempted' for a Cancel they never pressed on it; (2) the operator cancels a bulk run and the audit result comes back cancelled=true, uncached, and the Security strip shows 'This scan was cancelled early — X of Y principals were scored' (security_view.rs:236-246) — a coverage caveat for a cancel that never targeted the scan. The CancelFlag::cancel doc justifies stopping older generations as 'a run that was going to be superseded anyway', which only holds when all runs on a flag are the same kind; the docstrings' 'never run at once' premise is false given keep-alive views and per-component busy signals, so this is not a documented trade-off. The same overlap also means every mounted BulkActionBar's `use_progress_stream(progress, events::bulk_progress)` (bulk_action_bar.rs:391-392) receives BOTH producers' events, so two concurrent bulk rows show interleaved done/total.
findings.proposal: Give each run kind its own identity. Minimal (S): add `bulk_cancel: CancelFlag` and `migration_cancel: CancelFlag` to AppState, point `cancel_bulk` and all `bulk_*` claims at `bulk_cancel`, the AAP migration at its own flag, and pin the command->flag mapping in repo_invariants/cancel.rs (e.g. a `bulk_*` command body must claim `bulk_cancel`, `run_audit` must claim `audit_cancel`). Robust (M): have `claim()` return the generation to the command, emit it in the first progress event (`run_id` on BulkProgress/AuditProgress), and add a `cancel_run(run_id)` command that does `cancelled.fetch_max(run_id)` only when it is the current generation — then each Cancel button stops exactly its own run and progress listeners can filter by run_id, fixing the interleaved bulk-progress rows too. Update the docstrings at bulk.rs:127, bulk.rs:143-145, audit.rs:14 and caching-and-search.md:350 to state the real rule.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is real. bulk.rs:125-134 asserts the audit and bulk loops 'never run at once'; that premise is false: views are keep-alive (web-rs/src/lib.rs:274,288 via util.rs:24-52 display toggle), BulkActionBar gates only on its own `busy` (bulk_action_bar.rs:459-461,620), AuditController::run gates only on `scanning` and never clears `result` (controller.rs:182-207), and AuditAppsPane renders its BulkActionBar whenever `total_items` is Some (audit_view/mod.rs:226-247) — so a re-scan leaves the table + bar usable. BulkActionBar is also hosted in application_list.rs:563, findings.rs:371, sso_certificates_dashboard.rs:108 and bulk_actions_view.rs:226, all reachable during a scan. All 10 bulk commands (bulk.rs:156,319,418,541,616,674,724,774,842,905) and the AAP migration (aap_migration.rs:52) claim audit_cancel; cancel() at state.rs:94-97 stamps `current`, so either Cancel stops every generation on the flag. Not a documented trade-off: the repo's own intent is that unrelated runs must not cross-cancel (state.rs:218-227 field docs, backup.rs:62-63, sharepoint.rs:823-825, and the `distinct_cancel_flags_are_independent` test at state.rs:733-744); the CancelFlag::cancel 'superseded anyway' rationale (state.rs:90-93) only holds for same-kind runs. caching-and-search.md:350 restates the sharing without the concurrency premise. Severity lowered from high to medium: no data corruption or leak — a bulk run stops at an item boundary and names the unattempted remainder (CHANGELOG 'A stopped bulk run no longer hides the apps it never reached'), the audit result is flagged cancelled and never cached (audit.rs:441-446), and both are re-runnable; the harm is a wrong-target cancel plus a misleading coverage caveat. Proposal note: a per-kind `bulk_cancel` still lets two bars' concurrent bulk runs cross-cancel (five hosts), so the run_id variant is the one that fully fixes it; the interleaved `bulk-progress` observation is real (every mounted bar subscribes, bulk_action_bar.rs:393, row shown while its own `busy`, :647).

findings.title: GraphClient has a single throttle_observer slot, so concurrent fan-outs on one tenant overwrite each other's tracker and ThrottleGuard::drop clears whichever run's observer is installed
findings.rationale: Each FanOutMeter::attach does build its own ConcurrencyThrottle (no shared tracker), and the recovery loop terminates within one 30 s tick after the last Arc drops (Weak upgrade fails -> break), so those two parts are sound. But the observer slot is one `Option` per GraphClient, and the audit, bulk delete/grant/expired-sweep, site sweep and DR backup all run against the same `Arc<GraphClient>` for the tenant. When run B attaches while run A is in flight, A's tracker is silently replaced: A's 429s now halve B's cap and A's own cap never halves again. When either guard drops first, `clear_throttle_observer()` removes the OTHER run's observer for the rest of its life, so a still-running fan-out runs with a fixed cap and no back-off — exactly the 'stale/missing observer' failure the guard exists to prevent, now in the concurrent case the guard's doc never considers. Distinct from F020 (halving window) and F031 (tick ordering).
findings.proposal: Make the slot multi-observer: `RwLock<Vec<Weak<dyn ThrottleObserver>>>`, `set_throttle_observer` pushes, `on_throttle` notifies every live Weak and prunes dead ones, and `ThrottleGuard::drop` removes only its own tracker (`Weak::ptr_eq`). Alternatively keep the single slot but make `clear_throttle_observer` a compare-and-clear (`Arc::ptr_eq` against the guard's own tracker) and log when an attach displaces a live observer. Add a unit test in client/tests/transport.rs that attaches two observers and asserts both see a 429 and that dropping one guard leaves the other attached.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real: client.rs:143 is a single `RwLock<Option<Arc<dyn ThrottleObserver>>>`, set_throttle_observer overwrites and clear_throttle_observer unconditionally clears (client.rs:262-268); ThrottleGuard::drop calls clear (throttle.rs:140-144). All attach sites use the shared per-tenant Arc from graph_for (audit.rs:133, bulk.rs:185 etc., sharepoint.rs:864 via sharepoint_client_checked:129, backup.rs:88), and concurrent fan-outs on one tenant are the normal case given keep-alive views (see finding 0). The only test (client/tests/transport.rs:267-297 `throttle_observer_fires_on_429`) attaches one observer; nothing in repo_invariants/fanout.rs pins observer lifetime. transport.rs:557 snapshots the observer per request, so an in-flight request notifies whichever tracker was installed when it started — consistent with the finding. Consequence is degraded adaptive back-off, not correctness: the transport still retries 429s honouring Retry-After (transport.rs:626-631), so the surviving run finishes at a fixed cap — the pre-adaptive behaviour sharepoint.rs:858-862 describes as the problem the throttle was added to fix. Medium is defensible given the repo built a RAII guard specifically to prevent a milder stale-observer case; the compare-and-clear (`Arc::ptr_eq`) variant is the smaller correct fix and the multi-observer Vec<Weak> the complete one.

findings.title: sweep_cancel is shared by the site sweep, Key Vault sweep, mailbox probe and per-app site panel, all of which can run concurrently from always-mounted panels; one panel's Cancel aborts the others
findings.rationale: The premise 'the two never run concurrently from the UI' is contradicted by the Resource Access module doc: the Mailboxes, Sites and Vault access panels are display-toggled, each with an independent busy signal, so an operator can start a site sweep, flip to Vault access and start a KV sweep, then probe a mailbox — three runs on one flag (and the per-app site panel in an app detail adds a fourth entry point). cancel() stamps `current`, so pressing Cancel on the 20-second mailbox probe also aborts a multi-minute site sweep and KV sweep; each then reports 'scan was cancelled early' (sites.rs:127-128, keyvault.rs:137-138) and is deliberately NOT cached, so the operator loses the whole scan and gets a coverage caveat for a Cancel they aimed elsewhere. Additionally two `sweep_site_permissions` runs (Resource Access Sites tab + app panel) can be in flight at once: both subscribe to `site-sweep-progress` (sites.rs:159, app_site_access_panel.rs:52) so their progress interleaves, and the tenant-wide sweep is paid twice because there is no single-flight on the sweep.
findings.proposal: Split into `site_sweep_cancel`, `keyvault_sweep_cancel`, `mailbox_probe_cancel` (or adopt the run_id cancel design from the audit_cancel finding) and give each frontend Cancel its own command; fix the docstrings at permission_tester.rs:443 and docs/architecture/resource-access-and-permission-tester.md:14-15. For the duplicate site sweep, wrap `sweep_site_permissions` in `state.single_flight(&sweep_cache_key(&tenant_id))` with a post-acquire cache re-check so the second caller joins the first's result instead of re-walking every site.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real: permission_tester.rs:441-444 claims 'the two never run concurrently from the UI'; resource_access/mod.rs:19-20 says all panels stay mounted (display toggle); sites.rs:186-189, keyvault.rs:190-193 and mailboxes.rs:173 each gate only on their own signal; all four Cancel handlers (sites.rs:235, keyvault.rs:239, mailboxes.rs:198, app_site_access_panel.rs:138) call cancel_resource_sweep (sharepoint.rs:999-1001), and sweep_cancel is claimed by sweep_site_permissions (sharepoint.rs:839), sweep_key_vault_access (keyvault_rbac.rs:96) and find_mailbox_reachers (permission_tester.rs:456). The deep-dive (resource-access-and-permission-tester.md:12-15) still says 'both long-running operations' — stale since the KV sweep and the per-app panel were added (bindings/keyvault_rbac.rs:3 acknowledges the sharing). Cancelled sweeps are deliberately not cached (sharepoint.rs:828-829, keyvault_rbac.rs:83-85), so a wrong-target cancel costs the whole multi-minute scan. Secondary claim verified: no single_flight on sweep_site_permissions (single_flight is used only in gallery.rs:112, search.rs:127, applications/cache.rs:243,325), and both the Sites tab (sites.rs:159) and the app panel (app_site_access_panel.rs:52) can run it concurrently. Caveat on that part of the proposal: single_flight is documented for read-through caches (state.rs:381-399); joining is fine here only because a cancelled/partial first run is not cached and the second caller's post-acquire re-check would then re-run — acceptable, but worth stating.

findings.title: Backup and restore share dr_cancel and are gated by independent signals in the same view, so cancelling a read-only backup aborts an in-flight restore mid-pass
findings.rationale: The DR view renders the Back up and Restore controls side by side; 'Back up this tenant' is disabled only while `busy` (dr.rs:237) and 'Restore into this tenant…' only while `restoring` (dr.rs:361-366), so an operator can start a backup and, while it walks a large tenant, load a file and start a restore. Both claim dr_cancel (gen 1 and gen 2); cancel_dr stamps current=2, so the backup's Cancel button stops the restore between passes. The restore report then reads '(cancelled before completing — partial)' (dr.rs:494) for a run whose Cancel button was never pressed, leaving shells created without permissions/owners/secrets. The backup-and-restore.md rationale only argues dr_cancel vs audit_cancel; it never considers backup vs restore overlap.
findings.proposal: Frontend S: disable the Restore controls while `busy` and the Back-up button while `restoring` so the two are mutually exclusive on the page. Backend S: add `restore_cancel: CancelFlag` with a `cancel_restore` command so the restore's Cancel is the only thing that can stop a write; keep `cancel_dr` for the backup.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real: run_backup gates on `busy` (dr.rs:54-61), do_restore never checks `busy` (dr.rs:150-155), both Cancel handlers call cancel_dr (dr.rs:96-98, 180-182 → backup.rs:331-333), backup_tenant and restore_tenant both claim dr_cancel (backup.rs:78, restore.rs:193); the Back-up button is disabled only by `busy` (dr.rs:237) and Load/Restore only by `restoring` (dr.rs:361-366). The consequence is accurate to the code: restore.rs:240-250 now breaks passes 2-5 on cancel too ('Both stop conditions, in every pass'), so a cancel during pass 1/2 does leave unwired shells — note backup-and-restore.md:173-175 ('never bare shells') is stale relative to that code, and the deep-dive (:126-129) argues only dr_cancel vs audit_cancel, never backup vs restore. Severity lowered to low: triggering it requires backing up a tenant and, mid-run, loading a file and confirming a restore into the same tenant — an unusual sequence — and the report flags the run cancelled. The frontend mutual-exclusion fix (disable Restore while `busy`, Back up while `restoring`) is trivial and sufficient; a separate restore_cancel is optional.

findings.title: AAP migration claims a cancel token 'so the operator can stop it' but no UI surface exposes a Cancel; the only things that stop it are the audit and bulk Cancel buttons
findings.rationale: The claim satisfies the repo_invariants rule for tenant-wide writers, but functionally the operator still cannot stop a migration from the surface that started it, so the comment's stated goal is unmet. Worse, because it rides audit_cancel, the migration IS stopped by unrelated Cancel presses (a running audit scan's Cancel, or any BulkActionBar Cancel), returning `incomplete: true` with the app in `unattempted` — see the audit_cancel finding. Since both UI callers are per-app (one batch), the check at aap_migration.rs:95 fires at most once, so today the token mostly serves the dead-session latch.
findings.proposal: Either give the migration its own flag plus a Cancel button in the Exchange scoping section's busy state and in the MigrateLegacyScope dialog (S), or, if per-app runs are the only supported shape, drop the 'operator could not stop a whole-tenant migration' comment and document that cancellation here exists only for the SessionDead break. Do the former if `app_id: None` is meant to become a UI feature.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real: aap_migration.rs:36-42,52 claims audit_cancel with a comment about the operator being unable to stop a whole-tenant migration; the only two frontend callers (exchange_scoping_section.rs:332-338 and dialogs/migrate_legacy_scope.rs:69-74) both pass Some(&app_id) and neither file references any cancel binding (grep confirms); the app-wide cancel callers are cancel_audit, cancel_bulk, cancel_resource_sweep and cancel_dr only. So the token's cancel half is reachable only via the audit strip's or a BulkActionBar's Cancel (see finding 0), while the SessionDead latch (aap_migration.rs:53,95) is what actually protects the per-app run. The claim does satisfy repo_invariants/cancel.rs (both the exists-once and before-first-await rules). Fair enhancement-level finding; either branch of the proposal is reasonable, and the comment should at least stop implying an operator-facing stop exists.

findings.title: sign_out prunes only graph_clients and exchange_clients; kv_clients, arm_clients and la_clients are never removed anywhere
findings.rationale: Not a credential leak: every client holds a ScopedTokenAdapter that asks the singleton auth service per request (token_adapter.rs:70-80), so a stale client fails with `not_signed_in` after sign-out. But the asymmetry is unexplained, the kv map is keyed per (tenant, vault) and only grows across a long session with several tenants/vaults, and a long-running fan-out that outlives sign-out keeps its `Arc<GraphClient>` and stops only when its next `bearer()` fails (dispatch::SessionDead) — sign_out cancels none of the three flags, so a bulk write continues until that failure and a run in its final local phase can still `cache.put` a `{tenant}|…` entry (e.g. audit.rs:441-446) after `invalidate_tenant` swept the tenant. The window is small, but it is the same-tenant/different-operator case the sign_out comment says it exists to prevent.
findings.proposal: In sign_out remove the tenant's entries from all five client maps (`kv_clients.lock().retain(|(t, _), _| t != &tenant.tenant_id)` plus arm/la `remove`), and add a repo_invariants check that every `Mutex<HashMap<…>>` client field on AppState is referenced in sign_out (or document why graph/exchange are the only two). Drop the 'cancel all three flags on sign_out' part, or tenant-scope it: the flags are process-wide, so cancelling them on sign-out of tenant A would also abort a run on tenant B, and in-flight runs already stop at their next `bearer()` via the SessionDead latch. The post-invalidate `cache.put` window is real but tiny and tenant-scoped; if it matters, guard the final put on the session still being signed in rather than on a flag.
findings.verifier_notes: Asymmetry confirmed: auth.rs:54-55 prunes only graph_clients and exchange_clients, while state.rs:207-214 declares kv_clients/arm_clients/la_clients, which are referenced nowhere outside state.rs (never pruned, kv keyed per (tenant, vault) so it grows monotonically). Introduced with the sign_out clearing in 06af5cc with no comment on why only two maps. Not a credential leak — every client holds a ScopedTokenAdapter that asks the auth singleton per request (token_adapter.rs:70-80). The cancel-flags proposal is the weak part: CancelFlag instances are process-wide, not per tenant, so the proposed `audit_cancel.cancel()` etc. in a per-tenant sign_out has cross-tenant side effects, and the runs it would stop already terminate via dispatch::SessionDead on the next token failure. The cache.put-after-invalidate observation (audit.rs:441-446) is accurate but the window is a few local statements and the data is the same tenant's.

findings.title: AppState cancel-flag field docs describe the retired AtomicBool reset model and name a command that does not exist
findings.rationale: CancelInner's own doc (state.rs:42-56) explains that `reset()` was removed precisely because it was a destructive write, yet the three field docs 40 lines below still say 'Reset to `false` at the top of every run' / 'Reset at the top of every sweep'. `audit_cancel` is also flipped by `cancel_bulk`, and `sweep_cancel` covers the KV sweep and mailbox probe and is flipped by `cancel_resource_sweep`, none of which the docs mention. F030 covers the stale reset narrative in run_bulk_seq, the deep-dive and cancel.rs, but not these field docs, which are the first thing a reader of AppState sees.
findings.proposal: Rewrite the three field docs: name every command that claims each flag and every command that cancels it, drop the 'Reset…' sentences, and reference `CancelFlag::claim`. If the flags are split per the other findings, do it in the same edit.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence real: state.rs:215-216 says 'Reset to `false` at the top of every run', :218-221 'Reset at the top of every sweep; flipped by `cancel_site_sweep`', :223-226 'Reset at the top of every backup/restore', while CancelInner's own doc (state.rs:42-56) explains reset() was removed and CancelFlag has no reset. `cancel_site_sweep` does not exist — the command is cancel_resource_sweep (sharepoint.rs:999, lib.rs:209). The docs also omit that audit_cancel is cancelled by cancel_bulk (bulk.rs:132-133) and claimed by 10 bulk commands plus the AAP migration, and that sweep_cancel is claimed by sweep_key_vault_access (keyvault_rbac.rs:96) and find_mailbox_reachers (permission_tester.rs:456). findings.title: claims.rs round-trip test pins the F070 wire-format bug: it asserts TransformationID is emitted and ID is absent, with no Microsoft-documented fixture
findings.rationale: An encoder->decoder round trip through one codec is a tautology for a wire format; the only external oracle is Microsoft's documented definition string, and none of the 8 claims tests uses one (contrast `the_two_thumbprint_fields_are_different_encodings_of_the_same_bytes`, which pins `DOC_CKI`/`DOC_THUMBPRINT` copied from Microsoft's reference). Microsoft's sample is `{"Source":"transformation","ID":"DataJoin","TransformationId":"JoinTheData",...}` with `OutputClaims[].ClaimTypeReferenceId == "DataJoin"`, so the entry needs BOTH keys. Because the test asserts the wrong shape, the F070 fix will fail this test and look like a regression; a maintainer 'fixing the test' would restore the bug.
findings.proposal: Replace lines 440-443 and 453-455 with `a_transformation_entry_matches_microsofts_documented_shape`: fixture = Microsoft's documented definition string (Source transformation, ID DataJoin, TransformationId JoinTheData, ClaimsTransformation with OutputClaims ClaimTypeReferenceId DataJoin); assert `parse_claims_definition` yields `id == Some("DataJoin")` and a new `transformation_id == Some("JoinTheData")`; assert `build_claims_definition` of that DTO emits both `ID` and `TransformationID`/`TransformationId` (read case-tolerantly) and that the OutputClaims reference resolves to the schema ID. Add the thumbprint test's rule to the module doc: wire-format tests use a Microsoft-documented sample, never a hand-built expectation. Lands with F070's DTO change.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is real: claims.rs:46-53 emits `TransformationID` INSTEAD of `ID` for a transformation-sourced entry, claims.rs:204 folds `ID`/`TransformationID` into one `id`, and the test at claims.rs:440-443 asserts `entry.get("ID").is_none()`. Microsoft's documented sample (learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity-platform/claims-customization-powershell, 'Use a claims transformation in tokens') is `{"Source":"transformation","ID":"DataJoin","TransformationId":"JoinTheData","JwtClaimType":"JoinedData"}` with `OutputClaims[].ClaimTypeReferenceId == "DataJoin"`, and the reference page states OutputClaims' `ClaimTypeReferenceId` 'is joined with the ID of the claim schema entry' while `TransformationID` 'must match the ID element of the transformation entry' — so both keys are required and the current shape can never resolve the output claim. Parsing Microsoft's sample today yields id="DataJoin" and silently drops `TransformationId` (the parser also only accepts the `TransformationID` casing, not the sample's `TransformationId`), so a re-save would emit `TransformationID: DataJoin` — worse than the input. No claims test uses a Microsoft fixture; the only non-tautological ones (463, 481-486) cover GroupFilter and the bool/string flag. The sso/mod.rs:1907-1912 comment quoted is real and is the same lesson. Severity medium is honest for a test that will make the F070 fix look like a regression. One extra note for the fix: Microsoft's PowerShell sample spells the top-level key `ClaimsTransformations` while the Graph resource doc and reference table use `ClaimsTransformation` (claims.rs:22 uses the latter); a case/plural-tolerant read would be prudent.

findings.title: Every plan_redundant_removals test passes `|_, _| false`, so the fail-closed veto branch that F022 breaks is dead in the suite; a for_test handler round trip would hit F022 by construction
findings.rationale: The `broader_is_confined` parameter exists only for the fail-closed veto, yet six tests pass a constant `false`, so the veto->skipped contract documented at 373-377 is unasserted and F022 (`continue` with no `skipped.push`) is invisible. `AppState::for_test` has no signed-in tenant, so `exchange_client` returns `not_signed_in`, `mail_scopes` becomes empty, and `broader_is_confined` returns true for every Graph mail permission — a handler-level test would have reported `Ok { removed: [], skipped: [] }` for an app with Mail.ReadWrite + Mail.Read and made the bug obvious.
findings.proposal: (1) `plan_reports_a_narrower_whose_only_cover_is_vetoed_as_skipped`: required=[Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Read], both granted, veto `|_, b| b == "Mail.ReadWrite"` -> `plan.is_empty()` AND `skipped == ["Mail.Read"]` (fails today). (2) `a_veto_never_plans_a_removal`: same fixture with `|_, _| true` -> `plan.is_empty()`. (3) Split `remediate_remove_redundant_permissions` into `_core(&AppState, ..)` and drive it with `AppState::for_test` + wiremock `GET /v1.0/applications/{id}` (both roles declared and granted): expect `skipped == ["Mail.Read"]` and `server.received_requests()` contains no PATCH/DELETE.
findings.verifier_notes: All six `plan_redundant_removals` call sites pass `|_, _| false` (remediation.rs:577, 593, 605, 624, 637, 648). The veto path at 256-264 filters vetoed broaders and then `continue`s with no `skipped.push`, contradicting the in-code contract at 373-377 ('the value shows up in `skipped` saying so') AND docs/architecture/audit-findings-and-remediation.md:238-240 ('if the broader grant has since been revoked or scoped away … the value is reported `skipped`, never removed'). `exchange_client` (exchange/mod.rs:90-99) returns `not_signed_in` when `tenant_context` is absent, which is exactly `AppState::for_test`'s state (state.rs:283-309), so `mail_scopes` is empty (remediation.rs:401) and `broader_is_confined` is true for every scopable Graph mail permission — a handler-level test would report `removed: [], skipped: []` for Mail.ReadWrite+Mail.Read. Proposed test (1) fails today by construction; (3) needs the `_core` split because `remediate_remove_redundant_permissions` (300-490) is monolithic over `State`. Not a documented decision anywhere. Medium is fair: the missing oracle hides a fail-closed contract violation on a security remediation.

findings.title: EntraReach and the Option-returning grant readers have no 'read failed' representation, so no fixture can express the F055/F056/F057 inputs; the 15 synthesize tests are exhaustive over a type that already lost the information
findings.rationale: `synthesize` is the tested seam and its table is thorough, but the failing input — a Graph read error — cannot be handed to it: `Option<Vec<String>>` folds Err into None and `EntraReach` has no variant for it, so F056 (`None => NotHeld` -> definitive `no_access`) is unreachable from any test by construction. The SharePoint side has the same shape (`Option<HeldSharePointGrants>`; `test_site_access` 1077-1101 handles None only when an entry was found), so F055 is equally untestable. F057's candidate discovery is inline in `find_mailbox_reachers` behind `State`.
findings.proposal: Change `orgwide_mailbox_grant` to `Result<Option<Vec<String>>, GraphError>` (or add `EntraReach::Unreadable`) and map Err -> `Unreadable`; add `an_unreadable_entra_grant_is_unknown_not_no_access`: `synthesize("a@x.com", &EntraReach::Unreadable, &RbacReach::None{had_assignments:false})` -> verdict "unknown", `has_access == false`, detail names the failed read. For sites, extract `site_verdict(held: Option<&HeldSharePointGrants>, hit: Option<EntryHit>, label)` (F068's shape) and add `no_entry_and_unreadable_grants_is_unknown` (None, None -> "unknown", never the 'holds no organization-wide SharePoint grant' sentence). For F057, extract `discover_mailbox_candidates(graph_assigned, ews_assigned)` and assert an EWS-only principal appears with `held == [EWS_FULL_ACCESS_AS_APP]`.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: `orgwide_mailbox_grant -> Option<Vec<String>>` uses `.ok()??` (permission_tester.rs:63-75) so a Graph error and 'no SP' are indistinguishable; `EntraReach` (177-192) has no unreadable variant; `None => EntraReach::NotHeld` at 404-411; `sharepoint_grants_held -> Option<HeldSharePointGrants>` (881-887) whose own doc says the caller 'must then report unknown', yet `test_site_access` (1091-1101) returns a definitive `no_access` with the 'holds no organization-wide SharePoint grant' sentence when no entry is found regardless of `held` being None. Every `synthesize` test (1358-1489) uses one of the five variants (NotHeld in six). The module doc (line 6) promises a missing right 'surfaces as an unknown verdict, never a hard error', so this is a contract the type cannot express, not a deliberate design. The one place None IS mapped to `unknown` (371-389) is the no-Exchange-client branch, which conflates the same two causes. Proposal shape (Result/Unreadable variant + extracted `site_verdict`) is consistent with how `probe_candidate` (748-770) already distinguishes `Err` from `Ok(None)`. Medium is honest.

findings.title: audit.rs tests the cache guard exhaustively but nothing tests what feeds `degraded`; score_one's swallowed SP lookup (F023) returns a clean Ok(AuditItem) the guard cannot see
findings.rationale: The predicate test proves 'degraded non-empty blocks the cache' for all 8 combinations, and `a_dead_session_stops_the_audit_but_one_bad_app_does_not` (1621) proves whole-item failures classify correctly — but a failed SP lookup becomes neither: score_one returns `Ok(AuditItem)` with `orgwide == HashSet::new()`, so the run scores the app as scoped, `degraded` stays empty and the guard is fed a lie. `ScoreCtx` (860-880) is `Arc<GraphClient>` + `Arc<Cache>` + resolver, i.e. constructible over wiremock, so this is a missing producer test, not an untestable path.
findings.proposal: Make score_one report coverage: return `(AuditItem, Option<AuditCoverageGap>)` or take `&Mutex<Vec<AuditCoverageGap>>`, pushing `GraphAppRoleAssignments` (or a new `ServicePrincipalLookup`) on the Err arm. Add `a_failed_sp_lookup_degrades_the_run_and_blocks_the_cache`: wiremock `GET /v1.0/servicePrincipals?$filter=appId eq 'app-1'` -> 503 (retry budget exhausted), one app with a Graph mail role granted; assert the gap is reported and `run_is_cacheable(false, false, &degraded) == false`. F029's source-scan pin of the `cache.put` guard is complementary, not a substitute.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: `score_one` swallows the lean SP lookup error to `None` and returns `Ok(AuditItem)` (audit.rs:1490-1497); the only `degraded` producers are the three tenant-wide gaps (246), `PerPrincipalScoring` (381) and `PermissionResolution` (389) — none inside `score_one`. The exhaustive guard test (1664-1680) tests only the predicate. Reachability nuance worth recording: `seed_lean_sps_from_index` (graph service_principals.rs:284-314) seeds only positive matches and is capped at the bucket size, so an app not in the index (or beyond the cap) falls to a live `GET /servicePrincipals?$filter=appId eq` in `get_service_principal_by_app_id_lean` (91-98) that can fail independently of the already-gapped index read — so the swallowed Err is a real, uncovered hole with a healthy index. With `sp == None` the app loses `has_admin_consent` and its org-wide grant lookup and is scored as holding nothing, and `run_is_cacheable` is fed an empty `degraded`. `ScoreCtx` (860-880) is plain Arcs/maps so a wiremock producer test is feasible. `ServicePrincipalIndex` gap (1170) covers the whole-index failure only. Medium is fair.

findings.title: backup.rs's only wiremock test constructs a SessionDead it never asserts and fixtures a 500 that can never latch it; Pass 3 and the restore passes are AppHandle-bound so F039/F038/F037 had no test that could exist
findings.rationale: The test passes a fresh `SessionDead` and never reads `is_dead()`; its failing fixture is a 500 (Transient), so `note_graph_failures` (349-352) never trips in the suite and the latch is asserted nowhere. Pass 2/3 helpers and every restore pass take `&AppHandle`, so no test can construct them — which is how Pass 3 shipped with no `SessionDead`, swallowing per-MI failures, and how no code path ever emits the documented `kind == "managedIdentity"`. `backup_app_chunk` already has the right seam (`report: &(dyn Fn(usize) + Sync)`); the sibling passes do not.
findings.proposal: (1) `a_reauth_fatal_read_latches_the_session`: same fixture but obj-2's GET returns the auth-failure shape whose `ui_code()` is `refresh_missing`/`not_signed_in` (or drive `note_graph_failures` directly with a `GraphError` whose ui_code is fatal) and assert `session.is_dead()`; assert a Transient 500 does NOT latch. (2) Give `backup_managed_identities` the `report` closure + `&SessionDead` seam and test: `$batch` 503, `/servicePrincipals/mi-1/appRoleAssignments` 500 -> `skipped == [SkippedObject{kind:"managedIdentity", object_id:"mi-1", ..}]`, plus the latch case. (3) `restore_managed_identities` over wiremock: `list_managed_identities` -> 503 -> one ManualItem whose reason says the destination could not be read (never 'not found — recreate via IaC'); `restore_enterprise_app` with `get_service_principal_by_app_id` -> 503 -> reason distinguishes Err from Ok(None).
findings.verifier_notes: All quoted evidence is real. backup.rs:1097-1104 passes `&SessionDead::new()` and never reads `is_dead()`; obj-2's fixture is a 500 (Transient, 1067-1070), so `note_graph_failures` (346-353) is never observed latching anywhere in the suite. `backup_managed_identities` (675-683) takes `&AppHandle` and has no `SessionDead`; its phase-1 per-item errors `unwrap_or_default` (694-705) with no `skipped` push, and `SkippedObject::new` is only ever called with "application" (406/416/426) and "enterpriseApp" (572), so the documented `managedIdentity` kind (dto/backup.rs:78) is dead. `backup_enterprise_chunk` (512) is also AppHandle-bound. restore.rs: `list_managed_identities().await.unwrap_or_default()` (733) turns a failed destination read into 'every MI not yet recreated', and `restore_enterprise_app` (653-663) folds `Err` and `Ok(None)` into 'Service principal was not created (the app had none in the backup)'. restore.rs has 7 pure `#[test]`s (937-1134), no wiremock. Medium is honest for a DR artifact.

findings.title: SiteSweepResult fixture and DTO have no truncation dimension, so the F059 regression test ('a capped sweep is not complete and not cached') cannot be written until the type carries it
findings.rationale: The nearest oracle, `a_failed_site_increments_failed_and_never_reads_as_no_grants` (1174), tests the per-site fold; the cap is applied one layer up (`list_all_sites(MAX_SITES_PER_SWEEP)` at 843, silently `truncate(max)` in the graph client) and neither the result struct nor the cache guard has a field for it. The audit's sibling `AuditExportCoverage.truncated` is iterated by `only_a_complete_undegraded_run_is_cacheable`; the sweep has no such predicate to table-test.
findings.proposal: Add `#[serde(default)] truncated: bool` to `SiteSweepResult` and `AppSiteAccessDto` (carried by `from_sweep`) and include it in `is_complete`; make `list_all_sites` return `(Vec<Site>, bool)` like `list_applications_all`; extract `sweep_is_cacheable(cancelled, sites_failed, truncated)` beside the cache write and table-test all 8 combinations exactly like audit.rs:1664; add a dto test that a truncated sweep `!is_complete()`.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: `SiteSweepResult` fixture (sharepoint.rs:1234-1241) and DTO `is_complete` (dto/sharepoint.rs:130-132) have no truncation dimension; cache guard is `!cancelled && sites_failed == 0` (988). `list_all_sites(max)` silently `out.truncate(max)` and returns `Ok` (graph client/sharepoint.rs:87-106), and the caller only passes `MAX_SITES_PER_SWEEP = 5_000` (758, 843) — the sole 'truncated' comment in sharepoint.rs (956) is about a dead-session partial run, not the cap. Precedent for the proposed shape exists: `list_applications_all(q, cap)` returns `(Vec, truncated)` and the audit consumes it at audit.rs:230-234. `AppSiteAccessDto::from_sweep` (dto 109-126) would need the field too. No doc mentions the cap as a deliberate silent limit (sharepoint-selected.md's only '5 000' is the per-library scope guidance). Medium is fair: at >5 000 sites an empty per-app list would read as 'no grants' under `is_complete()`.

findings.title: sp_index_tests is a weaker copy of its app_name_index twin: the untyped-get test asserts only `.is_none()` (which the twin's own comment says cannot tell a miss from an eviction) and the invalidate_app_lists case is missing

findings.title: sso/mod.rs: the cert-lifetime gate is table-tested but the OIDC secret lifetime has no gate and no twin test (F074); F071/F075 sit in State-bound bodies with zero wiremock coverage although configure_saml/configure_oidc already take &GraphClient

findings.title: grant_single_permission_core, grant_admin_consent_core and create_application_core already take &GraphClient, so F001/F004 partial-write regression tests need no AppState refactor — they were simply never written

The seam existed; no partial-failure test was added, so the 'Err after real writes' shape (which the same file fixed elsewhere with `(outcome, Option<UiError>)` at 887-890) went unnoticed.
findings.proposal: `grant_single_permission_core_reports_the_landed_manifest_patch_when_sp_creation_fails`: GET /v1.0/applications/{id} 200 (no SP), PATCH 204, GET /servicePrincipals?$filter=appId 200 empty, POST /servicePrincipals 503 -> today `Err`; after the fix `(GrantResult{declared:true,..}, Some(err))`; assert `server.received_requests()` includes the PATCH. Same for `grant_admin_consent_core` (SP POST 201 then appRoleAssignments 503). `create_application_core_carries_the_new_object_id_on_partial_failure`: POST /applications 201 {id:"obj-1"} then POST /servicePrincipals 503 -> error names obj-1 (the `augment_with_object_id` shape sso/mod.rs already uses). One correction to the proposal: graph's `make_client` is `pub(crate)` inside the graph crate's test module (client/tests/common.rs:45), not importable from the desktop crate — the tests need a local constructor (see finding 10).

findings.title: F054's two halves are each tested but never joined: targets_from_declared is proven to include EWS while the only resolver-level test feeds a non-mail permission, so the hardcoded Graph resource in resolve_mail_scopes was never exercised with full_access_as_app
findings.rationale: The resolver test proves the non-mail short-circuit by pointing the client at an unreachable base (`127.0.0.1:9`) and asserting `Ok(empty)`; nobody wrote the inverse — that a mail-scopable value does NOT short-circuit — and no test passes `EWS_FULL_ACCESS_AS_APP` through `resolve_mail_scopes*`, which is the one place the Graph-only filter drops it. This is distinct from F171 (duplicate pure tests): it is the missing join between two well-tested layers.
findings.proposal: `the_ews_scope_is_resolved_not_short_circuited`: same unreachable-base client, `&[EWS_FULL_ACCESS_AS_APP.to_string()]` -> assert `Err` (the probe was attempted), never `Ok(empty)`; a second variant for `["Mail.Read"]` as the positive control. After the F054 fix, a wiremock EXO base returning a `Scoped` row asserts the map contains the `full_access_as_app` key.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: exchange/tests.rs has exactly one `resolve_mail_scopes*` test (210-229) and it feeds `User.Read.All`; `declared_targets_span_graph_and_the_legacy_ews_scope` (81) proves targets include EWS but stops there. In mail_scopes.rs, `resolve_mail_scopes` filters with `exchange_role_for_resource_permission(MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID, p)` (108-116); `core::scoping` (106-117) maps the Graph resource to `graph_mail_role(value)`, so `full_access_as_app` yields None and is dropped — an EWS-only set short-circuits to `Ok(empty)`. `get_mail_permission_scopes` feeds `targets_from_declared(..).graph_value` (312-315, whose comment explicitly includes EWS) into it (336) and re-filters with Graph again at 341, so EWS never produces a `MailScopeEntry`; the held path (424-435) gets `Unknown` for `full_access_as_app`. So the proposed inverse test would fail today and expose F054. Note the test target must be `resolve_mail_scopes` (the enriched path); `resolve_mail_scopes_audit_cached` (228-245) legitimately sees Graph-only values because the audit routes EWS through `ews_full_access_sps` separately. Medium is fair.

As a standalone refactor it is low severity; its value is as an enabler for the handler tests proposed elsewhere.

findings.title: `resolve_password_window` and `generate_self_signed` return bare `String` errors, forcing substring oracles; the CA `ca_unavailable` collapse is a documented shared design and should stay
findings.rationale: In each case two distinct causes (licence vs consent; end-before-start vs over-cap; bad CN vs bad validity) share one code or a `Result<_, String>`, so the test's only discriminator is copy text — a wording edit breaks the suite while a swapped classification would not necessarily fail it, and the frontend cannot branch on the cause either. The rest of the slice's prose asserts (readiness role names, tester `detail` sentences) sit beside a typed `Verdict`/`verdict` assertion and are acceptable as secondary checks.
findings.proposal: Give `resolve_password_window` and `generate_self_signed` small error enums (e.g. `EndNotAfterStart | LifetimeOverCap | EmptyCommonName | ValidityOutOfRange`) with a `code()` mapped into `UiError`, and rewrite credentials.rs:375/394 and cert.rs:425 to match variants (keep one prose assertion on the exact user-facing sentence). For Conditional Access, keep the single `ca_unavailable` code; if a typed discriminator is wanted, have `premium_feature_err` classify via an internal enum tested in graph_err, and delete the duplicate prose test in conditional_access.rs rather than adding new codes.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is real: conditional_access.rs:249-259 discriminates license vs consent by message substring; credentials.rs:43 maps a bare `String` (`resolve_password_window -> Result<_, String>`, 59-68) to the single `invalid_secret_window` code and tests 375/394 substring-match; `generate_self_signed -> Result<GeneratedCert, String>` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/cert.rs:92-95, not commands/applications/) with `contains(&MAX_VALIDITY_DAYS.to_string())` at 425. But the CA half is a documented deliberate decision: `map_ca_err`'s doc (conditional_access.rs:138-142) says 'a missing license vs. consent gets a distinct message, every variant degrades to `ca_unavailable`', sharing `graph_err::premium_feature_err` with the Activity tab; the frontend branches only on the code and renders the message (conditional_access_tab.rs:66-68), so no consumer needs the split, and graph_err already has its own (also prose-based) `license_vs_consent_split_and_retryable_classification` test (125-160) that the CA test duplicates. Splitting `ca_unavailable` would touch two tabs' bindings for no behavioural gain. The `Result<_, String>` helpers are the legitimate, small part.

findings.title: progress.rs's runtime generic is the wrong seam; the ProgressSink trait bulk.rs proved works is private and re-invented as a closure in backup.rs, leaving 18 AppHandle-bound emit sites that keep audit/backup/restore/sharepoint/tester untestable
findings.rationale: The lib.rs `#[cfg(test)] #[path = "../build_support.rs"]` mount (425-427) is the right tool for pure parsers that must also compile into build.rs; progress.rs has no such need, and its `R` generic is unusable without `tauri/test` (deliberately dropped, bulk.rs:40-45). Nothing is silently excluded today — there are no feature-gated tests — but the trait seam that unblocked bulk's four driver tests was never lifted, so every other long-running command's inner loop still takes a concrete `AppHandle` and cannot be constructed in a test. This is the structural cause behind the backup/restore/audit gaps above; F015 covers only the misleading doc comment.
findings.proposal: Move `ProgressSink` into progress.rs as `pub(crate) trait ProgressSink { fn emit<P: Serialize + Clone>(&self, event: &'static str, payload: P); }` with `impl<R: tauri::Runtime> ProgressSink for AppHandle<R>` and a `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) struct Recorder`; change `backup_managed_identities`, `backup_enterprise_apps`, `restore::emit`, the audit fan-out and the sweep helpers to `&impl ProgressSink`; delete bulk's local trait and backup's `report` closure; reword the progress.rs doc per F015. Then the `_core` bodies proposed in the findings above need only `&AppState` + `&impl ProgressSink`.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: progress.rs:18-24 is generic over `R: tauri::Runtime` and its doc promises `MockRuntime`/`tauri::test::mock_app()`, but `tauri = { version = "2", features = [] }` (src-tauri/Cargo.toml:31) and bulk.rs:40-45 records that the `test` feature was deliberately dropped (Windows STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND), so the generic is unusable in tests. `trait ProgressSink` (bulk.rs:46-54) is private to bulk; backup.rs re-invents the seam as `report: &(dyn Fn(usize) + Sync)` (359-364). `emit_progress(` has 18 call sites across 7 files (audit 3, backup 1, bulk 7, keyvault_rbac 2, permission_tester 2, restore 1, sharepoint 2); concrete `app_handle: &AppHandle` params at backup.rs:512, 679, 941, restore.rs:921 (and export.rs:40). No `cfg(feature`/`tauri::test`/`MockRuntime` outside the two doc comments, so nothing is silently excluded today — the finding says so. lib.rs:425-427 is a different mechanism. This is the structural root of findings 3/4/5's untestability; medium is fair for an enabler. The proposed generic-method trait is fine with `&impl ProgressSink` (not `dyn`).

findings.title: set_saml_urls, set_oidc_redirect_uris and set_claims_mapping bust both tenant-wide indexes (invalidate_app_lists) for detail-only writes — the F026 mis-tier in sso, unnoticed because no SSO handler has a test
findings.rationale: None of these three writes adds, removes or renames an application or service principal, so nothing in `sp_index`, `app_name_index`, the Enterprise Apps list or the search corpus changes; yet each drops all of them, forcing the multi-second `/applications` + `/servicePrincipals` re-enumeration the tiered invalidators exist to avoid (cache.rs:134-147 documents the cost). `app_roles.rs` uses `invalidate_app_details` for the same kind of in-place PATCH. Not a documented decision: no comment justifies the tier at any of the three sites. `rotate_saml_signing_certificate` (746) is borderline (SP keyCredentials) and already busts the cert board separately.
findings.proposal: Replace the three `invalidate_app_lists` calls with `invalidate_app_details(&state.cache, &tenant_id)` (the SSO tab reads live; the detail payload embeds identifierUris/redirectUris). Once the SSO bodies get `_core(&AppState, ..)` seams, add the credentials.rs-shaped test: after a successful `PATCH /v1.0/applications/{id}` the detail row is gone and `sp_index_hit`/`app_name_index_hit` still return `Some`. Consider a `repo_invariants` rule that `invalidate_app_lists` may follow only a `create_*`/`delete_*`/`ensure_service_principal`/rename call in the same function.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: `set_saml_urls` (sso/mod.rs:706-708), `set_oidc_redirect_uris` (1727-1729) and `set_claims_mapping` (1662) each call `invalidate_app_lists` after an in-place application PATCH / SP policy assignment; `rotate_saml_signing_certificate` (746) does too. `invalidate_app_lists` (applications/cache.rs:107-133) drops `sp_index`, `app_name_index`, the search corpus, the MI list and the credential-expiry list, with the re-enumeration cost documented at 134-147. Nothing those writes change lives in the list tier: `ApplicationListRowDto` (dto/applications.rs:37-50) carries no identifierUris/web/spa, `EnterpriseApplicationDto` (dto/enterprise_application.rs:10-26) carries no SSO/claims fields, the search corpus derives from the two name indexes, and `core::audit` has no redirect/identifier rule. The cached `ApplicationDetail` (applications/mod.rs:238-244) embeds the `Application` (`identifier_uris`, models.rs:249), so `invalidate_app_details` is the right tier, exactly as `app_roles.rs:336-339` does for its in-place PATCH. No comment justifies the list tier at any of the three sites, and no SSO handler is tested. Medium is fair: every SSO URL edit forces the tens-of-seconds tenant re-scan the tiered invalidators exist to avoid.

findings.title: managed_identity.rs tests stop at ARM scope-string classification; the per-subscription flatten that duplicates management-group assignments (F072) has no test and no seam
findings.rationale: The nearest test proves the 'Management group' label is produced for MG-scoped ids, i.e. the code expects such rows, but the fan-out/flatten that receives the same MG row once per subscription is inline in the `State` command and untested; a dedupe-by-assignment-id regression would ship silently.
findings.proposal: Extract `flatten_assignments(per_sub: Vec<(String, Option<Vec<RoleAssignment>>)>) -> Vec<(String, RoleAssignment)>` that dedupes on `RoleAssignment.id` (keeping the first subscription label, or labelling MG rows by scope) and test: two subscriptions each returning assignment `ra-1` at `/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/mg` plus one sub-scoped `ra-2` -> exactly two rows.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified: managed_identity.rs:251-258 flattens `per_sub` inline with no dedupe, and rows are built one per (subscription, assignment) at 305-325; `scope_level` returns 'Management group' (424, tested at 523) so MG-inherited rows are expected input. ARM's `list_role_assignments_for_principal` (azapptoolkit-arm client.rs:58-70) queries `/subscriptions/{sub}/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments?$filter=principalId eq '..'`, which returns assignments inherited from management-group/root scope, so one MG assignment surfaces once per subscription and inflates the roles table. Tests (497-557) never construct `per_sub`. Dedupe on `RoleAssignment.id` is sound because ARM assignment ids are full resource ids that embed the assignment's own scope, so an MG assignment has one id across subscriptions. Low is honest.

findings.title: `throttled` error message leaks Rust `Option` Debug formatting ("retry after Some(30)s" / "retry after Nones") and never says to wait
findings.evidence:
crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/http_error.rs:76-77
            #[error("throttled (429); retry after {retry_after_secs:?}s")]
            Throttled { retry_after_secs: Option<u64> },

crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/error.rs:25-26
    #[error("throttled (429); retry after {retry_after_secs:?}s")]
    Throttled { retry_after_secs: Option<u64> },

crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/lib.rs:133-138 (no_hint form used for GraphError)
                    UiError {
                        code: err.ui_code().to_string(),
                        retryable: err.is_retryable(),
                        message: err.to_string(),
                    }

apps/desktop/web-rs/src/components/ui/detail_load_error.rs:35
            <Body1 class="form-error">{message}</Body1>
findings.rationale: `{retry_after_secs:?}` is the Debug formatter for `Option<u64>`, so the string every client (Graph via the macro, Exchange by hand, ARM/KV via the macro) hands the UI is literally `throttled (429); retry after Some(30)s` or `throttled (429); retry after Nones`. `ui_error_from!` copies `err.to_string()` into `UiError.message`, and DetailLoadError / the toast sink render it verbatim, so after `with_retries` has already exhausted three Retry-After waits the operator reads Rust internals instead of "Microsoft Graph is throttling; wait N seconds". No frontend site branches on `throttled`, and the GUI fixtures use the friendly string `"Too many requests"` (tests/gui/credentials_dashboard.rs:36, managed_identities.rs:68) that the backend never produces, so no test can see the leak. This is not a documented trade-off; the http_retry docs go to lengths to honour Retry-After exactly but the value never reaches the screen in readable form.
findings.proposal: Replace the derived Display for the `Throttled` arm in `http_error_enum!` (and the hand-written `ExchangeError`) with a manual `impl Display` fragment: `Some(n)` → "{api} is throttling requests (429). Wait {n} s, then retry."; `None` → "{api} is throttling requests (429). Wait a moment, then retry." (the macro already has `api_display`, so the API name is available). Add a unit test in `arm`/`keyvault` error-conformance tests asserting the message contains neither "Some(" nor "None", and change the two GUI fixtures to the real backend string so the rendering is pinned end-to-end.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is real. crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/http_error.rs:76 and crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/error.rs:26 both use `{retry_after_secs:?}` — Debug on Option — so the Display is literally `throttled (429); retry after Some(30)s` / `retry after Nones`. `ui_error_from!` (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/lib.rs:126-129 hint form, 141-145 no_hint form for Graph) copies `err.to_string()` into `UiError.message`; DetailLoadError renders it verbatim (apps/desktop/web-rs/src/components/ui/detail_load_error.rs:35) and so does the toast (`{t.message}`). No frontend code branches on `throttled` (only a bulk_action_bar unit test constructs the code), and the two GUI fixtures use the string "Too many requests" (tests/gui/credentials_dashboard.rs:36, managed_identities.rs:68) which the backend never emits. No unit test pins the Display text — graph tests match on the variant only (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/tests/transport.rs:324-330), and the ARM/KV error_conformance tests check codes/retryability, not messages. The backend does hand-write friendly text for two gated readers (graph_err.rs:91, activity.rs:172) but every ordinary command goes through `UiError::from`. Not a documented trade-off. Refinement to the proposal: no manual `impl Display` is needed — thiserror accepts extra format args with `.field` shorthand, e.g. `#[error("throttled (429); retry after {}", .retry_after_secs.map_or("a moment".to_string(), |s| format!("{s} s")))]`, which keeps the macro's derive intact for both the macro and the hand-written ExchangeError.

findings.title: Network errors drop the cause: `err.to_string()` on reqwest 0.13 yields only "error sending request for url (…)", hiding DNS/timeout/TLS/proxy at all six sites and in the retry log
findings.rationale: Since reqwest 0.12 the `Display` impl no longer appends `source()`, so `err.to_string()` yields `error sending request for url (https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/applications?$top=999)` for a DNS failure, a connect timeout, a TLS interception failure and a proxy 407 alike. The desktop shows this verbatim via DetailLoadError / toast (`network: error sending request for url (…)`), and the sign-in card shows `error [network]: http: error sending request for url (https://login.microsoftonline.com/…/oauth2/v2.0/token)` with the generic hint. The one piece of information an operator behind a corporate proxy needs ("connection timed out" vs "dns error" vs "invalid peer certificate") is available on `reqwest::Error` (`is_timeout()`, `is_connect()`, `source()` chain) and is discarded at all six construction sites. README/F247 asks for proxy/TLS guidance; without the cause on screen, that guidance cannot be matched to a symptom.
findings.proposal: Add a dependency-free `azapptoolkit_core::http_retry::describe_error_chain(e: &dyn std::error::Error) -> String` that joins Display of `e` and each `source()` (hyper/hyper-util already say "client error (Connect)", "dns error: …", "connection refused", "invalid peer certificate"), and use it at the six `Network(...)` sites and in a manual Display for `AuthError::Http`. Optionally prefix a class (`timed out` / `could not connect`) at the call sites that hold the concrete `reqwest::Error`, where `is_timeout()/is_connect()` are available without touching core's dependency set. Also log the described error in `with_retries`' warn line. Unit-test with a refused localhost port asserting the cause appears.
findings.verifier_notes: Substance confirmed: reqwest 0.13.5 (Cargo.lock:3915-3916) Display at registry src/error.rs:257-304 writes only the kind + ` for url (…)` and never the `source()` chain. All six construction sites use `err.to_string()` (graph transport.rs:571 and 585, arm/transport.rs:60, keyvault/client.rs:196, exchange transport.rs:188 and 196), and `AuthError::Http` is `#[error("http: {0}")]` (auth/error.rs:47-48). Worse than stated for Graph/ARM/KV: `with_retries` logs only label/attempt/retry_after (http_retry.rs:205-211), never the error, so the cause is not even in tracing; only Exchange's hand loop logs `?err` (exchange transport.rs:182). Two corrections: (1) README has no proxy/TLS guidance (grep proxy|TLS|firewall finds only rustls mentions), so the "README/F247 asks for proxy/TLS guidance" premise is unsupported by README itself. (2) The proposal puts the helper in azapptoolkit-core using `reqwest::Error::is_timeout()/is_connect()`, but core has no reqwest dependency (crates/azapptoolkit-core/Cargo.toml:22-26 lists only parking_lot, async-trait, tokio, url); AGENTS.md says dependencies are a cost.

findings.title: `UiError.retryable` drives a Retry action at only one toast site; `run_toast_err` discards the op it already holds
findings.rationale: The DTO contract says `retryable` advises a retry button, every client computes it via `is_retryable_code` (throttled/server_error/network_error), and the toast primitive supports a sticky Retry action — yet the only consumer is the admin-consent button in permissions_tab. `report_command_error_for` always passes `None`, and the pinning test (state/mod.rs:722-731) asserts a `network` error with `retryable: true` gets no action. errors.rs:70-74 explains the sink cannot replay because it receives only the `UiError`, but `CommandState::run_toast_err` *does* hold `op`; it just types it `FnOnce` so it cannot be re-invoked. Net effect: a 429/5xx/network failure on any of the ~24 `run`/`run_toast_err` call sites and the ~56 inline `error.set(Some(e.message))` sites is a 10-second auto-dismissing red toast (errors without an action are not sticky, toast.rs:129) with no way back except finding and re-clicking the control — the exact "dead end" the module docs say the sink exists to prevent.
findings.proposal: Scope the change to `CommandState::run_toast_err`: take `op: impl Fn(String) -> Fut + Clone + 'static` there only (leave `run`/`run_with` as FnOnce), and when `e.retryable` build a `ToastAction` that re-invokes `run_toast_err` with the same `on_ok`/`op`, passed through a new `Session::report_command_error_with_retry(&e, feature, Some(retry))`; keep `report_command_error(_for)` behaviour and flip the state/mod.rs:722 pin only for the new entry point. Alternatively trim the "retry button" sentence at crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/lib.rs:42-43 so the flag's contract matches the one hand-rolled consumer.
findings.verifier_notes: Facts check out: the only `.retryable` consumer is apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/tabs/permissions_tab.rs:121; `report_command_error_for` always passes `None` (state/errors.rs:160); the pin at state/mod.rs:722-731 asserts a retryable `network` error gets no action; only error toasts WITH an action are sticky (toast.rs `sticky = Error && has_action`); `use_command` takes `op: impl FnOnce` (use_command.rs:49). But the finding overstates the gap: (a) every load-failure surface goes through `DetailLoadError`, which ALWAYS offers Retry regardless of the flag (detail_load_error.rs:6-9), so ignoring `retryable` there is by design; (b) errors.rs:70-74 documents as a decision that the sink receives only the UiError and that call sites holding a re-runnable op replay it themselves; (c) `CommandState::run` puts the message inline next to the control that triggered it, so re-clicking is the retry; (d) counts are approximate — 24 `run`, 16 `run_toast_err` (13 in sso_tab.rs), 9 direct `report_command_error` callers, ~55 `error.set(Some(e.message))`. What is real and worth fixing: the 16 `run_toast_err` sites and 9 direct `report_command_error` sites give a 10 s auto-dismissing toast for a 429/5xx/network failure although `run_toast_err` holds the op. Converting `run`/`run_with` from FnOnce to Fn+Clone across all sites is a larger refactor than the payoff warrants.

findings.title: `unauthorized` (client 401, including the CAE "re-auth needed" path) renders as bare "unauthorized (401)" with no action; the three ui_hints tell the operator to sign out, contradicting the in-place recovery design
findings.rationale: `unauthorized` is deliberately excluded from `REAUTH_FATAL_CODES` (reauth.rs:64-81) so a fan-out keeps going — that rationale is about halting loops, not about what the operator sees. On screen a Graph 401 (revoked token, CAE challenge the silent re-mint could not satisfy) is the text `unauthorized (401)` in a toast or `unauthorized (401) [unauthorized] Retry` in DetailLoadError, while the remedy the transport itself names ("surfaces to the caller to re-auth") lives one click away as the top-bar "Refresh token" control (shell.rs:492) whose handler already falls back to `reauthenticate` on a dead session. Meanwhile the Exchange/KV/ARM hints say "Sign out and back in", which AGENTS.md ("A dead session forces re-auth in place… never sign the user out") and the shell comment ("still no sign-out, so the cached lists + audit run survive") explicitly reject, and `premium_feature_err` says "Your session expired. Sign in again" (graph_err.rs:88-91) with no control to do so. F353/F427 cover the *dead-session* codes not reaching the sink; this is the 401 class, which reaches the sink and is still a dead end.
findings.proposal: 1) Extract shell.rs's refresh-token handler into `Session::spawn_refresh_token()` (silent `refresh_session` → on `is_reauth_fatal` fall back to `reauthenticate`). 2) In `report_command_error_for`, add a branch before the plain toast: `if e.code == "unauthorized" { push_toast(Error, "Your access token was rejected — refresh it and retry.", Some("Refresh token"), Some(spawn_refresh_token)) }`. Do NOT add the code to `REAUTH_FATAL_CODES`. 3) Reword the three `Unauthorized` ui_hints and `premium_feature_err`'s Unauthorized arm to "use Refresh token (next to Sign out), then retry" — the Exchange `Forbidden { had_diagnostics: false }` hint already uses exactly that phrasing. 4) Add a GUI test next to tests/gui/reauth.rs asserting an `unauthorized` mock produces a toast with a "Refresh token" action.
findings.verifier_notes: Every quote is real: transport.rs:495-498 ("surfaces to the caller to re-auth") and 677-683 (CAE re-mint failure → `GraphError::Unauthorized`), http_error.rs:67-68 bare "unauthorized (401)", the three "Sign out and back in" hints (keyvault/error.rs:35-37, arm/error.rs:33-35, exchange/error.rs:124-128), `premium_feature_err` "Your session expired. Sign in again" (graph_err.rs:88-91), and the sink falling through to a plain toast (state/errors.rs:157-160). No frontend code branches on the string "unauthorized" (zero hits in web-rs src and tests) and tests/gui/reauth.rs covers only `refresh_missing` and `network`. The top-bar handler (shell.rs:108-150, button at 492-506) already does silent `refresh_session` → on `is_reauth_fatal` → `reauthenticate`, i.e. exactly the lever a 401 needs, and docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md:101 is headed "Force re-auth in place — never make the user sign out" — so the three hints contradict a documented invariant. Excluding `unauthorized` from `REAUTH_FATAL_CODES` is pinned by reauth.rs:64-81 and the proposal respects it. Extra support: exchange/error.rs:116-123 (the no-diagnostics 403 hint) already uses the "Refresh token (next to Sign out)" wording, so the Unauthorized hint five lines below is inconsistent within the same file. Severity medium is fair: a 401 is a dead end with advice that drops every data cache.

Pin it with a GUI assertion on the permissions_tab admin-consent failure toast (mock `grant_admin_consent` with a `forbidden` error whose message contains `\n\n`).
