findings.title: ARM, Key Vault and Exchange reads burn ~4 min (Log Analytics ~2 min) on a firewalled host before a cause-less network error; only Graph has a connect budget
findings.evidence:
crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client.rs:165-172
            .timeout(Duration::from_secs(60))
            // … Without a separate connect budget a host that
            // accepts no connection burns that whole ceiling before the retry
            // loop even sees a failure, and does it once per attempt. …
            .connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10))

crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/client.rs:36-40
        let http = reqwest::Client::builder()
            .user_agent(concat!("azapptoolkit/", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")))
            .timeout(Duration::from_secs(60))
            .build()

crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/loganalytics.rs:27-31  `.timeout(Duration::from_secs(120))` (no connect_timeout)
crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/client.rs:74-78  `.timeout(Duration::from_secs(60))` (no connect_timeout)
crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/client.rs:54-58  `.timeout(Duration::from_secs(60))` (no connect_timeout)

crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/transport.rs:56-61 (network failure → Attempt::Retry, Transient)
crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/client/transport.rs:178-188 (`if attempt < MAX_RETRIES { … sleep_with_jitter … continue; }`)
crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/http_retry.rs:30,34  MAX_RETRIES = 3; BASE_DELAY_MS = 1000

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sso/mod.rs:1282-1285
        reqwest::Client::builder()
            .timeout(Duration::from_secs(20))
            .build()
            .unwrap_or_default()
findings.rationale: The Graph client's own comment states the hazard precisely — a host that accepts no connection burns the whole total timeout once per attempt — but the fix was applied to Graph only. For a SYN-blackholed `management.azure.com`, `*.vault.azure.net`, `outlook.office365.com` or `api.loganalytics.io` (typical of an egress allow-list that admitted graph.microsoft.com only), each attempt runs to the 60 s ceiling (Linux/macOS; Windows' TCP stack gives up at ~21 s), and every transport retries network failures three times: 4×60 s + (1+2+4) s ≈ 247 s for ARM/KV/Exchange and 4×120 s + 7 s ≈ 487 s for a Log Analytics usage query. Reads have no `CancelToken`, so the operator sees a skeleton / "Loading…" / disabled button for four to eight minutes and then, per finding 2, `network: error sending request for url (…)` with no cause. Graph's worst case on the same box is 4×10 s + 7 s ≈ 47 s. The SSO metadata probe's `unwrap_or_default()` additionally falls back to a `reqwest::Client::default()` with no timeout at all if the builder ever fails.
findings.proposal: Add `.connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10))` to the four builders (arm/client.rs, arm/loganalytics.rs, exchange/client.rs, keyvault/client.rs) and to the SSO metadata probe, replacing `unwrap_or_default()` with the `expect("reqwest client builds")` the others use. To stop drift without adding reqwest to core, pin it with a repo_invariants source scan asserting every `reqwest::Client::builder()` outside azapptoolkit-auth is followed by a `.connect_timeout(` in the same expression (or house the shared builder in a crate that already depends on reqwest). Worst case for reads then drops to ~47 s, matching Graph.
findings.verifier_notes: Builders confirmed: only the Graph client sets `connect_timeout` (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client.rs:172, with the hazard comment at 165-171); ARM (arm/client.rs:36-40, 60 s), Log Analytics (arm/loganalytics.rs:27-31, 120 s), Exchange (exchange/client.rs:74-78, 60 s) and Key Vault (keyvault/client.rs:54-58, 60 s) do not; the SSO probe uses `.timeout(20 s)` + `unwrap_or_default()` (sso/mod.rs:1282-1285). `RetryBudget::may_retry` is `attempt < MAX_RETRIES` (3) so idempotent calls get 4 attempts. However the arithmetic is wrong for two cases: `with_retries` returns immediately when `reason == Transient && class == NonIdempotent` (http_retry.rs:195-203), and `retry_class_for` treats POST/PATCH as NonIdempotent (arm/transport.rs:128-133, keyvault/client.rs:267-271). Log Analytics `query` is a POST (loganalytics.rs:56-64), so a blackholed api.loganalytics.io costs ONE 120 s attempt (~2 min), not ~487 s; ARM/KV writes likewise get one attempt. The ~247 s figure holds for ARM/KV GET reads and for every Exchange cmdlet, because the Exchange hand-rolled loop (exchange transport.rs:178-188) retries network failures on all POSTs. No comment or doc records leaving the other clients out as deliberate (the Graph connect_timeout landed inside the PR #219 merge with a generic rationale). Reads indeed carry no CancelToken (AGENTS.md scopes cancellation to long-running writes). Note for the proposal: core has no reqwest dependency (core/Cargo.toml:22-26), so a `core::http_client::builder` adds a dependency edge.

findings.title: Offline at launch shows the plain sign-in card: `restore_session` folds a `network` failure into `Ok(None)` and the silent restore cannot be retried without relaunching
findings.rationale: The documented rationale ("the card is the recovery, and it already says what to do") holds for the cases the comment lists — nothing stored, a revoked token, a locked keyring — where the correct next step really is to sign in. It does not hold for the case the comment omits: the token endpoint is unreachable (laptop off-network, captive portal, proxy down). The refresh token is still valid (only `InvalidGrant` purges it), yet the operator is told to "Sign in to your tenant"; clicking opens a browser that cannot load login.microsoftonline.com, the loopback listener then waits up to 300 s (F113) and returns `loopback`, whose hint is the generic fallback. Nothing on screen ever says "you appear to be offline", and there is no way to retry the silent restore once connectivity returns short of restarting the app. The backend already computes the code (`UiError::from(err).code`) and throws it away.
findings.proposal: Keep `Result<Option<TenantContext>, UiError>` and, in `restore_session`, return `Err(ui)` only when `ui.code == "network"` (everything else stays `Ok(None)` per the documented rationale, which should be extended to name the offline case). In `Root`, on that `Err` render `SignInScreen` with a warn `Callout` ("Couldn't reach Entra ID to restore your session — check your network connection.") and a "Retry" button that re-invokes `restore_session`; add a GUI test mocking `restore_session` with a `network` error asserting the callout appears and `sign_in` is not called.
findings.verifier_notes: Code is as quoted: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/auth.rs:37-44 folds every `Err` (including `AuthError::Http` → code `network`) into `Ok(None)` after logging the code; web-rs lib.rs:167-174 ignores errors by design; only `InvalidGrant` purges the refresh token (auth/service/mod.rs:529-540), and `restore_session` (service/mod.rs:603-628) is a live token POST; the interactive loopback waits up to 300 s (service/mod.rs:274). But this is a documented deliberate decision, not an omission: the command's own doc (auth.rs:20-30) states "`Ok(None)` — never an error — is the answer for every way this can come up empty … an error toast at launch would add noise", and only its enumerated cases leave out the offline one. The consequence is also milder than described: the auth HTTP client has a 30 s timeout (service/mod.rs:95) so the restore fails fast; the interactive path ends in `loopback`/`network`, whose sign-in hints (sign_in.rs:155 and the 166 fallback) already say to check the network and retry; and nothing is lost — the keyring token survives and a normal sign-in works once online. The proposal's `RestoreOutcome` enum is a wire-shape change touching the binding, `demo::register_fixtures` and the Root match for a small UX gain.

findings.title: A mid-session token-refresh network failure surfaces as non-retryable `token_error`, not `network_error`: `token_adapter::token_error` flattens `AuthError::Http`
findings.rationale: Extends F110 (which covers `consent_required`). The same outage produces two different classifications depending on where it strikes: during the Graph call it is `network_error` (retryable: true, "network: …"); during the lazy refresh that precedes the call (`provider.bearer()` at transport.rs:498, ~every hour) it is `token_error` (retryable: false) with message `token: http: error sending request for url (https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/oauth2/v2.0/token)`. The auth-plane spelling `network` is hinted only on the sign-in card, so mid-session it never receives a hint either. Operators and any future `network_error`-specific UI treatment (finding 3) will miss the refresh-time half of network failures.
findings.proposal: In `token_adapter::token_error`, map `AuthError::Http(_)` → "network_error" only; leave `TokenExchange` as `token_error` unless `post_token` is first changed to distinguish 5xx from 4xx. Add a `core::reauth::TRANSIENT_PASSTHROUGH: &[&str] = &["network_error"]` (or extend `passthrough_code` to consult both slices) so the macro's `Token(t)` arm and ExchangeError::ui_code pass it through and `is_retryable` sees it. Pin adapter ↔ dto agreement in the dto agreement tests (lib.rs:254-297): `Http` yields `network` on the auth plane and `network_error` on the client plane, and both are retryable.
findings.verifier_notes: The split is real: token_adapter.rs:21-28 maps every AuthError other than NotSignedIn/RefreshTokenMissing/InvalidGrant/ConsentRequired — so `AuthError::Http` too — to `token_error`; the macro's `Token` arm passes through only `REAUTH_FATAL_CODES` (http_error.rs:131-133, reauth.rs:50-52); `is_retryable_code` excludes `token_error` (http_retry.rs:25-27); `From<AuthError>` maps `Http` → ("network", true) (dto lib.rs:169); the `network` hint exists only on the sign-in card (sign_in.rs:155). So an outage hitting the lazy refresh at graph transport.rs:498 surfaces as non-retryable `token_error` with "token: http: error sending request for url (…)", whereas the same outage one line later is retryable `network_error`. The proposal's second half is wrong, though: `post_token` (auth/service/mod.rs:168-198) returns `TokenExchange(format!("HTTP {status}"))` for EVERY non-2xx the body classifier does not recognise — including 400s for wrong tenant / unknown client — so mapping `TokenExchange` to `server_error` would make permanent failures retryable. The `TRANSIENT_PASSTHROUGH` slice idea is consistent with the existing `passthrough_code` pattern.

findings.title: Launch runs three concurrent full /applications paginations that one $select superset already covers
findings.evidence:
credentials.rs:63-72: `.list_applications_all(
    AppListQuery::default()
        .with_top(PAGE_SIZE)
        .with_select(vec!["id", "appId", "displayName", "passwordCredentials", "keyCredentials"]),
    Some(MAX_APPS),
)`
applications/mod.rs:53-63: `fn list_row_select() -> Vec<&'static str> { vec!["id", "appId", "displayName", "signInAudience", "publisherDomain", "createdDateTime", "passwordCredentials", "keyCredentials"] }` and :176 `client.list_applications_all(query, Some(APPS_MAX)).await?`
applications/cache.rs:334: `.list_application_index_named(Some(super::APPS_MAX))` (select `id,appId,displayName`)
home_dashboard.rs:29/44/69: `let apps = LocalResource::new(...)` / `let enterprise = ...` / `let creds = ...` all fire on mount
docs/architecture/caching-and-search.md:35: `There are exactly **two** cached tenant-wide directory enumerations, and no surface may run its own:`
findings.rationale: Home's five resources fire together on a cold tenant, so `list_applications_with_pairing` (list_row_select), `list_enterprise_applications` -> `app_name_index_cached` (id,appId,displayName) and `list_credential_expirations` (5 fields) each page the whole `/applications` collection concurrently: 3 x ceil(N/999) serial round trips (18 for 5,000 apps), two of them selecting `keyCredentials`, which applications.rs itself notes is under a 150-req/min/tenant throttle. `list_row_select` is a strict superset of both other projections, and `apps_pairing_key` and `credential_expirations_key` are invalidated by exactly the same two tiers (`invalidate_app_lists` at cache.rs:234-263 and `invalidate_app_credentials` at :277-292 both bust both keys), so the roll-up can be produced from the same scan with no freshness change. The pairing command already seeds the SP index from its own scan (mod.rs:181-193) but never seeds `app_name_index` from the `Vec<Application>` it holds, so the Enterprise card's join immediately re-enumerates the apps it just fetched. This also contradicts the caching doc's own invariant. F007 covers the SP-side duplicate; this is the /applications side.
findings.proposal: In `list_applications_with_pairing` (mod.rs ~170-220): take an `app_name_index` watch before the scan, and after the scan store (a) the lean index via `app_name_index_store_if_current`, and (b) the credential roll-up computed with `summarize_credentials` over the same `apps` under `credential_expirations_key` via `put_index_if_current` (its own watch), before converting rows. Make `list_credential_expirations` re-check the cache behind `state.single_flight(&apps_pairing_key)` (or call the pairing core) instead of scanning; make the name-index fetch share the same gate. Expected effect: 18 -> 6 `/applications` round trips at launch on a 5,000-app tenant, and the credential card lands with the apps card instead of after its own scan. Add a repo_invariants pin that `list_applications_all(` appears only in the pairing core, audit and bulk.
findings.verifier_notes: Every quoted line is real. credentials.rs:62-74 selects {id,appId,displayName,passwordCredentials,keyCredentials}; applications/mod.rs:53-64 `list_row_select` is a strict superset of that and of the `id,appId,displayName` projection `list_application_index_named` sends (graph client applications.rs:374-375, called from applications/cache.rs:333-335). home_dashboard.rs:29-82 fires `apps`, `enterprise` and `creds` together; `list_enterprise_applications` reaches `app_name_index_cached` via `indexes_cached` (enterprise_application.rs:95). The pairing core seeds only the SP index (mod.rs:179-195) and never `app_name_index`, and no `single_flight` gate exists for `apps_pairing_key` (grep: gates only in search.rs, gallery.rs, cache.rs). Both roll-ups are busted by the same two tiers (`invalidate_app_lists` cache.rs:105-133 and `invalidate_app_credentials` cache.rs:150-161 each drop `apps_pairing` and `credential_expirations`), so deriving the credential rows from the pairing scan changes no freshness contract. The 150 req/min `keyCredentials` throttle note is at crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/applications.rs:213-216. docs/CHANGELOG-archive.md:2991-2994 records that the credential scan was recognised as 'duplicating the apps list's own scan' and was only cached, not shared, so the cold-load triple scan is a known, half-fixed gap rather than a deliberate design. One nuance: the caching-and-search.md:35 invariant is about the two *indexes* (the same doc at :220 treats the pairing/enterprise/MI list caches as separate), so 'contradicts the doc' is a stretch, but the credential command is exactly the third bare `/applications` scan that invariant's spirit forbids. Implementation cautions for the proposal: strip the `list_row_select` rows to id/appId/displayName before storing them as the typed `app_name_index` (otherwise credential arrays get pinned into an index six surfaces hold an Arc to), take the extra watches before the scan (`a_watch_is_captured_before_the_fetch_it_guards_not_after` in repo_invariants/cache.rs), and note `list_applications_all(` currently has four call sites (mod.rs x2 in one fn, audit.rs:174, bulk.rs:168, credentials.rs:63), so the proposed pin would drop to three.

findings.title: Restored dock mounts every parked detail pane hidden at launch, each firing its full Graph detail fetch before Home paints
findings.evidence:
open_items_workspace.rs:138: `<For each=move || session.open_items.get() key=|it| it.id let:item>` and :238 `style:display=move || if shown() { "flex" } else { "none" }`
state/tenant.rs:38: `self.restore_open_items();` (inside `set_active_tenant`, i.e. at sign-in/restore)
state/open_items.rs:217-218: `/// `shown_items` is deliberately left empty — the dock comes back, the\n/// overlay does not.` and :240 `self.open_items.set(restored);`
application_detail_pane.rs:39-51: `let detail = LocalResource::new(move || { ... applications::get_application_detail(&t.tenant_id, &id).await })` (fires on mount, not on show)
applications/mod.rs:252-282: wave 1 `try_join(get_application, list_owners)`, wave 2 `get_service_principal_by_app_id`, wave 3 `try_join(list_app_role_assignments, list_oauth2_grants)`, then `resolve_required_resource_access`
findings.rationale: `restore_open_items` repopulates `open_items` during `set_active_tenant`, the keyed `<For>` mounts a window for every item, and each pane's `detail` LocalResource runs on mount regardless of `shown`. So an operator who parked 8 items (F370: unclamped) pays 8 x (4 Graph waves + permission resolution) — roughly 40 Graph calls plus 8 IPC payloads — the instant the shell appears, none of them visible (the overlay is deliberately closed), all competing with Home's five tenant-wide scans on the same per-tenant Graph throttle and the same tokio runtime. frontend-workspace.md:124-126 documents mounting ALL windows so that chip switches don't refetch, which is an interactive-time argument; it says nothing about restore, and the restore path has no design note. The chip labels come from `open_items` titles, so the dock needs no pane to render.
findings.proposal: Gate each restored window on first show: in `open_item_window`, wrap the pane body in the existing `keep_alive`-style visited latch seeded from `shown_items` (mount when `shown()` first becomes true, then keep alive), or give `OpenItem` a `restored: bool` that defers the body until focused. Items opened interactively keep today's eager behaviour. Expected effect: launch Graph traffic drops by up to ~40 calls and 8 detail payloads on a full dock; chips still restore instantly. Add a GUI test in the open_items_dock shard asserting that a restored, un-shown item records no `get_application_detail` invoke.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence holds, with one path slip: the detail pane is apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/application_detail_pane.rs (not components/); its `detail` LocalResource at :39-51 runs on mount and tracks only tenant/object_id/reload, not `shown`. open_items_workspace.rs:128-140 mounts a window per `open_items` entry inside `<Show when=open_items non-empty>`, :238 hides by `style:display`, and the `<Show>` opens because `open_items` is non-empty even when `shown_items` is empty. tenant.rs:38 calls `restore_open_items` from `set_active_tenant`; open_items.rs:217-240 restores without clamping and leaves `shown_items` empty. The enterprise pane (enterprise_application_detail_pane/mod.rs:104-118) and the MI window (managed_identities/detail_window.rs:59-95: `list_managed_identities`, `list_held_app_role_grants`, mail scopes) behave the same. frontend-workspace.md:124-126 justifies keep-alive for chip switches only; neither it nor the CHANGELOG (:86 'parked per tenant across restarts') addresses restore-time fetching, and open_items_dock.rs has no restore test (its six tests all drive `open_item` interactively). The proposal is feasible with existing primitives: `util::keep_alive` (util.rs:24-49) with a visited latch is already the pattern in security_view.rs:58-95, and `ts::call_count` (ipc_mock/mod.rs:289, re-exported by test_support) supports the suggested assertion. Mitigations that keep this at medium rather than high: the set is bounded by MAX_OPEN_ITEMS=8 (writes cap it; a snapshot cannot exceed it), the backend caches `get_application_detail` for 60 min so an eager fetch is not wasted if the operator later opens the chip, and the MI pane's list read is a cached-index hit. The `get_application_detail` fan-out is 4 waves plus `resolve_required_resource_access` (applications/mod.rs:248-282), as stated.

findings.title: Home pulls the entire cached AuditRunResult (and four other full collections) over IPC to render counts, duplicating the Security controller's copy
findings.evidence:
home_dashboard.rs:84-96: `let cached_audit = LocalResource::new(move || { ... let _ = session.audit_reload.get(); async move { match tenant { Some(t) => audit::get_cached_audit(&t.tenant_id).await, ... } } });`
home_dashboard.rs:416 `let c = posture_counts(&r.items);` and :424 `let findings: Vec<_> = ranked_actionable_findings(&r.items)`
audit_view/controller.rs:28 `pub result: RwSignal<Option<AuditRunResult>>,` and :131 `let cached = audit::get_cached_audit(&tenant_id).await;`
commands/audit.rs:501-513: `pub fn get_cached_audit(...) -> Option<AuditRunResult> { ... let run: CachedAuditRun = state.cache.get(CacheKind::Audit, &key)?; let items = run.items; ... Some(AuditRunResult { tenant_id, total_apps: items.len(), items, ... })`
core/audit/types.rs:514 `pub struct AuditItem {` — 21 pub fields incl. `issues: Vec<String>`, `recommendations: Vec<String>`, `remediations: Vec<RemediationAction>`, `certificates`/`secrets: Vec<CredentialSummary>`
findings.rationale: The Security Posture tile shows three severity counts, a timestamp and a handful of finding-group counts, yet it receives every `AuditItem` of the cached run — up to 10,000 items with five Vecs each (several to tens of MB of JSON) — serialised by the backend, transferred through the Tauri IPC bridge and deserialised in WASM. The audit controller does the same for its own `result` signal, so a warm sign-in transfers the run twice and holds two copies in WASM memory for the session (Home is keep-alive), and every `bump_audit_reload` repeats the Home transfer. On the backend, `get_cached_audit` reads the run via the untyped `cache.get`, walking the whole `Value` tree per call. The same pattern applies to the other four cards: `list_applications_with_pairing` (10k rows, also fetched again by the Apps list on the same `apps_reload` bump), `list_enterprise_applications`, `list_managed_identities` and `list_credential_expirations` are each pulled whole to compute two or three counts.
findings.proposal: Add a `get_cached_audit_summary` command returning `{ completed_at, posture: PostureCounts, groups: Vec<(key, worst_tone, count)> }`, moving `posture_counts` / `group_findings` counting into `azapptoolkit-core::audit` (or `dto`) so Home and the Security strip keep one count source; store `CachedAuditRun` via the typed `put_typed_index_if_current` so the backend read is a refcount clone. Optionally a `get_inventory_summary` for the four list cards (counts computed backend-side from the cached rows). Expected effect: Home's IPC payload shrinks from multi-MB collections to a few hundred bytes, one audit copy lives in WASM instead of two, and `audit_reload` no longer re-ships the run.
findings.verifier_notes: All citations check out: home_dashboard.rs:84-96 loads the whole `AuditRunResult` and :416/:424 reduce it to counts; controller.rs:28 holds a second copy hydrated at :131 (SecurityView-owned, security_view.rs:42); audit.rs:501-513 reads via untyped `cache.get`, which deserialises by walking the shared `Value` tree on every call (core cache.rs:657-670); `AuditItem` (core audit/types.rs:514-560) carries 21 fields including five Vecs. The Apps list resource (application_list.rs:225-236) and Home's `apps` both track `session.apps_reload`, so a bump re-ships the pairing rows twice over IPC even though the backend serves a cache hit. posture.rs is already the single frontend count source (its header says so), so the real change is moving `posture_counts` to core/dto so the backend can compute it. Three cautions for the proposal, not refutations: (1) `get_cached_audit` is documented as 'the only command that answers from cache alone' (audit.rs:490-500) and `repo_invariants::a_command_answering_from_cache_alone_checks_the_session` will require the new summary command to call `tenant_context` too and that doc sentence to change; (2) `put_typed_index_if_current` PINS the entry and `pinned_cache_writes_stay_on_the_tenant_wide_indexes` only accepts keys in PINNABLE_KEYS (repo_invariants/cache.rs:194-203) — use plain `put_typed` (core cache.rs:864) instead, which is enough since the Audit bucket holds only tenant-wide entries and the run is TTL/invalidation-bound; (3) `ranked_actionable_findings` carries UI titles/tones and should stay frontend-side, with the backend shipping only per-key counts.

findings.title: Credential-expiry roll-up is stored with plain `put` although the `put_index` doc names it as a pinned tenant-wide index
findings.evidence:
credentials.rs:97: `state.cache.put(CacheKind::Lists, cache_key, &rows);`
core/cache.rs:711-720 (doc of `put_index`): `/// Like [`Self::put`], but marks the entry **pinned**: exempt from LRU eviction ... Use only for tenant-wide *index* entries that cost a full directory scan to rebuild and that several surfaces read — the service-principal index, the app-registration pairing rows, the credential-expiry roll-up. These share a bucket with thousands of cheap per-app entries, so without the pin a single mail-heavy audit run evicts them`
For contrast, enterprise_application.rs:115 and managed_identity.rs:88 use `state.cache.put_index_if_current(watch, &rows);`
findings.rationale: F006 already records that this store is unguarded against the store-after-invalidate race; what is new is that it is also the only tenant-wide roll-up written with plain `put`, so it is LRU-evictable by the per-app `app_detail|`/`mail_scopes|` churn that shares the `Lists` bucket — exactly the scenario the `put_index` doc describes — and the doc claims it is pinned when it is not. The effect is a silent full `/applications` rescan for the Home credential card and the Credential Expiry tab after a detail-heavy audit or browsing session, within the 60-minute TTL.
findings.proposal: In `list_credential_expirations` take `let watch = state.cache.generation_for(CacheKind::Lists, &cache_key);` before `list_applications_all` and replace `state.cache.put(CacheKind::Lists, cache_key, &rows)` with `state.cache.put_index_if_current(watch, &rows);` — this both pins the roll-up (matching the `put_index` doc and the three sibling list stores) and closes the store-after-invalidate race. No repo_invariants change is needed: the `_if_current` form is already covered by `pinned_index_writes_are_guarded_except_the_static_gallery_corpus` and the watch-order test, and PINNABLE_KEYS only governs the direct `put_index(` forms. If finding 0 is adopted, the store moves into the pairing core and inherits its own per-key watch instead.
findings.verifier_notes: The core claim is correct: credentials.rs:97 is a plain `state.cache.put`, while core cache.rs:711-720 (`put_index` doc) explicitly names 'the credential-expiry roll-up' as one of the pinned tenant-wide indexes, and the sibling list stores (enterprise_application.rs:115, managed_identity.rs:88, applications/mod.rs:220) all use `put_index_if_current` behind a `generation_for` watch. So the doc claims a pin the code does not apply. Two corrections. (a) The proposal's 'add the key to the repo_invariants pin that covers the other put_index_if_current list stores' has no target: `pinned_cache_writes_stay_on_the_tenant_wide_indexes` skips every `_if_current(` call (repo_invariants/cache.rs:146-149) and PINNABLE_KEYS (:194-203) lists only the two indexes and the two corpora — `apps_pairing_key`/`enterprise_key`/`mi_key` are not in it either. Switching to `put_index_if_current` is automatically covered by `pinned_index_writes_are_guarded_except_the_static_gallery_corpus` and `a_watch_is_captured_before_the_fetch_it_guards_not_after`; nothing needs adding. (b) Eviction realism: the Lists bucket capacity is max(MAX_CACHE_SIZE=5000, MAX_PER_OBJECT_CACHE_SIZE=10_000) = 10,000 entries (constants.rs:56/70, cache.rs:601-603), so the roll-up is evicted only after >10k per-object `app_detail|`/`mail_scopes|` writes inside the 60-minute TTL — plausible only on very large tenants. Severity low is honest. CHANGELOG-archive.md:1845-1850 lists the pinned set as `sp_index`, `apps_pairing`, the corpora — consistent with the roll-up never having been pinned despite the `put_index` doc.

findings.title: trunk build --release ships unminified CSS and JS: Trunk's `minify` defaults to `never` and nothing enables it
findings.evidence:
Trunk.toml:1-6: `[build]\ntarget = "index.html"\ndist = "dist"\n# Optimization is selected by the caller's `--release` flag ... so there is no `release` default to set here.` (no `minify` key)
justfile:51-52: `web-build-release:\n    trunk build --release --locked`
index.html:19-22: `data-wasm-opt="z"` ... `<link data-trunk rel="css" href="styles.css" />`
styles.css is 120,706 bytes (`wc -c`).
Upstream trunk `src/config/types/minify.rs`: `pub enum Minify { /// Never minify #[default] Never, /// Minify for release builds OnRelease, /// Minify for all builds Always }` and `src/config/models/build.rs`: `/// Control minification. #[serde(default)] pub minify: Minify,`
findings.rationale: The index.html comment shows the team already tuned the wasm side (`wasm-opt=z`, and Cargo.toml's `opt-level = "z"`, `lto`, `strip`) for startup, but Trunk applies `minify` separately and its default is `Never`, so the release bundle carries the 120 KB stylesheet and the wasm-bindgen JS glue verbatim (comments, whitespace, long identifiers). Every webview start parses them; a typical minify pass removes 30-40% of the CSS and more of the glue. The cost is modest because assets load from the local asset protocol, but the fix is one config line and has no effect on the GUI tests (they build via `cargo test`, not Trunk) or the dev loop (`on_release` leaves `trunk serve` untouched).
findings.proposal: Add `minify = "on_release"` under `[build]` in apps/desktop/web-rs/Trunk.toml (or `--minify` in `web-build-release` and `web-build-pages`), rebuild once and eyeball the Pages demo for any CSS the minifier changes semantically (custom properties and `@media` blocks are safe). Pin the Trunk version CI installs (`tool: just,trunk` is unpinned in ci.yml/release.yml/pages.yml) so the minifier behaviour is reproducible.
findings.verifier_notes: Trunk.toml:1-6 has no `minify` key and the comment only covers `--release`; justfile:51-52 runs `trunk build --release --locked` (the tauri.conf.json:8 `beforeBuildCommand`) and web-build-pages likewise; styles.css is 120,706 bytes (`wc -c`). Upstream trunk `src/config/models/build.rs` has `/// Control minification. #[serde(default)] pub minify: Minify` and `src/config/types/minify.rs` defines `Minify { #[default] Never, OnRelease, Always }` with `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]`, so `minify = "on_release"` under `[build]` is the correct spelling and the default really is no minification. CI installs trunk unpinned (`tool: just,trunk` at ci.yml:152, release.yml:131, pages.yml:44 via taiki-e/install-action), so the version-pin suggestion is accurate. The GUI tests build through `cargo test --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (justfile web-itest-size), not Trunk, and `trunk serve` omits `--release`, so the claimed blast radius is right. Two things I could not verify from this box: which Trunk release introduced `minify` (the upstream CHANGELOG fetch 404'd) and the exact trunk version CI currently resolves (trunk is not installed here); since install-action pulls latest, the option is present. Minification touches HTML/CSS/JS only; the wasm is already wasm-opt'd (`data-wasm-opt="z"`, index.html:19-22). Modest win, one-line fix, severity low is honest.

findings.title: Shipped frontend bundle size is never measured or recorded — only the debug GUI-test shards are gated
findings.evidence:
justfile:146-150: `web-itest-size:
    ...
    CEILING_MB=52
    DEPS=target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/debug/deps` (measures `gui_*.wasm` test shards only)
justfile:51-52: `web-build-release:
    trunk build --release --locked` (no size output)
docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md: grep for `bundle`/`wasm`/`size`/`KB`/`MB` finds only the WebView2 runtime (`~127 MB`) and CHANGELOG-baking notes — no figure for the shipped `.wasm`/`.js`/`.css`.
findings.rationale: The repo has invested heavily in wasm size for the test shards (a 52 MB ceiling, opt-level notes, a strip rationale) because size failures there are opaque, but the artifact that matters to operators — the release wasm the webview instantiates at every launch — has no recorded baseline, so a dependency bump or a new view that doubles it (Leptos view trees are known to bloat) lands unnoticed until someone complains about startup. There is no number to compare a `just web-build-release` against, and the release workflow uploads `bundle/` without reporting what is inside.
findings.proposal: Add a `web-size` recipe that, given an existing `apps/desktop/web-rs/dist/`, prints raw and gzip byte sizes of `dist/*.wasm`, `dist/*.js`, `dist/*.css` (and optionally fails or warns past a soft ceiling ~1.5x today's wasm). Call it from release.yml after 'Build bundles' and from pages.yml after `web-build-pages`, appending the table to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` — both jobs already run the release Trunk build, so this costs seconds. Do not add it to `verify-full` (which builds the frontend in debug and mirrors CI's debug-only `web` job); instead document `just web-build-release && just web-size` as the local way to check, and record the current baseline numbers in docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md next to the crypto pins.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: `web-itest-size` (justfile:146-175) measures only `target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/debug/deps/gui_*.wasm`; `web-build-release` prints nothing; no `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, `du` or size step exists in ci.yml/release.yml/pages.yml (release.yml:180-184 uploads `bundle/` blind); docs/DEVELOPMENT.md and release-updater-demo.md mention only the ~127 MB WebView2 runtime (DEVELOPMENT.md:121) and the GUI-shard ceiling (frontend-workspace.md:227) — no shipped `.wasm`/`.js`/`.css` figure anywhere. The one correction is the `verify-full` hook: `_verify-core` (justfile:293) builds the frontend in DEBUG (`web-build`), and CI's `web` job never builds release either, so wiring a release Trunk build (opt-level z + lto + codegen-units 1, minutes per run) into `verify-full` would slow the local gate and break the 'CI parity' the recipe claims (justfile:318-329). The measurement belongs where release builds already happen.

findings.title: Graph/ARM/Key Vault transports send no client-request-id and never capture request-id/Date — Microsoft-support correlation is impossible for every non-Exchange failure
findings.rationale: Microsoft Learn ('How to debug Microsoft Graph API calls', 'Best practices for working with Microsoft Graph § Reliability and support') says: generate a unique GUID per request, send it as `client-request-id`, log it, and always log the response `request-id` and `Date` — 'they're required when you report issues ... to Microsoft Support. Without these headers, diagnosing the issue is difficult.' Today a Graph 403 (`forbidden (403): {body}`), a 404, a post-budget 5xx or a 429 surfaces with status+body only; there is no identifier a support engineer can hand to Microsoft, and no log line at all is written for the terminal failure in the transport. The repo's own DEVELOPMENT.md policy ('log the ui_code/request id') is met only by the Exchange client.
findings.proposal: In `send_core_url_with` (and `scoped_get`/`scoped_send_core`, ARM `send_with_retry`, KV `send_core_url`): (a) mint a v4 GUID per logical request (move `commands::guid::new_v4_guid` into `azapptoolkit-core` so the crates can use it; `rand` is already a dependency) and set `client-request-id`; (b) on any non-success capture `request-id`/`client-request-id`/`Date` (ARM: `x-ms-request-id`, `x-ms-correlation-request-id`; KV: `x-ms-request-id`; batch: the same keys from each sub-response `headers` map) and append them to the error detail the way Exchange's `compose_error_detail` does (`… (request-id: …, client-request-id: …)`) so the UiError message and any toast carry them; (c) emit one `tracing::warn!(method, path_without_query, status, request_id, client_request_id, "graph request failed")` at the terminal-failure site (Attempt::Done(Err(..)) paths and budget exhaustion). Pin with a wiremock test in `tests/transport.rs` asserting the request header is present and the ids appear in the error. Effect: every failure in the log and the UI is correlatable by Microsoft support; the 429/5xx question 'which endpoint' becomes answerable.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is real. crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/transport.rs:499-513 builds only Authorization/ConsistencyLevel/Prefer/Content-Type; 586-600 read only Retry-After and WWW-Authenticate. A repo-wide grep for client-request-id / request-id / x-ms-request-id / x-ms-correlation hits ONLY the Exchange client (crates/azapptoolkit-exchange/src/client/transport.rs:216,221,235 and its tests) — Graph, ARM (crates/azapptoolkit-arm/src/transport.rs:72-77) and Key Vault (crates/azapptoolkit-keyvault/src/client.rs:~200) never mint or capture a correlation id, and batch.rs:52-58 reads only retry-after from the sub-response header map. docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:348-351 does state 'log the ui_code/request id, never a raw body'. Not handled anywhere else (no repo_invariants test, no architecture doc decision). One correction to the proposal: `rand` is a dependency of src-tauri only (apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:86), not of azapptoolkit-core or -graph, so moving `commands::guid::new_v4_guid` into core adds `rand` to that crate (already in Cargo.lock, but AGENTS.md treats deps as a cost — worth stating). Also keep the appended ids out of the raw-body path so the DEVELOPMENT.md policy holds. Severity medium is fair for a support-oriented tool whose Exchange client already sets the standard.

findings.title: README says a failed update *install* is logged, but `perform_update` failures are never logged (check failures already reach the file via the plugin's log::error! bridged by LogTracer)
findings.rationale: An operator whose fleet never sees updates (proxy blocking github.com, signature mismatch, malformed latest.json) is told by the README to look in the log — and the log is empty. `check_for_update` maps the plugin error straight into a UiError and the launch path pattern-matches `Ok(Some(_))`, dropping `Err(_)` without a trace. This is distinct from F036/F139 (the unread opt-out) and F250 (bug template fields): here the documented diagnostic path does not exist.
findings.proposal: In apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/updater.rs add `tracing::warn!(error = %e, "update install failed")` at the `.map_err(updater_err)` sites in `perform_update` (and for the `app.updater()` failure in both commands); optionally `tracing::info!(current = %update.current_version, available = %update.version, "update available")`. Do not duplicate the check-failure line the plugin already emits. Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: The quoted lines are real (README.md:252-253, updater.rs:19-21 has no tracing call, shell.rs:164-167 drops Err). But the headline claim 'nothing logs it / the log is empty' is false for the check path: tauri-plugin-updater 2.12.0 (Cargo.lock) emits `log::error!("failed to check for updates: {err}")` on a network failure, `log::error!("update endpoint did not respond with a successful status code")` on non-2xx and `log::error!("failed to deserialize update response")` on a malformed latest.json (vendored src/updater.rs:550,555,561), and the backend's `tracing_subscriber::registry()...try_init()` (lib.rs:357-366) is `SubscriberInitExt::try_init`, which installs `tracing_log::LogTracer` because tracing-subscriber's default `tracing-log` feature is on (workspace Cargo.toml:53 sets no default-features=false; Cargo.lock lists tracing-log under tracing-subscriber 0.3.23; vendored util.rs:61-74). Those records land in the daily file at ERROR under target tauri_plugin_updater::updater, which the default `info` filter admits. So the proxy-blocked and malformed-manifest scenarios ARE logged. What is genuinely unlogged: `app.updater()` construction failure, and every `perform_update` failure — the plugin has no log call in download/download_and_install/install (only 4 error/warn sites in the whole plugin, the 4th is a deb-package warn), so a signature-verification or download failure leaves no line, and README's 'or install' half is unmet.

findings.title: Startup panics with zero diagnostics if the log file cannot be created: install_tracing `.expect()`s the appender before any subscriber or panic hook exists
findings.rationale: `create_dir_all`'s error is ignored, then `build()` is unwrapped. On a read-only or unwritable app-data dir (locked-down %APPDATA% redirection, a sandboxed/kiosk profile, HOME unset so the fallback is the install directory) the very first thing the process does is panic — before `install_panic_hook` and before any `tracing` subscriber — so a double-clicked GUI app 'just doesn't open', the advertised log directory holds nothing, and stderr is invisible. The panic hook's own doc comment (lib.rs:374-378) explains exactly why an unlogged crash is unacceptable; this path defeats it.
findings.proposal: Install the panic hook first (it only needs `tracing` macros, which are no-ops until a subscriber exists — or buffer: install a stderr-only subscriber first). Make the file appender optional: `match builder.build(&log_dir) { Ok(a) => Some(non_blocking(a)), Err(e) => { eprintln!(...); None } }`, register the file layer via `.with(file_layer_option)` (tracing-subscriber supports `Option<Layer>`), then after init `tracing::warn!(log_dir = %log_dir.display(), error = %e, "file logging disabled")`. Consider surfacing the same fact in the config screen / About so the operator learns the log is not being written. Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is real: lib.rs:11-12 calls `install_tracing()` before `install_panic_hook()`; lib.rs:340 discards the `create_dir_all` error and lib.rs:353 `.expect("failed to initialize rolling log file appender")`; config_directory() falls back to `PathBuf::from(".")` when APPDATA/HOME is unset (lib.rs:418). tracing-appender 0.2.5 (Cargo.lock) `Builder::build` → `from_builder` → `create_writer` returns `InitError` 'failed to create log directory' / 'failed to create log file' (vendored rolling.rs:189,788-799), so an unwritable app-data dir (or CWD = install dir when APPDATA is unset) panics before any subscriber or hook exists — the process exits with nothing on disk and stderr invisible for a double-clicked app, exactly the failure the panic-hook doc comment (lib.rs:374-378) says is unacceptable. No test or doc treats this as deliberate. The proposal (optional file layer via `.with(Option<Layer>)`, eprintln + post-init warn) is sound; installing the hook first alone would not help (no subscriber yet), so the appender-optional change is the load-bearing part. Likelihood is low but impact is total; medium is defensible.

findings.title: No failure or mutation logging at the command boundary: write-command files have zero tracing and the UiError conversion is a pure map
findings.rationale: The operator reports 'Remove password failed' or 'the tool disabled sign-in on the wrong app'. The log has nothing: the Graph transport logs no terminal failure, the `From` conversion is a pure map, the toast is ephemeral. Even successful destructive writes (bulk delete, disable sign-in, AAP migration, DR restore) leave no local record of which object was touched when — only Entra's server-side audit log knows, which the support engineer may not have access to. Backend-wide there is exactly one `error!` (the panic hook) and 65 `warn!`s, none on the common command failure path.
findings.proposal: (1) Hook logging where it can be body-free: add `tracing` as an optional dep of azapptoolkit-dto under `backend` and in the `ui_error_from!` arms / `From<AuthError>` emit `tracing::debug!(code = %code, retryable, status = ?err.status(), "error crossed into UiError")` — code/status only, never `%err`/message (DEVELOPMENT.md:348-351); or, cleaner, log at the terminal-failure site in each transport (finding 0c) where status + request-id are known, and leave the From impl pure. Reserve `warn!` for the command boundary (e.g. a thin wrapper or the `dispatch`/`run_bulk_seq` cores) so recovered probe errors don't alarm. (2) Ring buffer of last-N (code, status, timestamp) for the diagnostics bundle — no message text. (3) `info!(command, %tenant_id, %object_id)` in the single-sourced write cores (`remediate_*`, `run_bulk_seq`, restore) for destructive writes. Pin (1) with a capturing-subscriber test asserting the body does NOT appear.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/lib.rs:139-149 is a pure map (dto has no tracing dep, Cargo.toml lists none); web-rs/src/state/errors.rs:157-160 only toasts; the per-file counts are exact (remediation 5 cmds/0 tracing, restore 3/0, expose_api 6/0, app_roles 3/0, credentials 8/0, owners 6/0, federated 4/0, authentication 2/0, grants 4/0, scope_group 5/0, aap_migration 1/0, graph_roles/defaults/config/updater 0; bulk.rs only the three join-error warns; exactly 1 `tracing::error!` and 65 `warn!` across backend+crates). The Graph transport logs no terminal failure. So the gap is real. But proposal (1) as written violates a documented policy: `source = %err` would write the raw response body, because `http_error_enum!` derives Display as `forbidden (403): {0}` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/http_error.rs:70; likewise Api/Server carry `body`), and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:348-351 says 'log the ui_code/request id, never a raw body that could carry token material'. Also a `warn!` inside every `From` conversion fires for errors the caller then recovers from (audit.rs:66 treats code `cancelled` as expected; ARM transport.rs comment: a 400 `Api` is a Logs probe miss; 404 probes), so it would be noisy and misleading at warn level.

findings.title: Webview panics and surfaced IPC errors are never persisted to the backend log — no frontend→backend log command exists
findings.rationale: F425 documents that any non-UiError IPC rejection panics the whole WASM app. When that (or any other frontend panic — an `expect` in a view, a Leptos runtime error) happens in a release build, the operator sees a frozen or blank window; the panic message exists only in a devtools console that release builds cannot open, so a bug report can contain nothing but 'it went blank'. The backend log, the one artifact support asks for, is silent because nothing bridges the two worlds.
findings.proposal: Add `#[tauri::command] fn log_frontend(level: String, message: String)` (command + `generate_handler!` + `bindings/diagnostics.rs` stub; cap message length; re-emit at `tracing::{warn,error}!(target: "webview", %message)`). In `run()` set a custom hook that (a) calls `console_error_panic_hook::hook(info)` and (b) SYNCHRONOUSLY calls the JS `invoke` (a `#[wasm_bindgen] extern` to `window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.invoke` returning a Promise that is dropped — the IPC post happens on the call, not on await) — no `spawn_local` inside the hook. Guard with `is_tauri()` / `not(feature = "demo")` and register a no-op fixture in `demo::register_fixtures` (demo_fixture_coverage.rs). Separately, have `Session::report_command_error_for`'s plain-toast branch call the async binding with `code` + message. Effort M.
findings.verifier_notes: Premise verified: apps/desktop/web-rs/src/lib.rs:69 installs only `console_error_panic_hook::set_once()`; src-tauri/Cargo.toml:32-33 has just updater + dialog plugins (no tauri-plugin-log); tauri.conf.json has no `devtools`; no console/log bridge anywhere in web-rs/src (only the hook dep); README Logs (422-431) covers the backend file only. The F425 premise is also real: tauri-sys (git rev 289bd29, src/core.rs:26) does `swb::from_value(err).unwrap()` on a rejection, so a non-UiError rejection panics the WASM app. However the proposed mechanism will not work: wasm32-unknown-unknown is panic=abort, so after the hook returns the module traps; a `leptos::task::spawn_local` scheduled inside the hook is a microtask that re-enters wasm after the trap, when the instance is in an undefined state — the future is not reliably polled and the IPC never leaves. The hook must issue the IPC synchronously.

findings.title: No diagnostics affordance beyond cache stats: no 'Open log folder' / 'Copy diagnostics', no bundle command — operators are told to hand-locate and hand-redact log files
findings.rationale: Support triage today requires the operator to know the platform path, find today's file among 14, guess which lines matter, and redact by hand. The app already holds everything a minimal bundle needs (version, `cache_stats`, the resolved tenant id/cloud, the log directory) but exposes none of it together, and the one dialog that exists is about cache tuning. The bug template's version field even points at a menu that does not exist off macOS (see the docs finding).
findings.proposal: Add `#[tauri::command] fn get_diagnostics_bundle(state) -> DiagnosticsBundleDto` in commands/diagnostics.rs: version, `std::env::consts::{OS,ARCH}`, cloud, configured tenant id, `log_dir` path, `CacheStatsDto`, the last N UiErrors (ring buffer from the boundary-logging finding), and the tail (last ~200 lines) of today's `azapptoolkit.<date>.log` read from `log_directory()`. Frontend: an account-menu item 'Copy diagnostics' that renders it as text and writes it to the clipboard (the clipboard path already exists for secrets) plus a read-only path display 'Log folder: …' with a copy button — no new plugin needed; if an OS reveal is wanted later, `tauri-plugin-opener::reveal_item_in_dir` is the standard route. Update the bug template to say 'Account menu → Copy diagnostics'. Effect: one click produces what the template asks for, already scoped to today and free of hand-redaction guesswork.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is real: the account menu (shell.rs:396-470) offers Access Readiness, Settings, Cache diagnostics, Check for updates, Sign Out and the version/What's new — nothing that reveals the log path, copies diagnostics or bundles state; commands/diagnostics.rs exposes only cache_stats/clear_cache/invalidate_list_cache/set_cache_enabled/set_cache_config; `log_directory()` (lib.rs:390) is referenced nowhere outside install_tracing; a repo-wide grep for 'log folder', 'reveal_item', 'diagnostics bundle' finds nothing in code, docs or CHANGELOG. bug_report.yml:47-53 asks the operator to hand-locate and hand-redact log lines, and :32 points at a Help menu that does not exist (see finding 10). The clipboard helper the proposal wants to reuse exists (web-rs/src/util.rs:79 `copy_text`). Caveats for implementation: the bundle text should carry the same 'redact tenant/object ids' caveat the template gives (or elide them), and the 'last N UiErrors' part depends on finding 3's ring buffer landing first. Medium is fair for a feature gap that the repo's own issue template exposes.

findings.title: Retry/throttle log lines carry no endpoint, status or reason — a 429 storm and a 5xx outage look identical, and inner $batch 429 re-batches are silent
findings.evidence:
http_retry.rs:207-212 (the only log line on the retry path):
  tracing::warn!(
      attempt = budget.attempt(),
      label,
      retry_after_secs = ?retry_after_secs,
      "transient failure; retrying"
  );
crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/transport.rs:552: `let outcome = with_retries("graph", retry_class, |_| {` — constant label, attempt number discarded, nothing logged inside the closure.
crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/batch.rs:283-300 (inner-429 re-batch loop): the only side effect is `obs.on_throttle(max_retry_after)` and `budget.wait(max_retry_after).await;` — no tracing call.
findings.rationale: The task's headline failure mode — a 429 storm during a 10k-app audit — produces N identical `transient failure; retrying label="graph" attempt=1 retry_after_secs=Some(…)` lines plus `throttle: throttled, reducing in-flight cap`. `RetryReason` (Throttled vs Transient) and the HTTP status are not logged, so a Graph 503 incident and a tenant-quota 429 are indistinguishable in the file; the endpoint family (`/servicePrincipals`, `/$batch`, `/sites/{id}/permissions`) is unknown, so the engineer cannot tell which fan-out is being throttled. When the budget is exhausted nothing is logged at all — the error becomes a toast. The `$batch` path, 'the throttle-happiest endpoint in the API' per its own comment, logs no inner retries.
findings.proposal: (1) Log `reason = ?reason` and the retried error's `ui_code()`/status in `with_retries` (E: Display is available; add a `status: Option<u16>` to `Attempt::Retry` or log `%err`). (2) Pass a label that names the request: `format!("graph {method} {path}")` where `path` is the URL with query stripped (`url::Url::path()`) — no `$filter` values, hence no PII; ARM/KV can do the same. (3) In `batch_chunk`, `tracing::info!(throttled = throttled.len(), pending = urls.len(), attempt = budget.attempt(), ?max_retry_after, "$batch: re-batching throttled sub-requests")` and a `warn!` when the budget is spent. (4) When `!budget.may_retry()` log `warn!(label, attempts, "retry budget exhausted")` before returning `Err(err)`. Effort S; all inside `http_retry`/transport, covered by existing paused-clock tests.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is real: crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/http_retry.rs:207-212 logs only attempt/label/retry_after_secs; `reason` and the error's status are in scope but dropped, and budget exhaustion (204-206) returns `Err(err)` with no line at all. Graph passes the constant label "graph" (transport.rs:552), Key Vault "key vault" (client.rs:175); ARM passes a caller `label`. batch.rs has zero `tracing::` calls — the inner-429 re-batch loop (283-300) only calls `obs.on_throttle` and `budget.wait`, and the throttle's own line is `throttle: throttled, reducing in-flight cap` (commands/throttle.rs:119) with from/to/retry_after only. So a 429 storm and a 5xx outage are indeed indistinguishable in the file and the endpoint family is unknown. Two implementation notes: `with_retries` has no `E: Display` bound, so logging `%err` needs either a bound or a `status: Option<u16>` on `Attempt::Retry` (the latter is preferable — `GraphError::Server`'s Display embeds the response body, which DEVELOPMENT.md:348-351 says not to log); and the path-only label proposal should use `Url::path()` so `$filter` values never appear. Existing paused-clock tests cover the loop, effort S.

findings.title: `target = "azapptoolkit::graph"` / `"azapptoolkit::cache"` are recorded as a field named `target`, not as the event target, while both layers hide the real target with `with_target(false)`
findings.evidence:
service_principals.rs:188-192:
  tracing::debug!(
      target = "azapptoolkit::graph",
      first_page = page.items.len(),
      "service-principal index first page"
  );
Same form at service_principals.rs:209,216,257; commands/applications/mod.rs:143,151; enterprise_application.rs:74,77; managed_identity.rs:57,60; permissions.rs:55,58 (`tracing::debug!(target = "azapptoolkit::cache", kind = "Lists", key = %key, "hit")`).
tracing-0.1 macros.rs:21,55,663: the target override is spelled `target: $target:expr`; `$($k:ident).+ = $($fields:tt)*` is the field arm.
lib.rs:359-365:
  .with(fmt::layer().with_target(false).compact())
  .with(fmt::layer().with_ansi(false).with_target(false).with_writer(file_writer))
findings.rationale: The authors intended a stable logical target so operators could filter `azapptoolkit::cache=debug`; instead each line gains a bogus `target="azapptoolkit::cache"` field, the real target stays the module path, and the intended filter matches nothing. Because both fmt layers set `with_target(false)`, the support file shows no module attribution at all — a `warn` from the graph crate, the auth crate or a command is indistinguishable except by message text (the README's `azapptoolkit_graph=trace` advice works only because the real target is the module path).
findings.proposal: Replace `target = "..."` with `target: "..."` at the 13 sites (compile-checked), and turn `with_target(true)` on for the FILE layer only (keep stdout compact). Add a repo-invariant test that greps for `tracing::\w+!\(\s*target =` to keep the misspelling from returning. Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified against tracing 0.1.44 (Cargo.lock) macros.rs: the `debug!`/`warn!` arms spell the target override `target: $target:expr` (arms at lines 88-100 of the macro), and `target = "..."` falls into the field arm `($($k:ident).+ = $($field:tt)*)` (line 181), so it is recorded as a field named `target` while the real target stays module_path!(). The repo itself demonstrates the correct form — the auth crate and state.rs use `target: "auth"` (crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:175,192; token_cache.rs:366; state.rs:351,366; commands/auth.rs:41) — so the intent is clear and the 12 misspelled sites (not 13: service_principals.rs:189,209,216,257; applications/mod.rs:143,151; enterprise_application.rs:74,77; managed_identity.rs:57,60; permissions.rs:55,58) are a slip. Both fmt layers set `.with_target(false)` (lib.rs:359-365), so the file carries no module attribution either. No repo_invariants test guards tracing macro syntax (files: cache, cancel, commands, fanout, release, sources, trust). Proposal (fix spelling, `with_target(true)` on the file layer only, grep-based invariant) fits repo conventions. Low is honest.

findings.title: Startup banner records only version and log_dir — OS/arch, cloud, configured tenant id and build profile are missing, so the first thing support needs is not in the log
findings.evidence:
lib.rs:368-372:
  tracing::info!(
      version = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
      log_dir = %log_dir.display(),
      "azapptoolkit starting"
  );
state.rs:248-256 logs the tenant/client id only when they are UNSET (`"AZAPPTOOLKIT_TENANT_ID is not set; sign-in will fail until configured"`); nothing logs the resolved value or its source (env / settings.json / baked). bug_report.yml:36-43 asks the operator to type the OS by hand.

Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is real: lib.rs:368-372 logs only version + log_dir; state.rs:247-256 warns only when tenant/client id equal the unset sentinel and never records the resolved value or which of env / settings.json / baked won (`resolve(...)` at 235-246 discards that). bug_report.yml:36-46 asks for the OS by hand. findings.title: The security audit — the app's flagship long run — writes no start/finish summary line (duration, totals, coverage gaps, cancelled), unlike the site sweep
findings.rationale: 'The audit took 40 minutes / stopped at 60% / shows fewer findings than yesterday' are the questions a support engineer gets; the log cannot answer any of them — a fully successful run of 10k apps leaves zero lines, a cancelled run leaves zero lines, and the `degraded` coverage gaps (which the UI correctly refuses to cache) are never recorded. The site sweep already demonstrates the one-line pattern.
findings.proposal: At `run_audit` entry `tracing::info!(%tenant_id, "audit started")`; capture `Instant::now()`; at the end `tracing::info!(total, scored = items.len(), unscored, degraded = ?degraded, cancelled, elapsed_secs = start.elapsed().as_secs(), "audit complete")`. Same two lines for `backup_tenant`, `restore_tenant` and the `bulk_*` commands via `run_bulk_seq` (count, failed, cancelled). Effort S.
findings.verifier_notes: Evidence is real: `run_audit` (audit.rs:127-133) has no entry line; the only completion-adjacent line is the conditional `audit completed with unscored principals` warn at 380; grep for Instant::now/elapsed in audit.rs returns nothing; a clean or cancelled run logs zero lines and `degraded` gaps are never recorded. The contrast holds: sharepoint.rs:964-970 emits `site sweep complete` with total/sites_scanned/sites_failed/cancelled, and docs/architecture/resource-access-and-permission-tester.md:36 documents that as the pattern ('the run ends with one `site sweep complete` summary log line'). backup.rs has six per-item warns but no summary `info!`, restore.rs and bulk.rs have none (bulk.rs only the three join-error warns). Low/S is honest; the proposal mirrors an existing repo idiom.
